## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `f8e2a4d`

**Stoa v0.1 BETA adoption pattern: single self-extracting `stoa.md` + sidecar layout + `/stoa <subcommand>` namespace + tracked-artifacts coherence + per-operator opt-in.**

Locks the ship-vehicle for v0.1 BETA distribution to Stoa internal teams. Multi-turn refinement trail this session resolved ~12 design questions; this entry consolidates them into the single adoption decision.

**The ship vehicle.** A single self-extracting markdown file `stoa.md` that adopters download into their repo. On first Claude session after install, the file's embedded install kit creates the artifact set, edits `.gitignore`, then self-edits to remove the install kit (becomes slim ~100-line operational rules).

**Adopter repo footprint after install** (4 files created + 2 edits):

- `stoa.md` — slim methodology (post-extract); imported via `@stoa.md` from the operator's `CLAUDE.md`
- `.stoa/installed` — marker (version + ISO timestamp + canonical-source URL + git-hash of `stoa.md` at install + operator handle from `git config`)
- `.stoa/artifacts.md` — per-project tracked-artifacts list (operator-populated; flat list of `<path> → 1-2 line role description`; read on-demand, never auto-imported)
- `.claude/commands/stoa.md` — single dispatcher for all `/stoa <subcommand>` invocations
- *Edits:* operator's `CLAUDE.md` (gets `@stoa.md` import line; one-time, never auto-touched again); operator's `.gitignore` (auto-appends `# Stoa local settings` block + `.claude/settings.local.json` line)
- `.claude/settings.local.json` — gitignored — stores per-operator opt-in preference key `stoa.beta`

**The `/stoa <subcommand>` namespace.** All Stoa interactions live under one slash command; ALL subcommands also prose-invokable per the methodology's loose-framework principle.

Active subcommands (do real work in v0.1):
- `/stoa help` — command surface + starting paths
- `/stoa init` — bulk repo scan + propose tracking artifacts (incremental on re-runs; flat list per-file accept/decline OR all/none mode)
- `/stoa track <path>` — operator-initiated single-file tracking (granular complement to `init`)
- `/stoa opt-in` — set `stoa.beta = "opt-in"` for this operator in this repo
- `/stoa opt-out` — set `stoa.beta = "opt-out"`
- `/stoa status` — read marker + opt-in state + tracked artifacts count

Stub subcommands (exist but say *"this integration ships post-v0.1, coming after beta retrospective"*):
- `/stoa ask @<handle> <question>` — Slack-bridged cross-laptop handoff (was `/ask @<handle>` in `b4f2e9c`; refined under namespace here, not contradicting)
- `/stoa respond <question-id>`
- `/stoa publish-doc <path>`, `/stoa fetch-comments <path>`, `/stoa triage-comments <path>`, `/stoa request-review <path>`
- `/stoa announce-plan <wal-id>`

Total 14 subcommands; all in one `.claude/commands/stoa.md` dispatcher (~250-300 lines, loaded only when `/stoa` invoked).

**Per-operator opt-in.** Three banner states printed once per session:
- *Active* (`stoa.beta = "opt-in"`): `[stoa v0.1 BETA] This project is handled via Stoa. Opt-out: /stoa opt-out`
- *Inactive* (`stoa.beta = "opt-out"`): `[stoa v0.1 BETA] Stoa NOT active in this repo. Opt-in: /stoa opt-in`
- *Undecided* (key unset): `[stoa v0.1 BETA] Stoa is available. /stoa opt-in / /stoa opt-out / /stoa help`

Stoa rules enforced only when active. Multi-operator A/B testing (some operators opt-in, others opt-out in the same repo) is supported by construction — preferences are gitignored, per-operator. The fragmented audit trail this produces IS the beta signal.

**Tracked artifacts (Pattern Y, renamed from "project documents").**

The right framing for what to track is **artifacts that need coherence with design decisions** — extension-agnostic. Includes markdown design docs, HTML demos, diagrams, runbooks, audience summaries, KB material. Excludes auto-generated build outputs (heuristics: filename markers `*.generated.*`, `auto-*`, `*-autogen*`; header markers `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED -->`, YAML frontmatter `generated: true`; vendor / dist / build / node_modules / `.git` / anything in `.gitignore`).

Each tracked entry has the same shape: `<path> → 1-2 line operator-prose role description`. No categorized typology (rejected after surveying actual practice in PoC + spinoff — both maintain a flat list of canonical artifacts with prose roles, not a strict taxonomy). The detection-vocabulary table earlier proposed was over-engineering; Pattern Y matches what teams actually do.

**Pre-flight check** (~30 tokens at top of slim `stoa.md`, always loaded): if `.stoa/installed` missing AND no install kit in this file → surface broken-state warning ("Stoa partial-install — re-fetch `stoa.md` from `<url>`") and skip rule enforcement that session. Detects the wrong-repo-copy case where someone copies a post-extract slim file without its companion artifacts.

**`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape** (when opted-in only): ephemeral chat-only suggestions, never written to file content; operator's content stays operator's content. First-occurrence-per-session-per-file; declined-not-this-kind persists per-project; never act without explicit yes.

**Prose ↔ slash command equivalence.** All subcommands are prose-invokable per loose-framework principle. `stoa.md` includes a small mapping section listing intent → subcommand routings. Slash commands are formal entry points; prose is the natural interface.

**Auto-update via git-hash.** The `.stoa/installed` marker records the canonical-source git-hash at install time. v0.2's `/stoa update` (deferred) compares with current upstream hash; proposes update if different (operator-driven; never auto-pulls). Handles forks-with-modification cleanly — operators see the diff before applying; can keep their fork.

**Coexistence with existing `CLAUDE.md`.** The 1-line `@stoa.md` import is the only edit to operator's `CLAUDE.md` — happens once, at install. Stoa updates go to `stoa.md` only; the project's `CLAUDE.md` (with project-specific rules) is preserved across Stoa version bumps. Operators are free to fork `stoa.md` locally and edit for their needs; this is first-class behavior, not deviance.

**Versioning.** Methodology calendar continues at *2026-05*; adoption-package version is *v0.1 BETA*. Both are stamped in `stoa.md`'s header. Banner shows just `v0.1 BETA` (less verbose for every-session display). v0.1 ships only the active subcommands; integration-dependent commands ship as stubs.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision (landed in the same commit):**

- `stoa.md` (NEW) — the canonical adoption-package file at `spinoff-ai-assisted-development/stoa.md`.
- `starter-CLAUDE.md` — deprecated; replaced with a redirect note to `stoa.md`.
- `proposed_methodology.md` — `/ask @<handle>` → `/stoa ask @<handle>` syntax updates throughout; references to `starter-CLAUDE.md` → `stoa.md`.
- `executive_summary.md` — same syntax + reference updates.
- `getting_started.md` — full rewrite of install steps for v0.1 (single-file self-extracting flow, opt-in banner UX, separate-commit recommendation, post-extract caveat about copying between repos).
- `workflow-demo.html` — file tree (scene 6) shows post-install layout; command syntax in scenes 1/2/3 updated to `/stoa ask @<handle>`.

**Refs:** `b4f2e9c` (drop role-to-handle mapping; preserved in spirit — handles are still the addressable identifier; this entry refines syntax under the `/stoa` namespace), `4f8c3a2` (proposal refactor that opens the slot for v0.1 adoption work), `e4a7c3b` (second-order benefits — the data dividend; v0.1's `.stoa/installed` marker records the install hash so v0.2 can begin asking the methodology-evolution questions empirically), `c8b4d09` (loose-framework + AI-as-interpreter — prose-equivalence and Pattern-Y coherence-without-typology both honor this), `9c2b5fa` (doc-set suggestion menu — Pattern Y aligns with this section's existing intent), `7a3f128` (prior-art positioning — Stoa as methodology, not product, is preserved by adopter-fork-friendliness)

**Open follow-ups deferred to v0.2** (not blocking v0.1 ship):
- `/stoa update` (auto-update via git-hash comparison)
- `/stoa untrack <path>` (granular removal complement to `track`)
- Pre-flight check potentially moves to a Claude Code hook (eliminates the ~30-token cost; needs hook installation in the kit)
- Per-category preference flip after `/stoa init`'s "not this kind" decline (more granular control)
- Integration adapters (Slack, Jira, GDocs) — the 7 stub subcommands become active

## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `a3f9c21`

**Stoa v0.1 BETA scope: explicitly support AI assistants beyond Claude Code (Codex first); Claude-Code-first defaults preserved. Concrete canonical-source URL resolved against this repo.**

A scope clarification on `f8e2a4d` (v0.1 BETA adoption pattern). The original v0.1 design was Claude-Code-first by construction (`CLAUDE.md` auto-read, `@stoa.md` import syntax, `.claude/commands/` slash dispatch, `.claude/settings.local.json` per-operator opt-in). Beta-readiness review surfaced the question: *does this work for engineers using Codex (or another AI assistant)?* Decision: yes, with documented adaptation; the portable surface area is large enough that Stoa is methodology-first, not Claude-Code-first.

**What's portable across AI assistants:** the methodology core. `stoa.md` itself, the install kit, `.stoa/installed`, `.stoa/artifacts.md`, `context_log.md`, and prose intent recognition all work in any AI that can read repo files and follow instructions. The install kit is markdown-as-instruction-to-AI; any agent that follows operator prompts and can edit files can run it.

**What's Claude-Code-specific** (and how Codex adapts):

1. **`CLAUDE.md` auto-read at session start** → Codex equivalent: `AGENTS.md`.
2. **`@stoa.md` import syntax** → no equivalent in Codex; instead `AGENTS.md` instructs the AI in prose to read `stoa.md` (and the dispatcher) at session start. The instruction-to-AI replaces the file-import directive.
3. **`/stoa <subcommand>` slash dispatch** → prose invocation in Codex (typing `/stoa init` literally still works because the AI recognizes the text from `stoa.md`'s prose ↔ subcommand mapping section; just no command-completion or `$ARGUMENTS` templating).
4. **`.claude/settings.local.json` per-operator opt-in** → not loaded by Codex. v0.1 BETA Codex users operate as **always opted-in** (silence mechanism deferred to v0.2 if Codex adoption grows).

**Codex setup pattern** (documented in [`getting_started.md`](getting_started.md) §"Using Codex (or another AI assistant)?"): same `curl` to drop `stoa.md`, then wire `AGENTS.md` to *"At the start of each session, read `stoa.md` and `.claude/commands/stoa.md` (if it exists) and follow their rules."* instead of using the `@stoa.md` import line in `CLAUDE.md`. The install kit then runs identically — Codex's edit tools handle the file writes; the install proposal + confirmation flow is unchanged.

**Beta validation status.** Claude Code path is the supported beta target. Codex path is **hand-traced "should work"** — not validated against a live Codex install. Codex beta participants are explicitly running the first known Codex-Stoa session and asked to flag any AI-behavior gaps in `#stoa-beta`. The methodology framing (*"Stoa as of 2026-05"*) treats *"AI is good enough to interpret loose framework"* as a load-bearing assumption — Codex-as-target is a falsifiable claim, and v0.1 BETA is the first stress-test of that claim across a non-Claude assistant.

**Concrete URL resolution.** Placeholders in `stoa.md` (`<acme-platform>/spinoff-ai-assisted-development/...`) and `getting_started.md` (`<stoa-url>/spinoff-ai-assisted-development/...`) resolved to GitHub URLs against this repo:

- **Human-readable references** (canonical-source pointers, broken-state warning, install marker, install-complete message): `https://github.com/ivan-avramov/acme-platform/blob/main/spinoff-ai-assisted-development/<file>`
- **`curl`-installable references** (Path A + Codex setup `curl` commands): `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ivan-avramov/acme-platform/main/spinoff-ai-assisted-development/<file>` (raw-content URL — blob URLs return HTML pages, not file content)

The blob/raw distinction is documented in `getting_started.md`'s "Source URL for v0.1 BETA" callout so beta participants don't accidentally `curl` the blob URL and get an HTML page. v0.1 BETA distribution is gated to Stoa internal teams via this repo; future versions may move to a dedicated source location.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision:**

- [`getting_started.md`](getting_started.md) — added §"Using Codex (or another AI assistant)?" between "What gets installed" and "Pick a project" (5-row adaptation table; replacement Step-1 `curl` + `AGENTS.md` wiring; Step-4 opt-in skip note; untested-in-beta caveat).
- [`getting_started.md`](getting_started.md) — Path A `curl` and Codex `curl` commands now use concrete raw-GitHub URLs; "Source URL for v0.1 BETA" callout rewritten to give both blob and raw URLs with the rationale.
- [`getting_started.md`](getting_started.md) — Prerequisites line cross-references the new Codex section.
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) — pre-flight check, broken-state warning, source-repo pointer, install-marker template, install-complete message, and stub-command "Track follow-up at" message all get concrete blob URLs.

**Refs:** `f8e2a4d` (v0.1 BETA adoption pattern this scopes — most of the integration glue defined there is preserved as Claude-Code-first defaults; Codex is the first portable-target case study), `9d2f8a3` (Kiro prior-art research — established Stoa as methodology, not product, which makes multi-agent support a natural extension rather than a fork), `c8b4d09` (loose-framework + AI-as-interpreter — prose-equivalence of slash commands is what makes Codex compatibility work without re-architecting; Codex users invoke via prose and the AI routes per the same mapping section), `e4a7c3b` (second-order benefits — multi-agent adoption itself becomes a methodology-evolution data point: do Codex sessions produce comparable WAL discipline to Claude sessions? v0.2's analytics can ask)

**Open follow-ups deferred to v0.2:**

- Portable opt-in mechanism that works under both Claude Code and Codex (e.g., `.stoa/operator-<email>.local` gitignored file readable by either AI).
- `stoa-install.sh` script that detects `claude` vs `codex` CLI and wires the appropriate sidecar (`CLAUDE.md` vs `AGENTS.md`) automatically.
- Codex-specific dispatcher pattern if `.claude/commands/` non-loading proves to be a recurring friction point (e.g., move dispatcher logic into `stoa.md` proper, or replicate as `AGENTS-COMMANDS.md`).
- Any AI assistant beyond Codex (e.g., Cursor, Aider, Continue, JetBrains AI): same playbook — sidecar instruction file + prose invocation + opt-in adaptation. Each new target is a similar hand-traced exercise until validated in a beta.
- Move `<acme-platform>` / `<stoa-url>` placeholder convention out of `stoa.md` entirely: hardcode the canonical-source URL in the v0.2 install kit (it's a beta-time placeholder; once the source location stabilizes, no placeholder is needed).

## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `b7d4e08`

**WAL guardrail: AI refuses off-pattern mutations to `context_log.md` and surfaces a warning with three options (append-as-entry, save-elsewhere, override) instead.**

Operationalizes founding principle #3 (append-only WAL with stable identity). The principle was stated declaratively in `f8e2a4d`'s adoption pattern; this entry adds the AI-enforcement rule that prevents accidental violations.

**Trigger.** Concrete failure mode: an operator asks the AI to append something to `context_log.md` that isn't a WAL entry — an Excalidraw JSON export, a transcript, a code dump, a stack trace, a screenshot caption. The AI, being helpful, would just append it. The WAL becomes a junk drawer; the audit trail stops being audit-grade. Other failure modes the rule covers: in-place edits to existing entries, deletions, reordering, rename/move.

**Rule.** When Stoa is active (`stoa.beta = "opt-in"`), the AI must:
1. Recognize when a requested operation on `context_log.md` is off-pattern.
2. Refuse to perform it; surface a `[stoa]` warning naming the violation.
3. Offer three options: (a) append-as-WAL-entry rationalizing the content, (b) save-elsewhere (separate file or tracked artifact), (c) override-and-proceed (with a note that Stoa won't enforce coherence on the resulting state, and the operator can append a `rollback` entry afterward if they want the deviation auditable).
4. Wait for operator choice before acting.

**The only methodology-defined operation** is appending a complete, well-formed WAL entry (one of `decision`, `won't-do`, `table`, `branch`, `rollback`, `observation`). All other mutations are off-pattern.

**Off-pattern includes:**
- Editing an existing entry's body, ID, or refs in place.
- Deleting an entry or any part of one.
- Appending non-WAL content (JSON, transcripts, file exports, code dumps).
- Reordering entries (chronological order is contract).
- Renaming or moving the file.

**Not off-pattern** (proceed silently): appending a well-formed WAL entry; reading the WAL; iterating on an entry the AI just drafted in the same turn before operator confirmation.

**Why a guardrail and not a `[stoa]` suggestion.** `[stoa]` suggestions propose; the operator chooses; default is silent. A guardrail refuses by default and requires explicit override. The asymmetry matches the asymmetry of the failure: a missed tracking suggestion costs little (one undocumented artifact), but a junk-drawer WAL destroys the methodology's audit-trail value-prop and is harder to recover from than to prevent.

**Override is non-frictionless on purpose.** A typo fix in a recently-appended entry technically requires the operator to confirm override (one extra round-trip). This is the right tradeoff: the friction is small; the prevented failure mode is large; and surfacing the warning every time keeps the operator's mental model of "the WAL is append-only" honest. If override fatigue becomes a real complaint in beta, v0.2 can add a "small clarifications" carve-out — but the default starts strict.

**Opt-out behavior.** Guardrail applies only when Stoa is active. Opted-out / undecided operators see no warning — they have explicitly opted out of methodology enforcement, and `context_log.md` is just a markdown file at that point.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision:**

- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) — added §"WAL guardrail (active only)" between §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" and §"Tracked artifacts (coherence discipline)". Section spells out the off-pattern detection list, the warning shape, and the not-off-pattern carve-outs.
- No update to [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) — the founding principle #3 (append-only WAL) already establishes this; the guardrail is the AI-enforcement layer, an operational rule that lives in `stoa.md`. Operators consulting the methodology proposal don't need a separate guardrail callout; AIs reading `stoa.md` do.

**Refs:** `f8e2a4d` (v0.1 BETA adoption pattern — defines the WAL append-only principle this rule enforces; this entry slots into the same operational layer as §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" / §"Tracked artifacts" / §"Opt-in mechanic"), `c8b4d09` (loose-framework + AI-as-interpreter — the guardrail pattern is itself loose: AI recognizes off-pattern intent, surfaces options, operator decides; no strict-schema validator mediates, just AI judgment + operator confirmation), `e4a7c3b` (second-order benefits — WAL discipline at scale is what makes the data dividend possible; junk-drawer WALs poison the well for the methodology's own self-assessment loop)

**Open follow-ups deferred to v0.2:**

- Extend integrity guardrails to other stoa-managed files: `.stoa/installed` (immutable marker; should never be hand-edited), `.stoa/artifacts.md` (constrained format: flat `<path> → 1-2 line role description` list; off-pattern = appending free-form text, deleting entries silently, reordering).
- "Small clarifications" carve-out if override fatigue surfaces in beta — e.g., typo fixes within N hours of original append, or detected-trivial diffs (whitespace, single-character edits).
- Detection sharpening: the AI's recognition of off-pattern operations is judgment-based in v0.1. If false-positives or false-negatives cluster around specific patterns, codify those patterns as detection rules.

## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `d5a8f10`

**Coherence cadence: three trigger events for tracked-artifact walks. Adds AI-discipline post-decision propagation pass + operator-triggered `/stoa audit` to v0.1 BETA. Deterministic hooks deferred to v0.2 — pushing the loose-framework / AI-as-interpreter premise as far as it will go first.**

Beta-surfaced gap. Operator observed they keep having to ask the AI to do consistency audits. The methodology promises *"self-consistent state, by construction"* (value-prop #7), but v0.1's coherence mechanism (pre-commit drift walk against tracked artifacts, per `f8e2a4d`) covers only one of two distinct check classes. **Cross-cutting stale-reference sweeps** — finding references to deprecated patterns from older decisions that didn't fully propagate — were operator-on-demand and unreliable in practice. The audit pass `c2e1b8f` is the concrete demonstration: 7 propagation-lag fixes that should have landed when their underlying decisions did, but didn't.

**Three trigger events for coherence walks (all AI-discipline-based in v0.1 BETA):**

1. **Pre-commit drift walk** (already in v0.1, from `f8e2a4d`). On each commit, walk `.stoa/artifacts.md`; surface drift relative to *this* commit's changes; propose updates in the same commit.

2. **Post-decision propagation pass** (new). When a `decision`-type WAL entry lands, the AI **reflexively** walks the tracked-artifacts list looking for references the new decision supersedes — old terminology, deprecated file names, renamed slash commands, stale version stamps, prior shape of the just-changed thing. Trigger = appending the entry; walk happens on the same turn that proposes/writes the entry. Findings surface as `[stoa]` suggestions before the next commit. This is the rule that catches the propagation-lag class — references to old patterns that linger in other docs because nobody walked them when the decision settled.

3. **`/stoa audit`** (new). Operator-triggered full sweep on demand. Covers terminology drift, slash-command namespace consistency, URL placeholders, broken section anchors, version-stamp consistency, and propagation lag from older decisions. Used at beta-readiness reviews, milestones, after a flurry of edits, on demand. Implementation = AI judgment with grep + read across tracked artifacts (and the corpus when useful); never auto-fixes without confirmation. After applying fixes, propose appending an `observation` WAL entry recording the audit — same shape as `c2e1b8f`.

**Loose framework, AI as interpreter — pushed all the way.** All three triggers rely on AI compliance, not enforcement tooling. This is a deliberate test of how far that premise scales. The methodology's `2026-05` framing already treats *"AI is good enough to interpret loose framework"* as a load-bearing assumption; coherence cadence is a direct stress-test of that assumption. If reflexive-AI-walk + on-demand-audit is sufficient — operators stop having to ask and propagation lag stops accumulating — the framework stays loose. If recurring-reminder fatigue persists in beta despite the new rule + command, that's the signal to escalate to v0.2 hooks (Claude Code hooks or git hooks that fire the same passes deterministically).

**`[stoa]` suggestion shape applies.** When the post-decision pass or `/stoa audit` surfaces findings, they appear as `[stoa]` suggestions (chat-only, ephemeral, never auto-write). Operator decides each: accept-and-fix, reject-with-reason, override. Same discipline as tracking suggestions and drift suggestions.

**Why operator-triggered for `/stoa audit`, not auto-fired.** The post-decision propagation pass (#2) catches drift around a single just-settled decision; that's reflexive AI behavior with a clear trigger. The full audit (#3) is broader — it scans the corpus against all recent supersession relationships and is heavier. Auto-firing it would either be too frequent (every commit) or arbitrary (every N commits). Explicit invocation matches when the operator actually wants verification (release prep, major milestone, "I've done a lot of editing recently"). v0.2 may add scheduled triggers if beta surfaces a clear cadence preference.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision (this commit):**

Primary (the decision itself):

- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) — added §"Coherence cadence (active only)" between §"Tracked artifacts (coherence discipline)" and §"Prose ↔ subcommand mapping". Three-trigger model spelled out.
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"Prose ↔ subcommand mapping" — added prose-route for `/stoa audit` (*"audit consistency"* / *"check for stale references"* / *"sweep the docs"*).
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"Command surface" — added `audit` to the v0.1 active subcommand list.
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"First-run install kit" → embedded `.claude/commands/stoa.md` dispatcher: added `audit` to the `help` printout, added `### audit` subcommand spec (what to check, how to run, discipline).

Propagation-pass findings (the new rule firing on its own decision — dogfooding):

- [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) §"7. Self-consistent state, by construction": old phrasing said *"Pre-commit doc-discipline cadences enforce alignment"* (single-trigger language pre-dating this entry). Updated to reflect the three-trigger model with a pointer to [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"Coherence cadence" + the AI-discipline-as-stress-test framing.
- [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) §"What's not yet specified" → "Agent hooks generalized library": old phrasing said *"Stoa has only `/stoa check-coherence` + a sketched pre-commit doc-discipline cadence"* (now superseded). Updated to *"Stoa v0.1 BETA has the three-trigger AI-discipline coherence cadence but no deterministic event hooks"*; reframed the hook-library proposal as the v0.2 escalation path if AI-discipline proves insufficient in beta.
- [`getting_started.md`](getting_started.md) Step 4 (`/stoa opt-in` description): old phrasing said *"pre-commit coherence discipline applies"* (single-trigger). Updated to *"coherence cadences activate (pre-commit drift, post-decision propagation, on-demand `/stoa audit`); the WAL guardrail starts enforcing append-only on `context_log.md`"* — also picks up the `b7d4e08` WAL guardrail (which had been silently activated by opt-in but not documented in the opt-in description).

**Refs:** `f8e2a4d` (v0.1 BETA adoption pattern that established tracked-artifacts list + pre-commit drift walk; this entry adds the second and third triggers as siblings), `c2e1b8f` (the audit pass that triggered this decision — concrete demonstration of what propagation lag looks like and what catching it costs when it has to be operator-prompted), `c8b4d09` (loose-framework + AI-as-interpreter — coherence cadence is the next test of how far that premise reaches), `b7d4e08` (WAL guardrail — same shape as the new rule: AI surfaces, operator decides, no enforcement tooling)

**Open follow-ups deferred to v0.2:**

- Beta retrospective question: *"Did operators stop having to ask?"* If yes, the loose-framework premise scales. If no, escalate to deterministic hooks and revisit which AI-discipline rules are operator-noticed-as-missing vs invisible drift.

## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `f8b3c52`

**Make the AI-quality-dependency framing explicit. Stoa is AI-assisted by design; quality depends on agent capability; mistakes happen. The looseness is the value, not a flaw — rigid alternatives have repeatedly failed because engineers route around them.**

Operator-surfaced. The looseness principle (`c8b4d09`) established the mechanism (AI as interpreter, no strict-schema enforcement); this entry adds the **honest framing** of what that mechanism implies for adopters — including why we're choosing this tradeoff over the rigid-validator alternative. The framing was implicit before; making it explicit changes nothing about how Stoa operates but sets adopter expectations correctly.

**The framing (5 points):**

1. **Stoa is AI-assisted by design.** Quality and consistency depend on the agent doing the interpretation. A strong model (high-quality context handling, faithful instruction-following, low confabulation) makes Stoa reliable. A weak model — or a strong one running out of context — introduces drift.

2. **Mistakes happen.** They're interpretation slips by an AI reasoning over loose conventions, not bugs in coded rules. Recovery is via the WAL (durable record survives noisy AI surfaces) + `[stoa]` suggestions (next session catches what the last one missed) + `/stoa audit` (operator-triggered sweep).

3. **Why we accept this:** rigid alternatives have repeatedly failed. Methodologies that encode their discipline as strict validators, mandatory schemas, gate-checks before commit, lint-rules at PR time — engineers reject them at scale. Not because rigor is bad, but because engineers want **freedom to experiment**: to deviate, to try unusual approaches, to skip ceremony when it doesn't fit. A methodology that punishes experimentation gets routed around or quietly abandoned (same effect).

4. **The asymmetry:** *better to be occasionally fuzzy than universally bypassed.* AI mistakes are recoverable; operator-bypass is catastrophic. The looseness is what makes adoption possible at all.

5. **Value compounds with agent capability.** As models improve, Stoa's interpretation reliability rises and the AI-fuzziness cost drops. v0.1 BETA's premise is that agents are *already* good enough; the beta tests that empirically. v0.2 hooks are the escalation path if the answer is *"not yet."*

**Adopter expectation set:** Stoa adopters are signing up for a methodology whose quality depends on the AI they give it. Run it with a strong model and current context; budget for the AI to occasionally miss things; trust the WAL to be the durable record even when AI surfaces are noisy.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision (this commit):**

Primary:

- [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) §"The loose-framework principle" → new subsection §"What this means in practice" — the five framing points covered in adopter-facing prose.
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"Founding principles" → principle #1 (*"Loose framework, AI as interpreter"*) — extended with one-sentence flag of AI-quality dependency + link to the proposal section.
- [`executive_summary.md`](executive_summary.md) — added §"The honest tradeoff" between *"Why now"* and *"What you get"*. Stakeholder-prose summary of the same framing.

Propagation-pass findings (per `d5a8f10`'s post-decision rule firing on this decision): no additional propagation lag detected. The framing is new explicit content; no pre-existing references contradict it.

**Refs:** `c8b4d09` (loose-framework principle this entry surfaces — `c8b4d09` accepts the AI-interpreter premise; this entry surfaces what that premise *implies* about quality, mistake-tolerance, and why-not-rigid alternatives), `d5a8f10` (coherence cadence — directly motivated by the same AI-discipline-not-coded-rules logic; the AI-driven consistency walks ARE the kind of mechanism that depends on agent quality), `b7d4e08` (WAL guardrail — same shape: AI surfaces, operator decides, no enforcement tooling), `9d2f8a3` (Kiro prior-art — Stoa's *non-product, non-strict-tool* framing fits with the loose-framework rationale here)

**Open follow-ups:**

- **Concrete model-quality threshold for adopter recommendation.** v0.1 BETA assumes *"a current frontier model with adequate context"*; we haven't articulated where the cliff is (e.g., *"Claude Opus 4.6+ / Sonnet 4.6+ recommended; smaller models likely insufficient for the post-decision propagation pass"*). Beta will surface this empirically as people try Stoa with various models.
- **Failure-mode catalog.** When the AI does miss something — what does that look like in practice? A short *"common AI-mistake patterns and how to recover"* appendix in `getting_started.md` would set expectations and shorten the recovery path.
- **Cost-per-decision telemetry.** As `[stoa]` suggestions fire on every conversation, the AI's overhead grows. The cost-transparency surface (already a v0.2 follow-up from `9d2f8a3`) is the place this lands.

## 2026-05-09 — `decision` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `a4d9e02`

**Add a "spark" section near the end of the proposal naming non-software domains where Stoa might apply (novel writing, movie production, songwriting, automotive parts design, business planning, portfolio management). Framed as afterthought + invitation, not load-bearing claim. Cross-domain validation is open and explicitly invited.**

Operator-surfaced. The intuition: Stoa's primitives (WAL, refining sessions, tracked-artifact coherence, AI-as-interpreter, loose framework) are domain-agnostic by construction; the PoC validated software design but the same shape plausibly applies wherever decisions accumulate over time and a team needs rationale to survive. The decision is not whether Stoa generalizes (we believe it does), but **how much weight to put on that claim in the proposal**.

**The framing chosen:** afterthought, near the end of the proposal, sparky and invitational rather than authoritative. Reasoning:

- The methodology's evidence is one infrastructure-software trial. A heavyweight cross-domain section claims more than the evidence supports.
- The user's tone signal: *"a spark for people to potentially pickup on and get creative with"*. That tone — *"if you're working in domain X, try this and tell us"* — invites adoption attempts without overselling.
- The proposal's primary audience is Stoa (a software org). Cross-domain framing as the headline would muddle the value-prop for that audience.
- Honest about untested. Cross-domain claims are hand-traced reasoning, not validated evidence. Calling them out as speculation prevents over-promising.
- Invitational call-to-action at the end ("we'd love to hear what worked, what cracked, and what needed reshaping") creates an explicit feedback channel for cross-domain experimentation. If someone runs Stoa on a novel and reports back, that's how the generalization story moves from speculation to substance.

**Section placement:** between §"How to start tomorrow (smallest viable adoption)" and §"Working notes" — semantically the right spot because "How to start tomorrow" calls to action for the immediate audience (Stoa software teams), and the spark calls to action for future broader audiences (anyone in any domain). Working notes is operator-scratch, intentionally to-be-deleted-before-sharing.

**Substrate-vs-content distinction made explicit.** Methodology core is portable (the five primitives). Domain-specific layers: integration adapters (git/Slack/Jira equivalents), vocabulary recipes (decision/plot-beat/design-choice), default cadences (parallel-tight in software vs. sequential-slow in some creative pipelines), and **AI affordances per domain** — the AI-quality-dependency framing from `f8b3c52` directly bears on this. Stoa's value compounds with AI's *domain-specific* capability: where AI is strong now (prose consistency, plot coherence), Stoa pays off now; where AI is weaker (judgment-heavy creative novelty, specialized engineering tolerance analysis), Stoa's value follows AI maturity.

**Doc updates flowing from this decision (this commit):**

- [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) — added §"A spark — Stoa beyond software?" between §"How to start tomorrow" and §"Working notes". Six speculative-domain examples (novel, movie, song, automotive, business plan, portfolio). Substrate-vs-content paragraph. Invitation to report cross-domain attempts.

Propagation-pass findings (per `d5a8f10`'s post-decision rule): no propagation lag detected. The spark section is net-new content; no pre-existing references contradict it. The executive summary stays scope-conservative (Stoa audience first); cross-domain framing is appropriately confined to the proposal's tail.

**Refs:** `c8b4d09` (loose-framework principle — domain-agnostic by construction; this entry is a downstream observation that the principle implies cross-domain portability), `f8b3c52` (AI-quality dependency — explains *why* cross-domain value varies even when the primitives apply uniformly: AI affordances differ per domain), `9d2f8a3` (Kiro prior-art — Stoa-as-methodology-not-product framing makes cross-domain adaptation a natural extension rather than a fork)

**Open follow-ups:**

- **First non-software trial.** Pick one domain (likely candidate: technical-book authoring or research write-up — async + Markdown-friendly + AI-good-at-prose). Run a 6-week trial parallel to the software beta; compare what crosses cleanly vs. what cracks.
- **Per-domain vocabulary recipes.** If cross-domain adoption becomes real, ship "starter vocabularies" — the per-domain default labels for entry types, role names, and primitive names. v0.1 BETA's framing is software-default; cross-domain users would benefit from less translation overhead.
- **Per-domain integration adapters.** Software's git/Slack/Jira anchor is heavy and assumes engineering tooling. Adapters for Scrivener/Google Docs/email (writers), Final Draft/Frame.io (filmmakers), Bloomberg Terminal/Excel (portfolio managers) would be a v0.3+ exploration.
- **Cross-domain retrospective channel.** If cross-domain experiments happen, the feedback can't all squeeze into `#stoa-beta` (which assumes a software-Stoa audience). A separate `#stoa-cross-domain` or equivalent surfaces this without polluting the primary beta signal.

## 2026-05-10 — `observation` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `e7c4b29`

**Empirical scalability analysis of the WAL: where the cliffs are, what scales naturally, what doesn't, and a layered mitigation menu (subagent delegation, log-splitting, digests, RAG). Recorded as context, NOT as settled plan — concrete v0.2+ choices to be revisited once beta surfaces real-world WAL size data.**

Triggered by operator question on whether the WAL is a scaling bottleneck. Honest answer: yes, beyond a few MB. The analysis below quantifies the cliffs and surveys mitigation options, but **the v0.2+ implementation choices are deliberately left open** — the right answers depend on what beta adopters actually experience, and committing to a path now would over-fit on speculation.

**Empirical reference points (this codebase):**

- [`acme-platform/conversation_log.md`](../conversation_log.md) (PoC, ~3 months active): **316KB / 2,798 lines / 42 entries** → ~7.5KB / 67 lines per entry.
- [`spinoff/context_log.md`](context_log.md) (Stoa methodology, ~1 month): **136KB / 1,316 lines / 36 entries** → ~3.8KB / 37 lines per entry.

Average entry size has been **~5-7KB** — uncomfortably high relative to a leaner discipline (1-3KB target with link-out for depth).

**Per-Stoa-repo extrapolation** (commit count proxies decision volume, ~1 WAL entry per 25 commits, ~5KB per entry — survey of 17 Stoa repos at `/Users/username/workspace/` on 2026-05-10):

| Repo | Commits | Age (y) | Estimated WAL size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `acme-code` | 142,320 | 8.4 | **~28 MB** |
| `snowflake-native-app` | 16,781 | 2.7 | ~3.4 MB |
| `stoa-sdk` | 14,458 | 2.3 | ~2.9 MB |
| `acme-control-plane` | 11,653 | 8.6 | ~2.3 MB |
| `spcs-control-plane` | 10,582 | 2.5 | ~2.1 MB |
| `modeler` | 7,452 | 3.0 | ~1.5 MB |
| `stoa-docs` | 925 | 0.9 | ~185 KB |

Of 17 repos surveyed, **roughly half are at or past the single-file cliff** if Stoa were retroactively applied. `acme-code` is dramatically so.

**Where the cliffs are:**

| Project age / WAL size | Tokens | Access pattern |
|---|---|---|
| 0-1y / <1MB | <250K | Single-file. AI grep + read in parent context. No friction. |
| 1-3y / 1-3MB | 250K-750K | Single-file or year-bucketed split. Subagents for cross-cutting. |
| 3-10y / 3-15MB | 750K-3.75M | Year/phase-bucketed split. WAL-librarian subagent default. Digest for orient. |
| 10y+ / 15MB+ | 3.75M+ | Same plus optional RAG. Cold-storage archival. |

**What scales naturally:** append-only writes (O(1)), targeted grep + read (~10MB ceiling), GitHub markdown rendering, conflict-free git merges.

**What doesn't scale:** whole-WAL synthesis in a single parent context (degrades past ~3MB, broken past ~5MB), new-joiner orient without a digest, cross-WAL queries (cross-repo decisions, methodology meta-analysis).

**Layered mitigation menu (NOT a settled plan — sub-questions for v0.2+ revisit):**

1. **Entry-size discipline** (v0.1+, applied this commit indirectly): push toward 1-3KB entries with link-out for depth. Cheap; should already be applied. Current ~5-7KB average suggests this is itself a behavioral question worth flagging in beta.
2. **AI access pattern discipline** (v0.1+, this commit): never slurp the WAL into parent context. For non-trivial queries (cross-cutting, orient-style, multi-entry history), delegate to a WAL-librarian subagent. AI-discipline, not new tooling — Claude Code subagents already exist.
3. **Year/phase-bucketed log-splitting** (v0.2 candidate): boundary choices open. Year-bucketed (calendar) vs size-bucketed (~1MB chunks) vs phase-bucketed (project milestone). Each has tradeoffs: calendar is predictable but doesn't track project intensity; size is uniform but breaks at arbitrary points; phase is meaningful but requires operator action.
4. **AI-generated digest** (v0.2-v0.3 candidate): periodic summary of current state + key decisions. Live WAL appends as before; digest is the fast-read entry point. Cadence (operator-triggered? on-commit? weekly?) and format (chronological? by-topic? by-status?) open.
5. **RAG indexing** (v0.3+ optional escape valve): for projects past ~15MB or with many concurrent agents querying the WAL. Adds infrastructure; clashes mildly with the loose-framework principle. Reserved for cases that need it.

**Why this is observation-not-decision:** the layered menu is the right *shape* of answer, but the concrete cutoffs (split boundary in MB? digest cadence? RAG threshold?) depend on beta evidence. Committing now would either over-engineer (specifying things adopters don't need) or under-engineer (missing patterns we haven't seen). Better to record the analysis as context and revisit when there's real-world WAL-size data from beta projects.

**Doc updates flowing from this observation (this commit):**

- [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md) — added §"Scalability — the WAL bottleneck" between §"What this proposal does NOT claim" and §"How to start tomorrow". Threshold table + mitigation menu + honest acknowledgment that the full story is v0.2+ and unsettled.
- [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) — added §"WAL access pattern (active only)" between §"WAL guardrail" and §"Tracked artifacts". Trivial-vs-non-trivial query rule; subagent delegation for non-trivial queries; AI-discipline, no new tooling.

Propagation-pass scan (per `d5a8f10` — observation entries don't strictly trigger the rule, but ran it anyway): no propagation lag found. The existing §"What's not yet specified" entry on multi-file rotation still reads as accurate (rotation is *still* deferred; this entry quantifies why and surveys options without choosing). The §"Long-lifecycle properties" entry in §"What this proposal does NOT claim" stays accurate (long-horizon behavior is still unverified empirically). No contradictions surfaced.

**Refs:** `c8b4d09` (loose-framework principle — the scaling story is in tension with this; subagent delegation is preferred over RAG infrastructure as the v0.1+ default precisely because it stays loose), `f8b3c52` (AI-quality dependency — large WALs stress AI capability differently than small ones; subagent delegation partly keeps each AI call's context within its quality envelope), `d5a8f10` (coherence cadence — same shape: AI-discipline, not deterministic tooling; pushes how-far-AI-discipline-scales as the load-bearing question)

**Open follow-ups (revisit when beta data arrives):**

- **Empirical entry-rate measurement.** What's the actual WAL-entries-per-commit ratio in beta projects? The "1 per 25 commits" assumption is a guess; real data will tighten or widen the threshold table.
- **Entry-size discipline as explicit rule.** Current ~5-7KB average is high relative to the 1-3KB target. Should `stoa.md` push harder on lean entries — perhaps a `[stoa]` suggestion *"this entry is getting long; consider link-out for depth"* on entries over some threshold?
- **Split-boundary choice.** Year-bucketed (calendar) vs size-bucketed (1MB chunks) vs phase-bucketed (project milestone). Each has tradeoffs noted above. Beta project data should clarify which boundary makes the best tradeoff in practice.
- **WAL-librarian subagent prompt template.** v0.1's rule is "delegate to a subagent for non-trivial queries"; the actual subagent prompt is operator-or-AI-improvised today. A canonical template would standardize quality. Belongs alongside the v0.2 dispatcher.
- **Digest format and trigger.** Manually-generated `digest.md`? Auto-generated by `/stoa digest`? Cadence-based or commit-count-based? Format: chronological vs by-topic vs by-status?
- **Cross-repo WAL aggregation.** When decisions in one project affect another (per the meta-repo open question in [§"What's not yet specified"](proposed_methodology.md#whats-not-yet-specified)), the scaling question compounds. How does an AI synthesize across N project WALs? Subagent-per-WAL with a coordinator? Single-shared meta-WAL?
- **Beta retrospective question:** *"Did your project's WAL fit single-file for the duration of the beta? Did AI synthesis stay fast? Did `/stoa orient` stay usable as the WAL grew?"*

## 2026-05-10 — `observation` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `f3a8d61`

**Add-on to [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29) (WAL scalability): WAL compaction may give enough headroom that AI context-window growth catches up before structural mitigations (log-splitting, RAG) become necessary.**

Operator-surfaced sequel to `e7c4b29`. The mitigation menu there listed entry-size discipline (#1) as cheap-and-immediate, but treated log-splitting / digests / RAG (#3-#5) as the structural answers for Stoa-scale projects.

**The bet:** aggressive compaction discipline + AI context-window growth = the structural answers may stay optional, not required, for most projects through their lifecycle.

- **Compaction = entry-size discipline + link-out for depth + periodic digest + archival summarization of completed phases.** Push WAL footprint toward 1-3KB per entry; let AI synthesize summaries of dormant areas.
- **AI context windows are growing quickly.** Opus 4.7 is 1M tokens today; trajectory suggests 2M+ near-term, 10M+ within a few model generations. If a project's compacted WAL stays under ~3MB and base-tier context reaches ~3M+ tokens, **the bottleneck disappears entirely** — projects fit in a single AI session, no rotation or RAG needed.

**Why observation, not decision:** falsifiable but not yet falsified. Two empirical questions: (1) does compaction discipline hold in beta — do operators write 1-3KB entries reliably, or do they drift toward 5-10KB? (2) does AI context-window growth track expectation? Both must hold for the bet to land. If either fails, structural answers come back.

**What this changes about `e7c4b29`'s plan:** doesn't change the cliff thresholds (still where they are at current model context). Does change the priority ordering — compaction discipline becomes the load-bearing answer first; structural answers move further down the priority queue. The §"Scalability — the WAL bottleneck" section in [`proposed_methodology.md`](proposed_methodology.md#scalability--the-wal-bottleneck) doesn't need rewriting; this entry is the next-level commentary on its mitigation menu.

**Refs:** [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29) (parent scalability analysis; this is the addendum), [`f8b3c52`](context_log.md#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f8b3c52) (AI-quality dependency — the value-compounds-with-AI-capability thesis extends here as value-compounds-with-context-window-growth), [`d5a8f10`](context_log.md#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--d5a8f10) (coherence cadence — the post-decision propagation pass becomes a candidate compaction enforcer: every settled decision is an opportunity for AI to fold rationale into compact-form)

**Open questions (revisit when beta data arrives):**

- **Compaction-discipline measurement.** Track average entry size in beta projects. Drift above ~3KB suggests the bet is in trouble.
- **AI context window trajectory.** Watch model releases. 2-3M base-tier within a year vs. stall.
- **Per-project vs cross-project headroom.** Compaction handles single-project WAL; cross-WAL queries (cross-repo decisions, methodology meta-analysis) compound the bottleneck. The bet may hold per-project but not cross-project.

## c91f4a2 — observation — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.1 BETA solo-mode trial: 28 scenarios run via fresh-Claude subagents; 7 spec gaps surfaced; 6 fixes applied to `stoa.md`; reusable test harness shipped at [`tests/`](tests/). Pre-commit harness re-run validates all changes.**

This entry records the trial that produced the v0.1 BETA spec sharpening + the harness as a durable artifact. The trial itself is a methodology-on-methodology event: Stoa applied to its own validation.

**Note on header form:** this entry is the first in this WAL to use the new canonical form `## <id> — <type> — <date>` per the just-spec'd [`stoa.md` §"WAL entry form"](stoa.md). Earlier entries used a richer form (date-first + author tags inline). Older entries are append-only-grandfathered. Author info now lives on a body line just below the header (`**Authors:** ...`) — preserves the long-standing author-tagging convention for this WAL while keeping the canonical heading minimal (ID + type + date only). v0.2 will reconcile if author-tagging proves load-bearing across more projects.

### What ran

28 scenarios across 10 categories, every one driven by a freshly-spawned Claude subagent (no memory of prior turns) — the most authentic available test of whether `stoa.md` is self-sufficient.

- **Install (4)** — success, decline, no-CLAUDE.md, idempotent re-open.
- **Opt-in mechanic (3)** — opt-in/out toggles, broken-state warning when slim `stoa.md` lands without companion artifacts.
- **WAL operations (2)** — first decision creates `context_log.md`; all 6 entry types appended (decision, observation, won't-do, table, branch, rollback).
- **WAL guardrail (5)** — every forbidden op refused with verbatim warning + 3 alternatives (in-place edit, deletion, raw-content append, reorder, rename).
- **Tracked artifacts (3)** — `/stoa init` walk, `/stoa track` override, `/stoa audit` drift detection.
- **Coherence cadence (2)** — post-decision propagation pass fired *reflexively* on a settled decision; pre-commit drift walk caught code↔doc mismatch and split unrelated commits.
- **Session restart (2)** — fresh session synthesized a 3-entry decision arc; fresh session caught accumulated drift while answering an unrelated operator question.
- **WAL queries (3)** — categorical recall (won't-do), cross-WAL synthesis (cross-cutting analysis with delegation-justification), end-to-end synthesis.
- **Codex emulation (2)** — Codex-constrained subagent install + post-install (deferred from harness; manual real-Codex runbook lives at [`tests/codex-smoke-test.md`](tests/codex-smoke-test.md)).
- **Update flow (2)** — repo-extensions add + simulated upstream update preserves operator content via marker contract.

### Spec gaps surfaced + fixes applied

Seven gaps surfaced. Six fixed in [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) this commit:

1. **`canonical-hash` field** unobtainable at install time (install runs locally; no source-repo access). Renamed to `stoa-md-hash` (the local file's hash at install time, used by v0.2's `/stoa update` to detect upstream changes). Status output updated to match.
2. **WAL entry header form drift between sessions.** Beta data showed 3 different shapes (H2 with date / backtick prose without date / backtick prose with date) — broke naive `^## [0-9a-f]{7}` queries. New §"WAL entry form (canonical)" pins the header form `## <id> — <type> — <date>`; body stays loose.
3. **`.gitignore` create-vs-append underspecified.** Install kit Step 3 now explicitly says "create if missing, otherwise append."
4. **Self-edit method underspecified.** One subagent left a stray `stoa.md.new` from a `cat > .new && mv` pattern that didn't `mv`. Step 6 now mandates atomic in-place writes.
5. **Codex compat gap in install kit Step 5.** Original spec only handled `CLAUDE.md`. New spec has explicit Claude-Code branch (CLAUDE.md + `@stoa.md`) and Codex branch (`AGENTS.md` + prose pointer; create from scratch is OK; Step 4 silently skipped).
6. **Bold-the-line convention** — beta data showed prose-mode `[stoa]` proposals blur into normal turn text. New paragraph in §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" mandates bold one-liners. Applies most strongly to prose-mode hosts (Codex) but everywhere for cross-host consistency.

The 7th — **`/stoa status` mis-reports opt-in for Codex hosts** (reads `.claude/settings.local.json` which Codex doesn't write to) — mostly addressed via the dispatcher's status-output update in this commit (Codex hosts report "active (Codex host — always-on)"); full validation pending real Codex.

### New design: repo-specific extensions section

Operator-flagged: `stoa.md` is a repo-specific extension from a certain hash; Claude Code often remembers project rules in `CLAUDE.md` or methodology-shaped rules in the methodology file itself. Updates need to preserve operator content. New §"Repo-specific extensions (operator content — preserved across updates)" added to slim portion of `stoa.md` with a programmatic anchor — `<!-- repo-extensions-below : preserve everything below this line across stoa.md updates -->`. Update contract: everything above marker = upstream-replaceable; everything below = operator-owned, preserved verbatim.

Validated end-to-end via harness scenarios U1 (operator adds a Linear-ticket-reference rule below marker; stoa.md goes 229 → 247 lines; canonical portion byte-for-byte preserved) and U2 (simulated upstream update merges new prose mapping into canonical portion; operator content survives; no stray `.new`). Subagent self-discipline win during U1: noticed the new "decision entries cite Linear tickets" rule applied to *the very entry recording the rule* and left a `Linear: <TBD>` placeholder rather than fabricate.

### Test harness — durable artifact

Lives at [`tests/`](tests/). 23 Claude Code scenarios + 1 manual Codex runbook.

- [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) — overview, how to run, when to run.
- [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md) — all 23 scenarios with verbatim prompts + expected outcomes + verification commands.
- [`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh) — bash automation for setup + verify + clean. Drive step (subagent prompts) is unavoidably manual — Stoa's whole premise is *AI as interpreter*.
- [`tests/codex-smoke-test.md`](tests/codex-smoke-test.md) — manual runbook for real-Codex validation (~30min, gated on a Codex user).

Codex compatibility intentionally **outside the harness**: subagent emulation under Claude can test whether `stoa.md`'s instructions are followable, not whether real Codex CLI parses them identically. Trial dir prepared for real-Codex execution at `/tmp/stoa-codex-real-20260510-075818`; smoke test deferred to whoever has Codex installed.

**Pre-commit re-run** against the updated `stoa.md`: A1 (install) + U1 (extensions add) + U2 (update preservation) + C1 (first canonical-form WAL entry) + C2 (all 6 entry types in canonical form) + G1 (guardrail refusal) all pass. One harness regex bug caught and fixed in the process (the `[a-z-]+` type pattern didn't allow the apostrophe in `won't-do`; tightened to `[a-z'-]+`).

### Notable subagent-discipline wins (load-bearing for the methodology premise)

Three behaviors that exceeded what spec or prompt mandated — direct evidence that "AI as interpreter" can carry loose-framework rules:

1. **Audit caught unintentional drifts.** `/stoa audit` flagged 2 issues I'd unwittingly introduced in scenario setup (off-by-one op count in README; internal contradiction in design.md), beyond the 3 deliberately-injected drifts.
2. **Pre-commit subagent split unrelated commits.** Caught that the working tree had pow-op work AND an unrelated tests-decision WAL entry; split into two semantic commits without being asked to.
3. **U1 subagent caught self-referential issue.** Operator's new "decision entries cite Linear tickets" rule applied to the very entry recording the rule; subagent left `Linear: <TBD>` placeholder rather than fabricate an ID.

These are exactly the cases where rigid validators fail (no schema covers all of them) but a capable AI gets right by interpretation. Reinforces [`f8b3c52`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f8b3c52)'s thesis: methodology value compounds with AI capability.

### What stayed underspecified (logged for v0.2)

- **WAL guardrail warning vs `[stoa]` proposal styling.** Bold-the-line applies to proactive suggestions; the WAL guardrail's multi-line warning template still uses blockquote + backticks. Consistent? G1 subagent flagged this. Worth pinning.
- **WAL ID cross-references in body prose.** Canonical form pins headers; in-body cross-refs (e.g., backticked IDs vs `[id](#id)` Markdown links) still convention-driven. C2 subagent flagged.
- **Rollback linkage mechanics.** Founding principle #3 says rollbacks supersede via type, but the link itself is body prose, not a structured field. Long rollback chains may stress this.
- **First-entry separator.** `---` between entries is canonical; whether the first entry in a fresh `context_log.md` has a leading `---` or not is unspecified. C1 subagent flagged.
- **`context_log.md` file preamble.** Title + "what this is" preamble is operator-content; canonical-form spec doesn't address it. C1 subagent flagged.
- **Author tagging.** Canonical form excludes author info by design (minimal). This WAL has used inline author tags for 50 entries. v0.2 question: absorb authorship into canonical as optional, or leave body-side?

### Open follow-ups

- **Real Codex smoke test.** Trial dir prepared at `/tmp/stoa-codex-real-20260510-075818`. Gated on a Codex user. Findings template lives in [`tests/codex-smoke-test.md`](tests/codex-smoke-test.md) §"Observations log."
- **Push to `main`.** Required to enable [`tests/codex-smoke-test.md`](tests/codex-smoke-test.md) Step 2a (curl from upstream). Until pushed, only the local-clone path (Step 2b) works.
- **Beta retrospective should include harness scoring.** Did each project's WAL stay greppable under the canonical form? Did `/stoa update` preserve operator content cleanly? Did the bold-the-line convention surface drift better than unbolded?
- **Harness extension to multi-laptop / shared-flow.** v0.1 BETA validates solo flow. Shared-flow validation (multi-author refining sessions, Slack handoff via `/stoa ask` once it ships) needs different harness shape.

**Refs:** [`d5a8f10`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--d5a8f10) (coherence cadence — trial validated post-decision propagation pass + pre-commit drift walk fired reflexively), [`f8b3c52`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f8b3c52) (AI-quality dependency — three subagent-discipline wins above are direct evidence), [`e7c4b29`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29) (WAL scalability — trial added empirical data: 10-entry / 200-line WAL fits comfortably in parent context, no subagent delegation needed), [`f3a8d61`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f3a8d61) (compaction add-on — trial implicitly validates the bet; entries averaged ~3KB, well within compacted-WAL territory), [`a3f9c21`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--a3f9c21) (Codex compatibility — Codex emulation surfaced the install-Step-5 gap that this commit fixes; full real-Codex validation deferred)

## 2026-05-10 — `observation` — Authors: [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)] — `7c2f9b4`

**Two-tier WAL: a size-bounded *working* WAL for daily AI operations, the full WAL preserved untouched for analytics.**

Operator-surfaced sub-thread off [`f3a8d61`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f3a8d61) (compaction add-on). Entry-size discipline + AI context growth was the original bet. This refines the mechanism: rather than (or alongside) per-entry shrinking, **operate two artifacts**:

1. **Full WAL** (`context_log.md`) — durable, append-only, never compacted. Source of truth for any analytics, audit, methodology meta-analysis, or "show me the whole arc on Topic X" query. Humans almost never read it; AI subagents do.
2. **Working WAL** — derived, size-controlled, regenerated periodically. Holds compacted forms of settled decisions, summarized digests of completed phases, and the most-recent N entries verbatim. This is what the daily refining sessions, `/stoa orient`, and pre-commit drift walks load. Bounded so it fits comfortably in parent context regardless of project age.

**Why both, not just compaction-in-place:** compaction-in-place forces a tradeoff between *current operability* and *full-history fidelity* — every byte you trim from a stale entry is a byte the future-archaeology query loses. Two-tier breaks the tradeoff: the working WAL stays lean for daily ops, the full WAL keeps full fidelity for the rare-but-important analytics path.

**Open mechanism questions** (the obvious next refining session):

- **What triggers a working-WAL regenerate?** Pre-commit drift walk? Scheduled cadence? Explicit `/stoa compact-wal`? Some hybrid?
- **What does the compactor preserve verbatim vs. summarize?** Likely: most-recent N entries + all `decision`-type entries above some load-bearing threshold (e.g., entries referenced by ≥M others) + AI-summarized rollups for everything else. Settled decisions likely keep their headers + supersession links + 1-line gist; rejected `wont-do`-type entries collapse to a one-liner cluster summary.
- **How does cross-reference integrity survive compaction?** Working-WAL entries need stable IDs that resolve to full-WAL entries. Likely: working-WAL entries carry their hex IDs unchanged, with a "see full WAL" pointer for the rolled-up cases.
- **Does the working WAL get committed, or regenerated locally per operator?** If committed: stays in lockstep across operators; conflicts on regeneration. If local: no conflict surface, but each operator may see a different working WAL at any moment. First instinct: regenerate locally; the full WAL is the canonical artifact.
- **Does AI need access to the full WAL for some operations?** Likely yes — `/stoa orient` for a new joiner asking "why did we settle X" needs full-history grep. The working WAL is for steady-state daily ops; specific archaeology queries fall back to the full WAL via subagent delegation.

**Why observation, not decision:** the design is sketched, not built. Beta v0.1 is solo-mode + small projects; the pain that motivates this won't surface until a beta WAL crosses ~1MB. Logging the idea now so it's available when that pain shows up, and so the v0.2 mitigation menu doesn't have to be re-derived from scratch.

**What this changes about [`f3a8d61`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f3a8d61):** doesn't supersede — composes. `f3a8d61`'s bet was that compaction discipline + AI growth obviate structural mitigations; this entry says the *form* of compaction worth trying first is two-tier, not in-place. Both bets succeed or fail together: if entry-size discipline doesn't hold, the working-WAL still helps (compactor does the trimming the operator didn't); if AI growth stalls, the working-WAL becomes load-bearing earlier than expected.

**Refs:** [`f3a8d61`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f3a8d61) (parent — compaction add-on; this is the mechanism sub-thread), [`e7c4b29`](#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29) (root scalability analysis), [`d5a8f10`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--d5a8f10) (coherence cadence — the regenerate trigger likely composes with the post-decision propagation pass)

**Beta retrospective question:** *"At what WAL size did daily-ops latency start to feel slow? Did the two-tier idea become attractive, or did entry-size discipline alone hold?"*

## d4a2f81 — decision — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Top-level reframing: exec summary leads with agentic-coding-enabler + PM/Eng bridge, not with the ADR comparison. ADR mentioned once honestly in intro; not a recurring drumbeat. Top 3 value-props restructured around the new framing.**

Question: How should the exec summary frame Stoa's value? External feedback flagged that the doc was over-stuffed (7 value-props, 4 framings competing in ~1500 words) and that the GenAI dependency was understated. Reading pattern observed: skimmer lands on *"design as engineering activity,"* pattern-matches to *"yet another design-doc methodology,"* and bails before reaching the differentiated claims.

Alternatives considered:
- **(a) Lead with ADR comparison.** Reviewer instinct — frame Stoa as ADR + AI. Risk: positions Stoa reactively, dilutes the proactive claim, makes it look like a refinement of an existing pattern rather than a new design-time category.
- **(b) Lead with code-coupling claim** (Self-consistent state). Strong differentiation against ADR, but doesn't speak to the urgent audience pain point (AI-assisted coding produces toys for non-trivial things).
- **(c) Lead with agentic-coding-enabler + PM/Eng bridge.** Names the user's actual pain (vibe-coding doesn't scale), positions Stoa as the upstream cognitive work that fixes it, and brings the PM ↔ Engineering integration into the lede.

Chosen: **(c)**. Single-sentence pitch carries two value-adds: (1) produces deeply-refined phased implementation plans agentic coding tools need; (2) keeps code/design/rationale in lockstep. PM intent + Engineering architecture named explicitly as the inputs the refining session integrates.

Rationale: ADR is real prior art but most audience readers don't use it. Defending against ADR makes the doc feel reactive. Leading with the urgent claim (AI-coding economics shifted; refinement is the new bottleneck) lands the value-add directly. ADR gets a single honest mention in the intro acknowledging artifact-shape isn't novel, then the doc moves to Stoa-positive framing.

Knock-on effects: top 3 value-props restructured around the new framing — (1) Produces the spec agentic coding can execute, (2) Self-consistent state, (3) Staggered + threaded refinement (async-native). Four supporting props demoted to H3 subsection. *"Why now"* section removed entirely (don't argue for AI being good; assume it and pitch Stoa). Propagation through proposed_methodology.md (6 focused edits), workflow-demo.html (new Scene 8), aurora-pivot-demo.html (closing tie-in), stoa.md (operational rules), getting_started.md (intro tweak).

**Refs:** [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10) (v0.1 BETA solo-mode trial that established the prior framing); commit `c95ac03` (baseline before this reframing).

## e5b3c92 — decision — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Adoption is dial-able: minimum (background WAL logging) is valid; maximum (deliberate refining sessions + full coherence cadence) is recommended. Refining is the recommended mode, not prescribed.**

Question: How prescriptive should Stoa appear in the exec summary and proposal? The doc was reading as *"you must do full refining sessions on every question"* — which contradicts the loose-framework principle and is brittle for operators who want minimal engagement.

Alternatives:
- **(a) Refining sessions as default/required mode.** Risk: operators who can't sustain the discipline route around the methodology or opt out entirely. Same failure mode as ADR's *"write before finalization"* discipline that rarely sticks in practice.
- **(b) Refining as recommended; minimum usage (background logging) also valid.** Operator dials in or down based on stakes of the work. Even minimum (AI watches for substantial decisions, proposes WAL entries) beats no methodology.

Chosen: **(b)**. Added explicit *"Adoption is dial-able"* paragraph in exec summary §"What Stoa is" and in proposal §"The loose-framework principle." Both make clear: refining is recommended but not prescribed; use as much of Stoa as the work needs.

Rationale: Loose-framework principle (founding #1) extends to adoption itself. The opt-in mechanic gives binary on/off; the dial-able framing fills the middle. Meet operators where they are; minimum-usage beats opt-out by a wide margin. The minimum is genuinely useful — a casual decision log with AI-mediated lookup beats no record at all.

Note: stoa.md intentionally does **not** carry this framing explicitly. The dial-able principle is structurally embedded via opt-in + chat-only suggestions + operator-decides discipline. Adding more text to stoa.md would be context pollution; the framing belongs in human-reader docs (exec, proposal).

**Refs:** [`d4a2f81`](#d4a2f81--decision--2026-05-10) (top-level reframing this was part of).

## a8d2c41 — decision — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Added "Stoa is NOT" pattern-match deflection sections to exec summary and proposal (6 bullets each). Honest acknowledgment of ADR as prior art + sharper distinctions, not defense of novelty. ADR section in proposal gains 5 prose distinctions before its existing comparison table.**

Question: How to handle the prior-art-confusion that an unprepared reader might bring (Stoa = ADR? = waterfall? = a new artifact format? = a replacement for personal AI workflows?) without making the doc feel defensive?

Alternatives:
- **(a) Defend novelty claims.** Risk: reads as posturing; ADR readers will check the claim and find the artifact-shape overlap is real.
- **(b) Lean into honest acknowledgment + sharper distinctions.** Acknowledge what's not novel (artifact shape); name what is (operational layer + async primitives + code-coupling + in-process deliberation + workflow-enforced depth). Use a pattern-match-deflection section to clear the decks early.

Chosen: **(b)**. New §"Stoa is NOT" section (6 bullets) in both exec and proposal — NOT a new artifact format / NOT a strict methodology / NOT a replacement for personal AI workflows / NOT waterfall / NOT a synchronous-team tool / NOT an agentic coder. Plus the proposal's ADR section now has 5 prose distinctions before its existing comparison table: artifact vs operational layer; post-hoc vs in-process; code-coupling; thin-ADRs-via-workflow; async primitives.

Rationale: Pretending novelty hurts credibility. Naming the prior art + the sharper deltas is stronger than defending against the confusion. The *"Stoa is to ADR what CI is to running tests by hand"* metaphor (added in proposal) captured the operational-layer claim better than any defensive framing.

**Refs:** [`d4a2f81`](#d4a2f81--decision--2026-05-10) (top-level reframing this was part of).

## c91e7f3 — decision — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**stoa.md stays lean — operational rules only. Positioning lives in exec and proposal. Trim restatements that don't change AI behavior; preserve operational WHY context for lower-tier models.**

Question: As the framing in exec and proposal got tightened, what should propagate to stoa.md (the shipped operational rulebook the AI loads at every session start)?

Alternatives:
- **(a) Mirror the new framing in stoa.md** for consistency across artifacts.
- **(b) Strictly operational** — stoa.md is loaded into AI context on every session; every line costs tokens. Positioning lives upstream; stoa.md carries only what changes AI behavior.

Chosen: **(b)**. Made one operationally-useful addition to stoa.md §"What Stoa is" — *"Refining sessions should aim for spec depth that's actionable by an agentic coder; if a decision is too vague to implement against, it's not yet settled."* This grounds the depth-target judgment-call with WHY context.

Trimmed: a second *"Stoa is not an agentic coder"* paragraph (pure positioning the exec/proposal already own); two restatements of the be-succinct heuristic in §"WAL entry form" body-content guidance. Net: −65 words from stoa.md, retaining behavior-changing content.

Rationale: Founding principle #1 (AI quality is load-bearing) is most fragile with Sonnet/Haiku-tier models. Per-session context budget is a real constraint. Keep operational WHY for judgment-call rules (lower-tier models need it to interpret aesthetic instructions like *"actionable depth"*); drop pure positioning paragraphs (any-tier model executes the same regardless of presence).

**Open follow-up for v0.2:** model-capability-aware verbosity — AI reads its own model identity at session start and adjusts reinforcement depth accordingly. Beta data should inform whether this is needed.

## 7e4c1a6 — observation — 2026-05-10

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Methodology discipline gap discovered: Opus 4.7 with stoa.md in context failed to reflexively propose WAL entries across an extended refinement cycle (5+ settled decisions, 6 artifacts edited, 3 commits made). This is the v0.1 BETA's load-bearing premise failing in real time, on the AI most-equipped to follow it.**

What happened: The refinement cycle spanned exec rewrite + propagation to proposed_methodology.md + workflow-demo restructure + aurora-pivot tie-in + stoa.md trimming + getting_started.md tweak. Multiple distinct decisions settled along the way (top-level reframing; dial-able adoption; Stoa-is-NOT deflection; context-pollution discipline; new demo scene). None were proposed for WAL entry by the AI. All five decisions reached the filesystem; none reached `context_log.md` until the operator explicitly asked *"did we write WAL entries along the way?"* after the cycle had concluded.

Why it matters: The methodology's load-bearing premise is *"AI is good enough to interpret loose framework — reflexive WAL proposal catches settled decisions."* This run is a counter-example. If Opus 4.7 with 1M context misses 5+ reflexive triggers in a row, lower-tier models (Sonnet, Haiku) will miss them more reliably. **Fast-iteration mode is the dominant adoption mode** when teams are excited; slow-deliberate refining sessions are the minority case.

Diagnosis of the failure mode:
- The existing trigger (*"propose a WAL entry when a refining session has reached a conclusion"*) relies on the AI **noticing** settlement.
- In fast-iteration mode (operator approves → AI executes → next decision settles → AI executes → ...), settlement and execution blur together. There is no obvious pause point.
- AI was prioritizing execution velocity. Each settled call was followed immediately by propagation. No reflexive *"was that decision logged?"* self-check fired.

What's changed in response: [`b3d2e94`](#b3d2e94--decision--2026-05-10) added two structural mitigations to stoa.md — explicit settling-cue linguistic patterns + a 4th coherence-cadence trigger (pre-commit WAL audit). Layered defense: catch in-flight when possible, catch at commit-time as the backstop.

**Beta retrospective questions to weigh heavily:**
- *"How often did operators have to remind AI to log a settled decision?"*
- *"Did the pre-commit WAL audit catch the cases the in-flight trigger missed?"*
- *"At what cadence did the failure mode reappear, and how did it correlate with the model tier in use?"*

If the answer is *"frequently, even with the v0.1 BETA hardening,"* that's the signal to escalate to v0.2 hooks — specifically a git pre-commit hook that **blocks** commits when uncovered decisions are detected (deterministic backstop where AI-discipline alone is empirically insufficient).

**Refs:** [`b3d2e94`](#b3d2e94--decision--2026-05-10) (the mitigation), [`d5a8f10`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--d5a8f10) (coherence cadence — this is the discipline being tested), [`f8b3c52`](#2026-05-09--decision--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--f8b3c52) (AI-quality dependency framing — this run is empirical data on where the dependency breaks), [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10) (v0.1 BETA solo-mode trial — complementary discipline-gap observation from a different angle).
