## 9d4a1e6 — table — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Install-time token cost is the highest-friction part of v0.2 adopter UX. Empirical observation from the acme-platform v0.1.4 → v0.2.0 upgrade just now: ~200k+ tokens consumed across the upgrade session (pre-strip stoa.md is ~60k chars; AI reads it at session start, extracts each `#### path:` block, writes ~6 files, runs detection/wiring/self-strip, all while the full pre-strip content stays cached). Distribution evolution is the v0.3+ design space; this entry parks alternatives and identifies what beta data would drive a decision.**

Question: Stoa v0.1's design choice was *"single self-extracting file"* — operator drops one `stoa.md` into their repo; AI extracts it on first session; self-strips afterward. The v0.1.4 → v0.2.0 transition more than doubled the install kit size (added embedded `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` script templates plus the new Step 5 / Step 6 prose), pushing pre-strip from ~44k chars to ~60k. Install/upgrade sessions now spend an estimated **200k+ tokens** processing this. The cost is borne ONCE per repo at install + ONCE per upgrade, but it's a steep first-impression UX hit. The slim post-install file (~40k chars in v0.2.0) is fine for ongoing per-session cost.

What's driving the bloat:
1. **Embedded file templates** (~20k chars of bash + markdown for the hook scripts + dispatcher + artifacts/beta_tracker templates).
2. **Install kit prose** (~10k chars of Step 1–7 + failure recovery + classification rules).
3. **Whole canonical stoa.md** stays in AI context for the install session because Claude Code's CLAUDE.md auto-load reads it in full.
4. **Multiple tool calls** during install: Read stoa.md (60k), extract each `#### path:` block via Read or grep, Write each file (combined ~30k of output), Edit stoa.md to self-strip (~20k of operations).

Distribution alternatives considered (none chosen — parked for v0.3+ design):

**(α) Curl-the-extras pattern.** `stoa.md` becomes truly slim from drop-in (~40k chars, no install kit content). First-session install kit fetches templates from canonical URL just-in-time (`curl https://.../stoa-install-kit.md`). Pro: slim from day 1; no self-strip step ever; ongoing per-session footprint unchanged. Con: install requires network; canonical URL must stay live (versioned URLs help); install kit is no longer "self-contained" in the dropped file.

**(β) Two-file drop-in.** Operator drops both `stoa.md` (slim) AND `stoa-install-kit.md` (the install kit content). Install kit file is processed only on first session (when marker is missing); deleted afterward (or `.gitignore`d). Pro: slim from day 1; no network dependency; install kit is dropped alongside, not embedded. Con: two files to drop instead of one (small UX cost); needs documentation on what to do with `stoa-install-kit.md` after install.

**(γ) `stoa-install.sh` shell script.** Pure-bash install — no AI involvement. Operator runs `bash stoa-install.sh` (or `curl ... | bash`). Script writes all files, detects hooks, runs Step 5 wiring, sets up everything deterministically. AI session-start sees only the slim stoa.md from the very beginning. Pro: zero AI tokens for install; predictable; works in any host (Claude Code, Codex, raw terminal). Con: `curl | bash` carries security concerns; no AI-mediated interactive UX during install (operator must answer prompts via bash, not via the AI); deviates from founding-principle-#1's "AI-as-interpreter" stance — though only for the bootstrap moment.

**(δ) Compressed/encoded install kit inside stoa.md.** Install kit content base64-encoded or zlib-compressed within the file. Pro: smaller per-session footprint. Con: AI has to decode (extra work, more error-prone); not human-readable; doesn't really help token-cost (decoding is still tokens); breaks the "I can just read stoa.md to understand Stoa" property.

**(ε) Claude Code plugin / skill.** Ship Stoa as a host-native plugin or skill that loads only when invoked. Pro: aligns with Claude Code's architecture. Con: kills Codex compat (no equivalent); requires Claude-Code-specific infrastructure; complicates "Stoa is just markdown" simplicity.

**(ζ) Slim canonical + per-bump migration scripts.** `stoa.md` slim; version bumps ship as one-off migration shell scripts (e.g., `migrate-v0.1.4-to-v0.2.0.sh`) operators run once. The upgrade flow stays AI-driven for marker bookkeeping; the migration script handles file shape changes. Pro: minimal per-bump cost; migration scripts can be tested in isolation. Con: scripts proliferate; operators need to find/fetch the right one per upgrade.

Promising-with-tradeoffs analysis:
- **(α) and (β) are structurally similar** — both extract install kit content from a separate location (URL or filesystem). (α) requires network; (β) requires two-file drop. Both meaningfully cut install-session cost.
- **(γ) is the lowest-token option** but trades AI mediation for shell-script-trust. Worth considering for the bootstrap-only moment (subsequent operations stay AI-driven).
- **Hybrid: (β) + (γ).** Drop both `stoa.md` (slim) + `stoa-install.sh` (executable). Operator runs the script once; script writes files, runs `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`, etc.; never loads into AI context. Slim stoa.md is then session-active.

Beta data that would drive the decision:
- **How many beta adopters complain about install token cost?** If the 200k+ install is a one-time pain that nobody actually remembers a week later, fixing it is low priority. If operators flag it as an adoption blocker (especially for repos with already-large CLAUDE.md), it's load-bearing.
- **Are operators upgrading frequently enough that the cost compounds?** Per-upgrade is also ~200k+ (same pre-strip cost). If we ship versions monthly, beta adopters pay this monthly per repo.
- **What's the actual session-context bloat after install?** v0.2.0 slim is ~40k chars; that's not zero. Per-turn cost matters more than per-install if ongoing-cost dominates lifetime.
- **Codex compat constraints.** Any option that breaks Codex (e.g., ε) probably loses; Codex is a non-trivial portion of the adopter base.

Recommendation (non-binding; for v0.3+ scoping):
- **Short term (v0.2.x):** measure first — instrument the install session for actual token usage, report in beta tracker. Don't optimize blindly.
- **Medium term (v0.3 candidate):** **(β) two-file drop-in** if beta data shows install cost is a real blocker. It's the lowest-risk change that meaningfully cuts cost while preserving "drop in a repo" UX.
- **Bigger swing (v0.4+ if needed):** **(γ) `stoa-install.sh`** as an opt-in install path alongside (β). For operators who explicitly want zero-AI bootstrap; security model documented.
- **Avoid (ε)** unless Codex-equivalent plugin support emerges.

What this entry is NOT: a decision. v0.2.0 ships as-is. The distribution evolution is a v0.3 design space, parked here so the methodology owner has the alternatives + tradeoffs already enumerated when they pick it up.

**Refs:** [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) (the v0.2.0 cut that added the hook templates pushing pre-strip past ~60k); [`f4e7b2a`](#f4e7b2a--decision--2026-05-11) (the original 40k Claude Code warning observation that flagged install-kit bloat as a concern earlier; this entry extends that into a full distribution-design analysis); founding principle #1 (the "AI-as-interpreter, no new tooling" stance — option γ is the closest test of "is the bootstrap moment an acceptable exception?").

## 6f3e1ad — decision — 2026-05-11

**`Stoa v0.2.x: add phase-settlement WAL append cadence.`**

Status quo (v0.2.0): WAL entries primarily land at commit-time via cadence #3 (now deterministic backstop). Refining-session decisions are ephemeral by design (founding principle #2) — recoverable only if the AI's settling-cue self-check fires before context loss.

Problem: gap between phase-settlement and commit-time is where settled decisions sit ephemerally, vulnerable to `/compact`, `/clear`, laptop loss, AI rate limits, or out-of-session commits. Cadence #3's hook blocks but operators `--no-verify` past it. More fundamentally, decisions made and propagated through file edits during implementation never reach the WAL if the AI rationalizes the audit skip (the pattern documented in beta_tracker entries on cadence #3 misses).

Decision: introduce a **phase-settlement** trigger — WAL entries for a phase's settled decisions land BEFORE implementation begins for that phase. Matches DB-WAL semantics (write intent before mutation). Closes the ephemerality gap.

See [`2c81fb5`](#2c81fb5--decision--2026-05-11) (detection method), [`9a4d72e`](#9a4d72e--decision--2026-05-11) (entry shape), [`e1b0c47`](#e1b0c47--decision--2026-05-11) (spec placement), [`4b8d2f6`](#4b8d2f6--decision--2026-05-11) (relationship to cadence #3 hook).

## 2c81fb5 — decision — 2026-05-11

**`Phase-settlement detection hooks to AI-side trigger, not operator-phrase bullets.`**

Question: how does the AI detect phase-settlement?

Alternatives:
1. New operator-phrase bullets in settling-cue list (*"beaten this to death,"* *"on to the next phase,"* etc.) — requires operators to learn new phrases.
2. Hook to AI's existing *"want me to start implementing?"* / *"ready to start coding?"* offer pattern.

Operator observation in-session: *"the agent has repeatedly offered to start implementing and it has been quite reliable; I've received a lot of nudges 'do you think this is good enough to implement?' or 'I think we're ready — just say go.'"*

Decision: alternative (2). The AI's offer-to-implement IS the phase-settlement signal. New discipline: BEFORE making the offer, propose the WAL batch. Zero new operator-side learning; maximum leverage of existing reliable AI behavior.

Implementation: parent decision [`6f3e1ad`](#6f3e1ad--decision--2026-05-11).

## 9a4d72e — decision — 2026-05-11

**`Phase-settlement append shape: batch of per-decision entries, not one summary.`**

Alternatives: one summary entry capturing the phase; batch of per-decision entries reviewed in one pass.

Empirical analysis of PoC + spinoff WALs (~130 entries combined, conducted in-session):
- **acme-platform (per-decision discipline):** median 18 lines/entry, 18% rollback rate, rollbacks land cleanly on narrow targets. Zero header-form drift.
- **spinoff (drifted to summaries):** median 27 lines, max 87, **12% rollback rate — lower because rolling back a 65-line bundle has friction**, so operators don't. Forces prose-patched supersession (e.g., [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) *"augments rather than supersedes"*) in lieu of structured `rollback`-type entries. Sub-decisions not independently grep-able.

Decision: batch of per-decision entries. Each independently rollbackable. Operator friction mitigated by batching the **review moment** (one operator pass), not the entry granularity.

Implementation: parent decision [`6f3e1ad`](#6f3e1ad--decision--2026-05-11).

2. Paragraph appended to settling-cue section in §"[stoa] proactive suggestion shape".

## 4b8d2f6 — decision — 2026-05-11

**`Phase-settlement cadence does not supersede cadence #3 pre-commit hook; both are retained.`**

Question: does phase-settlement [`6f3e1ad`](#6f3e1ad--decision--2026-05-11) make the v0.2 pre-commit hook redundant?

Decision: no — retain both. They cover different failure modes:
- **Phase-settlement** — proactive, AI-mediated, pre-implementation. Catches decisions before coding starts, IN session.
- **Pre-commit hook** — reactive, deterministic, pre-commit. Catches out-of-session commits, mid-phase checkpoint commits, AI failures to fire phase-settlement, and decisions that manifest in code without going through an AI session.

Removing the deterministic layer because an AI-discipline layer was added would regress to AI-only enforcement — the exact pattern cadence #3 escalated **away from** in v0.2 (motivated by [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)). Both layers are needed; they compose, not duplicate.

Beta observation worth watching: hook `--no-verify` override rate. If high, it's a wording/UX problem (hook stderr clarity, escape-valve framing) to solve in v0.2.x — not an argument to remove the hook.

## 5e3b9d4 — decision — 2026-05-11

**`Extend /stoa audit with session-reflective sweep (initialization + WAL management + cadence-fire).`**

Question: how does the operator detect Stoa rule misses without bearing cognitive load of *"watch for 50 things"*?

Status quo (v0.2.0): `/stoa audit` does cross-cutting drift sweep (terminology, anchors, version stamps). Doesn't reflect on session conduct.

Operator framing: the AI is meta-blind to its own failure modes (this session demonstrated: pre-flight skip was self-caught only after operator asked). Self-reflection on misses must be **operator-triggered**, but the tool can do the heavy lifting once invoked.

Decision: extend `/stoa audit` with a **session-reflective sweep**. Coverage:
- **Initialization compliance** — pre-flight check ran; session-start banner printed.
- **WAL management discipline** — settling cues fired; phase-settlement trigger ([`6f3e1ad`](#6f3e1ad--decision--2026-05-11)) fired before implementation offers; cadences #3 / #4 fired when expected.
- **Cadence-fire compliance** — drift walks (#1), propagation passes (#2) ran where applicable.

Scope-limit: reflects on AI's current session context only. Decisions made pre-compact/clear are out of scope (lost with the context). Existing cross-cutting drift sweep is preserved alongside.

See [`8a7c2f1`](#8a7c2f1--decision--2026-05-11) for output shape (propose-not-auto-write).

## 8a7c2f1 — decision — 2026-05-11

**`/stoa audit surfaces candidates; operator confirms; no auto-write to beta_tracker.md.`**

Question: when `/stoa audit` finds a Stoa-rule miss in session-reflective sweep, should it auto-append a `beta_tracker.md` entry or propose for operator confirmation?

Alternatives:
1. Auto-append on detection — fastest path; no operator friction; entry lands with timestamp + AI's self-reflection.
2. Propose candidate, operator confirms before append — operator-in-loop; adds friction; entry quality controlled.

Decision: alternative (2). Rationale: **the AI is meta-blind to its own failure modes** (this session: pre-flight skip was self-caught only after operator asked, not autonomously). Auto-append risks low-quality entries from a meta-blind reflector. Operator-in-the-loop preserves entry-quality bar while still moving discovery work to the tool.

Implementation: each candidate surfaces as a bold `[stoa]` one-liner with the proposed entry's headline. Operator says yes/no per candidate; AI writes the confirmed entries to `.stoa/beta_tracker.md`.

Implementation parent: [`5e3b9d4`](#5e3b9d4--decision--2026-05-11).

## a91d4b7 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`Install instructions drop curl; adopters download stoa.md from GitHub UI. v0.3.0 → v0.3.1 BETA.`**

Question: a first-time adopter ran the published `curl -o stoa.md https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ivan-avramov/stoa-ai/main/stoa.md` from `README.md:10`, then `claude` + `hi`. Claude replied `"how can I help you"` — no `[stoa]` banner, no large-file warning, no install kit. Diagnosis live with the adopter: stoa-ai is a **private repo during BETA**. `raw.githubusercontent.com` doesn't accept git credentials; curl silently saved a 404 text response (a few hundred bytes — well under Claude Code's 40k-char large-file warning threshold). The `@stoa.md` import resolved a useless file; pre-flight had nothing to detect.

Alternatives:
1. Keep `curl`, document `gh api repos/.../contents/stoa.md --jq .content | base64 -d` as the auth path. Con: `gh` is not universally installed at Stoa laptops; install instructions should not assume tooling.
2. Keep `curl`, document the `Authorization: token $(gh auth token)` header form. Same con as (1) — depends on `gh`.
3. Drop `curl` from published install. Tell adopters to open the file in the GitHub UI in their browser, hit **Raw**, save it as `stoa.md` in their project root. The browser uses their authenticated GitHub session — works on private repos with zero tooling assumption.

Chosen: alternative (3). Lowest-common-denominator path; works for anyone with browser access to the repo. Same change applied to `README.md` install snippet, `getting_started.md` Path A + Codex setup + upgrade flow + manual-fallback subsection. Curl reference removed everywhere it appeared as the published install path.

Version bump: v0.3.0 → v0.3.1 BETA — adopter-visible change to the install path; warrants a patch bump per existing versioning rule.

Beta observation worth watching: a `stoa-install.sh` script (currently roadmapped) becomes more attractive now that the canonical manual path is "open browser, click Raw, save." A script could `gh api ...` with graceful fallback to printing the browser instructions. Defer to v0.3.x driven by beta-tracker signal — not adding now.

Diagnostic gap surfaced: Claude Code's large-file warning didn't fire on the 404 text body because it was too small. There's no symmetric small-file warning (e.g., "imported file is unusually small — likely a fetch failure"). Out of scope for Stoa to fix host behavior, but the install instructions now mention the failure mode explicitly so adopters can self-diagnose if they reach for `curl` anyway.

**Refs:** [`b7e94d2`](#b7e94d2--decision--2026-05-11) (sibling v0.3.1 change).

## b7e94d2 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`Install kit creates a starter context_log.md with header + format reminder + empty placeholder.`**

Question: install kit Step 2 writes `.stoa/artifacts.md` and `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` as visible empty starter files but does **not** create `context_log.md`. The WAL — the most important Stoa artifact, the load-bearing primitive everything else hangs on — only materializes when the first WAL entry is appended. Operators don't see the file they're meant to populate until after they've produced a decision. The meta-files exist; the primary file doesn't.

Alternatives:
1. Status quo. Con: artifact asymmetry; the most important file is invisible at install time; operators have to remember `context_log.md` is the WAL.
2. Install kit writes a starter `context_log.md` with header + format reminder + empty placeholder. Skip-write if file already exists (preserve operator content). No seed entry — empty WAL is the correct first state.
3. Install kit writes a starter with a seed `stoa:install`-type WAL entry recording the install itself. Pro: chain integrity from entry zero. Con: noisy; first real decision is no longer the first entry; preserves no information not already in `.stoa/installed`.

Chosen: alternative (2). Starter file content matches the shape of the methodology — header, brief format reminder mirroring §"Append-only WAL with stable identity", parenthetical "(no entries yet — your first refining session will propose one)" placeholder so adopters know the empty state is intentional, not a bug. The `.stoa/artifacts.md` and `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` patterns are reused. No seed entry — chain integrity is not weakened by an empty WAL; the first real decision lands as entry one and is correct as such.

File inventory in `getting_started.md` updated from "7 files" to "8 files." Install kit Step 1 surface message lists `context_log.md` in the create-list so adopters confirm the new file before any writes.

Version bump: v0.3.0 → v0.3.1 BETA — new artifact appears in adopter repos at install time; adopter-visible change.

**Refs:** [`a91d4b7`](#a91d4b7--decision--2026-05-11) (sibling v0.3.1 change).

## f3c9a04 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`Test harness A1 + AUTO1 extended for starter context_log.md; new A5 scenario for skip-on-conflict.`**

Question: v0.3.1's install kit creates a starter `context_log.md` ([`b7e94d2`](#b7e94d2--decision--2026-05-11)). The existing harness (`tests/scenarios.md` A1 install + AUTO1 cold-hi) verifies `.stoa/installed`, `.stoa/artifacts.md`, the dispatcher, slim stoa.md, etc., but predates the starter WAL artifact. Without updating, the harness keeps passing even if a future regression silently drops the starter from the install kit — exactly the failure class the harness exists to catch.

Decision:
1. Extend **A1 verification** to assert `context_log.md` exists at repo root post-install with the canonical starter header (first line `# Context log`; contains the "(no entries yet …)" parenthetical). Setup needs no change — A1's fresh trial dir already has no `context_log.md`, so the install must create it.
2. Extend **AUTO1 verification** identically (same post-conditions as A1, different drive prompt — A1 instructs the AI explicitly, AUTO1 just types `hi` and tests autonomous trigger).
3. Add **new scenario A5 — "preserve existing context_log.md on install"**. Setup: fresh trial dir pre-seeded with a non-empty `context_log.md` (e.g., one pre-existing WAL entry). Drive prompt: identical to A1 (run install per stoa.md). Verify: post-install, `context_log.md` content is byte-identical to pre-install — install must NOT clobber operator content. Validates the skip-on-conflict branch of install kit Step 2 for the new starter file. Belongs in Category **A** (install).

Why a separate scenario rather than a sub-check in A1: skip-on-conflict is a distinct branch with a different setup precondition (file pre-exists). Bundling it into A1 would conflate two test classes; isolating it as A5 mirrors how `.stoa/artifacts.md` and `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` would (and arguably should) have skip-on-conflict scenarios of their own — A5 sets the pattern for adding them later if a regression surfaces.

Implementation parent: [`b7e94d2`](#b7e94d2--decision--2026-05-11).

Status: spec'd here; `tests/scenarios.md` + `tests/harness.sh` edits land in a follow-up commit alongside or after the v0.3.1 changes, depending on adopter-priority weight.

**Refs:** [`b7e94d2`](#b7e94d2--decision--2026-05-11), [`a91d4b7`](#a91d4b7--decision--2026-05-11).

## 7e2a014 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Install kit moved from `stoa.md` (repo root) → `installkit/stoa.md` to free the root `stoa.md` slot for the dogfooded slim driver post-install.**

Question: stoa-ai will install Stoa on itself (dogfooding, Phase 2 PR D in [`sketches/refactor.md`](../sketches/refactor.md)). After install, the repo root contains a slim `stoa.md` (~376 lines). But the install kit (the full self-extracting file, ~916 lines) is conventionally also named `stoa.md` at the canonical source. Two files cannot occupy the same path. How should the install kit be hosted in stoa-ai?

Alternatives:
1. Rename the install kit to `stoa_install_kit.md` at repo root. Adopters fetch this name and rename to `stoa.md` locally. Pro: discoverable; signals "this is the distribution." Con: every adopter has to remember to rename on save. Real footgun in the browser-Raw-save flow — the only working install path while the repo is private during BETA, since `raw.githubusercontent.com` rejects unauthenticated requests and `curl -o` is therefore not on the table.
2. Keep the filename `stoa.md` but move it to a subpath: `installkit/stoa.md`. Adopters navigate to that path on GitHub, click Raw, save with default name (`stoa.md`). Pro: zero rename step; the file ends up correctly named at the adopter's project root by default. Con: two files with the same name in one repo (root `stoa.md` post-install + `installkit/stoa.md`) — minor cognitive cost for grep/IDE-search results.

Decision: alternative (2). The private-repo browser-Raw-save flow forces the choice — option (1)'s "remember to rename" friction would bite beta operators on every install and every upgrade. Option (2)'s subpath discriminates roles (root = running file; `installkit/` = distribution) without forcing a rename, and aligns naturally with Phase 2's planned source-vs-built distinction (`src/` source units + assembled `installkit/stoa.md`).

Adopter-visible changes:
- Canonical-source URL inside the install kit (and adopter `.stoa/installed` markers post-upgrade) becomes `https://github.com/ivan-avramov/stoa-ai/blob/main/installkit/stoa.md`.
- `getting_started.md` install + upgrade instructions point at the subpath; `README.md` install section updated to match.
- Existing adopters on v0.3.0 (none yet — acme-platform is still on v0.2.0) would need to manually re-fetch from the new path on upgrade; no auto-redirect.

No version bump: v0.3.1 is unpublished beyond stoa-ai's `main`; this lands as part of the v0.3.1 batch alongside [`a91d4b7`](#a91d4b7--decision--2026-05-11), [`b7e94d2`](#b7e94d2--decision--2026-05-11), [`f3c9a04`](#f3c9a04--decision--2026-05-11), under the same version stamp.

Phase 2 implication: [`sketches/refactor.md`](../sketches/refactor.md) previously named the assembled build output `stoa_install_kit.md` at root. Updated in this same commit to `installkit/stoa.md` for consistency.

**Refs:** [`c0a3e7b`](#c0a3e7b--decision--2026-05-11) (the canonical-home move that produced this repo).

## 4d6a82c — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Upgrade-flow procedural detail moved from slim `stoa.md` → `/stoa upgrade` subcommand in the dispatcher. v0.3.1 → v0.3.2 BETA. Slim drops 42k → ~31k chars, under Claude Code's 40k "large file" threshold.**

Question: slim `stoa.md` at v0.3.1 measures 41,973 chars / 380 lines — past Claude Code's 40k "Large file will impact performance" threshold. The warning fires every session-start for adopters, friction with no operational value. Section-size audit found one outlier: the `## Upgrade flow (agent-driven)` section is 12,309 chars / 29% of the slim. It is the only large section that is **on-demand procedural detail** (fires once per upgrade), not active session discipline (fires every session). Adopters pay its context cost every session for content they invoke rarely.

Alternatives:
1. Tactical trim of redundant prose across all sections. ~5–10% reduction; doesn't reliably clear 40k; risks removing operational context.
2. Move upgrade flow to a separate `docs/upgrade-flow.md`, slim links to it; AI reads on demand. Works but adds a file to adopter installs and a context-load step at upgrade time.
3. **Move upgrade flow into a `/stoa upgrade` dispatcher subcommand.** The dispatcher (`.claude/commands/stoa.md`) is already a spec-owned embedded artifact in adopter installs; slash-command files load **on invocation**, not at session start, so the upgrade procedure costs zero session tokens until the operator types `/stoa upgrade`.

Decision: alternative (3). Implementation:
- **Dispatcher template** in `installkit/stoa.md` gains a new `### upgrade` subcommand carrying the full 7-step procedure + rationale paragraphs + two-class definition + scope/evolution notes. Help-subcommand surface list adds `/stoa upgrade`.
- **Slim's `## Upgrade flow` section** shrinks to a ~750-char stub: the `[stoa]` surface message + dispatcher-subcommand pointer + Codex prose-mapping note + bootstrap-case caveat for the v0.3.1 → v0.3.2 cutover.
- **Net slim size:** 41,973 → ~31,400 chars. Comfortably below the 40k threshold.

**Bootstrap caveat (one-time cross-version cutover).** Existing v0.3.1 adopters' installed dispatchers don't yet have the `upgrade` subcommand. On the v0.3.1 → v0.3.2 transition, `/stoa upgrade` returns `Unknown subcommand`. The slim stub explicitly handles this: AI reads the procedure from the install-kit dispatcher template (`#### path: .claude/commands/stoa.md` → `### upgrade`) which is still present in the pre-strip local `stoa.md` because Step 6's self-strip is the procedure's last step. Running it inline once refreshes the dispatcher (Step 3 overwrites it with the latest template), so subsequent upgrades use the standard `/stoa upgrade` path. One-time bootstrap; transparent on every subsequent upgrade.

**Warning-as-signal framing (operator UX).** Operator reads `getting_started.md`, knows to manually re-download `stoa.md` when a new version ships. After they drop the new file in and start Claude Code, the "large stoa.md will impact performance" warning fires — this IS the signal that the file is the pre-strip install kit, not the slim, and that they should run `/stoa upgrade` to apply. The warning serves as a free reminder. After upgrade, slim shrinks below 40k and the warning never fires again. Friction is one-time, scoped to upgrade events.

Adopter-visible: slim shape changes, dispatcher gains a subcommand, version bump v0.3.1 → v0.3.2 BETA.

This refactor was queued in [`sketches/refactor.md`](../sketches/refactor.md) §"Why refactor" as one of three drivers for the Phase 2 layout overhaul, but it landed earlier and independently because slim-size friction surfaced first via the install warning. Phase 2's broader `src/` source-vs-built reshuffle remains queued for v0.4.

**Refs:** [`7e2a014`](#7e2a014--decision--2026-05-11) (install-kit moved to `installkit/stoa.md` — same v0.3.1 batch; sibling work).

## 3e8b5c9 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Atomic-write discipline amended: `Edit` OR `Write` allowed; shell utilities still forbidden; `Write` preferred for the self-strip step. v0.3.2 → v0.3.3 BETA.**

Question: in v0.3.2's first dogfooded `/stoa upgrade` run (stoa-ai, the bootstrap v0.3.1 → v0.3.2 cutover), the AI got stuck on Step 6 (self-strip) for 10+ minutes. The procedure said *"use the host's Edit tool exclusively"* — the only allowed path was a single `Edit` call with a ~30k-char `old_string` (the full install-kit block to delete). The AI has to reconstruct that exact old text from prior `Read` chunks before the tool can match, which is order-of-magnitude slower than the obviously equivalent `Write` call (concatenate slim + repo-extensions; overwrite). The rule was protecting against the real failure mode ([`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10) — `sed -i` bypassing the host's read-state cache and breaking subsequent Edits), but its expression overshot: it banned `Write` along with the shell utilities, even though `Write` IS host-tracked and has none of the cache-divergence problem.

Alternatives:
1. Leave the rule as-is; accept the slow self-strip as cost of safety. Con: 10+ min friction every upgrade; defeats the v0.3.2 slim-size win on UX grounds; future versions only get slower as install kit grows.
2. Allow `Write` for the self-strip specifically (carve-out). Con: special-cases one step; risks future drift if other large operations land in the procedure.
3. **Amend the rule globally: forbid shell utilities (the real failure mode), allow both `Edit` and `Write` (both maintain the host's read-state cache invariant). Recommend `Write` for the self-strip because the delta is wholesale-delete and the size argument applies.**

Decision: alternative (3). The shell-tool prohibition is the load-bearing constraint — it prevents the cache-divergence failure mode observed in [`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10). `Write` is a separate, host-tracked tool that doesn't have that failure mode and is dramatically faster for large-delta edits. The original wording confused "host-tracked tool" with "the Edit tool specifically" — fixing the wording, not the rule.

Updates in this commit:
- **Dispatcher template `### upgrade` Step 6** (installkit/stoa.md ~line 727): atomic-write paragraph rewritten — "Edit or Write" + "Prefer Write for self-strip" rationale + Read+Write recipe.
- **Install kit Step 6** (installkit/stoa.md ~line 871): paralleled to the same wording so the install path and the upgrade path are symmetric.
- **Shell-utility prohibition** (still inline at both spots): keeps the `sed` / `awk` / `perl -i` ban + references [`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10) (original incident) and this entry.

Adopter-visible: spec wording change (any operator who reads stoa.md to understand discipline sees the new "Edit or Write" rule). v0.3.2 → v0.3.3 BETA bump.

## e9b3f47 — table — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Phase 2 PR C (`src/` carve-up of `installkit/stoa.md` + `build.py`) deferred — `installkit/stoa.md` stays monolithic for now; root `stoa.md` remains the dogfooded slim driver. PR A, PR B, PR E from the sketch are still in scope.**

Question: should the install kit's embedded artifact blocks (dispatcher, hook chain, wal-audit, templates) be carved out of `installkit/stoa.md` into `src/embedded/*` with `build/build.py` assembling the canonical kit? Sketched at [`sketches/refactor.md`](sketches/refactor.md) §"Proposed layout" + open question #2.

Three drivers in the sketch: source review surface (PRs against fenced code blocks are awkward to diff/review), local edit ergonomics (bash inside markdown fences loses LSP/lint), dogfooding clarity. Counter-considerations weighed in this session:

1. **Source-review surface is theoretical until external review traffic arrives.** Stoa is pre-adoption — one beta adopter (acme-platform, v0.2.0); the primary author edits solo. The pain isn't load-bearing yet.
2. **Build infra is real ongoing cost.** `build.py` + a drift-prevention check (so `installkit/stoa.md` can't ship out-of-sync with `src/`) is new failure surface to maintain on a methodology still evolving fast (v0.1 → v0.3.3 in weeks).
3. **Cross-cutting edits get worse short-term.** Substantive changes like [`4d6a82c`](#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (upgrade-flow → `/stoa upgrade` subcommand) touched dispatcher + install kit + slim driver together; in the carved-up world that's N file edits + build verify, vs. one focused edit pass today.

Decision: leave `installkit/stoa.md` monolithic. Defer, don't reject — the drivers are real, just premature.

Trigger to revisit:
- First external PR against `installkit/stoa.md` that fumbles a fenced code block.
- Adoption ramp produces sustained external contribution traffic.
- Methodology stabilizes (edit churn drops) so build infra cost amortizes.

Cheaper interim mitigation if local edit ergonomics surface as pain before then: a small `tools/extract.sh` (~30 lines bash) pulling embedded blocks to a scratch dir for syntax-checking. No commit-time drift contract. Not building this now either — surface on demand.

Sketch open questions resolved/affected:
- **#1** (build language Python vs Bash) — moot; no build.
- **#2** (source-of-truth model) — settled: `installkit/stoa.md` is hand-edited canonical; root `stoa.md` is the dogfooded install output. No `src/` carve-up; no separate slim source.
- **#3** (commit dogfooded state) — already implicit via PR D landing first; committed.
- **#6** (v0.3.x vs v0.4.0) — without PR C the refactor is much smaller; argues v0.3.x.
- **#7** (slim-driver text about source/built split) — moot; no split to describe.

Still in scope for Phase 2: PR A (move depth docs to `docs/`), PR B (move demos to `demos/`), PR E (`integrations/` scaffold).

**Refs:** [`c0a3e7b`](#c0a3e7b--decision--2026-05-11) (Phase 1 migration; predecessor); [`4d6a82c`](#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (v0.3.2 slim-size refactor, which already noted *Phase 2's broader `src/` source-vs-built reshuffle remains queued for v0.4* — this entry converts "queued" to "tabled"); [`sketches/refactor.md`](sketches/refactor.md) (the working sketch; resolves open questions #1, #2, #6, #7).

## c1d5b8e — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Session-start banner requirement removed from spec. Agents no longer emit `[stoa vX.Y.Z BETA] Stoa active for this session...` on each session start. v0.3.3 → v0.3.4 BETA.**

Question: should the session-start banner spec'd in [`stoa.md`](stoa.md) §"Opt-in mechanic" be kept? Surfaced during this session's `/stoa audit` session-reflective sweep — the AI ran the pre-flight successfully but never emitted the banner. Operator confirmed: the miss is recurring and the right move is to drop the requirement, not to log yet another beta-tracker entry about it.

The banner's information payload is small — *"Stoa is active; remove the import to disable."* Both facts are stated in `stoa.md` itself (§"Opt-in mechanic") and the disable mechanism is one line in `CLAUDE.md`. An adopter who needs the info already has it; a per-session reminder buys little.

Alternatives:
1. Keep the spec; tighten the imperative wording (more "MUST emit" language).
2. Keep the spec; rely on `/stoa audit`'s session-reflective sweep to catch the miss after-the-fact.
3. **Remove the spec.** Recurring miss + low info value → simplest fix is to stop asking.

Decision: alternative (3). Stoa's loose-framework principle reserves AI accountability for *load-bearing* discipline (WAL appends, cadence fires, settling cues) — a cosmetic session-start banner doesn't belong on that list. Removing it eliminates a recurring beta-tracker entry class without losing functionality. Operators who want active-status confirmation can read `CLAUDE.md` (the `@stoa.md` import is right there) or run `/stoa status`.

**Edit surface** (all canonical; dogfooded artifacts regenerated by `/stoa upgrade`):
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section §"Opt-in mechanic": drop banner paragraph + quoted message; keep the `**Rationale.**` paragraph.
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section §"Coherence cadence" #5 (`/stoa audit`): drop "session-start banner fired" from initialization-compliance coverage.
- `installkit/stoa.md` install-kit section's dispatcher template `### audit`: same audit-coverage edit.
- `docs/getting_started.md` §"Step 4 — Stoa is active": rewrite banner-confirmation paragraph; drop quoted banner. §"What to watch out for" audit description: drop banner from initialization-compliance line.

**Adopter-visible:** yes — agents stop emitting the banner. Patch bump v0.3.3 → v0.3.4 BETA per the patch-when-adopter-visible default. All version-stamp callsites in `installkit/stoa.md` move together (H1, line-3 adoption-package stamp, embedded dispatcher header, status output template, install-complete message, marker template, install commit example).

**Refs:** [`stoa.md` §"Opt-in mechanic"](stoa.md#opt-in-mechanic) (removed-spec location); ad-hoc `/stoa audit` session-reflective sweep on 2026-05-11 that surfaced this (no WAL entry for the audit itself — operator declined logging the three candidates).

## 5c9e2a8 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Slim driver aggressively trimmed for per-session context economy. `installkit/stoa.md` slim section drops from ~32K → ~21.5K chars (~33% reduction). Drops `docs/*` pointer refs (slim driver is strictly agent-context; depth pointers don't serve the agent and 404 in adopter repos anyway), drops the entire §"Pointers for depth" section, and tightens verbose explanatory prose throughout. Same v0.3.4 BETA bump.**

Question: how aggressively should the slim driver — loaded into every session's context — be trimmed? Operator's framing: *"context strictly for the AI to use; context bloat must be at a minimum; goal is the smallest viable spec for Claude Sonnet and above without sacrificing quality."*

The trim targets prose elaborations that explain *why* a rule exists when capable agents can interpret the rule itself. Sonnet+ doesn't need rationale paragraphs to follow imperatives. Examples cut:

- **Pre-flight block** (~1500 chars): drops the *"Skipping this check leaves the repo..."* nag (already implied by MUST); compresses the diagnostic-probe discipline (4 bash patterns → 1 sentence); compresses field-state handling into terser cases.
- **§"What Stoa is"** (~400 chars): drops the framing paragraph; keeps the actionable settling-judgment sentence (*"if a decision is too vague to implement against, it's not yet settled"*).
- **§"Founding principles"** (~400 chars): keeps bolded titles + 1 sentence each; drops elaborations on AI-as-interpreter / why-rigid-validators-fail.
- **§"Opt-in mechanic"** (~500 chars): keeps one paragraph; drops "No per-operator preference file" + the v0.1 BETA `.claude/settings.local.json` historical rationale.
- **§"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape"** (~700 chars): drops compact/clear rationale paragraph (covered by cadence #4); drops bold-the-line UX rationale (keeps the rule); tightens discipline list.
- **§"WAL entry form"** (~500 chars): drops "Why pin the header" explanation (just states the rule); drops "Exceptions" forward-looking note.
- **§"WAL access pattern"** (~400 chars): drops "AI-discipline, not new tooling" rationale paragraph.
- **§"Coherence cadence"** (~700 chars): drops "Why the loose-framework default holds for four of five" paragraph (Sonnet+ infers); tightens cadence #4 auto-compaction parenthetical; tightens cadence #3 escalation paragraph.
- **§"Beta tracking"** (~600 chars): tightens to 3 sentences; drops "feedback loop" rationale paragraph.
- **§"Pointers for depth"** (~700 chars): whole section dropped (per [`f5a7c63`](#f5a7c63--decision--2026-05-11) — wait, this entry was drafted but not appended; folded into this umbrella). Adopters' agents don't follow URLs to source-repo material; operators can find the source repo via README.
- **§"Upgrade flow"** (~300 chars): drops "For Codex hosts" paragraph (covered by prose-mapping); drops "Out of scope for v0.3.x" historical-scope note.
- **§"Repo-specific extensions"** (~600 chars): tightens contract paragraph; drops "Use this section for" examples; condenses AI-discipline list.

**What stays load-bearing and untouched:** pre-flight branching logic (marker check, version match, hook-activation cases); settling-cue trigger list; AI-side phase-settlement trigger; all WAL guardrail rules (off-pattern + not-off-pattern lists); all five cadences' core specs; prose ↔ subcommand mapping; repo-extensions marker contract and the marker line itself.

**Method.** Edits land only in `installkit/stoa.md` (canonical). Dogfooded artifacts (root `stoa.md`, `.claude/commands/stoa.md`, `.stoa/installed`) NOT edited in this commit — operator regenerates them locally via `/stoa upgrade` after the PR lands. Earlier-in-this-session direct-edits to dogfooded artifacts were reverted to HEAD when the discipline gap surfaced; the rule lives at [`a4e8c12`](#a4e8c12--observation--2026-05-11)'s "Dogfooded spec-owned artifacts NOT edited" note and is saved to operator-side memory for future sessions.

**Adopter-visible:** yes. Adopters who run `/stoa upgrade` to v0.3.4 get a substantially leaner slim driver — ~21.5K chars vs. ~32K before, well under Claude Code's 40K "large file" threshold. Same v0.3.4 BETA bump as [`c1d5b8e`](#c1d5b8e--decision--2026-05-11) (banner removal — sibling trim decision in this PR).

**Refs:** [`c1d5b8e`](#c1d5b8e--decision--2026-05-11) (session-start banner removal — sibling slim-trim decision in same PR); [`a4e8c12`](#a4e8c12--observation--2026-05-11) (layout-refactor observation with the "dogfooded artifacts not directly edited" rule); [`4d6a82c`](#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (v0.3.2 slim-size refactor — predecessor; this entry continues the slim-shrink discipline).

## 8a4c2e7 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Test harness modernized for v0.3.4: `tests/scenarios.md` + `tests/harness.sh` brought from the v0.1 BETA install surface to current. `.gitignore` / `settings.local.json` checks dropped (those artifacts deliberately removed in v0.1.3); modern install artifacts (`.stoa/beta_tracker.md`, `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`, `.githooks/pre-commit`, `context_log.md` starter, `core.hooksPath` git config) now verified. B1/B2 (`/stoa opt-in` / `/stoa opt-out`) scenarios removed entirely — those subcommands no longer exist. UP1/UP2 generalized to be version-agnostic.**

Question: how to bring the test harness (`tests/scenarios.md` + `tests/harness.sh`) current with the v0.3.4 install spec? Audit during this PR's smoke-test of A1 surfaced that the harness reflects the v0.1.x install surface — 2 of 10 verify checks failed on artifacts that were deliberately removed (`.gitignore`, `settings.local.json` entry).

**Layers of staleness identified and fixed:**

1. **Canonical path** — `CANONICAL_STOA_MD` pointed at root `stoa.md` (the dogfooded slim driver). Adopters fetch `installkit/stoa.md` (the full self-extracting kit), and install scenarios need that. Phase-1 leftover from when the install kit lived at root. **Fix:** `CANONICAL_STOA_MD="$REPO_DIR/installkit/stoa.md"`.

2. **Removed-feature scenarios** — `B1` (`/stoa opt-in` writes `settings.local.json`) and `B2` (`/stoa opt-out` toggles) test subcommands that haven't existed since v0.1.3 (when settings-based opt-in was abandoned for the simpler `@stoa.md` import model). **Fix:** removed both scenarios from `scenarios.md` and both `setup_*` / `verify_*` functions from `harness.sh`. C1's dependency rewired from B1 → A1 directly.

3. **Stale verify post-conditions** — `verify_A1`, `verify_A2`, `verify_A3`, `verify_AUTO1` all checked for `.gitignore` (which the install kit no longer creates) and `settings.local.json` entries. They also missed checks for artifacts added in v0.1.4–v0.3.x: `.stoa/beta_tracker.md`, `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` (executable), `.githooks/pre-commit` (executable), `context_log.md` starter, `core.hooksPath` git config, `hook-script-hash:` marker field. **Fix:** dropped stale checks, added current ones, added hash-cross-verification (compute `git hash-object .githooks/pre-commit`, compare against marker's `hook-script-hash:`).

4. **Version-hardcoded scenarios** — `UP1`/`UP2` hardcoded `v0.1.1` → `v0.1.2` strings (both in `scenarios.md` expectations and in `setup_UP1` / `verify_UP1` / `verify_UP2`). The mechanism (detect-mismatch → apply-upgrade) is timeless, but the version strings rot with every bump. **Fix:** `setup_UP1` now reads the current marker version, decrements the patch (with minor-decrement fallback if patch=0), saves both to `$STATE_DIR/UP1_{CURRENT,STALE}_VERSION` for the verifies to compare against. Works for any future version transition without code change.

5. **Spec drift** — `scenarios.md` title said "v0.2 BETA"; expected-line-counts said `~520 → ~230` (current is `~882 → ~242`); UP scenarios prefaced with "v0.1.2 BETA"; coverage matrix listed B1/B2 + said "32 scenarios." **Fix:** title bumped to v0.3.4 BETA; line counts refreshed; UP intro generalized; coverage matrix updated (30 documented, 23 with harness automation).

**What remains stale / out of scope for this pass:**

- PRE1–PRE7 (v0.2 pre-commit hook walk-throughs) — still marked as walk-throughs; not promoted to harness commands. That's its own substantial work (each requires fixture state + chain-hook behavior verification).
- S1/S2/Q1/Q2 — still partly manual review (synthesis-quality assessment can't be programmatically verified without an oracle). Unchanged.
- Codex compatibility — still manual via `tests/codex-smoke-test.md`. Unchanged.

**Smoke-test pass:** re-ran `harness.sh verify A1` on the existing A1 trial dir post-modernization — 15/15 checks pass (up from 8/10 prior). Confirms the modernization works against a real post-v0.3.4-install state.

**Refs:** harness audit during the v0.3.4 PR's `/stoa audit` aftermath (no WAL entry for the audit itself); [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md) (modernized); [`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh) (modernized).

- **E — Coherence cadence (2/2):** E1 (post-decision propagation pass fired reflexively → design.md updated), E2 (pre-commit drift walk → README+design updated; `--no-verify` correctly chosen for mechanical extension).
- **S — Session restart (2/2 manual):** S1 (decision-arc synthesis with grep-bounded reads — subagent noted absence of WAL-librarian sub-subagent tool and fell back gracefully), S2 (between-session drift detected; one-line `[stoa]` chat note; no derail).
- **Q — WAL queries (2/2 manual):** Q1 (categorical recall — distinguished explicit won't-do from rejected-alternatives; surfaced rejected-then-adopted supersession for Typer), Q2 (cross-WAL synthesis re: `pow` op — nothing tabled/branched needs reopening).
- **U — Update flow (2/2):** U1 (Linear-ticket rule added to repo-extensions), U2 (upstream stoa.md update applied; marker + operator content preserved).
- **UP — Upgrade (2/2):** UP1 (version-mismatch detected, `[stoa] stoa.md is v0.3.4 but marker says v0.3.3 — run /stoa upgrade` surfaced verbatim, zero file writes), UP2 (full upgrade applied; marker bumped; hash recomputed; no strays).

**Harness bugs found + fixed in-flight:**

1. **`clone_from` copied uncommitted source WT into target.** A4 (idempotency test) failed initially because the source A1 trial dir had install-result files in WT but uncommitted; the clone copied that dirty state. Fix: `clone_from` now snapshots the source's WT into a commit before cloning (`git add -A && git commit` if there's anything to commit). All clone-from-based setups now produce clean-WT targets. ([`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh) `clone_from`.)

2. **`setup_D3` / `setup_S2` committed drift mutations through the cadence-#3 pre-commit hook.** Since the trial repo has Stoa installed (with the WAL-audit hook wired), commits that touch tracked artifacts without staging `context_log.md` get blocked. The harness's drift-injection commits are deliberately bypassing the WAL-discipline (they ARE the drift the audit tests are designed to catch) and should use `--no-verify`. Fixed both setups.

**Trial-run efficiency notes:**

- Total wall-clock for the 26 runs: ~40 minutes (parallelized phases where possible: 4 subagents in parallel for Phase 1, 4 for Phase 2, 5 for G1-G5, 6 for the final phase).
- Token cost per subagent run varied widely: install scenarios (read 882-line full kit) ~80–90K; post-install scenarios (read 242-line slim) ~35–50K; guardrail tests (refuse + don't act) ~35K.
- Total tokens roughly ~1.2M across all subagent invocations.

**Calibration observation:** the AUTO1 redrive needed because the original "for any yes/no you ask, assume yes" simulation wording wasn't strong enough — the subagent surfaced the install proposal then stopped to wait for actual confirmation. The redrive language ("the operator HAS ALREADY answered yes to all confirmations; treat the yes as pre-given") worked. **Beta-tracker-worthy** as a Stoa-driver-prompt finding: subagents default to caution on multi-file mutations, which is fine in production but defeats single-turn simulation if the prompt isn't explicit.

**Refs:** [`8a4c2e7`](#8a4c2e7--decision--2026-05-11) (harness modernization decision — this entry verifies its outcome); [`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh) (modernized + 2 bug fixes); [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md) (modernized).

## e1c47a2 — decision — 2026-05-11

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Install-kit Steps 3 and 5 reshaped: `hook-script-hash` written directly by Step 3 instead of Step-3-placeholder + Step-5-replace dance. Step 5 only modifies the marker on the conflict-resolution path (operator picks skip-hook). v0.3.4 → v0.3.5 BETA.**

Question: the install kit's Step 3 (write `.stoa/installed` marker) and Step 5 (wire hook chain) currently dance on the `hook-script-hash:` value. Step 3 writes a placeholder-form value; Step 5 computes the hash from `.githooks/pre-commit` (already on disk from Step 2) and rewrites the line. Three subagents flagged this independently in the v0.3.4 test run (A1, A3, AUTO1 anomaly notes) — each chose to write the real hash directly in Step 3 since the file already existed. Net result identical; the spec reads as two writes when one suffices.

Decision: collapse the happy path into a single Step 3 write. Step 5 only modifies the marker if the operator chooses option (1) skip-hook at the conflict-resolution prompt (in which case the line gets rewritten to `skipped` and the hook script gets deleted).

**Why simpler:** fewer states in the linear install path. The `pending` placeholder state remains valid in the marker SCHEMA (used by the upgrade flow for the interrupted-v0.2-upgrade case, and surfaced by the pre-flight check) but doesn't need to exist in the install-kit happy path. Reads more linearly; subagents stop needing to "interpret" the spec.

**Edit surface (installkit/stoa.md only):**
- **Step 3 template's `hook-script-hash:` line**: drop the inline `OR-"skipped"` alternative from the placeholder description. The canonical install-kit happy path writes the real hash directly; the skip alternative is captured in Step 5's conflict-resolution branch.
- **Step 3 notes paragraph for `hook-script-hash`**: rewrite. Says: "compute from `git hash-object .githooks/pre-commit` (written in Step 2). Step 5's conflict-resolution path may rewrite this to `skipped` if the operator opts out of hook wiring."
- **Step 5 "Record hook-script-hash" paragraph** (currently the last block before the verification section): drop. Hash is already recorded by Step 3 in the happy path. Step 5's existing skip-case rewrite logic (the `if operator chose option (1)... write hook-script-hash: skipped` block) remains unchanged.

**Adopter-visible:** yes — the install procedure adopters' agents follow is one step shorter. Same `hook-script-hash:` end state. Patch bump v0.3.4 → v0.3.5 per the patch-when-adopter-visible default. All version-stamp callsites in `installkit/stoa.md` move together (H1, line-3 stamp, embedded dispatcher header, status output, install-complete message, marker template version, install commit example).

**Not affecting:** the upgrade flow's `pending`-placeholder pattern (interrupted-v0.2 case in dispatcher's `### upgrade` subcommand) — that's a distinct sequence; pre-flight check still handles `pending` correctly.

**Dogfooded artifacts NOT edited** in this PR (root `stoa.md`, `.claude/commands/stoa.md`, `.stoa/installed`, hooks) — auto-generated by `/stoa upgrade` against the canonical. Operator runs upgrade locally to bring them to v0.3.5.

**Refs:** [`f1b3a92`](#f1b3a92--observation--2026-05-11) (v0.3.4 test run that surfaced the spec ambiguity — three subagents noted the dance independently); [`3e7d4b2`](#3e7d4b2--decision--2026-05-11) (dogfooded-artifacts-NOT-directly-edited rule that scopes this PR).

## a91f3d4 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Demos: fast-forward button + in-memory remember-viewed-scenes.**

Both demo HTMLs (`demos/aurora-pivot-demo.html`, `demos/workflow-demo.html`) replay entrance animations on every scene revisit. Back-forth navigation = friction.

Added:
- A JS `Set` of scene indices the viewer has navigated away from; on return visits, those scenes render with a `.instant` class that overrides `lineIn` / `msgIn` entrance animations via `!important`, snapping everything to its final state.
- A "⏭ skip" button (Enter shortcut) that marks the current scene viewed and applies `.instant` mid-animation.

**Deliberately in-memory only** (no cookie / localStorage). Rationale: a page refresh should restore the full first-time playback for demo-replay scenarios — the friction is back-forth navigation, not between-session memory. Persisting across refreshes would surprise viewers opening the demo fresh.

**Side decision: a scene counts as "viewed" the moment the user navigates away from it** (next/prev), not after its longest animation-delay elapses. Simpler signal; matches the failure mode (back-forth = annoyance) without needing per-scene duration calculations.

Infinite animations (`.typewriter-cursor` blink, `.node.pulse`, `.phase.active` pulse) are deliberately left running under instant mode — they're not entrance animations.

## 7c4b9d2 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Multi-author semantic-merge protocol: cadence #6 adds pre-pull WAL semantic audit. Three-bucket classification (CLEAN / CONVERGENT / CONTRADICTING) with arc-grouped presentation over M×N entry-level detection; post-pull integrity check restores union-eaten separators.**

When two operators on separate clones each append WAL entries, a pull/merge reconciles them. Text-level union concatenation works for append-only files but says nothing about *semantic* compatibility — e.g., Alice's "go ahead with X" merging cleanly with Bob's local "won't do X" creates an internally contradictory WAL with no warning.

Adding **cadence #6 — pre-pull semantic-merge audit** to the coherence cadences. Fires before any `git pull` / `git fetch && git merge` / `git push` that auto-triggers a pull, regardless of trigger: slash command (`/stoa pull`), prose intent (*"pull"* / *"sync"* / *"rebase"*), or AI-internal during casual `"commit"` / `"push"` flow.

Audit:
1. Compute `M` = upstream new entries since common ancestor; `N` = local new.
2. Run **M×N pairwise classification at the entry level** (catches cross-arc conflicts the arc view alone would miss).
3. Group results by inferred arc for **presentation** (matches operator mental model; M×N detail stays under the hood).
4. Classify each pair: **CLEAN** (disjoint/supporting), **CONVERGENT** (same conclusion independently — keep both entries + propose observation), or **CONTRADICTING** (halt; resolution menu with rollback / reconciling decision / defer).
5. **Post-pull integrity check.** Empirical smoke-test finding (v0.3.6 BETA, see [`tests/multi-author-merge-test.md`](tests/multi-author-merge-test.md) §"Known empirical artifact"): after `git pull --rebase` with `merge=union`, the line-level union strategy correctly preserves content + ordering + linearity, but can eat the `---` separator at the union boundary between Alice's last entry and Bob's first entry. AI runs a structural-fix pass post-merge: verify every non-first `## <hex> — <type> — <date>` header is preceded by `---`; insert if missing. Never re-orders entries, never modifies bodies. The second exception to the WAL guardrail, narrowly scoped (see [`2e8f3a1`](#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12)).
6. Pass 2: cross-artifact propagation over `M + N` arcs, walking Bob's committed-HEAD tracked artifacts only. Working-tree artifact edits out of scope; sanity-warn fires if any present.

Casual-flow protection: AI's pre-push divergence detection fires cadence #6 before any pull. `/stoa pull` is the explicit operator-facing form; cadence is the rule.

**Refs:** [`2e8f3a1`](#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12) (rebase substrate + integrity-repair carve-out); [`9d1c5b4`](#9d1c5b4--decision--2026-05-12) (attribution); [`4a7e6c0`](#4a7e6c0--decision--2026-05-12) (integration-order rule); [`6f2b8a3`](#6f2b8a3--decision--2026-05-12) (working-tree handling); [`1b5d9f7`](#1b5d9f7--decision--2026-05-12) (audit extension).

## 2e8f3a1 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**WAL merge strategy: rebase-not-merge with `merge=union` for `context_log.md`. Pull strategy enforced via `branch.<main>.rebase = true` (operator-prompted at install); `.gitattributes` writes `merge=union`. AI post-pull integrity check restores separator structure at the union boundary.**

Append-only WAL files conflict at the EOF region under git's default 3-way merge. Two options considered: merge-with-union, or rebase-with-union. Decision: rebase, because (a) linear history matches the WAL's narrative, (b) deterministic file order under rebase ("ours" = rebase target = upstream first; "theirs" = replayed local commits second → always Alice-then-Bob), (c) under merge with `pull.rebase = false`, ordering reverses (Bob-then-Alice) — inconsistent integration-order invariant across operators. Empirically validated by the v0.3.6 BETA smoke test (MT1 vs MT3 in [`tests/multi-author-merge-test.md`](tests/multi-author-merge-test.md) Phase 1).

**Three pieces ship together:**
1. `.gitattributes` — `context_log.md merge=union`. Per-file conflict resolution; applies during normal merges AND during per-commit replays inside rebase.
2. Git config — `branch.<main>.rebase = true` for the canonical branch (auto-detected). Operator-prompted at install (same discipline as `core.hooksPath`). Declinable.
3. AI discipline — when AI runs pulls itself (cadence #6 / `/stoa pull`), always uses `--rebase` explicitly regardless of repo config.

**Empirical artifact: union eats the boundary separator.** Smoke testing v0.3.6 BETA showed `merge=union` produces correct content + ordering + no conflict markers BUT can swallow the `---` separator at the concatenation boundary between Alice's last entry and Bob's first entry. Within each side's batch separators stay intact; only the boundary is at risk. **Methodology compensation:** AI runs a post-pull integrity check (cadence #6 step 6) that restores missing boundary separators. This is the **second exception to the WAL guardrail** (alongside append), narrowly scoped — structural-fix only, never re-orders entries, never modifies bodies or hex IDs, scoped to immediate post-rebase state. Operator can revert with `git checkout HEAD -- context_log.md` if the repair looks wrong; the operation is mechanical.

**Tradeoffs accepted:**
- Entry header date and file position can diverge under rebase (Bob's earlier-dated entry rebased after Alice's later-dated entry). File position becomes "when this entered the canonical record"; entry date stays "when this was authored." Both meaningful. Chronological-order rule in the WAL guardrail rephrased — see [`4a7e6c0`](#4a7e6c0--decision--2026-05-12).
- Operators who decline the git-config setup risk inconsistent ordering if they pull without `--rebase`. AI-discipline backstop covers AI-driven pulls; pre-flight check (v0.3.6+) surfaces a warn on missing config.
- AI must do a tiny structural-fix mutation post-merge (separator restoration). Considered a fair cost vs. the alternative of a custom WAL-aware merge driver (more code, more failure modes, more install-kit complexity).

**Why no custom merge driver:** `merge=union` plus rebase semantics plus a small structural-fix AI pass gives deterministic linear order with correct boundary structure. Future versions may revisit if the boundary-munging proves more invasive than empirically observed.

**Refs:** [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12) (cadence #6 that the rebase model serves); smoke-test report in [`tests/multi-author-merge-test.md`](tests/multi-author-merge-test.md) §"Known empirical artifact".

## 9d1c5b4 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**WAL entry form: `Authors:` field becomes required; `Participants:` optional. Format from [`docs/proposed_methodology.md §3 Attribution`](docs/proposed_methodology.md#3-attribution) adopted into installkit canonical form.**

`docs/proposed_methodology.md` specifies per-entry attribution (`Authors: [@handle;tool(model)]`, `Participants: [...]`). The installkit canonical form did not require this — only `## <hex> — <type> — <date>` followed by free-prose body. Operators (including this repo) have been adding `**Authors:**` informally; spec didn't enforce.

With multi-author semantic-merge work landing (cadence #6, [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12)), formal attribution is now useful — generates clearer findings (*"Your `<hex_B>` by `@bob` contradicts upstream `<hex_A>` by `@alice`"*) than relying on `git blame` alone.

**Canonical form, v0.3.6+** (after the `## <hex> — <type> — <date>` header):
```
**Authors:** [@handle;tool(model)]
**Participants:** [@other_handle, ...]   <!-- optional; omit line if empty -->
```

Format per actor: `@<handle>` for humans; `;<tool>(<model>)` suffix when AI involved (`@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)`). Pure-AI: `<role>;<tool>(<model>)` without `@`. The `;` separator preserves human accountability — AI is session-context, not co-decider.

**No backfill.** Existing entries pre-v0.3.6 may lack `Authors:`. Reader logic tolerates both shapes; `git blame` is the fallback for unattributed entries.

**Refs:** [`docs/proposed_methodology.md §3 Attribution`](docs/proposed_methodology.md#3-attribution); [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12).

## 4a7e6c0 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**WAL chronological-order rule rephrased: file position encodes integration order, not authored-date order.**

The WAL guardrail off-pattern list said: *"Reordering entries (chronological order is part of the contract; older entries above newer ones)."* This held when entries were single-author and append-only. Under multi-author rebase-merge (see [`2e8f3a1`](#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12)), Bob's earlier-dated entry may legitimately end up after Alice's later-dated entry after rebase.

**New phrasing** in the WAL guardrail off-pattern list:

> *"**Manual** reordering of entries (file order encodes **integration order** — the sequence entries entered the canonical branch's linear history. Each entry's date header is authoritative for *when authored*; file position is authoritative for *when integrated*. Rebase-induced reordering during cadence #6 pulls is methodology-operation, not off-pattern; manual hand-edited reordering is.)"*

**Distinction matters:**
- *"When was this decided?"* → read the date header inside the entry.
- *"In what order did decisions enter the shared record?"* → read top-to-bottom in the file.

This invariant matches how git already works for every other linearly-versioned doc. Manual reordering of entries is still off-pattern (operator-side bypass); rebase-induced reordering is allowed (methodology operation). AI never mutates existing entries during the merge (rebase + union strategy delivers correct order automatically). No named carve-out in the WAL guardrail beyond this rule rephrasing and the narrow post-pull integrity-repair exception ([`2e8f3a1`](#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12)).

**Refs:** [`2e8f3a1`](#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12); [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12).

## 6f2b8a3 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Multi-author merge — working-tree handling: WAL appends must be committed before pull; tracked artifact edits stay uncommitted but get a sanity-warn from Pass 2.**

During cadence #6 ([`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12)), Bob's state at pull time has three layers: committed-N entries, working-tree WAL appends, and uncommitted artifact edits. Each handled differently.

**Working-tree WAL appends:**
- Git refuses merge when `context_log.md` has uncommitted changes (would conflict with incoming merge).
- AI MUST detect uncommitted WAL appends pre-pull and surface: **`[stoa] You have uncommitted WAL entries. Commit them first (cadence #3 will fire), then re-run the pull.`**
- Once committed, they're part of N. Standard flow.

**Working-tree artifact edits:**
- Not blocked by git (only conflicts if upstream touches the same file; standard merge case).
- Pass 2 walks **committed HEAD only**, against the M+N arcs.
- If uncommitted artifact edits are present, surface a one-line sanity-warn: **`[stoa] You have uncommitted edits in tracked artifacts (X, Y). These weren't audited against the pulled arcs. If they reflect decisions, append WAL entries first — otherwise this audit doesn't cover them.`**
- Strength of warn doesn't scale with verdict; always one line; ignorable.

**Rationale:** the WAL is the source of truth. If a decision exists, the WAL knows; cadence #2 catches propagation. Uncommitted artifact edits without WAL entries are operator-error territory — the backstop warn catches the "Bob meant to log but forgot" case without complicating the audit.

**Refs:** [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12).

---

## 1b5d9f7 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`/stoa audit` extended with WAL internal-conflict sweep (third sweep, retrospective version of cadence #6).**

`/stoa audit` previously ran two sweeps: cross-cutting drift and session-reflective. Adding a third — **WAL internal-conflict sweep** — that retroactively catches what cadence #6 catches at pull time:

- **Contradicting decisions not linked by a `rollback`** — entries that disagree but neither references the other as a supersession.
- **Un-noted convergence** — two `decision` entries reach equivalent conclusions independently; no `observation` records the convergence. Cadence #6 would have proposed one at pull time; this sweep catches the case where convergence happened pre-cadence-#6 or the operator declined the observation then.
- **Partial-arc invalidations** — later `observation` entries contradicting earlier-but-still-active decisions.

Operator-triggered; AI-judgment; never auto-resolves. Findings surface as a structured report (clusters + entries + pattern type + recommended resolution). On operator confirmation, applied fixes get an `observation` WAL entry recording the audit. A clean sweep also gets an observation — useful audit-trail data.

**Refs:** [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12) (cadence #6, the at-pull-time version of this check).

## d8e4a2c — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`[stoa-preflight]` visible-output rule (v0.3.6+): AI must emit a structured preflight block as the first user-visible content at settling-cue / phase-settlement / multi-step-implementation trigger moments. Shifts WAL-coverage failure mode from silent omission to operator-visible omission.**

Settling-cue triggers and AI-side phase-settlement trigger were already in the methodology, but pure AI-discipline rules degrade silently under task-momentum pressure. This session (2026-05-12) empirically observed two consecutive failures of those rules in the v0.3.6 implementation flow: after "let's go" (kickoff) and after "yes, do C" (harness integration), the AI proceeded directly to tool calls without proposing WAL entries first. The 6 entries that should have landed before execution were instead drafted alongside completed spec edits — "decision lands before or alongside the spec edit" technically held at commit time, but "execution should not race ahead of logging" was violated.

Same failure pattern that motivated cadence #3's v0.2 escalation ([`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)): rule existed, AI knew the rule, AI skipped it under task-momentum pressure. Cadence #3 escalated to a deterministic git pre-commit hook — but git hooks fire on git operations, not AI operations, so they don't help here. Host-specific hooks (Claude Code's `UserPromptSubmit`, Codex equivalents) would fragment the methodology across host vendors — explicitly rejected.

**v0.3.6 mid-step: visibility-first, host-agnostic.** Before host-specific hook escalation, try making compliance VISIBLE rather than DETERMINISTIC. The AI must emit a literal `[stoa-preflight]` block as its first user-visible content at trigger moments. Block contents: trigger type, settled decisions this phase, hex IDs already in the WAL, proposed new entries, status. Failure mode shifts from silent omission → visible omission (operator sees missing block, calls it out, AI corrects in-turn).

**Triggers** (the AI MUST emit a preflight at any of these):
- Operator settling-cue phrase ("let's go" / "yes apply" / "yes do it" / "go ahead" / "commit" / "push" / etc.) after substantive back-and-forth.
- AI phase-settlement offer ("want me to start implementing?" etc.) — preflight before the offer, not after.
- Start of a 3+ Edit/Write/Bash tool-call sequence on the same problem (implementation-shape work).

**Non-triggers** (to avoid preflight noise):
- Single read tool call, single status check, casual question response.
- Operator's casual yes/no to small questions ("should I read the file?" → "yes").
- Follow-up clarifications within an already-active phase that already had a preflight that turn.

**Tradeoff accepted:** still AI-discipline at root; a perfunctory "none" block could skip the check. Net win: forces conscious address every turn + operator-visible artifact + recoverable in-turn rather than after-the-fact. If beta data shows preflight-discipline also degrades, v0.4 may escalate to host-fragmented hooks — but with data justifying the host-fragmentation cost, not speculation. Bloat acceptable in beta because we're discovering what works.

**Refs:** [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) (cadence #3 v0.2 escalation — parallel pattern); empirical observation logged in `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` (this session's two-miss incident).

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Drop pre-v0.3.3 backward-compat clauses from slim stoa.md. Adopters older than v0.3.3 must do a fresh install rather than incremental upgrade; the migration carry-overs in the slim spec no longer earn their per-session token cost.**

`/stoa upgrade` lands and is dogfooded; the slim file's per-session context cost is a real concern (operator flagged the v0.3.5 → v0.3.6 ~80-line growth). Cleaning legacy carry-overs is the cheap win — frees ~12 lines of per-session context for every adopter session.

- Cosmetic `in v0.2` / `in v0.1` version stamps in cadence intro + command surface (the version stamp is in the H1; in-prose ones are noise).

**Operator-facing implication.** Adopters on Stoa < v0.3.3 hitting `/stoa upgrade → Unknown subcommand` will need to fresh-install from the canonical installkit. Acceptable cost: that population is small (Stoa is in BETA; the only external adopter is `ivan-avramov/acme-platform` on v0.2.0, who upgrades on a coordinated schedule, not incrementally).

## f2a3c91 — decision — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Track `docs/*` for coherence discipline: `executive_summary.md`, `getting_started.md`, `proposed_methodology.md` added to `.stoa/artifacts.md`.**

Operator ran *"stoa track docs/*"* — first tracking action in this repo. ## b4d8e1c — observation — 2026-05-12

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**AI-discipline-degradation arc: same defensive pattern converged across 4 entries over 2026-05-10 → 2026-05-12. Arc shape: empirical observation → structural mitigation → wording strengthening → visibility-first escalation. Surfaced by `/stoa audit` (see [`3c5e9d2`](#3c5e9d2--observation--2026-05-12)); useful v0.4-retrospective signal.**

The convergence:

1. [`7e4c1a6`](#7e4c1a6--observation--2026-05-10) — **empirical observation**: silent-decision failure pattern recorded.
2. [`b3d2e94`](#b3d2e94--decision--2026-05-10) — **structural mitigation**: settling-cue triggers + cadence #4 (pre-compact/clear) audit.
3. [`0b4e9c1`](#0b4e9c1--decision--2026-05-10) — **wording strengthening**: shift from descriptive to imperative (*"**AI: BEFORE … you MUST**"*) across the relevant rules.
4. [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) — **visibility-first escalation**: `[stoa-preflight]` block as required first-content output at trigger moments.

Each step was settled on its own merits without explicit reference to the prior step's pattern; the convergence is implicit in the WAL but not noted as an arc until now.

**Implication for v0.4 planning.** The arc shows the AI-discipline mitigation hierarchy in practice: (a) discipline rules alone degrade; (b) structural mitigations help but still degrade under sustained pressure; (c) imperative wording recovers some compliance; (d) visible-output requirements close more of the gap by making failures observable. If preflight-discipline ALSO empirically degrades, the next layer (host-specific hooks: Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` + Codex equivalent + others) is the obvious next escalation — and the arc gives a clear ladder for justifying that cost when the beta data arrives. Parallel to cadence #3's own arc (AI-discipline → git pre-commit hook, see [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)).

**Refs:** [`3c5e9d2`](#3c5e9d2--observation--2026-05-12) (the audit that surfaced this convergence); [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) (cadence #3's parallel discipline → hook arc).

## 6e1b3c4 — decision — 2026-05-14

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Add cadence #7 — end-of-implementation WAL audit.**

Surfaced via acme-platform beta-tracker entry 2026-05-14. Three architectural decisions encoded across a ~12-call implementation block went unlogged because no cadence fires at end-of-impl. Cadences #3 (pre-commit) and #4 (pre-compact) only fire at destructive boundaries; if the operator pivots to a new task without committing, decisions stay unlogged.

End-of-impl is the max-visibility moment — work has been built and tested, the AI knows what was actually decided. Cadence #7 is the back-stop for cases where settling-cues missed the directive (or the directive-cue list [`4c9a1f6`](#4c9a1f6--decision--2026-05-14) doesn't yet enumerate it).

Trigger: arc-shape signals primary, not call count.
- Arc-completion language (*"that's working now"*, *"tests pass"*, *"done with X"*).
- About to offer a next step (*"want me to..."*, *"shall we now..."*).
- About to switch problem domains.
- Fallback floor: ≥5 mutating tool calls (Edit/Write/Bash with side effects) on the same problem since last preflight. Calibration target — tune in v0.3.x based on beta data.

"Same problem" = no directive-cue arc-shift has fired since the last preflight.

Procedure: read back what the block built (paths, commands, endpoints, schema), ask which embody unlogged architectural decisions, emit `[stoa-preflight]` block, propose per-decision WAL entries.

Pairs with [`8f2a5d3`](#8f2a5d3--decision--2026-05-14) (drop start-of-impl preflight) — restructures the impl-time preflight surface from start-trigger to end-trigger.

## c5f7e21 — decision — 2026-05-14

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Rename `[stoa-preflight]` block field "Settled this phase" → "Settled across recent turns without a logged entry".**

Surfaced via acme-platform beta-tracker entry 2026-05-14 fix (iii). The original field name "Settled this phase" reads as forward-scoped — "what just happened in this turn?" — and the empirical failure mode was the AI correctly tracking this-turn decisions while incorrectly assuming prior-turn decisions had already been logged. Three architectural decisions encoded over a multi-turn impl block went unlogged because each individual preflight (when it fired at all) only audited the current turn's deltas.

The new framing shifts the question from forward-scan ("what just happened?") to backward-scan ("what's still un-logged?") — a small wording change with outsized behavioral effect because it forces the AI to look across recent turns, not just the current one.

Paired with the impl-time preflight restructure ([`8f2a5d3`](#8f2a5d3--decision--2026-05-14) drop start-of-impl trigger, [`6e1b3c4`](#6e1b3c4--decision--2026-05-14) add cadence #7) — together they shift the impl-time WAL audit from "at-the-start, forward-looking" to "at-the-end, backward-looking."
