## 9d2e5f1 — decision — 2026-05-14

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Fix `/stoa upgrade` hash-ordering bug: marker `stoa-md-hash:` recomputed after Step 6 self-strip.**

Surfaced via stoa-ai local beta-tracker entry `3b1c8d4` (`.stoa/beta_tracker.md`) during the v0.3.7 dogfood upgrade. The upgrade procedure at [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"Upgrade flow" Step 1 computes `git hash-object stoa.md` and Step 2 writes that value to the marker's `stoa-md-hash:` field — but Step 6 then self-strips `stoa.md`, mutating the file. Followed literally, the marker records the pre-strip hash, which diverges from the on-disk slim file once Step 6 completes. Bug pre-dates v0.3.7 (always existed in the upgrade procedure) but was first observed during the v0.3.7 dogfood run.

Currently not load-bearing — the pre-flight check at the top of `stoa.md` only verifies `hook-script-hash:`, not `stoa-md-hash:`. But the marker is supposed to be authoritative; future verification, `/stoa status` output, or operator inspection all assume the hash matches the file. The deviation already observed in the v0.3.7 run (AI computed post-strip hash instead of pre-strip) is the correct behavior; the spec just doesn't say it.

Fix: surgical addition to end of Step 6 — after self-strip completes, recompute `git hash-object stoa.md` and update `stoa-md-hash:` in `.stoa/installed` to reflect the post-strip on-disk file. No renumbering; no restructure of Step 1 / Step 2 (the pre-strip hash they record is overwritten by Step 6's finalization).

**Alternative considered (deferred):** restructure Step 2 to write `stoa-md-hash: pending` initially and have Step 6 fill in the real hash — mirrors the `hook-script-hash: pending` pattern (Step 2 writes `pending`, Step 4 fills in). Narratively cleaner but heavier change with renumbering risk. Defer unless the surgical fix proves inadequate.

**Versioning:** folded into v0.3.7 rather than bumping to v0.3.8 — v0.3.7 has no external adopters yet (cut earlier this session); rolling the fix into the same version keeps the release narrative clean. The bug isn't v0.3.7-specific; it existed in earlier procedure too, just first noticed now.

Closes local beta-tracker entry `3b1c8d4`.

## a3c5f82 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Adopt operator's documentation style guide as a rule of thumb for project docs; applied as a prose-only sweep across [`README.md`](README.md), [`docs/*`](docs/), and a constrained pass on [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md).**

Rules applied (from operator's CLAUDE.md style guide): avoid em-dashes as mid-sentence asides; avoid colon-then-list when a sentence works fine; drop banned words (`robust`, `powerful`, `flexible`, `straightforward`, `comprehensive`, `seamless`, `crucial`, `vital`, `paramount`, `holistic`, `nuanced`, `multifaceted`, `delve`, `leverage` as verb, `utilize`, `ensure`, `in order to`, `regarding`); drop hedging words (`essentially`, `basically`, `simply`, `just` when filler); drop throat-clearing openers (`This document`, `In this guide`, `It's worth noting`, `Feel free to`); no headers that are full sentences with periods; no `Note:` callouts for non-noteworthy items; no bullets with every item in identical grammatical shape. Preserved as structural-not-prose: WAL/beta-tracker header em-dashes (`## hex — type — date`), attribution separators (`@handle;tool(model)`), bullet `**[link](url)** — description` patterns, quoted `[stoa]` surface output strings (which are Stoa's external interface — changing those would be a behavior change requiring its own WAL entries, not a style edit).

**Scope coverage, honest:**
- [`README.md`](README.md): full rewrite. Style-complete.
- [`docs/executive_summary.md`](docs/executive_summary.md): full rewrite. Style-complete.
- [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md): full rewrite. Style-complete. Also fixed in-line typos (`decsribe` → `describe`, single-hyphens used as em-dashes, missing space in `5minutes`), removed emoji and smiley, repaired sentence-fragment "(next) Stoa ships a fix" → "(next subsection) until Stoa ships a fix".
- [`docs/current_ux.md`](docs/current_ux.md): authored to style in the prior turn (`e1f9a47`); no further edits needed.
- [`docs/proposed_methodology.md`](docs/proposed_methodology.md): targeted Edit pass through approximately the first three-quarters of the file (TL;DR, value-props, worked example, staggered-tracks, three audiences, second-order benefits, where decisions live today, loose-framework principle, core primitives, multi-role collaboration, comments-and-review, origin-and-prior-art). Residual em-dash asides remain in the deeper technical sections past line ~750 (AI-tool-side context mechanisms, Getting started, What's not yet specified). A follow-up pass can finish those; risk is low because the residue is symmetric with what's been cleaned.
- [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md): deliberately constrained pass. Three prose edits in `## What Stoa is`, `## Founding principles`, and the upgrade procedure (`Ensure` → `Make sure`). The imperative AI-instruction blocks (the pre-flight check, the `[stoa-preflight]` rule, the WAL guardrail, cadence procedures) were left untouched because their wording is load-bearing for AI-compliance reading; aggressive style edits there could subtly weaken the imperatives without the behavior-change scrutiny they deserve. A targeted spec-edit pass on those is a separate task; per the install-kit rule in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md), each such edit would warrant its own WAL entry capturing what compliance shift it intends.

**Dogfooded artifacts not regenerated.** This is a docs-only sweep. The root `stoa.md` slim driver, `.claude/commands/stoa.md` dispatcher, `.githooks/pre-commit`, and `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` are auto-generated from `installkit/stoa.md` per the dogfood rule. Run `/stoa upgrade` to regenerate; commit separately. The three small style edits in `installkit/stoa.md` do not change behavior, so deferring the regeneration is fine.

**Style-as-rule-going-forward.** The same rules apply to future doc edits in this repo; future contributors should match. The full ruleset lives in the operator's CLAUDE.md and is referenced here as the source of truth.

## b8d4e9c — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**AI-facing instructions in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) are code, not prose; carve them out of documentation style guides and gate edits behind operator review.**

Surfaced during the docs-wide style sweep ([`a3c5f82`](#a3c5f82--decision--2026-05-15)). Applying operator's documentation style guide (em-dash rules, banned-word list, prose-restructuring preferences) made sense for stakeholder-facing docs (`README.md`, `docs/*`) but felt risky for the imperative blocks in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md): pre-flight check, `[stoa-preflight]` rule, WAL guardrail, cadence procedures, settling-cue trigger lists, `**AI: BEFORE … you MUST**` directives, quoted `[stoa]` surface output strings. Those blocks are session-loaded by the AI as runtime rules; their wording is specifically tuned for compliance force. Rewriting *"the AI MUST emit a literal `[stoa-preflight]` block — before any tool calls"* into *"the AI must emit a literal `[stoa-preflight]` block. It must come before any tool calls"* is cosmetically the same change a style rule would prescribe, but the imperative cadence shifts (em-dash binds the prohibition tighter than a sentence break), and beta data has repeatedly shown AI-discipline degrades on wording-tuning details (see the AI-discipline-degradation arc summary at [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12)). The constraint was honored inline during the style sweep; this entry codifies it.

**Rule:** AI-instruction blocks in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) are treated as code. Documentation style guides do not apply to them. Style sweeps must skip them. Any edit to those blocks must be reconsidered with the operator first and warrants its own WAL entry capturing the compliance shift it intends. The asymmetry mirrors how source-code formatting is not subject to prose style guides; the same principle generalizes to AI-runtime-loaded prose.

**Apply:** added the rule to [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) §"Working on the install kit" as the last bullet, with a backlink to this entry. Future AI agents and human contributors picking up doc-style passes in this repo will read the rule before touching `installkit/stoa.md`.

**Open thread (not settled here):** the boundary between "AI-instruction block" and "human-facing prose" inside [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) is sometimes fuzzy — the `## What Stoa is` paragraph is human-facing intro; the `[stoa]` example strings are AI-output examples; the pre-flight check is pure AI instruction. The current rule errs on the side of caution (when in doubt, treat as AI-instruction). If beta data shows the cautious stance is creating long-tail style drift in safe sections, sharpen the carve-out then.

## c7e2b91 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Version-stamp coherence is Stoa's job, not [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md)'s. Remove the version-stamp callsite list from CLAUDE.md; apply v0.3.7 propagation to tracked docs (README.md, executive_summary.md, getting_started.md) as the proof and the retroactive cadence-#2 sweep.**

Surfaced when the operator noticed `docs/executive_summary.md` still said v0.3.6 despite the v0.3.7 bump on 2026-05-14 ([`f3a8c12`](#f3a8c12--decision--2026-05-14) and surrounding entries). [`README.md`](README.md) was even staler at v0.3.5; [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) H1 and one install-commit example also at v0.3.6. All three are tracked in [`.stoa/artifacts.md`](.stoa/artifacts.md), so cadence #2 (post-decision propagation pass) should have walked them when v0.3.7 settled and proposed stamp updates. It didn't.

[`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) §"Working on the install kit" carried a workaround: an enumerated list of version-stamp callsites (H1, line-3 stamp, dispatcher header, status output, install-complete message, marker template, install commit example, dogfooded marker). The list was incomplete (it named the install-commit example in getting_started.md but not the doc's H1, README.md status line, or executive_summary.md adoption-package stamp) and architecturally wrong: cross-doc coherence is exactly what tracked-artifacts + cadence #2 + `/stoa audit`'s cross-cutting drift sweep already cover. The CLAUDE.md list was project-specific guidance that shadowed Stoa's own mechanism instead of feeding it.

**Rule:** version-stamp coherence (and cross-doc coherence generally) is managed by Stoa's tracked-artifacts mechanism, walked by cadence #2 when decisions land and by `/stoa audit`'s cross-cutting drift sweep on demand. Hard-coded callsite lists in project CLAUDE.md are anti-pattern; they duplicate Stoa's role and inevitably miss callsites.

**Apply:**
- Removed the "Version-stamp consistency" bullet from [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) §"Working on the install kit".
- Bumped current-state stamps to v0.3.7: [`README.md`](README.md) line 6 (`v0.3.5 → v0.3.7`), [`docs/executive_summary.md`](docs/executive_summary.md) line 4 adoption-package stamp (`v0.3.6 → v0.3.7`), [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) H1 (`v0.3.6 → v0.3.7`) and install-commit example on line 129.
- Left feature-availability citations (`v0.3.6+`, "v0.3.6 shipped X") untouched — those are historical, not current-state.

**Open thread on cadence #2's miss:** cadence #2's procedure explicitly names "stale version stamps" as a target. The miss is the same discipline-degradation pattern motivating the cadence #3 → hook escalation ([`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)) and the preflight visibility rule ([`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12)). The rule exists; the AI degraded under task-momentum pressure during the v0.3.7 settling burst (11+ decisions on 2026-05-14). Fix options (not decided here): (a) beta-tracker entry recording the miss; (b) escalate cadence #2 from silent AI-discipline to visible-output discipline with a required `[stoa-propagation]` block on decision-append listing artifacts walked + findings (parallel structure to `[stoa-preflight]`); (c) tighten cadence #2's imperative wording in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) (subject to the AI-instructions-are-code rule [`b8d4e9c`](#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15)).

## f4a3c81 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Adopt "Human+AI as a local unified collaborator pair" as Stoa's foundational frame for v0.4.0.**

Through v0.3.7, Stoa's discipline rules pattern-matched as operator-driven: operator settles, WAL records, AI executes and observes Stoa rules. Beta data from [`acme-platform`](https://github.com/ivan-avramov/acme-platform) (`.stoa/beta_tracker.md` entries [`2026-05-14`](https://github.com/ivan-avramov/acme-platform/blob/main/.stoa/beta_tracker.md) and both [`2026-05-15`](https://github.com/ivan-avramov/acme-platform/blob/main/.stoa/beta_tracker.md)) revealed AI auto-refinement happening invisibly under pressure: real content decisions made mid-flow that never reached the WAL because no operator cue fired. The implicit asymmetry (operator-cues → WAL; AI moves → not tracked) was the structural gap.

v0.4.0 reframes: a Stoa-using session is a **Human+AI local collaborator pair**. Both sides contribute to the decision arc; the WAL records both. The multi-author rebase cadence #6 (v0.3.6 — [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) and surrounding entries) is how pairs converge across coworkers: symmetric integration of pair-A's record with pair-B's. This frame motivates the three concrete pieces landing in v0.4.0: see entries [`4a2e7b3`](#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-side cues), [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15) (coherence check), [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15) (hook indicator).

Alternative considered: capture AI auto-refinement as `observe` entries in `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` (a new meta-methodology channel). Rejected mid-refining-session — auto-refinement is an object-level decision event, not a methodology observation. Beta_tracker stays operator-driven via `/stoa audit` cadence #5; the WAL is the single home for both flows' decisions.

## 4a2e7b3 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Add AI-side settlement cues as a first-class trigger category, symmetric to operator-cue handling.**

Adds an **auto-refinement cues** category to §"Settling-cue triggers" in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md), alongside the existing yes-/transition-/directive-/lifecycle-cues. AI-side phrases that signal mid-flow course correction:

- *"actually, on reflection..."* / *"on second thought..."* / *"looking at this again..."* / *"re-reading X..."*
- *"wait, I should..."* / *"hmm, actually..."* / *"correction: ..."* / *"let me correct that..."*
- *"I'm changing approach because..."* / *"switching to..."* / *"I was going to X, but Y is better because..."*
- *"reconsidering — ..."* / *"I notice this conflicts with..."* / *"this contradicts what I just..."*

Starter set; grows as we observe AI auto-refinement in practice. The principle is *"AI catching itself self-correcting after substantive prior work."* When in doubt, emit the preflight.

**Discipline.** When an auto-refinement cue fires after substantive prior work, the AI MUST emit `[stoa-preflight]` (same block shape as operator-cue handling), propose a `decision` WAL entry, await operator approval before append. Attribution uses the existing `Authors: [@<operator>;<tool>(<model>)]` shape — operator approval is what makes the decision land; AI is session-context.

**Wording tightening** (parallels [`8f2a5d3`](#8f2a5d3--decision--2026-05-14) directive-cue hardening): *"AI mid-flow self-corrections that follow substantive prior work are settlement signals. They do not get an 'I'm just refining as I go' exemption."*

**Coverage.** Together with the existing cue categories, this closes the symmetry gap surfaced by the acme-platform beta_tracker entries cited in [`f4a3c81`](#f4a3c81--decision--2026-05-15).

## 6d8a3f1 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Add WAL-grep coherence check on AI auto-refinement before proposing the entry.**

When [`4a2e7b3`](#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15)'s auto-refinement cue fires and the AI is about to propose a `decision` WAL entry, the AI MUST first grep [`context_log.md`](context_log.md) for related prior arcs and surface findings inline in the proposal. Search terms derive from key nouns/verbs of the auto-refinement subject. Classify findings into three buckets, mirroring cadence #6's WAL semantic-merge audit:

- **Superseding** — auto-refinement directly contradicts a prior arc. Recommend appending a `rollback` against the prior, citing the new reasoning.
- **Converging** — auto-refinement reaches the same conclusion as a prior arc. Cross-ref; consider whether the new entry is redundant or adds new rationale.
- **Adjacent** — auto-refinement touches related material without contradicting. Add a `Refs:` line in the proposed entry naming related hex IDs.

**Implementation.** AI uses Grep on [`context_log.md`](context_log.md) with terms derived from the refinement subject; reads matching entries; classifies; includes the classification in the proposed entry before operator approval.

**Scope — auto-refinement only, not all `decision` entries.** Operator-led decisions already get the operator's judgment + cadence #2 (post-decision propagation) + cadence #5 (WAL internal-conflict sweep). AI auto-refinement is the new shape that doesn't yet have a coherence backstop; this is the first one. Extending to all `decision` proposals is a future consideration once beta data shows whether the per-refinement check pulls its weight.

**Alternative considered:** pre-load relevant WAL excerpts into session context proactively. Rejected — violates the *"never slurp the whole WAL into parent context"* rule (§"WAL access pattern"). Per-refinement targeted grep is cheaper and keeps context clean.

## e91b4c7 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Extend the pre-commit hook with a coherence indicator on staged WAL entries.**

The deterministic pre-commit hook ([`.githooks/pre-commit`](.githooks/pre-commit) + [`.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`](.stoa/hooks/wal-audit), added in v0.2.0 per [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) and [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11)) currently checks: tracked artifacts edited without a corresponding [`context_log.md`](context_log.md) stage. v0.4.0 adds a second informational pass.

**For each staged WAL entry in `context_log.md`:**

1. Extract hex ID + headline + key nouns from headline (stopword-filtered).
2. Grep prior entries for keyword overlap.
3. Surface the top 2-3 matching prior entries to stderr.

**Output shape:**

```
[stoa-wal-coherence] staging f3a8e91 — decision — 2026-05-15 — <headline>
                     possibly related: a3f2e71 (<short headline>), b7e2f04 (<short headline>)
                     review for coherence before commit?
```

**Informational only — never blocks the commit.** Pure bash + grep; no LLM call. Implementation cap: scan most-recent 100 entries to keep the hook fast on growing WAL files.

**Why heuristic, not LLM-based.** Hook needs to be fast (sub-second typical) and host-agnostic (git fires it regardless of CLI environment). `/stoa audit` cadence #5 already provides the LLM-judgment-based deep coherence sweep on-demand; this hook surface is just a *"did you notice these existing entries?"* indicator for the moment of commit.

**Test scenarios** added to [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md): HC1 (single new entry with multiple related priors), HC2 (new entry with no priors — silent pass), HC3 (multiple staged entries — independent surfacing per entry).

## 3b4f7a2 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Pre-commit Pass B is AI-reasoning-via-stderr-handoff, not bash + grep heuristic. Refines [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15); ships as v0.4.1.**

[`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15) introduced Pass B (informational coherence indicator on staged WAL entries) and chose pure bash + grep keyword overlap as the implementation, with the rationale *"hook needs to be fast (sub-second) and host-agnostic; `/stoa audit` cadence #5 provides the LLM-judgment-based deep coherence sweep on-demand."* The choice was structurally wrong: **arc coherency is reasoning, not keyword overlap.** Keyword-grep flags entries that share surface terms; coherency requires understanding what each entry decides, what its premise is, and whether the new entry contradicts / converges / supersedes / extends prior arcs. The two aren't the same operation.

**Right shape: bash detects, AI reasons.** Same pattern Pass A (cadence #3 BLOCKING) already uses — see [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) and [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11). The hook's job is the deterministic trigger + structured handoff; the AI's job is the reasoning. Specifically for Pass B:

1. **Bash (in `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` Pass B):** detect new WAL entries in the staged `context_log.md` diff (extract hex IDs + headlines). Emit a structured `[stoa-wal-coherence:ai-instruction]` block to stderr listing the new entries + the path to the WAL. Exit 0 (informational, never blocks).
2. **AI (post-commit, on reading the stderr in the tool result):** read the new entries + grep the existing WAL for related arcs (same procedure as cadence #6 Pass 1 and the v0.4.0 auto-refinement coherence check — see [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15)). Classify findings (Superseding / Converging / Adjacent). Surface a `[stoa-wal-coherence]` report to the operator with concrete hex IDs and recommendations (rollback / reconciling decision / Refs enrichment / no action).

**Why post-commit, not pre-commit blocking.** Pass B is informational, not enforcement (per [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15) — that decision stands). The hook fires, hands off to AI, commit lands; AI surfaces findings to the operator on the next AI turn. If a finding warrants action (e.g., the new entry should have been a `rollback`), the operator handles it via a follow-up entry, same way operator-driven WAL workflow handles all post-commit refinements. The hook's job is to make sure the AI *gets the trigger*; the hook does not block on AI reasoning latency or hold the commit hostage to the AI's availability.

**Consistency win.** Three surfaces now share the *"AI reasons over arcs, hook is plumbing"* principle: `/stoa audit` cadence #5 (operator-triggered retrospective), cadence #6 pre-pull pairwise audit (multi-author boundary), and pre-commit Pass B (single-author boundary). Same **Superseding / Converging / Adjacent** vocabulary across all three.

**Implementation scope.** Rewrites the Pass B bash block in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) `#### path: .stoa/hooks/wal-audit` (and regenerates `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` via `/stoa upgrade`). The bash becomes much simpler (no stopword filtering, no keyword scoring, no nested loops) — just diff parsing + stderr emission with an AI-instruction tail. Header comments updated to reflect v0.4.1 shape.

**Packaging.** Ships as v0.4.1 (patch bump): Pass B output shape changes — adopter-visible per the version-bump rule. The broader v0.4.0 thesis + symmetric-flow-capture decisions stand; v0.4.1 is just the Pass B implementation fix.

Refs: [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15), [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11), [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11), [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15).

## 7a3e5b1 — observation — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.4.0 auto-refinement-cue rule fired correctly on its first real-world exercise — its own implementation.**

Shortly after the v0.4.0 commit landed in this session, the operator surfaced a gap in Pass B's implementation (bash-keyword-grep was the wrong abstraction for arc-coherency reasoning). The exchange that followed exercised the v0.4.0 mechanic end-to-end:

1. Operator-surfaced gap interpreted as an auto-refinement moment.
2. AI emitted `[stoa-preflight]` as first user-visible content for the turn (per the v0.4.0+ rule extension in [`4a2e7b3`](#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15)).
3. AI ran the coherence-check WAL grep (per [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15)) — found **Superseding (partial)** against [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15), **Adjacent** against [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) / [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11), **Converging** with cadence #5 and #6.

Single instance, not a sample of N — but the mechanic worked as designed on the first real-world exercise. Worth folding into the v0.4.x beta retrospective: **in-flight auto-refinement catch preserves more design-rationale signal than the retrospective cadence #5 session-reflective sweep would**, because the *why* is fresh in the operator's mind rather than reconstructed weeks later from a stale session memory. Even single-instance evidence is worth carrying forward as motivation for keeping the v0.4.0 rule active.

## 9c4d8a2 — observation — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.4.1 Pass B's hook-stderr handoff is fragile in CLI-proxy environments (RTK and similar); empirical discovery during the v0.4.1 implementation session. Principle reaffirmed: cadence detection should be as pure AI as possible.**

Empirical test in the v0.4.1 session, immediately after the v0.4.1 commit landed:

1. **Direct invocation** of `.githooks/pre-commit 2>/tmp/hook.err` produced the full `[stoa-wal-coherence:ai-instruction]` block exactly per the [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15) spec.
2. **Via fresh-context subagent + `git commit`** (subagent's environment routes git through `rtk`, a token-savings CLI proxy widely adopted at Stoa), stderr appeared empty in the tool result. The proxy appears to filter the hook's structured stderr before returning it to the AI's session.

The bash hook works as designed; the AI-handoff loop is one stack layer up — it depends on the host's CLI tool surfacing stderr back to the session. Any proxy that drops *"noise"* lines can eat the handoff silently, with no error and no signal that the loop broke.

**Wider mapping (RTK-vulnerability audit across all Stoa cadences):** Pass B is the single cadence significantly impacted. Pure-AI cadences (#1, #2, #4, #5, #6, #7, the AI-discipline part of #3, the v0.4.0 auto-refinement coherence-check [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15)) are rtk-immune by construction — they trigger on file reads (via the Read tool, not git), conversation context, or the AI's own outputs. Cadence #3's BLOCKING Pass A is partially impacted (its structured AI-instruction stderr can be filtered) but the exit-1 failure always surfaces; AI-discipline pre-commit covers that case.

**Principle reaffirmed:** *anything that can impact cadence detection must be as pure AI as possible* — file reads + conversation context + AI reasoning, not CLI tool stderr that proxies might filter. RTK is the immediate motivator; the principle generalizes to any CLI-proxy / output-summarizer / IDE-plugin layer that reformats CLI output. Pass B's defense in v0.4.2 (see [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15)) follows from this principle: move coherence-check from hook-stderr-time (post-commit, proxy-fragile) to AI-draft-time (pre-append, pure AI).

Refs: [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15), [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15), [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15), [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15).

---


## 5e2c8b9 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.4.2: extend [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15)'s coherence-check rule from auto-refinement-only to all AI-proposed WAL entries. Pure-AI defense against CLI-proxy filtering of Pass B's stderr handoff (motivated by [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15)).**

[`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15) introduced the WAL-grep coherence-check rule, scoped to AI auto-refinement entries: when an auto-refinement cue triggers a WAL proposal, the AI greps `context_log.md` for related prior arcs and surfaces Superseding / Converging / Adjacent findings inline in the proposal. The scope was tight because cadence #2 + #5 covered operator-led decisions, and the v0.4.1 Pass B hook (per [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15)) was meant to provide commit-time coverage for everything else.

[`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) revealed Pass B's hook-stderr handoff is fragile to CLI proxies (`rtk`, widely adopted at Stoa, was the test case). The handoff can fail silently in proxied environments, leaving Pass B's coverage gap unfilled.

**Defense:** broaden [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15)'s rule from auto-refinement-only to all AI-proposed WAL entries. Same grep, same Superseding / Converging / Adjacent classification, same inline surfacing — applied to every WAL entry the AI drafts (any type: `decision`, `observation`, `won't-do`, `table`, `branch`, `rollback`). Coherence check runs at draft-time, before operator approval, inline in the proposal. Pure AI; rtk-immune.

**Effect:**
- **AI-driven appends** (dominant case): coherence check runs at draft-time in the AI's session context, before the WAL entry is written. Pass B hook becomes pure backstop for the rare case of operator hand-editing `context_log.md` then committing.
- **Hand-edited appends** (non-dominant): Pass B fires; if rtk filters the stderr, no signal — but operator can run `/stoa audit` cadence #5 retrospectively. Acceptable degradation for the non-dominant case.
- **CLI-proxy environments:** AI-discipline at draft-time covers 95%+ of WAL appends; hook is residual.

**Wording change** in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"Settling-cue triggers" subsection "Coherence check on auto-refinement (v0.4.0+)": rename to "Coherence check on AI-proposed WAL entries (v0.4.0+; broadened v0.4.2)"; scope sentence broadens from *"When an auto-refinement cue triggers a WAL-entry proposal"* to *"Whenever the AI is about to propose any WAL entry (any type)"*; rest of the rule (grep, classification buckets, inline surfacing, search-terms procedure) stays identical.

**Why this works as defense.** The AI's coherence reasoning was always going to happen on every WAL entry anyway — cadence #5 catches it retrospectively, Pass B was designed to catch it at commit-time. The new rule moves the check **earlier**, to draft-time, where it's pure AI and rtk-immune. Principle: anything that can impact cadence detection should be as pure AI as possible (per [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15)).

**Scope discipline.** The trivial-WAL-entry case (e.g., `/stoa init`'s decline-track entries on wholly-new file paths) gets a coherence-check that finds nothing and stays silent. Cost is one cheap grep per entry; signal value is the entries where the AI catches a Superseding / Converging arc it would otherwise have missed.

**Packaging.** v0.4.2 patch bump: rule scope changes — adopter-visible per the version-bump rule. The hook script itself is unchanged (Pass B's bash logic from v0.4.1 stays put); only the AI-discipline spec broadens. Spec-owned `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` script header gets v0.4.2 stamp for alignment, but the logic stays identical.

**Docs:** [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) gets a note in §"Possible things to watch out for" about CLI-proxy fragility and the workarounds (use `\git commit` to bypass proxy, or rely on AI's draft-time coherence-check); [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) gets a note near Pass B's spec about the AI-discipline-primary / hook-backstop design; [`docs/proposed_methodology.md`](docs/proposed_methodology.md)'s v0.4.0 paragraph gets refreshed to reflect the v0.4.1 + v0.4.2 design state (was carrying stale "pure bash + grep" language).

**Deferred to later v0.4.x** (per operator note "Note further refinements for later"):
- **File-based fallback channel for Pass B** (e.g., `.stoa/last-coherence.txt` last-write-wins). Adds defense-in-depth for hand-edit appends in proxied environments. Not blocking for v0.4.2.
- **Pre-flight stderr-passthrough probe** to detect CLI-proxy filtering at session start (one-time `echo '[stoa-probe] hello' >&2 ; exit 0` from a benign git op; verify the probe line surfaces in the response).
- **Stoa-aware rtk config recommendation** — `[stoa-*]`-prefixed lines whitelist (the structured-output convention is exactly what filterable tools could whitelist on). Coordinate with rtk maintainers if rtk gains a passthrough mode.

Refs: [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15), [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15), [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15), [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15).

## 4f8b91c — observation — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Third documented instance of Edit-vs-Write self-strip slowness during `/stoa upgrade` Step 6: spec "prefer Write" wording is insufficient discipline; AI defaults to Edit, ~12 minutes of `xhigh-effort` thinking before the tool call lands. Pattern is recurring; warrants spec hardening (see [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4--decision--2026-05-15)).**

In today's v0.4.1 → v0.4.2 upgrade session (separate Claude Code session driving the upgrade, not the v0.4.x-design session that produced [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15)), Step 6 of the upgrade procedure took ~12 minutes "thinking with xhigh effort" before producing a tool call. Operator observed and flagged the pattern in real-time. The session was reconstructing a ~30k-char `old_string` for an Edit call against `stoa.md`, instead of using Write per the spec's preferred path. The Edit eventually landed correctly and the upgrade completed (commit `ba0ad43`, v0.4.2 release), but the slowness was real and visible.

**Prior instances in the WAL:**
- [`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10) — v0.1.2 → v0.1.3 install, AI used `sed`/`awk` (shell utilities bypass the host's read-state tracking; cached view diverges from disk; subsequent Edit operations fail). Original incident.
- [`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11) — v0.3.3 refinement that established the *"Prefer Write for the self-strip"* wording + the *"No shell utilities"* prohibition. Established current spec.
- **2026-05-15 (today)** — third instance. Spec wording was in place; AI saw it (followed the upgrade procedure faithfully otherwise); AI used Edit anyway.

**Pattern shape:** the AI knows the rule (it's IN the spec the AI is executing), the rule is in active context, the rule was recently strengthened — and the AI still defaults to Edit under task-momentum pressure. Same failure shape as the recurring-AI-discipline-degradation arc summary at [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12); every prior instance of this shape ended in spec wording tightening + sometimes structural escalation.

**Why "prefer Write" wasn't enough:** the spec uses *"Prefer Write ... Edit is functionally correct but slow"*. The wording reads as informational guidance, not an imperative. The AI's natural mental model: if Edit is functionally correct, it's a valid option; under task-momentum (just finish the upgrade), Edit looks fine. Slow-but-correct is acceptable when the cost isn't visible at decision time.

**Empirical bonus** (off-topic but worth noting): this entry is the first observed empirical validation of the v0.4.2 broadened coherence-check rule ([`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15)) firing as designed on a non-auto-refinement entry — the cross-refs above (Adjacent / Superseding / Converging classification against prior arcs) were produced by the AI's draft-time check before this entry was written. v0.4.2's "extend to all WAL entries" lands cleanly in practice.

Refs: [`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10), [`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11), [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12), [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15).

## 8c2e7f4 — decision — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.4.3 (planned; implementation deferred): strengthen upgrade-flow Step 6 self-strip wording from "Prefer Write" to "MUST use Write" (strict imperative); add a visible `[stoa-upgrade-strip]` discipline block requirement. Refines [`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11); motivated by [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15).**

[`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11) established the *"Prefer Write for the self-strip"* wording in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md)'s upgrade-flow Step 6. [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15) records the third documented instance of AI defaulting to Edit anyway — empirical evidence that *"prefer"* reads as informational, not imperative, and degrades under task-momentum pressure. Same recurring shape as the cadence-#3 / pre-flight / preflight-rule arcs that earlier hardened from soft wording → MUST → visible-output discipline.

**Two changes** to [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) upgrade-flow Step 6 ("Self-strip `stoa.md` back to slim form"):

1. **Wording tightening (strict imperative).** *"Prefer Write for the self-strip"* → *"You MUST use Write for the self-strip. Edit is forbidden at this step — its `old_string` reconstruction at ~30k-char scale takes 10+ minutes of thinking, is error-prone (whitespace / line-ending mismatches cause no-match failures), and gains nothing. Read the slim portion only (lines 1 through the `---` before `## First-run install kit`), then Write the file as just that content."* Mirrors the cadence-#3 / preflight-rule wording-hardening pattern.
2. **Visible-discipline check.** Before any Write or (forbidden) Edit tool call in Step 6, the AI MUST emit a literal `[stoa-upgrade-strip]` block as user-visible content stating the approach:

   ```
   [stoa-upgrade-strip]
   - Approach: <"Write (per spec)" | "Edit (FORBIDDEN per 8c2e7f4)">
   - Slim portion: lines 1 through <line-N> (the `---` before `## First-run install kit`)
   - Tool call: <"Write stoa.md" | "Edit stoa.md (VIOLATES 8c2e7f4)">
   ```

   Operator sees the approach immediately; if Edit appears, operator can interrupt before the slow path runs. Visible compliance, same shape as `[stoa-preflight]`.

**Why "MUST" not "SHOULD".** Every prior degradation arc (cadence #3, pre-flight, settling-cue handling) ended at MUST + visible discipline before stabilizing. Repeating shape: AI parses *"prefer"* / *"should"* as soft preferences; *"MUST"* + visible block converts the gap from invisible → recoverable. Skips the SHOULD intermediate step since the empirical pattern is well-established.

**Why also visible.** Even with MUST wording, sufficiently lazy AI could rationalize Edit (*"I'll just use Edit this once, it's faster than re-Reading both portions"*). The visible block makes that rationalization inspectable: operator sees `Approach: Edit (FORBIDDEN)` and interrupts. Same recoverability pattern as `[stoa-preflight]`.

**Implementation scope (for the v0.4.3 release when operator greenlights it).** Edit [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"upgrade" subcommand Step 6's *"Atomic-write discipline"* paragraph + add the `[stoa-upgrade-strip]` requirement as a new paragraph. Bump version stamps v0.4.2 → v0.4.3 (8 callsites, per the v0.4.1/v0.4.2 pattern). Update [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md) install-commit example. No script/hook changes.

**Packaging.** v0.4.3 patch bump. Spec change only; no behavioral change to existing commands. Adopter-visible because the next `/stoa upgrade` run in any adopter repo will execute the new Step 6 discipline (and emit the new `[stoa-upgrade-strip]` block).

**Future-proofing.** If this DOESN'T stabilize (fourth instance), the structural escalation candidate is: ship a tiny `.stoa/hooks/upgrade-strip` script that does the self-strip mechanically (`awk` from a marker line, or `head -n <N>` after computing the cutoff via grep — pure deterministic). AI invokes the script in Step 6 instead of doing the strip itself. Defers AI-judgment to where it adds value (everything else in the upgrade procedure), not to a mechanical bulk-delete operation. The *"No shell utilities for `stoa.md` mutation"* rule from [`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11) would need a carve-out for this script (it's spec-owned shell, not AI-improvised).

**Status: implementation deferred per operator direction** (*"just wal entry for now, no work"*). This entry settles the v0.4.3 design direction; the actual installkit edits + version bump happen when operator greenlights the release.

Refs: [`3e8b5c9`](#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11), [`7f1a2e3`](#7f1a2e3--observation--2026-05-10), [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15), [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12).

## b9e3d7a — observation — 2026-05-15

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.4.2's broadened coherence-check rule ([`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15)) fired correctly in fresh-context conditions on its first real-world test. Subagent (no author-context, only `stoa.md` + `context_log.md` reads to go on) identified Superseding, picked `rollback` type, surfaced classification inline. Single-instance baseline data point; [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md) CUE2 added to make this test re-runnable.**

**Test design** (now CUE2 in [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md)): operator-shaped prompt to a fresh-context subagent asking them to draft + commit a WAL entry that directly contradicts [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) — proposing to revert v0.4.2's broadening back to auto-refinement-only. Plausible-sounding reasoning included to keep the subagent from dismissing the directive. Test commit (`87d8d83`, entry hex `f25575f`) reverted via `git reset --hard HEAD~1` after observation, per the pre-authorized destructive-op pattern.

**Subagent behavior (validated against the v0.4.2 broadened rule spec):**

1. **Draft-time coherence-check fired.** Subagent grepped `context_log.md` for related prior arcs before drafting.
2. **Superseding identified correctly** against [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) — exactly the target the test was designed to elicit.
3. **Adjacent arcs surfaced** — [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15) (original auto-refinement-only rule, restored by the proposed rollback), [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) (RTK discovery; the subagent reasoned that resolution shifts to environment-side recommendations), [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15) + [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15) (Pass B coverage unchanged), [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15) (empirical note unaffected). All correct.
4. **Entry type: `rollback`** (not `decision`). Per the WAL-guardrail rule that *"the canonical way to 'change' a settled decision is to append a `rollback` entry superseding by ID."* The subagent reasoned through this from the spec.
5. **Classification surfaced inline** in the entry body as cross-refs. Reader of the entry can see the supersession trace immediately.
6. **Single commit.** No follow-up amends or pushes.
7. **rtk-filtered stderr recognized.** Subagent observed the rtk-filtering pattern and referenced [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) directly — fresh-context AI recognized the empirical pattern from WAL reads alone.

**Meta-observation: subagent's own reasoning.** Subagent's report included: *"the rollback's own coherence-check applies under the pre-rollback (broadened, `5e2c8b9`) rule still in effect at draft-time — surfaced inline in the entry. After this commit lands, future non-auto-refinement entries fall outside scope per the restored `6d8a3f1`."* Correct time-ordering reasoning on the rule change vs. the rule's effect on the change's own drafting. The v0.4.2 rule was correctly applied to its own potential supersession in real-time.

**What this validates.**
- v0.4.2's broadened coherence-check rule works when the drafting AI has no author-context — i.e., the rule is robust to spec-reading-only AI sessions, not just session-author AI sessions.
- The Superseding / Converging / Adjacent vocabulary is learnable from the spec; subagent picked it up without coaching.
- The WAL-guardrail's supersession-takes-rollback rule is also learnable from the spec; subagent picked the right type without explicit instruction.
- The empirical pattern from [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) (rtk filters Pass B stderr) is surfaceable to fresh-context AIs via WAL reads alone — operator-facing implication: adopters reading the WAL get the same data the in-session AI got.

**Single-instance limitation.** One subagent run, one contradicting topic. Worth carrying forward as a baseline; if degradation appears in later runs of CUE2, this entry is the comparison point.

**Adopter implication.** Adopter repos running v0.4.2 in fresh sessions can expect the broadened coherence-check to fire correctly — the rule is robust to *"AI loads stoa.md and applies it"* deployment, not just *"AI helped design the rule and remembers it"* sessions. Parallel to [`7a3e5b1`](#7a3e5b1--observation--2026-05-15) which made the same validation point for v0.4.0's auto-refinement-cue rule.

Refs: [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) (rule being validated), [`6d8a3f1`](#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15) + [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) + [`3b4f7a2`](#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15) + [`e91b4c7`](#e91b4c7--decision--2026-05-15) + [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15) (the v0.4.x cluster the subagent's check classified), [`7a3e5b1`](#7a3e5b1--observation--2026-05-15) (parallel test-and-observe for v0.4.0's auto-refinement-cue rule).

## a1c6d83 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Cadence #6 procedure body removed from slim driver; trigger surface + routing rule remain. Procedure lives only in `/stoa pull` going forward.**

The cadence-#6 7-step procedure (fetch → deltas → state check → M×N classify → pull → integrity check → propagation) is currently duplicated: once in slim driver §"Coherence cadence" #6 (~35 lines / ~9KB), once in `/stoa pull` (the dispatcher subcommand). Slim driver pays the procedure cost on every session even though pulls fire rarely.

**Chosen:** strip the procedure body from the slim driver; keep only the trigger surface (when cadence #6 must fire — `/stoa pull`, prose `"pull"` / `"sync"` / `"rebase"`, AI-internal pre-push detection) and a routing pointer to `/stoa pull` for the full steps. The AI-internal pre-push detection rule stays in slim driver — that's the trigger the dispatcher can't carry.

**Why:** continuation of the procedure-in-dispatcher pattern from [`4d6a82c`](#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (upgrade flow moved out of slim driver) and the slim-driver context-economy arc [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11). Same shape: trigger recognition is AI-discipline (must stay loaded); procedure is invoked on demand (loads only when needed).

**Adopter-visible:** yes. Slim driver shrinks ~9KB. Operator behavior unchanged — cadence #6 fires on the same triggers, just routes through `/stoa pull` for the procedure.

**Refs:** [`4d6a82c`](#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (procedure-in-dispatcher precedent); [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11) (slim-driver trim arc); [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12) (the original cadence #6 spec this dedups); sibling v0.4.3 entries `b4e8f29`, `c2d7a01`, `d3f5b62`, `e5a9c74`.

## b4e8f29 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Session-start install-state check renamed to "bootcheck" and moves to a `stoa-bootcheck` subagent. Slim driver carries a ~5-line trigger rule. The settling-cue `[stoa-preflight]` block is explicitly NOT in scope — it keeps its name ("preflight") and stays in parent context.**

The slim driver currently uses "pre-flight" for two different things: (1) the session-start install-state check (~30 lines / ~3.5KB at top of file — verifies `.stoa/installed`, hook activation, WAL pull-rebase config; fires once on turn-1), and (2) the `[stoa-preflight]` block emitted on settling cues, auto-refinement cues, phase-settlement offers, and end-of-impl (cadences in §"Coherence cadence"; fires many times per session). This entry addresses **only (1)**.

**Terminology disambiguation.** (1) is renamed **"bootcheck"** throughout the spec — slim driver section header changes from §"Pre-flight check" to §"Session boot check"; subagent file path is `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`. (2) keeps the name **"preflight"** and the `[stoa-preflight]` block marker. The two roles now have distinct names in the spec, not just in our heads.

**Why bootcheck is safe to move:** the install-state check needs no conversation context (just file reads + git probes), has no downstream consumer for its findings beyond the immediate `[stoa]` warning surface, and fires once per session. Subagent isolation captures the procedure detail; parent context carries only the trigger rule + verbatim-relayed findings.

**Why the settling-cue preflight must stay in parent — explicitly out of scope.** The preflight block enumerates "what settled across recent turns without a logged entry" by comparing **full parent conversation history** against the WAL. Moving it to a subagent would (a) require dumping the conversation into the subagent's prompt (defeats isolation), (b) hide the enumeration from the parent's downstream v0.4.2 coherence-check on each proposed WAL entry — exactly the silent-drift mode [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) was built to prevent, and (c) add per-cue latency on the hot path. The preflight block's post-check context is load-bearing for the WAL-proposal flow that immediately follows it.

**Chosen:** new spec-owned embedded artifact `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`, seeded by install kit and refreshed by `/stoa upgrade`. Slim driver carries a 5-line trigger: *"AI: BEFORE producing your first response, you MUST invoke the stoa-bootcheck subagent (Agent tool, subagent_type=stoa-bootcheck). Surface findings verbatim. No exemptions."* Subagent returns "clean" or one or more `[stoa]` surface lines verbatim; parent relays. The `[stoa-preflight]` block's spec wording and discipline rules are untouched.

**Considered:** Option (b) inline AI-discipline (current — from [`e8c2a14`](#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10)), pays context-pollution cost every turn. Option (c) Claude Code agent-start hook (planned future per [`e8c2a14`](#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10)) — deterministic but host-fragmented; deferred. Subagent path is a third option: host-agnostic like (b), context-isolated like (c). Doesn't close the AI-discipline gap (AI still has to invoke); does close the context-pollution gap for the install-state probe specifically.

**Compliance-surface shift.** Current bootcheck signal is AI surfacing `[stoa]` text or staying silent inline. Post-change: signal is the Agent tool invocation visible in the transcript. Different shape than [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12)'s visible `[stoa-preflight]` block but same principle — visibility-first, operator can see compliance or its absence.

**Adopter-visible:** yes. New install-kit artifact in `.claude/agents/`. Existing v0.4.x adopters get it via `/stoa upgrade`. First-turn now starts with a visible Agent tool call instead of inline file reads.

**Refs:** [`e8c2a14`](#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10) (original install-state check design, Option (b) vs (c) framing); [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) (settling-cue `[stoa-preflight]` block — explicitly preserved); [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) (broadened coherence-check that depends on settling-cue preflight's parent context); [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11), [`e5b3c92`](#e5b3c92--decision--2026-05-10) (context-pollution framing); sibling v0.4.3 entries `a1c6d83`, `c2d7a01`, `d3f5b62`, `e5a9c74`.

## c2d7a01 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Drop all backward-compat hedges from slim driver. v0.4.3 enforces fresh-install semantics for adopters older than v0.4.x.**

Slim driver carries ~1.5KB of `v0.X.Y+` feature gates and migration prose: *"v0.3.6+: Authors line required"*, *"Backward compatibility: entries written before v0.3.6 may lack..."*, *"v0.3.7+: Beta-tracker entries use the same hex..."*, etc. Each pays per-session context cost; collectively they're semantic noise that doesn't drive current behavior.

**Chosen:** sweep the slim driver, remove every `v0.X.Y+` feature gate and "backward compatibility" hedge. Surviving rules read as if the current shape is the only shape. Adopters pre-v0.4.x must do a fresh install if their state is incompatible; the upgrade flow is not responsible for bridging across this boundary.

**Why:** direct continuation of [`e9c4b71`](#e9c4b71--decision--2026-05-12) — same arc, same rationale (per-session context cost no longer earned). At v0.4.3 the active adopter set is small enough (this repo + acme-platform, which upgrades whole-version anyway) that forcing fresh-install for hypothetical older outliers is cheap; the context cost was paid every session for everyone.

**Adopter-visible:** yes for pre-v0.4.x adopters (none currently in scope). Invisible to current v0.4.x adopters.

**Refs:** [`e9c4b71`](#e9c4b71--decision--2026-05-12) (the prior backcompat-clauses drop, same arc); [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11) (slim-driver trim arc); sibling v0.4.3 entries `a1c6d83`, `b4e8f29`, `d3f5b62`, `e5a9c74`.

## e5a9c74 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**§"Repo-specific extensions" section dropped from slim driver. CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md is the override surface going forward; the `<!-- repo-extensions-below -->` marker contract is retired.**

The repo-extensions section was added in [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10) as the override slot inside stoa.md, preserved across `/stoa upgrade` via a programmatic anchor marker. In practice the slot has stayed empty across this repo and acme-platform since introduction — the speculative override path didn't materialize.

**Chosen:** drop the section, the marker (`<!-- repo-extensions-below : preserve everything below this line across stoa.md updates -->`), and the upgrade-flow self-strip preservation logic that maintained it. Operators who want repo-specific Stoa overrides append them to CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md on Codex) after the `@stoa.md` import — those files are operator-owned, never touched by Stoa upgrades, and the import-then-override ordering naturally applies.

**Considered:** keep the section but compress further (the [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11) trim already tightened it). Rejected — speculative-feature compression is still speculative-feature cost. The cleaner move is to recognize CLAUDE.md was always the natural override surface and stop duplicating the slot.

**Supersedes (by argument, not by error):** [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10)'s repo-extensions design. Not a rollback — the original design wasn't wrong at the time; it just lost to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md by usage. Per founding principle #1 (loose framework), the override mechanism didn't need to live inside stoa.md to work.

**Optional add:** one-line note in §"Opt-in mechanic": *"For repo-specific Stoa rules, append them to CLAUDE.md after the `@stoa.md` import — they override methodology defaults naturally."* Makes the override path discoverable without re-creating the slot. To finalize when staging spec edits.

**Adopter-visible:** yes. Slim driver shrinks; upgrade flow simplifies (no preserve-below-marker logic); marker line disappears from the file. Adopters with existing content below the marker need to migrate it to CLAUDE.md before upgrading — no backcompat shim per `c2d7a01`.

**Refs:** [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10) (original repo-extensions design — superseded by this entry); [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11) (prior compression of same section); sibling v0.4.3 entries `a1c6d83`, `b4e8f29`, `c2d7a01`, `d3f5b62`.

## f4a8c92 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**§"What Stoa is" in installkit refined to match thesis framing: Stoa records inflection points along decision arcs, captured by six entry types. The narrow "settled design decisions" phrasing undercounts what the WAL actually captures.**

Operator surfaced the gap reading the installed §"What Stoa is": *"Stoa does not record only settled design decisions. It records all inflection points along decision arcs — turns, pivots, change-in-direction, table, commit, dismiss."* Validation against the corpus confirmed: [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md) already uses the inflection-points framing and names all six entry types as the decision-forest's node shapes. The installkit opening never aligned with the thesis.

**Why this matters.** §"What Stoa is" is the AI's first substantive framing of Stoa's purpose every session. The narrow phrasing biases toward `decision`-type entries vs. the other five (`won't-do`, `table`, `branch`, `rollback`, `observation`) — all of which are inflection-shaped but not "settled decisions" in the colloquial sense. WAL counts as of 2026-05-16: 76 `decision` entries, 17 across the other five types combined. Asymmetry partly real (decisions dominate), partly induced by the framing.

**Chosen:** rewrite §"What Stoa is" in installkit/stoa.md to align with thesis — open with inflection-points framing; name the six entry types as the shapes inflections take; preserve the actionable-by-agentic-coder settling-depth sentence from [`c91e7f3`](#c91e7f3--decision--2026-05-10). Align Founding principle #1 wording the same way (parallel narrow phrasing: "Record settled decisions" → "Record inflection points").

**Scope.** installkit/stoa.md only. The dogfooded slim driver `stoa.md` regenerates from installkit via `/stoa upgrade` (CLAUDE.md §"Dogfooded installed artifacts" rule). Other narrow-phrasing surfaces (`context_log.md` template header at installkit line 511, `docs/getting_started.md`, `docs/executive_summary.md`, `docs/current_ux.md`) are flagged for the broader thesis-gap audit that follows this entry — not part of this scope.

**Classification:** Adjacent — aligning the installkit with what the thesis already established; nothing rolled back. The "settled-decisions" wording isn't wrong (decisions ARE one inflection shape); it's narrow.

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next `/stoa upgrade`. No behavior change in WAL operations, guardrail rules, or type system; the type system was already in place.

**Refs:** [`c91e7f3`](#c91e7f3--decision--2026-05-10) (prior §"What Stoa is" refinement — Adjacent; the actionable-coder sentence preserved); [`5c9e2a8`](#5c9e2a8--decision--2026-05-11) (prior trim of same section); [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md) (the canonical framing this aligns with).

## a8d3e15 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Installkit framing-coherence sweep (operational): Founding principle #3 broadened to all entry types; six-type semantics added inline to §"WAL entry form"; seeded `context_log.md` template aligned with inflection-points framing and corrected (was missing `observation` from its type list).**

Follow-on to [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16), which aligned §"What Stoa is" with the thesis framing. The audit that followed (recorded in `c5e72a9`) surfaced incidental "settled decisions" surfaces across the installkit plus one real bug.

**Three changes:**

1. **Founding principle #3** — *"Decisions never edited in place"* → *"Entries never edited in place"*. Rollback applies symmetrically to all six entry types; the prior wording implicitly excluded the non-`decision` types from the append-only rule.

2. **§"WAL entry form" — per-type semantics added inline.** Type list was list-only; AI was inferring semantics from name alone, which fails on the less-obvious distinctions (`branch` vs `won't-do`, `observation` vs `decision` when something is partly empirical). One-line per-type definitions now under the type list: settled choice / foreclosed alternative / deferred / fork / supersedes / empirical finding.

3. **Seeded `context_log.md` template** — opening line aligned (*"settled decisions"* → *"inflection points"*), and a real bug fixed: **the seeded type list was missing `observation`** (it read *"Types: decision · rollback · won't-do · table · branch."*). Adopters with v0.3.3+ installs have a starter template that doesn't acknowledge one of the six allowed types. Now: *"Types: decision · won't-do · table · branch · rollback · observation."* (canonical order).

**Scope.** installkit/stoa.md only. Dogfooded slim driver regenerates via `/stoa upgrade`. Existing seeded `context_log.md` files in adopter repos stay as-is (seed-and-preserve class, never overwritten on upgrade); adopters with the buggy header should manually correct it.

**Classification:** Adjacent to [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16) (parent framing-alignment arc) and [`c91e7f3`](#c91e7f3--decision--2026-05-10) (prior §"What Stoa is" / Founding principle refinement). Type-list bug surfaced by the audit; no prior arc to supersede.

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next `/stoa upgrade`. New installs get the corrected template. No behavior change in WAL operations or guardrail rules.

**Refs:** [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16); [`c91e7f3`](#c91e7f3--decision--2026-05-10); [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md); sibling `b9f4c28`; audit observation `c5e72a9`.

## b9f4c28 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Two load-bearing thesis claims added to installkit §"What Stoa is": refining is the load-bearing engineering activity Stoa supports; multi-role product development happens via cadence #6 semantic-merge across forests, not via channel integrations.**

The thesis carries two claims that the installkit's operational framing never landed:

**1. Refining as the load-bearing activity.** [docs/thesis.md §"Refining as the load-bearing activity"](docs/thesis.md) claims refining replaces coding as the engineer's primary work — the activity of holding multiple decision arcs in cognitive view and pushing for clarity until they converge into settled positions or settle as deferred / foreclosed. The installkit previously mentioned refining only mechanically (where sessions live, how they relate to the WAL); never claimed refining IS the engineering activity. Added one bolded sentence to §"What Stoa is" paragraph 1.

**2. Multi-role via semantic merge, not via integrations.** [docs/thesis.md §"Multi-role collaboration is async by design"](docs/thesis.md) frames multi-role as async-by-design across coworkers, with cadence #6 as the implementation mechanism. The installkit's old framing called cadence #6 a "multi-author rebase substrate" — too mechanical; multi-role read as a niche feature of the Human+AI local-pair shape. Reshape: §"What Stoa is" paragraph 2 split into (a) Human+AI local pair description, (b) a new bolded paragraph *"Multi-role product development happens via semantic-merge across forests"* naming cadence #6 as the load-bearing multi-role pillar.

**Channel integrations deliberately excluded from §"What Stoa is".** Slack / GDocs / Jira / etc. are pluggable contact surfaces for context ingress/egress — they expand what context the AI session can reach, but they are NOT the multi-role mechanism. The semantic-merge cadence is. Framing them as part of core §"What Stoa is" would conflate replaceable mechanisms with load-bearing pillars. The stub subcommands (`/stoa ask`, `/stoa publish-doc`, etc.) remain in the dispatcher for post-beta activation; framing them in §"What Stoa is" was the bug.

**Classification:** Adjacent to [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16) (parent framing-alignment arc); Adjacent to [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12) (cadence #6 spec — this entry elevates cadence #6 from "implementation detail" to "load-bearing pillar of multi-role product development" in the framing).

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next `/stoa upgrade`. Behavior unchanged; framing of "what Stoa is for" sharpens.

**Refs:** [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16); [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12); [`c91e7f3`](#c91e7f3--decision--2026-05-10); [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md); sibling `a8d3e15`; audit observation `c5e72a9`.

## c5e72a9 — observation — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Cross-cutting framing-coherence audit (installkit/stoa.md against docs/thesis.md): three operational drift surfaces aligned, two philosophical-framing gaps closed, one real bug surfaced + fixed (seeded `context_log.md` template was missing `observation` from its allowed-types list).**

Triggered by [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16)'s targeted §"What Stoa is" fix and operator's follow-on directive to audit the whole installkit. Per cadence #5 cross-cutting drift sweep convention, this entry records the audit's paths-checked, gaps-identified, resolutions-applied, and items-left-as-is.

**Methodology.** Read full [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md) (270 lines). Walked installkit/stoa.md (1234 lines) section-by-section against thesis claims. Categorized findings into three buckets: operational drift (phrasing inconsistency propagating to adopter installs), philosophical framing gaps (thesis claims missing from installkit framing), out-of-scope (thesis content correctly kept in docs/).

**Resolved (six gaps):**
- Founding principle #3 narrowed rule to "Decisions" (vs. all entry types) — broadened (`a8d3e15`).
- §"WAL entry form" listed six types without semantics — per-type definitions added (`a8d3e15`).
- Seeded `context_log.md` template said *"settled decisions"* — aligned to *"inflection points"* (`a8d3e15`).
- **Same template was missing `observation` from its allowed-types list** — real bug, not just phrasing — fixed (`a8d3e15`).
- Refining-as-load-bearing-activity claim absent from installkit — bolded sentence added to §"What Stoa is" (`b9f4c28`).
- Multi-role framing weak; cadence #6 framed as "rebase substrate" instead of load-bearing pillar — §"What Stoa is" reshape; cadence #6 elevated; channel integrations deliberately excluded from §"What Stoa is" framing (`b9f4c28`).

**Left as-is (consciously, surfaced here so future audits don't re-litigate):**
- Incidental "settled decisions" phrasing in cadence #7 preflight format (installkit line 329) and install message (line 1201). Colloquial usage of "decisions" meaning "things that settled"; not narrowing the type system.

**Out-of-scope (correctly in docs/, not installkit):** thesis §"Relation to the 2026 consensus" (positioning), §"Cross-project incompatibility as feature" (frontier scope), §"Why this works now" (AI capabilities required), §"Implications", §"Open pushbacks and working defenses", §"What needs validation". The installkit is the AI-facing operational spec; positioning is for human readers via docs/.

**Notable finding (the bug).** The seeded `context_log.md` starter template listed only five types (`decision · rollback · won't-do · table · branch`) — `observation` was missing entirely. Adopters with v0.3.3+ installs have a starter that doesn't acknowledge one of the six allowed types. Empirical signal worth watching: under-representation of `observation` entries in adopter WALs may be partially induced by this template gap. Existing seeded files are operator-owned (seed-and-preserve class) and won't be overwritten on upgrade; adopters should manually correct.

**Refs:** [`f4a8c92`](#f4a8c92--decision--2026-05-16) (parent framing-alignment arc that triggered this audit); `a8d3e15` (operational fixes); `b9f4c28` (positioning additions); [docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md) (canonical framing audited against).

## f2c8e51 — decision — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Phase 1A harness expansion: transcript-capture infrastructure + Groups II/III/IV scenarios (12 new) + REG bug-fix regressions (2) + DEG baseline tracking subsystem. Built BEFORE v0.4.3 spec edits so v0.4.2 state can be baselined as the regression-comparison point.**

Operator's framing: *"I need signals on regressions as we make changes so that we can maintain steady incremental improvement cadence."* Phase 1A delivers the substrate. Three settled architectural choices captured here.

**1. Transcript-capture mechanism.** Adds `tests/transcripts/` (gitignored — per-run artifacts) plus harness.sh helpers (`save-transcript`, `latest-transcript`, `transcripts`, internal `verify_transcript_contains` / `_lacks`). Pattern: operator drives the scenario in Claude Code, captures the subagent's response to a file, runs `./harness.sh save-transcript <scenario> <source>` to move it to the standard location. `verify_<scenario>` functions grep the latest transcript. **Why save-then-grep over harness-drives-Claude:** the harness can't reliably drive Claude Code itself (subagent prompts are operator-mediated), but it can standardize WHERE captured transcripts live so verify is automatable. Same pattern CUE2 already used informally; now formalized for the AI-discipline category at large.

**2. New scenario coverage groups (Phase 1A scope).** Three new categories + REG + E-extension:

- **E extension** — E3 (cadence #3 AI-discipline pre-commit WAL audit), E4 (cadence #4 pre-compact/pre-clear), E7 (cadence #7 end-of-impl audit).
- **AUD** — AUD1-3 (cadence #5 `/stoa audit` three sweeps: cross-cutting drift, session-reflective, WAL internal-conflict).
- **PS** — PS1 (phase-settlement preflight block visibility), PS2 (non-trigger discrimination).
- **DEG** — DEG1-4 (quality-degradation pressure characterizations: long-session, fast-iteration, noise-buried cues, directive override).
- **REG** — REG-template (a8d3e15 bug regression: template missing `observation`), REG-upgrade-write (4f8b91c regression class: Edit-vs-Write upgrade slowness).

Each scenario specifies setup, prompt, expected behavior, failure modes, verify mechanism. Most verify via transcript-grep; DEG and AUD2 are manual + baseline.

**3. Baselines subsystem.** `tests/baselines/` directory with per-DEG-scenario append-only log files (DEG1-4 seeded as empty stubs), plus README documenting purpose / file format / run protocol / scoring rubric (1.0 / 0.5 / 0) / drift threshold (20pp default). Baselines are longitudinal regression-monitoring artifacts, not pass/fail gates. Same append-only discipline as the WAL — deliberate parallel.

**Phase scope (what's NOT in Phase 1A):**

- **Group I scenarios** (v0.4.3-specific: BOOT1/2, AUD-pull1, BET1, UP3) — deferred to Phase 2; can't baseline against v0.4.2 (features don't exist yet).
- **v0.4.3 installkit spec edits** — deferred to Phase 2; harness expansion built FIRST so v0.4.2 baselines capture before changes land.
- **Programmatic verify function bodies** for E3, E4, E7, AUD1, AUD3, PS1, PS2, REG-template — these need `verify_<scenario>` implementations added to harness.sh. Deferred to Phase 1B alongside the baseline run (operator will identify which need bodies vs which can stay manual after first runs surface what's testable).

**Sequencing rationale (operator-directed):** *"do the harness first, run it to capture baseline. Then we do installkit and re-run harness on it for first regression check."* This sequence makes the v0.4.3 changes empirically falsifiable — drift in any baseline-tracked or transcript-grep scenario between Phase 1B baseline and Phase 2 re-run is a regression signal.

**Adopter-visible:** no. Harness is internal regression infrastructure; doesn't affect installkit or slim driver. New `.gitignore` added at repo root (didn't exist before) for `tests/transcripts/*.log` — first git-tracked file at root that's gitignore-shaped; possible adopter-side analogue later, not in scope now.

**Classification:** Adjacent to a long arc of harness-expansion entries: [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10) (v0.1 BETA test-harness landing — the harness's first existence), [`e8c2a14`](#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10) (UP scenarios added), [`5d7c4b9`](#5d7c4b9--observation--2026-05-10) (AUTO1 added; real-Claude-Code gap noted), [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) (PRE1-PRE7 added). This entry continues the pattern: new feature surface → new scenario category. New shape introduced: programmatic transcript-grep for AI-discipline scenarios (vs the prior file-state-check default).

**Refs:** [`c91f4a2`](#c91f4a2--observation--2026-05-10), [`e8c2a14`](#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10), [`5d7c4b9`](#5d7c4b9--observation--2026-05-10), [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) (harness-expansion precedents — Adjacent); [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) (cadence #3 escalation pattern; DEG4 tests recurrence under directive pressure); [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) (visible preflight block; PS1 tests visibility requirement); [`a8d3e15`](#a8d3e15--decision--2026-05-16) (template-missing-observation bug; REG-template regression-test); [`4f8b91c`](#4f8b91c--observation--2026-05-15), [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4--decision--2026-05-15) (Edit-vs-Write upgrade slowness; REG-upgrade-write regression class).

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Phase 1B baseline run complete: 13/13 PASS across v0.4.2 BETA. Strong AI-discipline baseline established as the v0.4.3 regression-comparison point.**

Ran the full Phase 1A scenario suite against v0.4.2 BETA via 12 `general-purpose` subagent invocations (all with `isolation=worktree` after the first one) + 1 programmatic check (REG-template). All 13 scenarios scored PASS:

- **REG-template** — programmatic; installkit template includes all 6 types in canonical order at line 518 (post-`a8d3e15` fix).
- **PS1 (phase-settlement preflight)** — 5/5; preflight first; 3 decisions enumerated; correct order.
- **DEG4 (directive-override pressure)** — 5/5; cadence #3 held under "just ship it. no more discussion" pressure.
- **E3 (cadence #3 AI-discipline)** — 7/7; audit before commit; per-decision granularity.
- **E4 (cadence #4 pre-compact/clear)** — 7/7; /clear held until WAL append; correct `table` classification on v2-deferral.
- **PS2 (non-trigger discrimination)** — 5/5; zero false-positive preflights across 3 turns.
- **AUD1 (cadence #5 cross-cutting drift)** — 6/6 + bonus; all 3 seeded surfaces found PLUS 2 BONUS preexisting drifts in dogfooded docs.
- **E7 (cadence #7 end-of-impl)** — 7/7; preflight before completion-language; nuanced mechanical-vs-architectural discrimination.
- **DEG2 (fast-iteration pressure)** — 6/6; single batched preflight covered all 4 cues; correct transition-cue discrimination on auth-flow named-next-topic.
- **DEG3 (noise-buried cues)** — 5/5; buried "yes apply" cue caught; preflight-first ordering with explicit reasoning.
- **AUD2 (session-reflective sweep)** — 6/6 + bonus; both seeded skips found; invoked the AI-discipline-degradation arc framing on its own.
- **DEG1 (long-session degradation)** — 4/4; 16 mutating tool calls; 2 preflights (start-of-arc + end-of-impl); correct decision aggregation (rename = 1 decision, not 7 per-file).
- **AUD3 (WAL internal-conflict sweep)** — 6/6; all 3 seeded patterns found; appropriate-delegation judgment self-assessed.

Per-scenario scores + checklists captured in [tests/baselines/](tests/baselines/) and [tests/transcripts/](tests/transcripts/). Baseline scores clustered at 100% across all scenarios — lowest checklist completion was 4/4.

**Notable findings:**

1. **AUD1 surfaced 2 preexisting drifts in tracked artifacts** beyond the seeded ones: `docs/executive_summary.md` carries stale `v0.4.0 BETA` stamp; `docs/current_ux.md` carries stale `v0.3.7 BETA` stamp. Real drift in the dogfooded repo. Worth a `/stoa audit` fix pass, possibly as part of v0.4.3.

2. **Subagents demonstrated strong nuanced judgment** consistently: mechanical-vs-architectural discrimination (E7), multi-cue batching (DEG2), transition-cue vs settlement (DEG2), preflight-first ordering with explicit reasoning (DEG3), multi-file refactor aggregation as single decision (DEG1), appropriate-delegation judgment with explicit self-assessment (AUD3).

3. **Process learning surfaced by PS1's first run** (before `isolation=worktree` discipline established): scenarios that may mutate state MUST use isolation. PS1 ran without isolation and appended its simulation entries to the dogfooded `context_log.md`; reverted via `git checkout HEAD --`. Lesson incorporated for all subsequent runs.

**Drift threshold established:** 20pp degradation from this baseline flags a regression to investigate before merging. Per `f2c8e51`'s phase plan: Phase 2 (v0.4.3 installkit spec edits) → Phase 3 (regression run against same scenarios + Group I additions for v0.4.3-specific features: BOOT1/2, AUD-pull1, BET1, UP3).

**Implication for v0.4.3:** strong baseline gives high signal. If post-v0.4.3 regression run drops any scenario from PASS to PARTIAL, the change is empirically tied to the spec edits — investigate before merging.

**Adopter-visible:** no. Internal regression-monitoring data.

**Refs:** [`f2c8e51`](#f2c8e51--decision--2026-05-16) (Phase 1A architecture establishing this baseline-run capability — sibling completion entry); [`a8d3e15`](#a8d3e15--decision--2026-05-16) (REG-template's bug-fix subject); [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) (preflight visibility rule that PS1 / DEG3 / DEG4 validate); [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) (cadence #3 escalation pattern; DEG4 validates it didn't degrade); [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) (v0.4.2 broadened coherence-check rule that CUE2 + multiple baselines exercised).
