## e5d8c63 — observation — 2026-05-16

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Installkit fence convention: embedded blocks with markdown content (potentially nested 3-backtick code blocks) MUST use 4-backtick outer fence. Discovered during v0.4.3 /stoa upgrade regeneration; fixed by promoting the dispatcher block's outer fence from 3-backtick to 4-backtick.**

During the v0.4.3 dogfooded upgrade regeneration (the Step 3 / Step 6 work that follows `d4e8f31`), a fence-aware Python extractor walked `installkit/stoa.md`'s embedded blocks to write each artifact (dispatcher, hooks, bootcheck) to its live path. The dispatcher block's outer fence was 3-backtick (`\`\`\`markdown`), and the dispatcher's help-text content contained nested 3-backtick code blocks (sample output strings). CommonMark closes a 3-backtick fence on the first matching 3-backtick line — so the extractor captured only 12 lines of dispatcher content before the first nested fence closed the outer one.

**Fix.** Promoted the dispatcher block's outer fence from `\`\`\`markdown` to `\`\`\`\`markdown` (4 backticks), and the closing fence to match. Added a `> **Spec-owned.**` description blockquote above the fence noting the 4-backtick convention.

**General principle (new):** **Embedded blocks whose content is markdown** (with potentially nested 3-backtick code blocks) **MUST use 4-backtick outer fence.** Embedded blocks whose content is **non-markdown code** (bash scripts, templates, configs) can use 3-backtick outer fence safely — shell and template content doesn't contain nested fences.

Bootcheck ([`b4e8f29`](#b4e8f29--decision--2026-05-16)) already used 4-backtick fence; this entry generalizes that pattern to all markdown-content blocks. Future embedded markdown-content artifacts inherit by default.

**Why latent until v0.4.3.** Pre-v0.4.3, the dispatcher was operator-extracted via visual Read + Write (per the upgrade flow's Step 3 instruction). Human extraction visually disambiguates the outer fence from inner fences. The malformed-markdown nesting was invisible until programmatic extraction surfaced it.

**Adopter-visible:** indirectly. Adopters running `/stoa upgrade` continue using AI-driven Read + Write (which can handle the 4-backtick fence). The Step 3 wording in the dispatcher already says "Read the canonical install kit's #### path: ... block ... overwrite the local file" — operator-or-AI driven, both work post-fix.

**Refs:** [`b4e8f29`](#b4e8f29--decision--2026-05-16) (introduced bootcheck artifact with 4-backtick fence — the pattern this entry generalizes); [`d4e8f31`](#d4e8f31--observation--2026-05-16) (Phase 2 milestone where the bug surfaced during regen).

|---|---|---|---|

## d7c4e92 — observation — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**BOOT1/BOOT2 validated via `claude -p` sub-process pattern (deferral in [`b7a3f81`](#b7a3f81--observation--2026-05-16) lifted). Bootcheck subagent fires as the first tool call in a fresh main-agent session on all three return paths (clean, hook-not-active, version-mismatch); canonical `[stoa]` lines surface verbatim from the main agent. Two minor compliance deviations captured as beta-tracker candidate `e3b8a47`.**

**Why the deferral was lifted.** [`b7a3f81`](#b7a3f81--observation--2026-05-16) deferred BOOT1/BOOT2 because general-purpose subagents lack the `Agent` tool — they can't invoke `stoa-bootcheck` so they can't validate Agent-tool-invocation discipline. The unlock: `claude -p --output-format stream-json` spawns a fresh main-agent sub-process with full tool surface. Worktree-isolated, parseable, model-cheap (haiku is sufficient for discipline-rule validation).

**Method.**
- Worktree per scenario: `git worktree add /tmp/stoa-bootN HEAD`. BOOT2's worktree seeds `.stoa/installed` line 1 to `v0.4.2` (artificial mismatch against H1 `v0.4.3`).
- Sub-claude: `claude -p --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose --model haiku --permission-mode bypassPermissions "hello, what files are in this directory?"` → `/tmp/bootN.jsonl`.
- Parsed via `jq` for first `tool_use` event from `assistant` messages; verified `Agent` with `subagent_type=stoa-bootcheck` as first call; parsed `text` content for surfaced `[stoa]` lines.

**Results.**

| Run | First tool call | Bootcheck return | Main agent surface | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOOT1 (initial — worktree inherits parent's `core.hooksPath`) | `Agent(stoa-bootcheck)` | `[stoa] WAL-audit hook is not active in this clone. core.hooksPath is set to ".../.git/hooks" instead of ".githooks". To activate: git config core.hooksPath .githooks. AI-discipline (cadence #3) is the floor until you run it.` | Verbatim relay before answering operator | PASS |
| BOOT1 (clean — `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` set in worktree) | `Agent(stoa-bootcheck)` | `All checks pass.\n\nclean` | Pre-bootcheck narration ("I need to run the session boot check first"); no findings surfaced (clean path is silent) | PASS |
| BOOT2 (marker seeded `v0.4.2`; H1 `v0.4.3 BETA`) | `Agent(stoa-bootcheck)` | `[stoa] stoa.md is v0.4.3 BETA but the installed marker says v0.4.2. Looks like you pulled a newer stoa.md. Run /stoa upgrade to apply.` | Verbatim relay before answering operator | PASS |

**What this validates.**
- The bootcheck subagent fires as the FIRST tool call in a fresh main-agent session — covered all three return paths.
- Main agent relays bootcheck findings verbatim before engaging the operator's message (on non-clean paths).
- On the clean path, main agent proceeds silently to the operator's message (no findings to surface).

**Harness implication.** `claude -p` sub-process is viable for any future Agent-tool-invocation acceptance test (BOOT, future AUD-pull, others). A `harness.sh run-boot <scenario>` command codifying the worktree → seed → claude-p → jq-parse pattern is a candidate addition for v0.4.4 — defer for now.

**Compliance deviations noted (filed as beta-tracker `e3b8a47`):**
1. Bootcheck subagent prepends "All checks pass." to `clean` and augments hook-not-active line with extra diagnostic. Subagent spec says "Nothing else. No explanatory prose." — violated.
2. Version-mismatch line uses full H1 `v0.4.3 BETA` rather than bare version `v0.4.3`. Template `v<local>` ambiguous; subagent grabbed H1 as-is.

**Adopter-visible:** no — internal validation.

**Refs:** [`b7a3f81`](#b7a3f81--observation--2026-05-16) (Phase 3 deferral now lifted by this entry); [`b4e8f29`](#b4e8f29--decision--2026-05-16) (bootcheck subagent — this validates its end-to-end behavior); [`f2c8e51`](#f2c8e51--decision--2026-05-16) (Phase 1A regression-testing architecture — `claude -p` extends it to sub-process scenarios).

## 7e9c4a3 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Vector index as primary substrate for WAL semantic operations; two-layer architecture (vectors primary, headline-grep fallback). Adopts jina-embeddings-v2-base-en + sqlite-vec; index local/gitignored; `/stoa query` CLI exposes retrieval; AI prefers index when present, falls back gracefully when absent.**

Stoa's coherence cadences make semantic-similarity operations load-bearing — cadence #6 M×N pairwise audit, cadence #5 internal-conflict sweep, v0.4.2 broadened coherence check, post-decision propagation, WAL access pattern non-trivial queries. At single-operator small-WAL scale these work via lexical grep + LLM reasoning over full WAL. At the planning-horizon scale (cross-repo, 10-100 contributors, multi-year — see Refs below for the empirical analysis), three failures emerge: (1) WAL exceeds subagent context budget so full reads stop working; (2) terminology drifts across contributors so lexical match misses semantic equivalents; (3) cadence #6 LLM-pairwise becomes infeasible at M×N scale.

**Architecture.** Two layers:

- **Primary**: vector index. Local SQLite + sqlite-vec keyed on entry hex. Embeddings from `jina-embeddings-v2-base-en` (137MB, 8192-token context fits full entries without chunking, 768-dim, MTEB retrieval ~60). `/stoa query` is the AI's invocation surface; returns top-k=10 hex IDs + scores; AI must Read entry bodies before reasoning (audit transparency preserved).
- **Fallback**: headline-grep. `grep -A 3 '^## ' context_log.md` produces a metadata view; subagent reasons over it. Used when index is missing, corrupt, or fresh-cloned-before-install. No degradation in WAL access — Stoa works without the index, just slower at scale.

**Storage.** Index at `.stoa/index/wal_index.sqlite`. Gitignored, never committed. WAL stays canonical; index is derived state, rebuildable from the WAL at any time. Per-operator local; no shared mutable state.

**Model opinion is hidden.** No operator UX for model selection. Future swaps push via `/stoa upgrade`. Reduces UX surface area; one less moving part for AI or operator to mismanage.

**Why jina-v2-base-en specifically.** Long context (8192 tokens) lets full WAL entries embed without chunking — critical for cadence #6's pairwise comparison quality. Small footprint (137MB) keeps install reasonable. MTEB retrieval scores adequate for Stoa's corpus shape. Apache-2.0 license clean for redistribution.

**Empirical validation precedes lock-in.** First implementation task is a spike: embed this repo's 149-entry WAL + acme-platform's 42-entry WAL with jina-v2-base-en; run hand-labeled retrieval and pairwise tests; measure precision@5/10 and pairwise-threshold separation. If jina underperforms, fall back to bge-base-en-v1.5 with per-entry chunking.

**Coherence-check findings (v0.4.2 broadened rule):**

- **Converging** with [`e7c4b29`](#e7c4b29) (scalability mitigation menu — RAG / index was option 5, deferred to v0.3+ pending beta data). Now committing pre-beta-data because the planning-horizon (cross-repo + 10-100 contributors) makes the structural mitigation load-bearing regardless of small-team beta evidence. Original observation stays accurate as a historical capture of the cliff thresholds.
- **Converging via different reasoning** with [`f3a8d61`](#f3a8d61) (bet: compaction + AI context growth obviates structural mitigations). The bet's premise was per-project; vectors are required for cross-repo + multi-contributor scale, which the bet didn't cover. Bet stays active for small single-repo projects; vectors are insurance for the scaled case. Not a rollback.
- **Adjacent** to [`7c2f9b4`](#7c2f9b4) (two-tier WAL — full + working). Independent mechanism; vectors could index the full WAL while a future two-tier compactor handles a different concern.
- **Adjacent** to [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9) (v0.4.2 broadened coherence check) — vectors are the substrate that makes the broadened rule scale.

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next `/stoa upgrade` to the vector-enabled version. Adds Python dependency (see [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92)). No behavior change for operators below the lexical-grep cliff.

**Refs:** [`e7c4b29`](#e7c4b29), [`f3a8d61`](#f3a8d61), [`7c2f9b4`](#7c2f9b4), [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9); sibling batch entries [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8), [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4).

## 2f8b6d1 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Multi-layer index update lifecycle: post-commit hook (primary, non-gating) + lazy-on-query refresh + 4th `/stoa audit` sweep (auto-fix + conditional beta-tracker) + dispatcher-level staleness refusal (file-out-of-date pattern) + pre-commit hook extension for stash-pop gap + bootcheck info-surface on substantial lag. SQLite WAL-mode for parallel-session snapshot isolation.**

Index is derived state from the WAL; the lifecycle keeps it consistent across the operator workflows Stoa supports (commit, pull, stash-pop, parallel sessions, fresh clone, manual reset). Multi-layer defense by design — non-determinism in operator workflow warrants overlapping coverage. Each layer is idempotent (set-diff-based; re-embedding a hex is a no-op overwrite).

**Layers:**

1. **Post-commit hook (primary).** `.githooks/post-commit` invokes the embed script on new entries since last hook fire. Non-gating: hook failure doesn't block the commit; staleness is detectable and self-heals via other layers.
2. **`/stoa pull` step 4 (pre-merge).** Before cadence #6's M×N pairwise check, embed upstream-new entries into local index. Gating: cadence #6 can't run pairwise without the embeddings. Workflow-gated, not hook-gated.
3. **Lazy on `/stoa query`.** Health probe before query; if index lags WAL, refresh inline (small lag) or surface estimate + refresh (large lag). Catches anything other layers missed.
4. **`/stoa audit` index-coherency sweep (4th sweep).** Operator-triggered backstop. Set-diff `WAL hexes - index hexes`; embed missing with progress (every 10th); classify cause. If methodology gap (post-commit hook should have fired on commit X but didn't), propose beta-tracker entry. If operator-action divergence (reset, branch switch, fresh clone), silent fix.
5. **Dispatcher-level staleness refusal.** `/stoa query` / `/stoa audit` / `/stoa pull` check `.stoa/index/audit-state` against `git log --merges HEAD ^<last-audited>`. If unaudited merges in history AND uncommitted WAL appends staged → refuse with message routing operator to `/stoa audit` internal-conflict sweep. File-out-of-date pattern — closes the stash-pop gap where cadence #6 ran on pulled entries but not on stashed-then-popped local appends.
6. **Pre-commit hook extension.** Same staleness check at commit time; deterministic gate as backup to the dispatcher-level check.
7. **Bootcheck (info-only).** Silent on missing/stale-by-small; one info line on substantial lag (>50 entries) for operator visibility. No `[stoa]` suggestions for action.

**Parallel-session safety.** SQLite WAL-mode (`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`) gives readers snapshot isolation during concurrent writes. Two sessions running `/stoa audit` simultaneously converge to consistent state via INSERT-OR-REPLACE on hex primary key. Embedding work happens outside the transaction; only INSERTs serialize.

**Bootcheck remains read-only.** Steps 5/6 above are added to dispatcher subcommands and the pre-commit hook, not bootcheck. Bootcheck retains its read-only invariant.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Adjacent** to [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18) (original cadence #3 pre-commit hook decision). Extends the existing pre-commit hook with the staleness check; doesn't supersede.
- **Adjacent** to [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04) (v0.2.0 cut: pure-bash hooks + `core.hooksPath`). New post-commit hook follows the same pattern: spec-owned `.githooks/post-commit`, installed by install kit, refreshed by `/stoa upgrade`.
- **Adjacent** to [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2) (cadence #6 spec). Adds the `.stoa/index/audit-state` marker that cadence #6 maintains; cadence #6 spec needs a one-line addition: *"on successful pairwise check + pull, write last-audited-merge to `.stoa/index/audit-state`."*
- **Adjacent** to [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3) (vector architecture this lifecycle maintains).

**Adopter-visible:** yes on `/stoa upgrade`. New `.githooks/post-commit`. Existing pre-commit hook gains the staleness check. Dispatcher subcommands gain pre-flight check.

**Refs:** [`c2a6d18`](#c2a6d18), [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04), [`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2), [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3); sibling batch entries [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8), [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4).

## a5e3c92 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Python 3.9+ runtime + sentence-transformers + sqlite-vec required as Stoa baseline dependency. Auto-installed at install-kit first-run and on `/stoa upgrade` to vector-enabled version; failure mode is fail-loud per beta-required stance. Departure from prior "no new tooling" stance, justified by cross-repo + 10-100-contributor scale.**

This is a real expansion of Stoa's install footprint. Pre-vector, Stoa was shell + markdown + git hooks (~standard everywhere). Post-vector, Stoa adds Python 3.9+ + a venv at `.stoa/index/venv/` + ~150-200MB of disk (PyTorch + sentence-transformers + jina-v2-base-en model). The departure is intentional and bounded.

**Why this is acceptable given Stoa's "no new tooling" principle.** [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04) revisited the principle when adding git hooks: *"AI-as-interpreter, not new tooling" — where "new tooling" meant per-project scripts and validators that engineers route around. A git hook is standard git mechanism that every git user already has, not new tooling.* Python doesn't have that out — Python IS new tooling at the Stoa level. We're accepting it on different grounds: the value (semantic operations at multi-contributor scale) is load-bearing for Stoa's coherence promises, and there's no cheaper mechanical substrate for those operations (see [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3)'s analysis of alternatives).

**Concrete shape:**

- **Install kit first-run installs the index substrate.** New Step N in `installkit/stoa.md`: create `.stoa/index/venv` → `pip install sentence-transformers sqlite-vec` → download `jina-embeddings-v2-base-en` to shared cache → initial embed pass over current WAL. Fail-loud on any step: rollback, surface actionable error, do not partial-install.
- **Shared model cache** at `~/.cache/stoa/models/` (single download per operator; reused across all Stoa projects on the same machine). Industry-standard practice.
- **Apple Silicon: PyTorch MPS auto-detect**. `device=None` in sentence-transformers picks best available (MPS on macOS Apple Silicon, CUDA on Linux GPU, CPU otherwise). No platform-conditional install logic.
- **Python version floor: 3.9.** macOS Sequoia ships 3.9.6 by default; conservative floor. Adopters with older Python 3.x are rare; new install pip installs sentence-transformers which requires this floor anyway.
- **Model swap is via `/stoa upgrade` only.** No operator-level UX surface for swapping. Reduces decision space; future Stoa version can introduce a swap if needed.
- **Pin model in `.stoa/index/config.toml`** (hidden default, no operator-facing UX). On version mismatch at bootcheck, surface staleness; on `/stoa upgrade`, re-embed if pinned model changed.

**Initial-install cost transparency.** For WALs >500 entries, install prints estimate banner before embed pass: *"Embedding N entries; estimated ~X min on Apple Silicon MPS, ~Y min on Linux CPU. Progress every 50 entries."* No background option; install is synchronous; cost is one-time per adopter per repo.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Adjacent** to [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04) (the v0.2.0 hook decision that revisited "no new tooling"). This entry extends that revisit: standard-git-mechanism was the prior carve-out; Python is a stronger departure but justified on cadence-#6-feasibility-at-scale grounds.
- **Converging** with [`e7c4b29`](#e7c4b29) (RAG = mitigation #5 in the menu). The infrastructure-cost concern the original entry flagged is real; we're accepting it.
- **Adjacent** to [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3) (the architecture this dependency serves).

**Adopter-visible:** yes on `/stoa upgrade`. New disk footprint; install time scales with WAL size. Adopters without Python 3.9+ available will see fail-loud at upgrade time with a clear install instruction.

**Refs:** [`b7e2f04`](#b7e2f04), [`e7c4b29`](#e7c4b29), [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3); sibling batch entries [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8), [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4).

## 4d7f1a8 — table — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Rollover/SEAL WAL-split protocol deferred pending vector-index sufficiency assessment. Three motivations for rollover (AI context pollution, multi-author merge, long-term file size) reduce to one once vectors land: operator-UX-only (editor lag, diff noise, GitHub web view). Much weaker driver. Revisit if operator-UX pain materializes empirically.**

The three problems rollover would address are independent:

| Problem | Status |
|---|---|
| AI context pollution at WAL scale | Solved by vector index ([`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3)) |
| Multi-author append concurrency | Solved by cadence #6 + `merge=union` ([`7c4b9d2`](#7c4b9d2)) |
| Long-term file size (editor / diff / web-view UX) | Deferred — this entry |

With the vector index in place, the only remaining motivation for rollover is operator-experience: large `context_log.md` is slow in editors, noisy in diffs, painful on GitHub's web rendering. These are real concerns at long-horizon scale, but materially weaker than the AI-context concern that originally motivated the design exploration.

**Design sketch preserved** (revisit when needed):

- **SEAL entry type**: appending `SEAL` to the current log marks the rollover point. Same commit creates the new log file (e.g., `context_log_<seq>.md`) with a back-pointer entry referencing the SEAL via hex ID.
- **Seal is a coordinated single-operator operation.** Pull → verify no upstream seal → seal-commit → push immediately. Concurrent seals across operators fail at push time; loser rolls back their seal.
- **Numeric vs hash naming**: numeric (`context_log_00001.md`) is human-friendly but collision-prone; hash-based (`context_log_<seal-hex>.md`) is collision-free. Numeric + coordinated seal is the leaning, deferred for confirmation.
- **Cadence #6 redirect-on-rebase is the load-bearing complexity.** When operator pulls after upstream seal, their local appends to old `context_log.md` need to retarget to the new active log. Modifying git history during pull is delicate; needs careful test fixtures.
- **Index rebuild on rollover**: changes file pointers; full re-embed or hex-keyed incremental migration. Mechanism deferred.

**Tabled, not won't-do.** Stoa's planning horizon includes adopters with multi-year WALs; at 39K+ entries the operator-UX concerns become real. This entry holds the place; the design is recoverable when needed. The trigger to revisit: empirical operator complaints about editor / diff / web-view pain at WAL sizes Stoa adopters actually reach.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Adjacent** to [`e7c4b29`](#e7c4b29) (mitigation menu, option #3 "log-splitting"). This entry tables that option while taking option #5 (RAG/index) via [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3).
- **Adjacent** to [`7c2f9b4`](#7c2f9b4) (two-tier WAL). Independent mechanism; could compose with rollover if both eventually needed (two-tier handles working-vs-full; rollover handles file-size-of-full).

**Adopter-visible:** no behavior change. Design captured for future revisit.

## 9b2c8e4 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**§"Granularity guidance" added to `installkit/stoa.md` §"WAL entry form (canonical)". Lifts the per-decision-granularity principle from the phase-settlement-trigger procedure (where it currently lives) to discoverable guidance applicable to every WAL entry.**

The principle "write entries at the granularity at which you might want to roll back later" exists in the spec but is buried in the phase-settlement-trigger procedure (slim driver line 81: *"Per-decision (not one summary entry) — preserves rollback granularity"*). The location makes it look like a phase-settlement-specific rule; in practice it applies to every entry decision.

**Lifting it to a top-level subsection** under §"WAL entry form (canonical)" makes it discoverable in the natural location (where the AI is reading about how to shape an entry).

**Proposed text** (subsection added between §"Body content guidance" and §"Example"):

````markdown
### Granularity guidance

Write entries at the granularity at which you might want to roll back later.
A phase that settles 4 decisions appends 4 entries, not 1 summary — each
independently rollbackable via its own ID. The cost of an extra entry is
small; bundling decisions you later want to separate is irreversible (no
partial rollback).

When in doubt, split.
````

Three lines of guidance; same loose-framework feel as existing guidance.

**Why not a 4th founding principle.** Founding principles are constitutive (Stoa can't exist without them). Granularity is derived — it's how you use principle #3 effectively. Adding a 4th would dilute the original three.

**This batch demonstrates the principle.** Entries [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3), [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8), [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4) are 5 per-decision entries from one refining-phase settlement, not 1 summary. Each is independently rollbackable.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Converging** with [`9a4d72e`](#9a4d72e) (phase-settlement append shape: batch of per-decision entries, not one summary). Same principle; we're moving it from procedure-specific to general guidance. Original entry stays accurate; new section lifts the principle to a more discoverable location.
- **Converging** with the early pre-canonical-hex entry on granularity (*"one entry per settled point; never split a settled outcome into multiple entries just because the conversation arrived at it across several turns"*). Same principle from the other direction — don't over-fragment one outcome. Together, the two arcs say: match entry-to-decision 1:1.

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next `/stoa upgrade`. Spec text only; no behavior change.

**Refs:** [`9a4d72e`](#9a4d72e); sibling batch entries [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3), [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8).

## c4f9e87 — observation — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Empirical spike: BGE-base-en-v1.5 outperforms jina-embeddings-v2-base-en on Stoa's 147-entry WAL across retrieval (P@5 +15%, R@10 +3%) and pairwise discrimination (cleaner separation range), at ~5x lower encode latency on Apple Silicon MPS. Switching the spec's model recommendation from jina to BGE. 512-token truncation does not hurt quality — front-loaded entry structure (bolded headlines + first body paragraph) carries the discriminative signal; chunking not needed.**

**Spike methodology.** Hand-labeled retrieval test set: 8 natural-language queries with expected hex IDs (5 expected hits typical, range 2-5). Hand-labeled pairwise test set: 13 pairs (8 known-related, 5 known-unrelated). Same test set against both models. Measured P@5 / P@10 / R@10 for retrieval; cosine-similarity distributions for pairwise. Both models loaded via `sentence-transformers` on PyTorch MPS (Apple Silicon M-series).

**Numerical comparison (Stoa WAL, 147 entries):**

| Metric | jina-v2-base-en | bge-base-en-v1.5 |
|---|---|---|
| Retrieval Mean P@5 | 0.325 | 0.375 |
| Retrieval Mean P@10 | 0.225 | 0.225 |
| Retrieval Mean R@10 | 0.756 | 0.777 |
| Pairwise related mean | 0.941 | 0.851 |
| Pairwise unrelated mean | 0.886 | 0.767 |
| Pairwise separation gap | 0.016 (0.907→0.923) | 0.018 (0.796→0.814) |
| Suggested pairwise threshold | 0.915 | 0.805 |
| Encode latency (MPS) | 148ms/entry | 29ms/entry |
| Model size | 137MB | 440MB |
| Context window | 8192 tokens | 512 tokens |
| Custom code | yes (trust_remote_code) | no |
| transformers compat | needs `<4.50` pin | works on current |

**Operationally significant findings:**

1. **jina-v2 install fragility.** Required pinning `transformers<4.50` to load — jina's custom code imports `transformers.onnx` which was removed in transformers 4.50+. Real-world adoption hazard: adopters with pre-installed newer transformers (common in ML environments) would hit this immediately.
2. **Sibling-recall failure (jina).** Query 7 ("Vector index over the WAL — what's the architecture?") expected both `7e9c4a3` and `2f8b6d1` (just-appended siblings in the same design batch). jina ranked `7e9c4a3` #1 but missed `2f8b6d1` from top-10 entirely. BGE surfaced both. The cadence-#6 use case (find related arcs to a candidate entry) needs sibling-recall to work.
3. **Truncation is not a quality loss.** BGE's 512-token cap means each entry sees only its first ~512 tokens; jina's 8192 cap means full bodies. Yet BGE outperforms jina on retrieval. Empirical confirmation that Stoa's bolded-headline + first-paragraph convention front-loads the discriminative signal; tail content is elaboration, not differentiation. **Chunking not needed.**
4. **MPS speedup is real.** ~5x latency improvement on Apple Silicon — meaningful for adopter install on existing WALs (10K-entry install drops from ~25 min to ~5 min). Both models use MPS auto-detect via `sentence-transformers`.

**Why this is observation, not rollback against [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3).** The architecture decision (vector index as primary substrate; two-layer with headline-grep fallback) stands unchanged. The model parameter inside that decision shifts. Per granularity guidance ([`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4)), if model choice had been a separate entry, we'd rollback; bundled with the architecture entry, this observation records the parameter refinement and the implementation will pin BGE in `.stoa/index/config.toml`. **Reading the architecture entry later, future readers should follow the Refs to find this empirical addendum.**

**Operational implications for implementation:**

- Spec change: `jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-base-en` → `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` everywhere [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3)'s body mentions it. Historical record (the original entry text) stays per append-only discipline.
- Default pairwise threshold for cadence #6: `0.805` (was `0.915` if jina had been kept). Recorded as starting point; empirical tuning during real cadence #6 runs against multi-author scenarios.
- Truncation at 512 tokens is intentional, not a limitation. Document in implementation: "BGE sees first ~512 tokens per entry; Stoa's bolded headlines and front-loaded prose are the discriminative substrate by design."
- Install footprint: 440MB model vs 137MB — accepted given quality + speed wins; remains within reasonable Stoa-baseline footprint (~600MB total with venv + deps).
- Install procedure: no `trust_remote_code` argument; vanilla `SentenceTransformer("BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5")` call.

**Falsifiability bounds.** Single-corpus result (Stoa methodology repo, 147 entries). May not generalize to all adopter WALs — different writing styles, different terminology density, different entry-size distributions. **Re-run the spike on acme-platform WAL + first 1-2 external adopter WALs** once they ramp; if BGE underperforms in those contexts, reassess (likely fallback: bge-large-en-v1.5 or mxbai-embed-large-v1, accepting larger footprint).

**Test artifacts.** Spike scripts at `/tmp/stoa-vector-spike/spike.py` + `spike_bge.py`; venv at `/tmp/stoa-vector-spike/venv/`. Throwaway location; not part of repo. If we want to re-run periodically, the test set should land in `tests/` as a baseline scenario.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Adjacent (partial parameter supersession)** with [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3). Architecture stands; model parameter refined empirically. Architecture entry stays the canonical reference; this entry is the parameter-refinement addendum.
- **Adjacent** with [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92) (Python dep). Dependency story unchanged; only the model artifact pulled by sentence-transformers shifts. Slight footprint increase (137MB → 440MB).
- **Adjacent** with [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4) (granularity guidance). This case illustrates the principle's value: bundled decisions are harder to surgically update post-hoc; observation entries are the workaround when bundling was suboptimal in retrospect.
- **Adjacent** with [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1) (update lifecycle). Lifecycle is model-agnostic; no changes.

**Adopter-visible:** yes when implementation ships. Spec text changes; install downloads a different model file. Behavior equivalent or better.

**Refs:** [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`9b2c8e4`](#9b2c8e4), [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1).

## d6e8a37 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Cross-version upgrade automation: new install-kit Step 8 (post-`/stoa upgrade` catchup). Closes the gap where older dispatcher Step 3 lists miss spec-owned files added in newer versions. AI-instruction at root; visible `[stoa-upgrade-catchup]` discipline block; per-version explicit file enumeration; idempotent. Lives in install kit (stripped after upgrade); zero per-session cost.**

The v0.4.3 → v0.5.0 transition surfaced an upgrade-flow gap. v0.4.3's local dispatcher hardcodes a 3-file refresh list in `/stoa upgrade` Step 3. v0.5.0 introduces 5 new spec-owned files: `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` (pre-existing v0.4.3+ gap — never made it into v0.4.3's hardcoded list), `.githooks/post-commit`, `.stoa/index/embed.py`, `.stoa/index/query.py`, `.stoa/index/.gitignore` (all v0.5+ per [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3) / [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92) / [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1)). When a v0.4.3 adopter runs `/stoa upgrade` to land v0.5.0, the v0.4.3 procedure refreshes only the 3 files it knows about; the 5 new ones stay stale or absent. Adopters would otherwise need to either run `/stoa upgrade` twice or do a fresh install per [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01) convention — neither ideal.

**Mechanism.** New `## First-run install kit` Step 8 — Cross-version catchup (post-upgrade gap closure). The AI loads the full pre-strip stoa.md at session start (before Step 6's self-strip removes the install kit). After `/stoa upgrade` Steps 1-7 complete (using OLD local dispatcher), the AI continues into Step 8 from its cached install-kit content.

**Procedure (per release; v0.5.0 enumeration in installkit/stoa.md Step 8):**

1. Enumerate the new-version spec-owned-file set explicitly (8 files as of v0.5.0).
2. For each: verify presence + content match against canonical `#### path:` block in the pre-strip stoa.md (still in AI session context).
3. Refresh marked files via Write (per [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4) Write-not-Edit discipline).
4. If `.stoa/index/venv/` doesn't exist post-refresh: invoke `/stoa index install` (Step 5's Vector index sub-section).
5. Surface result to operator as `[stoa] Cross-version catchup complete: refreshed N files; vector index <state>.`

**Visible discipline.** Before executing, AI emits `[stoa-upgrade-catchup]` block (mirrors [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4) `[stoa-upgrade-strip]` pattern) showing what's being checked + action. Operator can verify; missing block signals AI skipped Step 8.

**Idempotency.** Step 8 is safe to re-run — file refresh overwrites with canonical content (no-diff = no-op); `/stoa index install` skips completed steps. If interrupted mid-run, re-running completes the remaining work.

**Per-version explicit enumeration vs. self-discovering Step 3.** Chose explicit enumeration over making Step 3 dynamically discover spec-owned blocks from the install kit. Self-discovery would future-proof but requires more parsing logic in AI-instruction prose AND only helps v0.5+ → future (since v0.4.3's local dispatcher already lacks the self-discovery logic, the immediate v0.4.3 → v0.5.0 transition still needs catchup regardless). Explicit enumeration is simpler to write/verify per release; each release adds to its own Step 8 list. Self-discovering Step 3 reserved for v0.6+ if empirical data shows per-version maintenance becomes repetitive.

**Reconciliation with [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01).** v0.4.3's [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01) dropped backward-compat hedges from the SLIM DRIVER (per-session context bloat). Step 8 is a backward-compat MECHANISM but lives in the INSTALL KIT — stripped from stoa.md after Step 6's self-strip; loaded only when adopters fresh-pull stoa.md. No ongoing per-session cost; different trade than the slim-driver bloat [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01) rejected. Consistent with the procedure-in-dispatcher / install-kit-only / slim-driver-lean principles.

**Reuses [`c91b07e`](#c91b07e) spec-owned/seed-and-preserve taxonomy.** Step 8 only refreshes SPEC-OWNED files (full overwrite safe; no operator content); SEED-AND-PRESERVE files are out of scope (existing seed-if-missing logic in upgrade Step 5 already handles those, per [`3e8f2c5`](#3e8f2c5) precedent). Parallel pattern: [`3e8f2c5`](#3e8f2c5) extended upgrade flow to seed missing seed-and-preserve files; this entry extends similarly to refresh spec-owned files the OLD dispatcher didn't know about.

**AI-discipline tradeoff.** Step 8 is AI-instruction at root — a sufficiently lazy AI could skip it under "/stoa upgrade said success, we're done" task-momentum pressure. Not deterministic prevention. Mitigations: imperative `MUST` wording, visible `[stoa-upgrade-catchup]` block (visibility-first per [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c) pattern), idempotency (re-run is safe). If empirical beta data shows Step 8 gets skipped, the structural escalation candidate is a `.stoa/hooks/upgrade-catchup` script invoked by the dispatcher — similar to the future-proofing escalation noted in [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4) for the self-strip step.

**Coherence-check findings (v0.4.2 broadened rule):**

- **Adjacent** to [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4) (v0.4.3 upgrade-strip discipline). Same visible-block pattern, same Write-not-Edit rule, same future-escalation escape valve.
- **Adjacent** to [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01) (v0.4.3 drop backcompat hedges). Step 8 adds backcompat but in install kit (stripped after upgrade), not slim driver — preserves per-session-cost-lean principle while still automating cross-version migration.
- **Adjacent** to [`c91b07e`](#c91b07e) (spec-owned vs seed-and-preserve taxonomy). Step 8 acts on spec-owned files specifically; reuses the established classification.
- **Adjacent** to [`3e8f2c5`](#3e8f2c5) (v0.1.4 generalization: upgrade flow extended to seed-missing seed-and-preserve files). Step 8 is the parallel extension for spec-owned files; same upgrade-flow-completeness principle.
- **Adjacent** to [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1) (v0.5+ artifacts Step 8 catches up).
- **Adjacent** to [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c) (`[stoa-preflight]` visible-output rule). Same visibility-first discipline extended to upgrade flow.

**Adopter-visible:** yes on v0.4.x → v0.5.0 upgrade. Two confirmation surfaces in sequence: standard "Install complete!" then "Cross-version catchup complete: refreshed N files; vector index <state>." After Step 8 completes, the installation is in full sync with v0.5.0 canonical; subsequent upgrades go through normal flow (dispatcher's Step 3 list now matches canonical).

**Refs:** [`8c2e7f4`](#8c2e7f4), [`c2d7a01`](#c2d7a01), [`c91b07e`](#c91b07e), [`3e8f2c5`](#3e8f2c5), [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c), [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3), [`a5e3c92`](#a5e3c92), [`2f8b6d1`](#2f8b6d1).

## 10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Hex ID format bumped from 7-char to 32-char UUIDv4 for new entries. Existing 7-char entries grandfather; reader regex accepts both lengths. Real RNG generation (`python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4().hex)"`) replaces AI-generated randomness. Partial supersession of [`e9fa237`](#e9fa237)'s "7 chars sufficient at project scale" claim — scale assumption shifts from per-project thousands to org-scale multi-tens-of-thousands.**

**Why the change.** Operator surfaced the concern: Stoa's planning horizon is org-scale (1000s of contributors over years × cross-repo federation). 7-char hex (16^7 ≈ 268M IDs) hits birthday-paradox collisions at ~16K entries — well within org-scale single-repo, near-certain cross-repo. Citations are URLs (UI-handled, not human-typed), so the aesthetic cost of longer IDs is moot. Function over form: pick the format with the strongest collision-resistance.

**Format: 32-char UUIDv4 (no-dash hex form).** 128-bit entropy = collision-safe at ~18 quintillion entries. Universally safe across any plausible scale. No-dash form (e.g., `10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b` — this entry's hex) over standard dashed form for simpler greppable regex (`[a-f0-9]{32}` rather than segmented pattern).

**Why not just longer hex (10 or 16 char)?** 10-char hex is collision-safe at ~1M entries (org-scale enough). 16-char (64-bit) is collision-safe at ~4B entries (universal). But once aesthetics is delegated to UI, every length above 7 is functionally equivalent until you hit the math floor. 32-char is the standard, well-supported, deterministically safe answer. Less ambiguity for future readers; matches the universal UUIDv4 convention adopters and tooling already understand.

**Why real RNG over AI-generated.** Empirical concern: AI-generated "random" hex has subtle bias patterns — language models bias toward vowel-shaped letter clusters, common digit positions, etc. At 7 chars this hasn't caused observable collisions in beta (149 entries here; ~42 in acme-platform), but as length-vs-entropy matters more for resistance, AI randomness becomes a real failure mode. Mandate `python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4().hex)"` at append time. One Bash tool call per entry; cheap; cryptographically sound.

**Backward compatibility — grandfather existing 7-char entries.**

- Reader regex: `[a-f0-9]{7}|[a-f0-9]{32}` (strict) or `[a-f0-9]{7,}` (permissive grep).
- Existing 7-char hexes stay valid forever — they're already unique within the current corpus (149 entries; collision probability ~5×10⁻⁹ at this size).
- New entries from v0.5.1+ use 32-char UUIDv4.
- Cross-references mix freely (e.g., `Refs: 7e9c4a3, 10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`).
- No DB migration needed — vector index hex column is TEXT (variable length).

**This entry uses the new 32-char format.** First WAL entry to adopt v0.5.1's UUID format. Hex generated via the prescribed mechanism (`python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4().hex)"`).

**Vehicle: v0.5.1 patch.** Small spec edit; focused commit; no entanglement with v0.5.0's vector-index work. Step 8 cross-version catchup ([`d6e8a37`](#d6e8a37)) is not needed for this transition — v0.5.0's dispatcher's standard Step 3 already refreshes `.stoa/index/embed.py` (where the regex bumps live) and the dispatcher itself. v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 upgrades go through the normal `/stoa upgrade` flow.

**Spec changes (v0.5.1 vehicle):**

- Founding principle #3 wording: refines hex format (7-char pre-v0.5.1 / 32-char v0.5.1+).
- §"WAL entry form (canonical)" gains explicit "Hex ID format" subsection + updated example using 32-char UUID.
- Bash grep regex bumped from `[a-f0-9]\{7\}` to `[a-f0-9]\{7,\}` (permissive 7-or-more; matches both formats).
- Python regex in embed.py bumped from `[a-f0-9]{7}` to `[a-f0-9]{7,}` (3 callsites).
- Version stamp v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 (8+ callsites).

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding (partial)** with [`e9fa237`](#e9fa237) (v0.1 rollback of content-hash claim; established 7-char hex sufficient at project scale). The "7 chars sufficient" sub-claim is superseded by this entry — the scale assumption shifts from per-project thousands to org-scale multi-tens-of-thousands. The "random not content-hash" decision from `e9fa237` remains active; only the length changes. Not a full rollback because the original entry's core decision (random IDs) is preserved.
- **Adjacent** to founding principle #3 (stable identity). This entry refines the format; doesn't change the principle.
- **Adjacent** to [`d6e8a37`](#d6e8a37) (cross-version catchup). v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 upgrades go through the dispatcher's standard refresh — no Step 8 catchup needed for this transition (v0.5.0 dispatcher already refreshes embed.py).

**Adopter-visible:** yes on v0.5.0 → v0.5.1 upgrade. After upgrade, new WAL appends use 32-char UUIDs. No backfill of existing entries; reader regex transparently handles both lengths. Adopters running `/stoa upgrade` see standard "Install complete!" confirmation.

**Refs:** [`e9fa237`](#e9fa237) (partial supersession), [`d6e8a37`](#d6e8a37), [`7e9c4a3`](#7e9c4a3).

## e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Cadence #1 escalation: `[stoa-propagation]` visible-output block required pre-commit. Closes the cadence-#2 drift-detection miss-class with a trigger-shape that matches release events.**

Two recorded instances of cadence #2 missing version-stamp drift across release boundaries: [`d4f9a13`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) (v0.3.6 → v0.3.7 on 2026-05-15) and [`b485bbf968c946248fec20591847d2df`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) (v0.4.3 → v0.5.1 on 2026-05-17). The b485 entry surfaced the structural root cause: cadence #2 fires on `decision`-append, but version stamps and release-event ripples don't ride on any individual decision. Trigger-shape and drift-shape do not align — a perfectly-disciplined AI walking artifacts on every decision would still miss the release moment.

**Decision.** Retrofit cadence #1 (pre-commit drift walk) with a required `[stoa-propagation]` visible-output block, parallel structure to `[stoa-preflight]`. Pre-commit is the correct trigger: every release lands as a commit, the AI has full visibility into staged content, and the visibility requirement makes compliance verifiable in-turn.

**Why over the alternatives** (per [`b485bbf968c946248fec20591847d2df`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) enumeration):

- *Option (b) tie to `/stoa upgrade`*: catches canonical version bumps but misses ad-hoc inline edits (which is what happened with v0.5.0 / v0.5.1).
- *Option (c) deterministic pre-commit hook*: survives discipline degradation but heavier escalation. The arc at [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) prescribes visibility-first before hook-fragmentation. (c) becomes the v0.6+ escalation candidate if (a) also degrades.
- *Option (a) visible-output*: cheapest move that addresses the trigger-shape mismatch. Same pattern that closed cadence #3 (deterministic hook, [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)) and the v0.3.5 → v0.3.6 preflight degradation (visible block, [`d8e4a2c`](context_log.md#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12)).

**Spec changes** (installkit/stoa.md only — root `stoa.md` regenerates via `/stoa upgrade`):

- §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape": new "Pre-commit propagation block" subsection — rule, format, why-visible, non-triggers, relationship to cadence #3.
- §"Coherence cadence" intro: "Six rely on AI judgment" → "Five rely on AI judgment; two structurally reinforced" — cadence #1 + cadence #3.
- §"Coherence cadence" #1: imperative retrofit — silent walk → visible-block-required walk.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), this is an AI-instruction block edit. The compliance intent: AI MUST emit `[stoa-propagation]` before any commit-staging tool call; missing block = visible omission the operator can call out in-turn. Failure mode shifts from silent → recoverable.

**Vehicle:** v0.5.2 patch (adopter-visible methodology change). Beta-tracker entries `d4f9a13` and `b485bbf968c946248fec20591847d2df` move to `applied-upstream-as-WAL-entry-e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d`.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none. Extends cadence #1 without contradicting existing entries.

## 81953a7cc72c4f9aa67f8a7f6dbc8773 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Bootcheck imperative enumerates boundary moments explicitly: session start, post-`/compact`, post-`/clear`. Closes the post-compact ambiguity that surfaced in [`5298f72679d5440c9cd172dd65d7a2cc`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md).**

Prior wording said *"BEFORE producing your first response in this repo"* — genuinely ambiguous against post-`/compact` resumption, because a continuation summary reads as "this is a continuation" rather than "first response." `5298f72…` (third recorded bootcheck skip; new failure shape) documented an AI rationalizing the skip from that ambiguity. The enumeration removes the gap.

**Decision.** Change `installkit/stoa.md` §"Session boot check" imperative to enumerate the three boundary moments. Lifecycle-cue boundaries that destroy install-state context all count: session start (no context yet), post-`/compact` (compaction destroyed it), post-`/clear` (clearing destroyed it).

**Why this alone is insufficient.** The arc at [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) predicts wording-only fixes degrade. This entry is paired with [`8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9`](#8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9--decision--2026-05-17) (visible-output escalation), which lands the structural backstop. The two travel together; this one closes the ambiguity gap, the next one makes the rule's compliance verifiable.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), this is an AI-instruction-block edit. Compliance intent: AI invokes bootcheck at three enumerated boundary moments, not just at session start.

- **Converging:** [`5298f72679d5440c9cd172dd65d7a2cc`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) Option (a); [`6f4e8c2`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) accumulating evidence for action.

## 8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`[stoa-init]` visible-output block required at each bootcheck boundary moment. Closes the silent-skip failure mode for session-init compliance, parallel to [`d8e4a2c`](context_log.md#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12)'s `[stoa-preflight]` and [`e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d`](#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17)'s `[stoa-propagation]`.**

Three recorded silent skips of the bootcheck rule across two repos: acme-platform 2026-05-11; this repo [`6f4e8c2`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md); this repo [`5298f72679d5440c9cd172dd65d7a2cc`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md). The arc at [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) prescribes visibility as the next escalation when wording-tightening saturates. Three observations across two repos justifies it.

**Decision.** AI MUST emit a literal `[stoa-init]` block as first user-visible content at each boundary moment (session start / post-`/compact` / post-`/clear`). Content of the block names the boundary and contains the bootcheck subagent's return verbatim. Missing block = visible compliance gap the operator can call out in-turn.

**Why this and not host-specific hooks.** Host-specific hooks (Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` + Codex equivalent + others) would be deterministic but heavyweight: host fragmentation, install complexity, hook chain conflicts. Visibility is the lighter move that survives the discipline arc; if it ALSO degrades, host hooks become the next candidate (and the empirical data then justifies the host-fragmentation cost).

**Block shape (consistent across the visible-output family):**

```
[stoa-init]
- Boundary: <"session start" | "post-/compact" | "post-/clear">
- Bootcheck return: <verbatim subagent output>
```

Sister blocks: `[stoa-preflight]` (settling-cue / phase-settlement / end-of-impl), `[stoa-propagation]` (pre-commit drift walk). Together they form the visible-output family — every Stoa cadence with discipline-degradation pressure has a visible block now (cadence #1, cadence #3 via hook + WAL preflight, cadence #7).

**Dependency on [`ed59a321317746008bb434f84e92ae71`](#ed59a321317746008bb434f84e92ae71--decision--2026-05-17).** The block surfaces the subagent's return verbatim. If the subagent augments output (per [`e3b8a47`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md), 2-of-3 paths violated output discipline), the block becomes unreliable. The paired entry tightens subagent output discipline so the visible block has a clean substrate.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), AI-instruction-block edit. Compliance intent: visible block as first user-visible content at each boundary; failure mode shifts silent → recoverable.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none — extends the visible-output family without contradicting existing entries.
- **Converging:** [`5298f72679d5440c9cd172dd65d7a2cc`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) Option (b); [`6f4e8c2`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) "Plausible v0.3.x" option.
- **Adjacent:** [`d8e4a2c`](context_log.md#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) (`[stoa-preflight]` precedent); [`e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d`](#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17) (`[stoa-propagation]` sibling); [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (escalation arc); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (code-not-prose discipline); [`81953a7cc72c4f9aa67f8a7f6dbc8773`](#81953a7cc72c4f9aa67f8a7f6dbc8773--decision--2026-05-17) (paired wording enumeration).

**Refs:** [`d8e4a2c`](context_log.md#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12), [`e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d`](#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17), [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12), [`81953a7cc72c4f9aa67f8a7f6dbc8773`](#81953a7cc72c4f9aa67f8a7f6dbc8773--decision--2026-05-17), [`ed59a321317746008bb434f84e92ae71`](#ed59a321317746008bb434f84e92ae71--decision--2026-05-17).

## ed59a321317746008bb434f84e92ae71 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Stoa-bootcheck subagent output discipline tightened: discipline reminder moved to top of file; WRONG/RIGHT examples added; version-template ambiguity resolved via explicit SemVer-prefix extraction. Addresses [`e3b8a47`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md).**

`e3b8a47` documented the subagent violating its own "no explanatory prose" output discipline on 2 of 3 BOOT validation paths: `clean` path prefixed with "All checks pass." (pure ceremony); hook-not-active path injected a diagnostic clause mid-line breaking the canonical text. Plus a third issue: the `<local>` template in the version-mismatch path was substituted with the full H1 string ("v0.4.3 BETA") rather than the SemVer prefix ("v0.4.3").

**Decision.** Apply options (a) + (c) from `e3b8a47`:

- **(a) Output discipline reminder moved to top of subagent file.** Added a callout right after the intro paragraph stating output rules — the canonical lines are mandatory verbatim, no preface, no augmentation outside the canonical line itself. Existing constraint at end of file shortened to a pointer.
- **(a) WRONG/RIGHT examples added in §"Output".** Two pairs: (i) `clean` path — no preface; (ii) `[stoa]` line — diagnostic permitted as parenthetical at end, NOT injected mid-canonical-text. Permits the genuinely useful diagnostic (the offending value) while deterring the ceremony.
- **(c) Version template disambiguated.** Procedure now explicitly extracts SemVer prefix from H1 via `grep -oE 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'`. The message template uses `<local-version>` and `<marker-version>` (SemVer prefix only — no BETA suffix). Eliminates template ambiguity that produced the H1-substring substitution in `e3b8a47`.

Skipped option (b) from `e3b8a47` (relax spec to allow augmentation). The diagnostic-on-error case has value; the prepend on `clean` doesn't. (a) preserves the useful case structurally while deterring the rest.

**Why this entry pairs with [`8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9`](#8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9--decision--2026-05-17).** The `[stoa-init]` visible block surfaces the subagent's return verbatim. If the subagent augments output, the visible block becomes unreliable. This entry produces a clean substrate so the visible block reports compliance evidence the operator can trust.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), AI-instruction-block edit (the subagent file is AI-discipline-loaded on invocation). Compliance intent: subagent emits the canonical line as the literal string with parenthetical diagnostic as the only permitted augmentation.

**Scope.** Edits go to the embedded `#### path: .claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` block in `installkit/stoa.md`. The on-disk `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` regenerates on `/stoa upgrade` per the spec-owned-refresh discipline.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none.
- **Converging:** [`e3b8a47`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) Options (a) + (c) — this entry adopts both.
- **Adjacent:** [`8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9`](#8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9--decision--2026-05-17) (paired escalation — visible block needs clean substrate); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15).

**Refs:** [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), [`8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9`](#8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9--decision--2026-05-17).

## 7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**v0.5.1+ UUID format propagated to stoa-managed append-only files beyond `context_log.md`: beta_tracker.md template, context_log.md starter, slim §"Beta tracking" general-principle statement now all reference 32-char UUIDv4 (v0.5.1+) with 7-char hex grandfathering.**

[`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17) bumped the WAL's hex ID format from 7-char to 32-char UUIDv4 (v0.5.1+) for collision-safety at org-scale. The decision applied to `context_log.md` immediately. The methodology principle that **all stoa-managed append-only files inherit the same hex ID rule** was implicit — the slim §"Beta tracking" general-principle line spelled it out but in its pre-v0.5.1 form ("7-char hex stable identity"). The install-kit-section templates (beta_tracker.md seed, context_log.md starter) carried matching pre-v0.5.1 wording.

Result: post-v0.5.1, the WAL used UUIDs but the methodology *spec* for beta-tracker and the *starter template* both still mandated 7-char hex. Adopters and even the dogfooded beta_tracker.md fell into mixed-format usage (recent entries [`5298f72679d5440c9cd172dd65d7a2cc`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) and [`b485bbf968c946248fec20591847d2df`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) used 32-char; earlier ones [`3b1c8d4`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md), [`6f4e8c2`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md), etc., used 7-char). The mix was tolerated under reader-regex permissiveness but never formally settled in the spec.

**Decision.** Propagate the v0.5.1+ UUID rule explicitly to all stoa-managed append-only files. Spec changes in `installkit/stoa.md`:

- §"Beta tracking" → "General principle": "Stoa-managed append-only files (WAL + beta-tracker) use stable hex IDs per entry. v0.5.1+ entries use 32-char UUIDv4 generated via real RNG; pre-v0.5.1 entries use 7-char hex and remain readable."
- `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` seed template: format note reads "Hex IDs match `context_log.md`'s format (v0.5.1+ entries: 32-char UUIDv4; pre-v0.5.1 entries: 7-char hex; both readable)" with explicit `python3 -c "import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4().hex)"` mechanism.
- `context_log.md` starter template: "Entry format: `## <hex-id> — <type> — YYYY-MM-DD` ... New entries (v0.5.1+) use 32-char UUIDv4; older entries use 7-char hex; both are valid."

**Adopter-visible:** yes on next install (fresh adopters get aligned templates) or `/stoa upgrade` (for content in spec-owned files — the seed templates fall under seed-and-preserve, so existing adopter copies remain at the pre-v0.5.2 wording until manual edit).

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding (partial)** of the implicit-7-char-hex-everywhere assumption in the pre-v0.5.1 §"Beta tracking" general-principle line. Same arc as [`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17) — this entry just finishes propagating that decision to the rest of the spec.
- **Converging:** none.
- **Adjacent:** [`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17) (parent decision); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction edit discipline — this entry touches the beta-tracker template wording, which counts as spec content).

**Refs:** [`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17).

## 5bde4a038d304217a8c94521059880f4 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Principle: history-of-evolution prose belongs in the WAL, not in spec-owned-artifact preambles. Installkit cleanup pass collapses historical-evolution prose in `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` preamble and `/stoa upgrade` subcommand rationales to current-state framing.**

The installkit section of `installkit/stoa.md` had accumulated historical-evolution prose in several embedded-artifact preambles and procedure rationales:

- `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` preamble enumerated v0.2 → v0.4.0 → v0.4.1 → v0.4.2 changes inline.
- `/stoa upgrade` "Why X matters" rationales used v0.1.x → v0.2 / v0.1.3 → v0.1.4 migration examples to motivate each step.
- `/stoa upgrade` "Scope (v0.3.x envelope)" and "v0.4 evolution path" sections were version-bound future-tense statements written from v0.3.x perspective.

Two problems:

1. **Operator-irrelevant.** A fresh adopter installing at v0.5.2 doesn't need to know the v0.1.3 → v0.1.4 migration story to understand why the upgrade flow seeds missing files. The current-state framing ("seed missing files for operators who installed earlier") is sufficient.
2. **Stale on every release.** Version-bound future-tense statements rot. "v0.4 evolution path" written in v0.3.x is misleading at v0.5.2 (the work either happened or didn't; the section needs ongoing rewrites).

**Decision.** Adopt the principle: **history-of-evolution prose lives in the WAL** (where it's append-only, dated, and authored). Spec-owned-artifact preambles state current-state behavior + the upgrade-refresh contract, nothing more. Rationale sections within the dispatcher use current-state framing without version-bound migration examples.

**Spec changes applied in this commit:**

- `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` preamble: collapsed v0.2/v0.4.0/v0.4.1/v0.4.2 history into current-state Pass A vs Pass B description; cross-refs slim §"Coherence cadence" for detail.
- `/stoa upgrade` "Why X matters" rationales: four per-step paragraphs collapsed into one paragraph using current-state framing; removed v0.1.x → v0.2 and v0.1.3 → v0.1.4 migration examples.
- `/stoa upgrade` "Scope (v0.3.x envelope)" → "Scope" (drop version binding).
- `/stoa upgrade` "v0.4 evolution path" section dropped entirely (forward-looking from v0.3.x perspective; v0.4 happened without this work; if still desired, it can be re-proposed as its own decision and live in the WAL).

**Going forward.** When proposing changes to spec-owned artifacts in `installkit/stoa.md`, avoid inline version-of-evolution narrative. Reference the WAL for history. Spec content describes current behavior + upgrade contract.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), AI-instruction-block edit (the trimmed prose was operator-facing and AI-discipline-loaded). Compliance intent: future spec edits don't re-introduce embedded version history.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none — this is a stylistic discipline overlaid on existing content; doesn't reverse a prior decision, just constrains future ones.
- **Converging:** none.
- **Adjacent:** [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline — applies); [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17) (v0.5.2 release vehicle — this entry refines the cleanup scope under that release).

**Refs:** [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17), [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15).

## b699d8b7def64a6fb7eb1f15d0fa2fad — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Apply load-on-invocation discipline more aggressively in slim spec: push `/stoa audit` cadence #5 procedure detail to dispatcher; relocate `/stoa upgrade` cross-version-catchup trigger from slim §"Upgrade flow" into dispatcher's procedure as Step 6b; tighten slim §"Command surface" to drop duplicate of `/stoa help`. Slim file ends v0.5.2 net -727 tokens vs v0.5.1 baseline despite three new visible-output features added this release.**

The v0.5.2 release added three visible-output features (`[stoa-init]`, `[stoa-propagation]`, retrofitted cadence #1) that grew the slim file by ~700 tokens. The slim-section redundancy pass earlier in the session saved ~50 lines but didn't offset the additions — net session-load cost was up. Operator pushed back: "I thought we found a way to save tokens; the section grew."

**Root cause.** The full pass (A+B+C+D items) targeted the install-kit section (L383-1976 of installkit/stoa.md), which doesn't load at session time. Session-load is determined by the slim section only. To actually reduce session tokens, slim content must shrink.

**Decision.** Apply load-on-invocation discipline more aggressively: slim file describes WHAT exists; dispatcher carries HOW. Three callsites:

1. **§"Coherence cadence" #5 (`/stoa audit`).** Replaced 4 sub-bullets of sweep procedure detail with a one-line summary listing the 4 sweep names + dispatcher pointer. Mirrors the existing `/stoa pull` cadence #6 pattern. Procedure detail at `installkit/stoa.md` L776-859 (`/stoa audit` dispatcher subcommand) is comprehensive — slim sub-bullets were pure duplicate.

2. **§"Upgrade flow" (cross-version catchup).** Removed the catchup paragraph from slim entirely. Replaced with a single-line dispatcher pointer noting "Procedure detail lives in `/stoa upgrade` dispatcher subcommand; carries Steps 1-7 plus cross-version catchup." Required paired dispatcher edit: added Step 6b to `/stoa upgrade` procedure invoking the install kit's Step 8 cross-version catchup. Without the paired edit, removing the slim trigger would have broken cross-version catchup entirely — the Step 8 trigger had nowhere else to fire.

3. **§"Command surface".** Tightened from full subcommand enumeration to `/stoa help` pointer + stubs note. Removed enumeration that duplicated `/stoa help`'s subcommand list.

**Measured savings.** cl100k_base tokens: 10,382 → 9,673 = **-709 (6.8%)**. Claude-estimate (×1.07): -758. Chars: -3,111. Lines: -6 (the line-count undercounts because removed content was dense long lines rather than many short lines).

**v0.5.1 → v0.5.2 net.** v0.5.1 baseline was ~10,400 tokens. v0.5.2 post-this-decision = 9,673 = **-727 tokens vs v0.5.1**, with three additional visible-output features (`[stoa-init]`, `[stoa-propagation]`, cadence #1 retrofit) folded in. Operator's "we should save tokens" goal achieved.

**Surface damage scan.** Two preserved-in-dispatcher contents (audit procedure detail; cross-version catchup procedure) remain accessible:
- `/stoa audit` invocation loads dispatcher's full sweep procedure — operator and AI get the detail when they need it.
- `/stoa upgrade` invocation now triggers Step 8 from dispatcher procedure (Step 6b). Cross-version catchup still fires; trigger moved from "session-load reminder" to "dispatcher procedure step", which is structurally cleaner (the dispatcher is what runs the upgrade anyway).

No surface lost. Three forms of safety:
- AI's invocation-time access to procedure detail (unchanged).
- Operator's `/stoa help` enumeration (unchanged — actually more discoverable now because slim no longer duplicates it).
- Cross-version catchup trigger (preserved via dispatcher Step 6b).

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), this is an AI-instruction-block edit at three callsites. Compliance intent: future spec edits should default to placing procedure detail in dispatchers (loads-on-invocation) and slim-section content to brief description + dispatcher pointers. Mirrors the existing pattern for `/stoa pull` cadence #6 (which already lives this way per L312 of slim).

**Generalization for future cadences.** Cadence #3 (pre-commit WAL audit), #4 (pre-compact/clear), and #7 (end-of-impl) all currently describe procedure inline in slim. These are AI-load-bearing imperatives that need to fire automatically (not on operator invocation), so moving them to dispatchers would break their trigger surface. They stay in slim. The discipline is: **operator-triggered cadences keep procedure in dispatchers; AI-triggered cadences keep procedure in slim.** This entry doesn't mandate that rule — operator can override per-cadence — but documents the pattern.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none — extends the load-on-invocation pattern without contradicting earlier decisions; `/stoa pull` cadence #6 already follows this pattern, so this entry generalizes it.
- **Converging:** none.
- **Adjacent:** [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17) (v0.5.2 release vehicle — this entry extends its scope); [`5bde4a038d304217a8c94521059880f4`](#5bde4a038d304217a8c94521059880f4--decision--2026-05-17) (history-in-WAL principle — same spirit: spec carries current behavior, not duplicates); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-edit discipline).

**Refs:** [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17), [`5bde4a038d304217a8c94521059880f4`](#5bde4a038d304217a8c94521059880f4--decision--2026-05-17), [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15).

## 758dde1d62234bacb8cd9d24f0624f66 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Track 5 test-suite artifacts in `.stoa/artifacts.md`: `tests/scenarios.md`, `tests/harness.sh`, `tests/README.md`, `tests/codex-smoke-test.md`, `tests/multi-author-merge-test.md`. Test infrastructure now subject to cadence #1 drift walks; future spec changes will surface test-side drift pre-emptively rather than going silently stale.**

The pre-commit test-harness check today caught a known-class drift bug: 10 `verify_*` regex callsites in `tests/harness.sh` still used pre-v0.5.1 `[0-9a-f]{7}` exact-length hex match instead of the permissive `[0-9a-f]{7,}` form. Same pattern as the wal-audit Pass B regex fix surfaced by today's installkit-vs-WAL coherency audit. Both were unfinished propagation from [`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17) (UUID format bump) and [`7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050`](#7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050--decision--2026-05-17) (UUID format propagation to stoa-managed append-only files).

Root cause of the test-side miss: `tests/` was not in `.stoa/artifacts.md`, so cadence #1 (pre-commit drift walk) and cadence #2 (post-decision propagation pass) never walked it. Test infrastructure drifts silently relative to spec changes.

**Decision.** Add the 5 test-suite artifacts above to `.stoa/artifacts.md` with operator-prose role descriptions. Each is now a drift candidate that cadence #1's `[stoa-propagation]` block will surface on commits touching related spec content. Particularly load-bearing:

- `tests/scenarios.md` — drift target whenever methodology rules in `installkit/stoa.md` change.
- `tests/harness.sh` — drift target on hex-format rules, on `[stoa-*]` block requirements (added in v0.5.2 — verify functions don't yet check for these), and on subcommand-set changes.
- `tests/codex-smoke-test.md` — drift target on `/stoa` surface changes (Codex CLI uses prose, but the test enumerates expected commands).
- `tests/multi-author-merge-test.md` — drift target on cadence #6 procedure or `.gitattributes`/`merge=union` substrate changes.

**Concomitant fix landed in this commit.** Bumped `tests/harness.sh:2` stale version comment from `# Stoa v0.4.3 BETA — test harness.` to a generic `# Stoa test harness.` — versions in source-file comments tend to rot; the project's `installkit/stoa.md` H1 + `.stoa/installed` marker are the authoritative version sources, and source-file comments shouldn't duplicate them.

**Implication for future scope.** With `tests/` tracked, cadence #1's `[stoa-propagation]` block will list test files in its walk. Operators should expect drift findings on test-side propagation when methodology rules change. v0.5.2 specifically: verify functions in `tests/harness.sh` don't yet check for the new visible-output family (`[stoa-init]`, `[stoa-preflight]` shape, `[stoa-propagation]`); driving the existing scenarios will pass under v0.5.2 (no NEW failure modes), but the harness doesn't yet positively verify the new block emissions. That's a separate test-coverage gap — surface as `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` entry if observed in beta, or extend scenario coverage in a follow-up commit.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding:** none.
- **Converging:** the audit-surfaced wal-audit Pass B regex fix earlier in this session is the same gap-pattern this entry's tracking decision aims to prevent in future. [`7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050`](#7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050--decision--2026-05-17) settled the propagation principle; this entry expands its coverage by making the test infrastructure visible to cadence #1.
- **Adjacent:** [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-edit discipline doesn't apply to tests/ specifically, but the same care applies); [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17) (v0.5.2 release vehicle — this tracking decision is folded in).

**Refs:** [`7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050`](#7f97a09d6e6f45aab8756f54fe36f050--decision--2026-05-17), [`10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b`](#10e373c9ce9f427e84429fcb4eac191b--decision--2026-05-17), [`a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace`](#a89b5dc71eb44eaf9164f5228dd84ace--decision--2026-05-17).

## dce295cbbc3244b7b822afc0649bc247 — decision — 2026-05-17

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Canonical-branch detection cascade unified across `stoa-bootcheck` subagent + `/stoa upgrade` Step 4b to match install kit Step 5's 3-step pattern (origin/HEAD → current branch → literal `main`). Closes a spurious-warning bug on local-only non-`main` repos.**

Surfaced empirically by BOOT4 (driven this session as part of the post-audit test-refresh validation): the BOOT4 trial dir was a local-only repo on `master` (no `origin/HEAD`); bootcheck fell straight to its literal `main` fallback, checked `git config branch.main.rebase` (unset), and fired the rebase-config warning. Meanwhile install Step 5 had correctly detected `master` via its 3-step cascade and set `branch.master.rebase=true`. The two detection paths disagreed in practice.

**Root cause.** Three callsites in `installkit/stoa.md` describe canonical-branch detection:

- **Install kit Step 5 §"WAL pull-rebase strategy" (L1766) — CORRECT.** *"Read it from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null` ... falling back to `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo main`."* Three-step cascade.
- **`stoa-bootcheck` embedded block (L1180 pre-fix) — BUG.** *"Detect canonical branch (`git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | xargs basename` → fallback `main`)."* Skipped the `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` middle step; fell straight to literal `main`.
- **`/stoa upgrade` Step 4b (L980 pre-fix) — BUG + STALE CLAIM.** *"Same procedure as install kit Step 5 §'WAL pull-rebase strategy': read `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null` (basename), fallback `main`."* Same skipped-step bug, plus the "same procedure" prose was misleading.

**Decision.** Align both buggy callsites with the 3-step cascade:

- L1180 (bootcheck): replaced single-fallback wording with the full cascade reference + step-by-step description.
- L980 (`/stoa upgrade` Step 4b): same fix; "same procedure" claim now actually matches.

**Impact.**

- Local-only repos on `master` (or any non-`main` branch with no `origin/HEAD`): bootcheck now detects the actual current branch, checks the correct rebase config, stays silent when it's set. No spurious warnings.
- Multi-author repos with proper `origin/HEAD` pointer: behavior unchanged (the first step in the cascade still wins).
- Operators who install Stoa on a non-`main` branch then later switch to `main`: bootcheck would now flag `branch.main.rebase` as unset (because the original install set `branch.<old-branch>.rebase`). Real warning, not spurious — operator can run `/stoa upgrade` to re-run Step 4b on the new branch.

**Validates** BOOT4 (post-`/clear` boundary, added in [`de2a6e27`](#de2a6e270b2947e9a9435d63373e4c75--decision--2026-05-17)): the test that surfaced this bug now passes cleanly on local-only repos.

**Compliance shift.** Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15), AI-instruction-block edits to both the embedded subagent definition and the dispatcher procedure. Compliance intent: any future canonical-branch detection logic in the install kit must use the same 3-step cascade.

**Adopter-visible:** yes, on next `/stoa upgrade`. Existing adopters running on `main` see no change. Adopters on non-`main` branches stop seeing the spurious warning after upgrade.

**Coherence-check findings:**

- **Superseding (partial):** the literal-`main`-fallback wording in bootcheck and upgrade Step 4b. Same callsite; in-place spec correction (not a WAL-style supersession — these are spec edits inside the install kit, not WAL entries).
- **Converging:** none.
- **Adjacent:** [`de2a6e27`](#de2a6e270b2947e9a9435d63373e4c75--decision--2026-05-17) (BOOT4 added this session — the test that surfaced the bug); [`c257d94d`](#c257d94d71014805b4a69d324ff58df8--observation--2026-05-17) (audit observation documenting test infrastructure refresh — BOOT4's surfacing of this bug is exactly the value the refresh aimed to deliver).

**Refs:** [`de2a6e27`](#de2a6e270b2947e9a9435d63373e4c75--decision--2026-05-17), [`c257d94d`](#c257d94d71014805b4a69d324ff58df8--observation--2026-05-17), [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15).
