## 717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16 — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Agent-first quality on the curated decision forest; RAG demoted to scalability fallback.**

Stoa's decision forest is curated, high-relevance-density data. At slurp-feasible scale, quality of coherence reasoning comes from Agent direct reasoning over the loaded corpus; rapid Agent capability evolution is the primary lever for quality improvements over time. RAG extends viable scale beyond what slurp supports and serves as fallback at scale. Within semantic-shape lookups (relatedness, conflict, convergence), RAG is preferred over grep/keyword-search; lexical and positional lookups (hex-exact, recency, literal markers) keep their grep paths.

**Why:** the WAL is append-only and operator-curated — every entry is signal, not noise. At small/medium scale the LLM's own attention is a better relevance filter than cosine similarity in embedding space; embedding pre-filtering replaces LLM judgment with a degraded proxy. Synthesis-contamination (LLM passively absorbing ambient signal from everything loaded) is weaker on curated data; the dominant cost of slurping is attention dilution at the upper end of the context window, which stays manageable below ~100K tokens. The bet is that Agent capability scales faster than RAG-tuning effort; 1M-token contexts already exist and grow rapidly.

**How to apply:**
- Default coherence-check path: subagent slurps the WAL into its own context, reasons directly. Parent stays lean.
- Slurp infeasible (WAL > ~30% subagent context budget) → RAG retrieval + LLM classification with bumped k for checkpoint contexts.
- Semantic-shape lookups: RAG > grep when slurp not chosen.
- Lexical/positional lookups (hex-exact, recency, decline-track markers): stay on grep regardless.
- Watch-signals: cadence #5 retrospective conflicts, cadence #6 pull-time semantic conflicts, beta_tracker entries reporting Stoa-missed-X. Persistent signal → revisit via rollback.

**Coherence-check findings:**
- Superseding: [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3) — direct reframing; vector index demoted from primary substrate. Rollback appended next in batch.
- Converging: [`c8b4d09`](context_log.md#c8b4d09--decision--2026-05-08) (loose framework, AI as interpreter). [`f8b3c52`](context_log.md#f8b3c52--decision--2026-05-09) (AI-quality dependency). [`f3a8d61`](context_log.md#f3a8d61--observation--2026-05-10) (compaction + context-growth bet).
- Adjacent: [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10) (scalability menu — RAG was #5 of 5). [`c4f9e87`](context_log.md#c4f9e87--observation--2026-05-17) (BGE empirical findings still apply at scale-extension).

## d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46 — rollback — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Rollback [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3) — vector index inverts from primary substrate to scale-extension fallback.**

Supersedes [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3)'s framing of the vector index as the primary substrate for WAL semantic operations. Under [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first quality principle), the primary substrate is Agent direct reasoning over the slurped WAL; the vector index serves as scale-extension fallback when slurp is infeasible.

**Why (the realization that drove the inversion):** the WAL is curated, high-relevance-density data — every entry is an inflection logged with intent. Combined with current trends where Agent capability outpaces RAG-tuning yield, the cost-benefit on direct reasoning vs retrieval inverts. The original "vectors primary, headline-grep fallback" architecture solved the right problem (semantic ≫ lexical at scale) but picked the wrong primary path. The actual ladder is: (1) slurped LLM reasoning, (2) high-k retrieval + LLM classification, (3) low-k retrieval mid-session, (4) headline-grep + LLM-pairwise as last resort. Vectors slot in at tier 2-3, not tier 1.

**What's preserved from [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3):** the vector-index architecture itself, the BGE-base-en-v1.5 model choice, the `/stoa query` interface, the index-coherency audit sweep, the existence of headline-grep as further fallback. The mechanisms survive; only the primary-vs-fallback framing inverts.

**What's superseded:** the "primary substrate" claim. References in the install kit and dispatcher procedure that implicitly treat vector-query as the default semantic-lookup path get rewritten in Phase 2 to route through `/stoa coherence`, which makes the slurp-vs-retrieve choice internally.

**Refs:** [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3) (target), [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (replacement framing).

## c86ea98f450f41a9abf7de0476173e2f — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Index-lifecycle gating severity softens under Agent-first — mechanisms preserved, refusal/blocking demoted.**

[`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17) established the multi-layer index update lifecycle (post-commit hook, lazy-on-query refresh, /stoa audit 4th sweep, dispatcher-level staleness refusal). Under [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle) and [`d45489b7`](#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18) (vector inversion to fallback), the mechanisms remain valuable but their gating severity shifts.

**What changes:**
- Dispatcher-level staleness refusal (`/stoa query` refusing to proceed on unaudited merges) → degraded-confidence note, not hard refusal. Index staleness affects scale-extension quality, not primary slurp path.
- Bootcheck info-surface on substantial index lag → silent or low-priority note, not a warning that demands operator action.
- Post-commit hook + lazy-on-query refresh → unchanged. Idempotent and cheap; keeps the index ready when needed.
- 4th `/stoa audit` sweep (index-coherency) → unchanged. Operator-triggered, auto-fixes; same shape as before.

**Why:** when the index is fallback infrastructure, its staleness is a quality degradation, not a correctness failure. Hard refusals create operator friction for a state that no longer breaks the primary path. The slurp-and-reason path doesn't depend on the index being current; coherence-check works without it (just slower at scale).

**How to apply:** when `/stoa coherence` invokes the subagent, the subagent decides slurp-vs-retrieve based on size. If slurp is chosen, index state is irrelevant for that invocation. If retrieve is chosen, the subagent surfaces "index N entries stale; quality may degrade" as a verdict-line note rather than refusing.

**Refs:** [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17) (target — mechanisms preserved, framing reconciled), [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first), [`d45489b7`](#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18) (vector inversion).

## d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Vector-index install becomes opt-in / scale-triggered under Agent-first — no longer first-run / fail-loud.**

[`a5e3c92`](context_log.md#a5e3c92--decision--2026-05-17) established Python 3.9+ + sentence-transformers + sqlite-vec as a Stoa baseline dependency with first-run auto-install and fail-loud discipline. Under [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first) and [`d45489b7`](#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18) (vector inversion), the install footprint becomes scale-extension infrastructure, not baseline.

**What changes:**
- First-run install no longer auto-runs `/stoa index install` unconditionally. Default first-run keeps the install footprint minimal (no Python venv, no model download).
- Operator opts in explicitly via `/stoa index install` when scale or workflow warrants.
- Alternatively, install kit auto-triggers `/stoa index install` when WAL size crosses a slurp-feasibility threshold (informational nudge, not blocking).
- Fail-loud on install failure: still appropriate when the operator HAS opted in. Don't degrade silently after explicit invocation.

**Why:** baseline-dep expansion has a real cost at first-run (network bandwidth, ~600MB disk, ~5min). Imposing this on adopters who may never hit the scale that justifies RAG is friction without payoff. The "AI is good enough today" thesis means small-and-medium adopters get full coherence-check quality without the vector substrate; large adopters install when needed.

**How to apply:**
- Install kit Step 2 / Step 5 (vector-index substrate): conditional — write `embed.py` / `query.py` / `.gitignore` unconditionally (small static files); skip venv + model download + initial embed by default.
- `/stoa index install` becomes the explicit operator entry to bootstrap the substrate.
- Future: a slurp-feasibility check during `/stoa audit` or bootcheck could surface an `[stoa]` nudge when the WAL outgrows the slurp budget.

**Refs:** [`a5e3c92`](context_log.md#a5e3c92--decision--2026-05-17) (target — install discipline reconciled), [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first), [`d45489b7`](#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18) (vector inversion).

## 89370375f20943ba8d06a319a429ed08 — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Highest-fidelity-tool-within-budget: 4-rung ladder for semantic-shape WAL lookups; grep carve-outs preserved.**

For semantic-shape WAL lookups (relatedness, conflict, convergence), Stoa picks the highest-fidelity tool that fits the budget at hand. The fidelity ladder, top to bottom:

1. **Slurped LLM reasoning** — subagent loads the entire WAL into its context, reasons directly. Best at slurp-feasible scale.
2. **High-k retrieval + LLM classification** — subagent calls `/stoa query` with bumped k; reads returned bodies; classifies. Best when slurp infeasible but quality matters (checkpoint contexts).
3. **Low-k retrieval + LLM classification** — same shape with default `k=10`. Best for mid-session continuous checks where latency budget is tight.
4. **Headline-grep + LLM-pairwise** — fallback when the vector index is missing, corrupt, or unavailable. Lowest-fidelity semantic-shape path.

**Grep carve-outs (lexical/positional; retain grep regardless of rung):**
- Hex-exact lookup (`grep '^## <hex>'`) — vector returns *similar*, not *exact*.
- Positional/recency (`tail` of headers; "last N decisions") — chronology, not similarity.
- Literal-marker lookups (e.g., "decline-track <path>" decisions in `/stoa init`; decline-decisions in bootcheck Step 3) — exact-string semantics, not paraphrasable.
- Set-diff operations (e.g., `/stoa index refresh`) — hex-only, circular with index.

**Why:** the ladder makes the slurp-vs-retrieve choice explicit and auditable. Without it, "use the index" reads as the default; with it, slurp is the named first preference and retrieval is named as fallback at scale. The grep carve-outs prevent the principle from over-claiming "always RAG over grep" — for lexical/positional/marker work, grep is the right tool.

**How to apply:** `/stoa coherence` subagent picks the rung based on WAL size + question shape. Rung 1 if WAL fits in ~30% of subagent context budget. Rung 4 if `/stoa query` reports `no-index`. Otherwise rung 2 (checkpoint) or rung 3 (mid-session). Grep carve-outs are always available and chosen by the call site, not by the subagent.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle that the ladder implements), [`d45489b7`](#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18) (vector inversion), [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10) (scalability menu — the ladder formalizes the implicit hierarchy), [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3) (vector mechanism, now slotted at rung 2-3).

## a8a0b7155913467b9c1ab1cbc027437a — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Three-tier WAL consultation: in-flight + WAL-not-indexed + indexed; extension of §"WAL access pattern".**

Coherence-shape WAL operations consult three memory tiers in order:

1. **Tier 1 — In-flight.** Candidates proposed this turn in AI conversation context. Not yet in WAL, not yet in index. Applies only when N>1 candidates exist this turn (intra-batch pairwise check; AI-side LLM work, small N). For single-candidate cases (A1 on one entry), Tier 1 is trivially empty.

2. **Tier 2 — WAL-not-indexed.** Entries in `context_log.md` newer than the index's `last_indexed_hex`. Handled transparently by `/stoa query`'s staleness gate (`installkit/stoa.md:1032-1037`): ≤50-entry lag → silent inline embed; >50 → banner + embed. Invoking `/stoa query` automatically pulls Tier 2 into scope.

3. **Tier 3 — Indexed WAL.** Standard vector retrieval via `/stoa query`.

**Index-absent fallback:** when `.stoa/index/wal_index.sqlite` is missing, tiers 2+3 collapse into headline-grep + LLM-pairwise. The verdict line names degraded confidence honestly.

**Why:** under [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first), the subagent layer chooses slurp-vs-retrieve, but the three tiers must all be in scope on the retrieve path too. Without explicit Tier 1, intra-batch contradictions in proposed batches get missed. Without explicit Tier 2, just-appended entries get missed until the post-commit hook fires.

**How to apply:** this rule extends §"WAL access pattern" in the slim spec — current text states the trivial-vs-non-trivial split; new §"Coherence-shape consultation" adds the three-tier rule. `/stoa coherence` procedure implements all three tiers; cadences that invoke it inherit the rule automatically.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first), [`89370375`](#89370375f20943ba8d06a319a429ed08--decision--2026-05-18) (fidelity ladder), [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17) (lazy refresh — Tier 2 mechanism).

## 8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Subagent slurps when feasible; parent stays lean; slurp cost paid per-checkpoint, not per-turn.**

`/stoa coherence` invocations route through a subagent that chooses between two paths:
- **Slurp path:** WAL size < ~30% of subagent's context budget → subagent loads the entire WAL into its own context, reasons directly over the corpus. Best fidelity per [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18).
- **Retrieve path:** WAL too large for slurp → high-k retrieval + LLM classification on returned candidates.

The parent (refining session) never carries the WAL in its context. The subagent pays the slurp cost per-checkpoint invocation. The WAL stays out of every-turn parent context but lands in subagent context when needed for high-fidelity reasoning.

**Why:** the parent's context is precious — it holds the live refining work. Loading the WAL into parent every turn would (a) pay the slurp cost continuously, (b) compete with task-work tokens, (c) cache-thrash across compactions. Subagent-pays-the-cost shifts the spending to checkpoint moments where the value is realized; parent stays operationally lean.

The ~30% threshold leaves the subagent ~70% of its context window for reasoning headroom. At 200K subagent contexts, that's ~60K WAL tokens — roughly 200-400 entries at typical sizes. As context windows grow (1M+ already exists), the slurp-feasible band grows with them.

**How to apply:**
- `/stoa coherence` always invokes a subagent (parent never reads the WAL beyond grep-for-specific-hex calls).
- Subagent reads the WAL size first (line count, byte count); compares against its budget; picks the path.
- Slurp path: subagent uses Read to load `context_log.md`; reasons; returns `[stoa-coherence]` block to parent.
- Retrieve path: subagent calls `/stoa query`; reads returned bodies; classifies; returns block.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle this operationalizes), [`a8a0b715`](#a8a0b7155913467b9c1ab1cbc027437a--decision--2026-05-18) (three-tier rule), [`89370375`](#89370375f20943ba8d06a319a429ed08--decision--2026-05-18) (fidelity ladder), [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10) (subagent delegation pattern), [`f3a8d61`](context_log.md#f3a8d61--observation--2026-05-10) (context-growth bet that makes this viable).

## b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706 — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Extract /stoa coherence as a triple-mode primitive; route 6 cadences through it.**

`/stoa coherence` becomes the unified primitive for coherence-shape WAL operations:

- `/stoa coherence <candidate>` — 1-vs-corpus classification. Used by A1 (coherence check on AI-proposed entries), A3 (phase-settlement batch), B3 (pre-commit WAL audit), B7 (end-of-impl audit), C-PassB (pre-commit hook AI-instruction handoff).
- `/stoa coherence --pairwise <M> <N>` — M×N pairwise classification across two committed-entry sets. Invoked by cadence #6 ([`7c4b9d2`](context_log.md#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12)) within `/stoa pull`'s outer procedure.
- `/stoa coherence --internal-sweep` — M×M conflict-detection across the full WAL (or a filtered subset). Invoked by cadence #5's WAL internal-conflict sweep ([`1b5d9f7`](context_log.md#1b5d9f7--decision--2026-05-11)).

All three modes return classified buckets in unified vocabulary: **Superseding** (new contradicts prior; rollback recommended), **Converging** (independent same-conclusion; cross-ref recommended), **Adjacent** (related, not contradicting; Refs: recommended). Cadence #6's prior CLEAN/CONVERGENT/CONTRADICTING vocabulary is rolled back to this unified set (rollback entry follows in this batch).

**Output shape:** `[stoa-coherence]` block (informational, not blocking) with the three buckets populated. Operator decides whether to act. Operator may always override with `/stoa coherence` invocation directly.

**Why:** the classification operation (Superseding/Converging/Adjacent) is shared across A1/A3/B3/B5/B6/B7/C-PassB. Without a shared primitive, each cadence reinvents the procedure — vocabulary drifts, AI instruction-following degrades, edits ripple unpredictably. One primitive with three modes makes the AI's task uniform: identify candidate(s) → call `/stoa coherence` → surface block in cadence's idiom.

**How to apply:**
- Dispatcher gains a `/stoa coherence` subcommand block (Phase 2 spec edit).
- Cadences A1, A3, B3, B5-internal-conflict, B7, C-PassB rewrite their procedural prose to invoke `/stoa coherence` (Phase 2 spec edit).
- Cadence #6 keeps its outer procedure for pull mechanics; its classification step (Step 5) invokes `/stoa coherence --pairwise`.
- `/stoa help` lists `/stoa coherence`; prose↔subcommand mapping routes natural-language doubt cues to it (Phase 2 spec edit).

**Coherence-check findings:**
- Superseding: [`7c4b9d2`](context_log.md#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12) — partial; cadence #6 vocabulary clause. Rollback follows in this batch. [`3b4f7a2`](context_log.md#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15) — partial; Pass B procedure invocation point. Rollback follows in this batch.
- Converging: [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) (broadened coherence check; already uses Superseding/Converging/Adjacent — Entry 3 finishes the unification). [`6d8a3f1`](context_log.md#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15) (auto-refinement coherence check; same vocabulary; would now route through `/stoa coherence <candidate>`). [`1b5d9f7`](context_log.md#1b5d9f7--decision--2026-05-11) (WAL internal-conflict sweep — `--internal-sweep` mode formalizes this).
- Adjacent: [`b3d2e94`](context_log.md#b3d2e94--decision--2026-05-10) (cadence #3 motivation).

**Refs:** [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15), [`6d8a3f1`](context_log.md#6d8a3f1--decision--2026-05-15), [`1b5d9f7`](context_log.md#1b5d9f7--decision--2026-05-11), [`7c4b9d2`](context_log.md#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12), [`3b4f7a2`](context_log.md#3b4f7a2--decision--2026-05-15), [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`8c65450c`](#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18).

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Rollback [`7c4b9d2`](context_log.md#7c4b9d2--decision--2026-05-12)'s CLEAN/CONVERGENT/CONTRADICTING vocabulary clause — unified to Adjacent/Converging/Superseding.**

## fabf69ef489c47049a1f8a232d124e58 — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Coherence-doubt cues as sibling category to settling-cues — compatibility-doubt + tentative-supersession; fire /stoa coherence pre-settlement.**

Introduce a new cue category alongside the existing settling-cue families ([`4a2e7b3`](context_log.md#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15), [`7b2e4d8`](context_log.md#7b2e4d8--decision--2026-05-14)) that triggers `/stoa coherence` (not a WAL proposal). Two categories:

1. **Compatibility doubt.** Operator explicitly asking "check this against prior arcs."
   - *"is this compatible"* / *"any contradictions"* / *"does this conflict with anything"* / *"does this fit"* / *"do you see a problem"* / *"are we going in circles"*

2. **Tentative supersession.** Operator considering overturning, not yet committed.
   - *"I think we got X wrong"* / *"I'm reconsidering X"* / *"X might not hold anymore"* / *"I'm not sure X still applies"*

**Concrete-proposition requirement.** Cues fire only when the doubt is about a specific proposition (specific proposed decision, specific prior entry, specific arc). Vague musings — *"I'm thinking about doing X"* — are not inflections and do not warrant coherence-check. Decline silently rather than search-on-vapor.

**When-in-doubt-fire rule.** Ambiguity between trigger and non-trigger defaults to firing `/stoa coherence`. False positives are cheap (operator ignores); missed checks are costly. Same discipline as the existing preflight rule (`installkit/stoa.md:121`).

**Non-triggers (explicit):**
- *"is this right?"* — too generic.
- Yes/no responses to small clarifying questions.
- Pure recall (*"what did we say about X"*) — routes to `/stoa query`, no candidate to classify.
- Code-review *"is this good?"* — domain check, not WAL coherence.
- Design-taste questions (*"is this overkill"*, *"does this read well"*) — aesthetic, not coherence.
- Coverage doubt (*"did we miss anything"*) — backstopped by B7 and `/stoa audit`.
- Stress-test (*"what could go wrong"*, *"push back"*) — coherence is one slice, not primary.
- Soft self-doubt (*"hmm, not sure"*, *"this feels off"*, *"wait, I think this doesn't work"*) — auto-refinement cues ([`4a2e7b3`](context_log.md#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15)) + A1 already cover.

**Overlap with auto-refinement cues (named explicitly):** the auto-refinement cue family ([`4a2e7b3`](context_log.md#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15)) includes *"I notice this conflicts with..."* — semantically adjacent to tentative-supersession. Rule: auto-refinement-cues fire AI-side (AI catching its own course-correction → propose WAL entry → A1 → /stoa coherence). Coherence-doubt cues fire operator-side (operator asking AI to check before settlement). Same phrases on different sides of the Human+AI pair; symmetric like other cue categories.

**Why:** existing settling-cues + A1 cover the "log it after settlement" half. Coherence-doubt cues cover the "check it pre-settlement" half — when operator is doubting an in-flight proposition rather than confirming a settled one. Without this category, the operator must explicitly invoke `/stoa coherence`; with it, doubt phrases auto-route.

**How to apply:** Phase 2 spec edit adds the coherence-doubt cue list to §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" (or sibling section). Prose↔subcommand mapping routes the phrases to `/stoa coherence`. Future beta tuning may adjust the phrase list based on operator-reported noise.

**Refs:** [`4a2e7b3`](context_log.md#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15) (auto-refinement cues — sibling category, explicit overlap), [`7b2e4d8`](context_log.md#7b2e4d8--decision--2026-05-14) (named-category restructure of settling-cues), [`4c9a1f6`](context_log.md#4c9a1f6--decision--2026-05-14) (directive-cues), [`8f2a5d3`](context_log.md#8f2a5d3--decision--2026-05-14) (non-trigger discipline), [`b0122b1f`](#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18) (`/stoa coherence` primitive cues route to).

## 0964a9106d4e49b0a780aed64e5948cd — observation — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Known limits of coherence checking — named, not hidden.**

The `/stoa coherence` architecture ships with four named failure modes worth tracking:

1. **Top-k cutoff.** Default `--k 10` for mid-session continuous checks; bumping to `k=20-30` recommended for checkpoint contexts; v1 ships with `k=10` across the board pending tuning data (per [`f85c13dd`](#f85c13dd1d3045a59870b77f1e4bb63b--table--2026-05-18) eval suite). A contradicting entry ranked k+1 by similarity gets silently missed on the retrieve path. Slurp path avoids this; retrieve path inherits it.

2. **Embedding model bias.** BGE-base-en-v1.5 ([`c4f9e87`](context_log.md#c4f9e87--observation--2026-05-17)) is solid for general English; may underperform on specialized domain terminology that diverges from training distribution. Mitigated by AI/LLM pairwise post-filter on returned top-k, not eliminated.

3. **LLM classification errors at the Adjacent/Converging boundary.** The three-bucket classification is fuzzy near boundaries. Near-misses can drift between Adjacent and Converging across runs.

4. **Running coherence cost.** Each `/stoa coherence` invocation adds ~1-3s for retrieval/slurp + LLM classification. At ~30 invocations per active session, that's ~90s of added latency. This is literally Stoa's value-add — the cost is justified — but not free.

**Why this is an observation, not a decision:** these are properties of the architecture, not commitments we're making. Naming them in the WAL means future drift-detection sweeps know to look for signal in these regions, and adopters know what failure modes to flag if they hit them.

**Mitigation pointers:**
- Top-k → telemetry-driven tuning ([`6cca784d`](#6cca784dd8bc492d81cd3367f9173cc1--table--2026-05-18)).
- Model bias → re-embed when a better model ships (install-flow handles this).
- Classification errors → eval suite ([`f85c13dd`](#f85c13dd1d3045a59870b77f1e4bb63b--table--2026-05-18)) gives precision/recall numbers to act on.
- Running cost → batch where possible; subagent caches its slurp within a single invocation; cadence cost-budgets are explicit.

**Refs:** [`b0122b1f`](#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18) (`/stoa coherence` primitive), [`c4f9e87`](context_log.md#c4f9e87--observation--2026-05-17) (BGE empirical), [`6cca784d`](#6cca784dd8bc492d81cd3367f9173cc1--table--2026-05-18) (telemetry table), [`f85c13dd`](#f85c13dd1d3045a59870b77f1e4bb63b--table--2026-05-18) (eval suite table).

## 2385dbac9f574ad4ad68b94c0356e7b3 — observation — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Retrieval improves quality when noise dilutes signal; reduces quality when LLM attention is sufficient. Crossover is size × density × specificity.**

A nuance behind [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle): the principle isn't "always slurp" or "always retrieve" — it's that the choice depends on whether noise dilutes signal in the loaded context.

**Three quality effects of retrieval-based pruning, independent of context budget:**

1. **Attention focusing.** When loaded context contains 10 highly relevant + 90 weakly-relevant entries, attention splits across all 100 and can be misled by surface similarity. Pruning concentrates attention. Quality move at scale.

2. **Synthesis contamination.** The LLM doesn't just attend selectively — it synthesizes ambient signal from everything loaded. Irrelevant entries influence framing, vocabulary, and connections proposed. Pruning eliminates this. **Weakened on curated data** like Stoa's WAL — every entry is at least loosely relevant — but not zero.

3. **Depth-per-entry trade.** Fixed budget: 50 entry headers vs 5 entry full-bodies. Retrieval lets you trade quantity for fidelity per entry.

**Counter-current:** at small scale, the LLM's own attention is a better relevance filter than cosine similarity. Embedding pre-filtering replaces LLM judgment with a degraded proxy. Pure quality LOSS when full-load is feasible.

**Principle:** retrieval improves quality when noise dilutes or contaminates signal in the loaded context; reduces quality when LLM attention is sufficient. The crossover depends on:
- **Corpus size** (more entries = more dilution).
- **Relevance density** (curated corpora = higher density = LLM-attention-friendly).
- **Question specificity** (narrow questions tolerate aggressive pruning; broad orient questions need breadth).

**Why this is an observation:** principled explanation behind [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18); informs `/stoa coherence` subagent's slurp-vs-retrieve choice. Names the trade-off honestly so future tuning has vocabulary.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle), [`f3a8d61`](context_log.md#f3a8d61--observation--2026-05-10) (compaction + context-growth bet), [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10) (scaling cliffs — Entry 8 provides the explanatory mechanism), [`8c65450c`](#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18) (subagent slurp-vs-retrieve operationalization).

## 85d114e2428a460cbfa3851750bc0060 — table — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Tabled: role-partitioning strategy for in-between scale (slurp infeasible but pure RAG insufficient).**

When the WAL outgrows slurp-feasibility (~30% of subagent context budget) but pure RAG retrieval is insufficient for quality, a middle layer becomes valuable: role-partitioning.

**Sketch (not yet specified):**
- AI discovers project roles by clustering WAL entries semantically (architecture, product, test, implementation, UX, etc.). Roles are AI-discovered and evolve, not fixed.
- Role manifest maintained as an artifact; updated during `/stoa audit` sweeps or on milestone boundaries.
- Subagent loads one role's entries + adjacent-role overlap into context; reasons natively.
- Cross-role overlap accepted as token cost for precision; AI tugs on overlap edges when reasoning hits the boundary.
- Pure RAG retrieval reserved for the deepest fallback case (overlap-pull also fails).

**Why tabled:** speculative until adopters hit the scale where this matters. v1 ships binary slurp-vs-RAG. Role-partitioning lands when adopter WAL hits ~5K entries (back-of-envelope: 100K-300K tokens, depending on entry length).

**Revisit triggers:**
- Adopter WAL approaches 5K entries.
- Beta reports of quality degradation at the "too big to slurp, too sparse for RAG" scale.
- Context window growth stalls (changes the slurp-feasibility calculation).

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle role-partitioning extends), [`8c65450c`](#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18) (subagent slurp-vs-retrieve), [`7c2f9b4`](context_log.md#7c2f9b4--observation--2026-05-10) (two-tier WAL — sibling deferred-design entry), [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10) (scalability menu).

## 0b962ef021784f9da224c798f81cdbec — table — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Tabled: post-hoc coherence-check mode — retrieval as second-opinion after Agent has reasoned over slurped WAL.**

Future work: a `/stoa coherence --post-hoc` mode where retrieval is used as a *second opinion* on Agent-direct reasoning, not as a *pre-filter*.

**Sketch:**
- Operator has been refining for some time with the WAL slurped in context (the Agent-first path).
- Before commit (or on demand), invoke `/stoa coherence --post-hoc`: subagent runs retrieval against the candidate(s); compares Agent-cited prior arcs against embedding-similar prior arcs.
- Mismatches between Agent-cited and embedding-similar surface as "you didn't reference these but they look related — relevant?"
- Retrieval as cross-check on Agent judgment, not replacement.

**Why this is interesting:** captures the quality-not-size case for retrieval — even when slurp is feasible, retrieval can backstop attention failures. The Agent doesn't always notice every relevant prior arc; a second opinion catches misses.

**Why tabled:** speculative; not v0.6.0 ship. v1 architecture is slurp-vs-retrieve binary. Post-hoc-as-cross-check is a different invocation pattern that needs validation.

**Revisit triggers:**
- Beta reports of "Agent should have flagged X but didn't" when slurp path was taken.
- Operator demand for explicit cross-check tooling.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first — Entry 12 is a refinement, not a competing path), [`b0122b1f`](#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18) (`/stoa coherence` primitive — host of the future mode), [`9c4d8a2`](context_log.md#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) (CLI-proxy fragility — second-opinion patterns address similar surface-fragility concerns).

## 0f497dce06184620acc06ddc6cfc48bc — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Always-tests + always-tracked discipline for stoa-ai repo — generalized from v0.6.0 scope to ongoing project rule.**

Project-level discipline rule landed in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) §"Testing discipline":

1. **Functional tests** (correctness) accompany every introduction or refinement of behavior — `tests/scenarios.md` + `tests/harness.sh` extensions.
2. **Quality tests** (regression baseline) accompany behavior changes with empirical-quality dimensions — labeled fixtures under `tests/fixtures/`.
3. Every test file is appended to `.stoa/artifacts.md` so cadence #1's drift walk catches behavior-vs-test divergence in future commits.

**Why:** [`ae7bc888`](#ae7bc88826084eac95fbe510ea2a325c--decision--2026-05-18) established the v0.6.0-specific test coverage scope (functional scenarios + labeled fixture for `/stoa coherence`). The general principle — always tests, always tracked — extends that one-shot scope into ongoing project discipline. Without this rule, future behavior additions could ship without coverage and the connection between spec and tests would drift silently.

**How to apply:** AI reads `CLAUDE.md` each session as project guidance. When proposing new behavior, also propose corresponding test scenarios + fixture cases. Cadence #1 (pre-commit drift walk) surfaces missing test updates as `[stoa-propagation]` block findings before commit lands.

**Adopter-visible:** no. This is stoa-ai repo discipline; not part of the install kit. Adopters set their own testing discipline via their own `CLAUDE.md`.

**Refs:** [`ae7bc888`](#ae7bc88826084eac95fbe510ea2a325c--decision--2026-05-18) (v0.6.0 test coverage scope — this generalizes that), [`f2c8e51`](context_log.md#f2c8e51--decision--2026-05-16) (Phase 1A harness expansion — related test infrastructure).

## 7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Tighten stoa-bootcheck output discipline — FIRST CHARACTER rule for AI-instruction compliance.**

The `stoa-bootcheck` subagent's canonical output is one of `clean`, `install-needed`, or one-or-more `[stoa] ...` lines. The slim spec's `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` definition includes WRONG/RIGHT examples that literally call out the preface failure mode (`"All checks pass.\n\nclean"` is WRONG; `"clean"` alone is RIGHT). Despite the in-spec warning, the v0.6.0 bootcheck observed emitting the WRONG pattern during this session's install-state verification (beta-tracker [`9e6c7fc1`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md)).

**Why:** the output is structurally consumed by main-agent code that parses the return for boundary-moment decisions. A friendly-prose preface breaks structural parsing — main-agent expects the first non-empty line to be `clean` / `install-needed` / `[stoa] ...`. Pre-existing across v0.5.x → v0.6.0; v0.6.0 regeneration didn't change the bootcheck definition (no version stamps to bump in that file). Need to escalate the discipline language per the visible-output arc at [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) — tighten wording before going structural.

**How to apply (FIRST CHARACTER rule):** add an emphatic leading directive to the `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` embedded block (in `installkit/stoa.md`):

> **FIRST CHARACTER of your response MUST be the literal letter `c` (for `clean`), `i` (for `install-needed`), or `[` (for a `[stoa] ...` warning line). No leading whitespace, no header line, no friendly preamble. The main-agent parses the first 16 bytes verbatim; any preface breaks structural compliance.**

Place at the top of the subagent's prompt, before the procedure body. If empirical beta data shows the FIRST CHARACTER rule still fails, escalate to (a) a sentinel-wrap (`RETURN: <verdict>`) or (b) a forgiving post-invocation parser in main-agent code.

**Adopter-visible:** yes, on next `/stoa upgrade`. Bootcheck subagent definition is spec-owned (refreshed every upgrade per Step 3).

**Closes:** beta-tracker [`9e6c7fc1`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) — status moves to `applied-upstream-as-WAL-entry-7c3be154`.

**Refs:** [`9e6c7fc1`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) (beta-tracker entry), [`8264e01b`](context_log.md#8264e01b858848f3a184ddd94cae9fc9--decision--2026-05-17) (`[stoa-init]` block format), [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (wording-tightening as escalation path before structural enforcement).

## d0283064d6cc4421a3353ec4304a4d80 — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Structured-selection cues as a sibling category to settling-cues — host tools returning operator option-selections fire as directive-cue settlements.**

Add a new cue category in §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" for tools that return operator selections from AI-presented option sets. The existing settling-cue triggers (yes-/transition-/directive-/lifecycle-/auto-refinement) are phrase-based; an option selected via a structured tool doesn't arrive as a phrase, so the AI may miss the settlement and skip A1 / `/stoa coherence` proposal.

**Known host implementations (as of 2026-05):**
- **Claude Code**: `AskUserQuestion` tool — always available; presents multi-choice + custom-option; returns structured selection.
- **Codex CLI**: `ask_user_question` (also referenced as `request_user_input`) — same shape; **Plan-mode-gated** currently (open issues #10384, #11536, #11565 push to widen to Default mode); stripped from `codex exec` (non-interactive) sessions.

**Rule:** when a host-provided structured-selection tool returns an operator selection AFTER the AI presented the option set as a substantive decision-axis (proposal-and-agree exchange in tool form), treat the selection as a **directive-cue settlement**. Fire A1; invoke `/stoa coherence` against the proposed-and-selected option; propose a WAL entry before executing.

**Non-triggers (avoid cue noise):**
- Tool-result for an option set that's NOT a decision-axis (e.g., AI asked *"which file should I read?"* → operator picks one; not an inflection).
- Plain conversational selections (operator types *"option B"* in chat) — already covered by directive-cue list; no new category needed.
- Cancel / decline returns — operator chose NOT to settle; treat as transition-cue or no-cue depending on context.

**How to apply:** spec patch in v0.6.1 adds this category in §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" alongside settling-cue triggers and coherence-doubt cues. Cue is scoped by shape (structured-selection from host tool), not by tool name, so future tools fit without spec churn.

**Severity / coverage gap honestly named:**
- Claude Code: `AskUserQuestion` always available — full coverage.
- Codex CLI Plan mode: covered.
- Codex CLI Default mode / `codex exec`: structured tool unavailable; settlement happens via plain text — existing directive-cue list catches. Backstops (cadence #3, cadence #7) catch anything that slips.

**Adopter-visible:** yes — new cue category in slim spec; reaches adopters on next `/stoa upgrade`. Codex Plan-mode adopters benefit immediately; Default-mode adopters fall through to the existing phrase-based settling-cues.

**Refs:** [`fabf69ef`](#fabf69ef489c47049a1f8a232d124e58--decision--2026-05-18) (coherence-doubt cues — sibling category pattern), [`4a2e7b3`](context_log.md#4a2e7b3--decision--2026-05-15) (auto-refinement cues — settling-cue category #5), [`7b2e4d8`](context_log.md#7b2e4d8--decision--2026-05-14) (named-category restructure of settling-cues), [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (visible-output escalation arc — structured tools are structural form of cue).

## fc3d3c37688c4391bcd95d8e7787698c — decision — 2026-05-18

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Pre-delegation settling principle — settle the decision-axis in the human+AI pair before delegating to subagent or scripted skill. Subagents and skills implement; they do not decide.**

New operational principle (sibling to Agent-first per [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18)). Closes a gap surfaced in this session's architectural Q&A about subagent-internal decisions and scripted-skill suppression of settling-cue discipline.

**Principle:** if you're about to delegate a substantive decision (architectural choice, design tradeoff, settlement of a degree of freedom) to a subagent or scripted skill, settle the decision-axis in the human+AI pair first via the normal refining flow. The settlement gets a WAL entry; the subagent/skill then executes against the settled decision.

**Why:** subagents don't auto-load `CLAUDE.md` (Stoa rules aren't active inside them); there's no operator-in-the-loop for WAL approval; subagent-internal decisions become opaque to the WAL. Similarly, skills with tightly-scripted procedures bypass the proposal-and-agree exchange that triggers settling-cue discipline — execution happens without inflection-capture. Pre-delegation settling pushes the inflection back to the moment where the human+AI pair can engage; the WAL captures the decision + the delegation boundary.

**How to apply:**
- Before invoking a subagent for substantive design/implementation work (not just retrieval, classification, or other procedural work — those are fine to delegate without pre-settlement), surface the decision-axis being delegated; propose a WAL entry capturing what's being asked + the chosen approach.
- Before invoking a scripted skill that will make AI decisions during its run, settle the decision-axis the skill will act on first.
- Subagent/skill returns its result; parent + operator process; cadence #7 (end-of-impl audit) catches any decisions that crystallized during execution but weren't pre-settled.
- `/stoa coherence` is the canonical example of procedural delegation done right: subagent does classification (a procedure), not architectural decisions. The classification vocabulary + slurp-vs-retrieve choice are already settled at the methodology level; the subagent applies them.

**Severity / enforceability:** principle-level, not structurally enforced. A sufficiently lazy delegation could bypass this. Backstops: cadence #7 (end-of-impl audit) + cadence #3 (pre-commit WAL audit). Worth watching for beta evidence of decisions slipping through delegation boundaries — would warrant escalation to a structured pre-delegation preflight (visible block) in a future version.

**Adopter-visible:** yes — new operational principle in slim spec §"Operational principles". Reaches adopters on next `/stoa upgrade`.

**Refs:** [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first principle — sibling operational principle), [`b0122b1f`](#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18) (`/stoa coherence` primitive — example of procedural delegation done right), [`8c65450c`](#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18) (subagent slurp pattern — procedural, not decisional), [`c8b4d09`](context_log.md#c8b4d09--decision--2026-05-08) (loose framework, AI as interpreter — pre-delegation settling preserves the human+AI pair as the inflection-resolver).

## d0bc5c08b6534676aedd09d109dd65e9 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Heritage canon explicitly welcomed into the thesis as supporting context, not as novelty-undermining.**

A sixty-year arc of work in design rationale, cognitive science, and knowledge management directly supports Stoa's load-bearing claims. Surfaced during structured deliberation: Engelbart (H-LAM/T amplification framework), Rittel & Kunz (IBIS), Newell & Simon (problem-space theory), Schön (reflective practitioner), Hutchins (distributed cognition), Nonaka (SECI externalization), Toulmin (argument model), Polanyi (tacit dimension), Star & Griesemer (boundary objects), Nygard (ADR append-only discipline), Evans (DDD bounded contexts), Skelton & Pais (Team Topologies cognitive load).

**Why:** the operator's framing developed independently of this canon. Claiming the lineage strengthens the thesis (positions Stoa in heritage) and pre-empts the academic-naivety read. The contribution Stoa makes (AI-as-maintainer closing the historical adoption gap, cross-forest semantic merge, scope-by-design) becomes sharper when bounded against the lineage.

**How to apply:** all references integrated into [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §Supporting canon subsections per claim. Each claim cites the directly-relevant ancestors. No claim of novelty for the substrate itself; novelty is named precisely (the maintainer claim, cross-forest semantic merge, attributed AI co-authorship).

**Refs:** [`d641aaf0`](#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19) (arc-formalization, sibling); [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §References.

## d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Decision-arc / inflection-point / decision-forest vocabulary preserved; arc formalized as the `Refs:`-connected subgraph emergent at AI query time, not a first-class data shape.**

The "decision arc" concept was previously fuzzy (no formal definition; risked the "metaphor wearing engineer's clothes" critique). Three options considered: (a) explicit `arc_id` field on entries, (b) transitive closure over `Refs:` edges, (c) AI inference at query time. Chose (c) with (b) as the underlying mechanism.

**Why:** consistent with founding principle #1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter). No schema migration required. `Refs:` density becomes the lever; sparse refs produce diffuse arcs, dense refs produce tight arcs. AI materializes arcs at query time using the existing data model.

**How to apply:**
- [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §"What Stoa is" already carries the formalization.
- [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"WAL access pattern" needs a one-paragraph spec addition defining an *arc* as the `Refs:`-connected subgraph terminating at a settled state, materialized by the AI at query time. The *decision forest* is the union of all arcs.
- Vocabulary (arc / inflection point / forest) preserved as-is. Topologically the structure is a forest of DAGs; rollback creates apparent loops via supersession nodes, not true cycles.

**Refs:** [`d0bc5c08`](#d0bc5c08b6534676aedd09d109dd65e9--decision--2026-05-19) (heritage canon, sibling); [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) needs the corresponding spec patch.

## 2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Scope-by-design framing supersedes "amplifies, does not grant intelligence" as the load-bearing point: substance quality is the human's responsibility; coherence quality is the AI's. Stoa makes no claims on providing intelligence.**

The prior framing ("methodology amplifies; does not grant intelligence") is correct but imprecise. Scope-by-design names *who is responsible for what*: substance comes from the human (engaged-expert input), coherence comes from the AI (the maintainer). This closes the working-memory-atrophy / cognitive-offloading critique cleanly — Stoa makes no claim on preventing atrophy; substance is operator responsibility by design.

**Why:** the new framing is empirically cleaner (testable per role) and rhetorically stronger (names the division of labor instead of negating a claim). It also makes the empirical bet on AI calibration explicit (coherence = AI's job, calibration is the measurable instrument).

**How to apply:**
- [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) Claim 4 already lands with this framing.
- [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"Founding principles" carries the prior framing and needs an edit: principle name stays ("amplifies"), but the explanatory text shifts to the substance/coherence division of labor.

**Refs:** [`9ac5eeb7`](#9ac5eeb7ea2e4c8e9016b7841c6c2b40--observation--2026-05-19) (force-multiplier observation, sibling); [`c171912f`](#c171912fb2ff4ce8ae27913df9987da2--decision--2026-05-19) (AI calibration bet, sibling).

Cadence #6's cross-forest semantic merge is the central novel mechanism in Stoa. No current methodology or tool offers continuous, automated, audit-trailed semantic merge with attribution. Two-tier consensus claim: procedurally verifiable standalone (cadence #6 verdicts + attribution + audit trail); substantively verifiable with an ontology substrate underneath.

**Why:** previously buried inside "AI's load-bearing roles." Promoting it makes the cross-team scale claim explicit and testable, and clarifies what makes Stoa different from ADR / RFC / decision-log patterns at multi-author scale.

## 295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Reconstruction-fidelity A/B testing canonized as the post-hoc calibration metric for autonomous WAL behavior.**

Architecture moves from live in-session compliance verification (visible-output blocks operator could ignore) to post-hoc reconstruction-fidelity audit. The A/B test: give the AI the WAL with the full session jsonl; give it the WAL alone; compare the artifacts produced. Both branches are non-deterministic generations from the same agent; the delta attributes to WAL coverage.

**Why:** three live-test users (operator + 2 others) all said "yup" without reading visible-output blocks. Live compliance verification doesn't work empirically — it becomes ceremony. Post-hoc reconstruction-fidelity testing measures whether the WAL captured load-bearing context, regardless of operator in-session attention.

**How to apply:**
- Beta-phase calibration uses session-jsonl capture at company-deployment level (per [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19)) to run the A/B test offline.
- Acceptance criteria per WAL entry type:
  - `decision`: artifact reproduces within original-generation variance
  - `won't-do`: reconstruction does NOT produce the foreclosed artifact (negative test)
  - `rollback`: reconstruction honors supersession (new state, not old)
  - `branch` / `table` / `observation`: downstream behavior change reflects entry
- Per-type metric tracking required to prevent `decision`-class dominance in the aggregate signal.

**Open residual:** the metric optimizes for the original artifact, which locks in original-quality. Sharper objective (artifact meets same requirements as original) is harder to instrument; deferred.

**Refs:** [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19) (session-jsonl capture); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes framing — reconstruction-fidelity is the audit of WAL-as-encoder).

## a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**PNG-bytes framing canonized: the WAL is AI-format with human-occasional inspection; humans interact with AI-rendered surfaces, not raw entries.**

The WAL is to AI as PNG bytes are to a viewer: encoded representation, not user interface. Text format is implementation-contingent (could be compressed binary plus a viewer with no methodology change). The human interface is what the AI surfaces: settlement proposals, coherence checks, conflict verdicts, distilled context at session start.

**Why:** answers the design-rationale-rarely-read empirical critique (Simula / Moran-Carroll pattern: even when rationale was captured, it wasn't consulted). Humans don't read raw WAL; AI consumes it and surfaces what matters at the right moments. Read-burden converts to trust-burden in the AI's distillation, which becomes the calibration question (see [`c171912f`](#c171912fb2ff4ce8ae27913df9987da2--decision--2026-05-19)).

**How to apply:**
- [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) Claim 3 response carries this framing.
- [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"WAL access pattern" can be sharpened with the AI-format-vs-rendered-surface distinction.

**Bounded:** humans still read the WAL at cadence #6 CONTRADICTING resolution, cross-team accountability, and onboarding context reconstruction. Framing is *runtime-primary AI, audit-occasional human*, not *AI-only*. Audit-trail property is preserved by the WAL staying text + git-tracked; if implementation switches to binary, the viewer becomes a required dependency rather than incidental.

**Refs:** [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity tests the encoder); [`c171912f`](#c171912fb2ff4ce8ae27913df9987da2--decision--2026-05-19) (calibration bet).

## 24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Session-jsonl capture at controlled-rollout deployments is the calibration mechanism for the beta phase. Baked-in telemetry is not pursued for the OSS phase.**

Two-phase split. Controlled-rollout phase (company-deployment): ship the full session jsonl; run reconstruction-fidelity A/B test offline; iterate on AI behavior. OSS phase: no baked-in telemetry (acknowledged failure mode in OSS-adjacent dev-tool projects); rely on issue reports plus user observation.

**Why:** captures the calibration signal during the phase where the operator controls deployment; doesn't try to extend telemetry into OSS-land where the data wouldn't flow anyway. Calibration tuning happens during controlled phase; the methodology hardens before OSS release.

**How to apply:**
- Tooling: session-jsonl capture pipeline + reconstruction-fidelity test runner.
- Beta sprint scope: 3-person sprint (3 weeks), then 2 teams of similar size, then an org, then the company. Asymptote target: ~3 months.
- Founding principle #2 (in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md): "refining sessions live in live AI conversation only; no on-disk file") needs a clarifying edit to permit passive telemetry capture in controlled-rollout deployments. Rule shape: no *authored* on-disk refining artifact; passive capture only; bounded to controlled-rollout.

**Open residual:** post-OSS calibration drift goes undetected. Bet is that controlled-phase calibration is sufficient and the methodology doesn't require ongoing tuning at OSS scale.

**Refs:** [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity metric); [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) §"Founding principles" needs the telemetry clarification.

## 7bf2b8c35ad34dbd93c45c3b3688f799 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Stoa's knowledge graph identified as the architectural complement for substantive consensus at enterprise scale. Two-tier consensus claim formalized: procedural standalone, substantive with KG underneath.**

Stoa's cadence #6 cross-forest semantic merge depends on cross-vocabulary translation; AI translation quality bounds the merge. A knowledge graph anchors entries to shared concepts, collapsing translation into a deterministic graph lookup for the domains the KG covers. Stoa's knowledge-graph platform provides this substrate at enterprise scale (several large enterprises); KG bootstrap is solvable via Stoa's modeling-experts + AI + UX + pipelines engagement.

**Why:** the boundary-object / translation residual raised against Claim 6 is real where teams have divergent vocabularies. Standalone Stoa stays at procedural verifiability. Stoa-on-Stoa delivers substantive verifiability where the ontology covers the domain. Bidirectional fit: Stoa needs translation substrate; Stoa's KG needs a decision-rationale layer over its data.

**How to apply:**
- [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §"Architectural complement" carries this.
- Any given engagement must be explicit about which tier (procedural / substantive) it's delivering. Procedural is the everywhere-default; substantive requires the KG.
- This is also the architectural piece that scales Stoa beyond software engineering into broader enterprise decision-making domains (finsec, supply chain, healthcare, regulated industries generally).

**Refs:** [`323aea18`](#323aea18c6c9410ba9f284786083f479--decision--2026-05-19) (verifiable consensus thesis point); [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §"Architectural complement".

## 9ac5eeb7ea2e4c8e9016b7841c6c2b40 — observation — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Stoa positions as a force-multiplier for the engaged-expert pool against the broader human-knowledge atrophy trend.**

Two trend observations from the cognitive-offloading literature: AI capability is rising sharply (Karpathy's Software 3.0, agentic engineering, asymmetry-of-verification regime); engaged human expertise is declining across the population (MIT Media Lab cognitive-debt study, Aalto skill-erosion research, Springer competency-erosion analysis). Stoa's bet is on the engaged-expert + AI pair specifically. The methodology amplifies engaged experts; non-engaged users get coherent records of mediocre decisions. The selection for engagement is intentional, not an adoption defect.

**Why it matters:** reframes the "smart-people target" concern. Not a market constraint but a deliberate selection for the cohort Stoa can amplify against a degrading baseline. The shrinking pool of engaged experts is the target population.

**Strategic implication:** sales / adoption positioning aligns with engaged-expert tier of any organization (architects, principal engineers, PMs, executives operating in their depth-of-domain). Non-engaged-tier adoption is acceptable but not the target.

**Refs:** [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (scope-by-design — the "what amplifies" claim); [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) Claim 4 response.

## c171912fb2ff4ce8ae27913df9987da2 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**AI classification calibration on Stoa's load-bearing tasks (settlement-cue recognition, cadence #6 verdicts, reconstruction-fidelity) is the accepted load-bearing empirical bet of the methodology. Aligned with industry trajectory; not viewed as thesis-threatening.**

The hallucination-detection / LLM-calibration literature consistently shows that AI produces high-confidence wrong outputs in some regimes. Stoa's cadence #6 has silent verdict surfaces (Converging / Adjacent classifications are not per-instance audited). The methodology accepts this bet rather than mitigating it, because (a) the bet is the same one the broader industry is making, (b) the reconstruction-fidelity loop catches downstream incoherence over time, (c) Stoa is the methodology for producing the right constraints to feed the AI — better experts and better models produce better outputs.

**Why:** the alternative (refuse to ship until calibration is solved) loses ground while the industry trajectory pulls forward. The methodology proceeds with the bet named and instrumented, not mitigated.

**How to apply:**
- Instrumentation: reconstruction-fidelity A/B test per [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19).
- Mitigation for silent-verdict surface (cadence #6 Converging / Adjacent classifications): bias the classifier toward over-flagging Superseding; consider periodic cross-checks with a different model or prompt.
- The substantive tier (per [`7bf2b8c3`](#7bf2b8c35ad34dbd93c45c3b3688f799--decision--2026-05-19)) narrows the calibration question further by anchoring to a KG, converting free-text classification into graph lookup.

**Refs:** [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity metric); [`7bf2b8c3`](#7bf2b8c35ad34dbd93c45c3b3688f799--decision--2026-05-19) (substantive tier narrows the bet); [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md) §The empirical bets.

## 9f70a1f3b299483cad04fd2bb6382e44 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Tracked-artifacts list expanded to include `installkit/stoa.md` and `docs/thesis.md`. Per Stoa's own principle that the WAL is the source of truth, every artifact (including the canonical install kit) is a downstream render and should be tracked for drift against WAL decisions.**

Previously, `installkit/stoa.md` was excluded from `.stoa/artifacts.md` on the rationale "it IS the source of truth; tracking it against itself doesn't make sense." That conflates two roles: (a) the canonical methodology spec that adopters fetch, and (b) the durable record of methodology decisions. Per Stoa's founding principles, only the WAL plays role (b); the install kit is itself a render of WAL decisions, subject to the same drift surfaced by cadence #1 against any other artifact. `docs/thesis.md` was also untracked; same logic applies — the thesis is the operator's position paper and should stay coherent with WAL evolution.

**Why:** the compensation argument (WAL entries' "How to apply" sections name installkit edits explicitly) works in theory but accumulates silent drift in practice when operators defer propagation. Tracking gives cadence #1 a deterministic surface for catching the drift at commit time. The four recent entries [`d641aaf0`](#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19), [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19), [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19), and [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) all named installkit patches that would have surfaced as drift findings if installkit had been tracked.

**How to apply:**
- Edit `.stoa/artifacts.md` to add two entries:
  - `installkit/stoa.md` — canonical install kit; self-extracting; the methodology spec adopters fetch. Drift candidate whenever WAL decisions land that change methodology, cadence shape, settling-cue lists, attribution format, founding principles, or AI-instruction blocks.
  - `docs/thesis.md` — operator's position paper on Stoa's foundations; six load-bearing claims with supporting and opposing canon plus reflexive disclosure. Drift candidate when methodology framing, the six claims, or the empirical bets evolve.
- Pre-commit cadence #1 now walks both files on every commit; drift surfaces in the `[stoa-propagation]` block.

**Refs:** [`d641aaf0`](#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19), [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19), [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19), [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) — the four recent entries that named installkit patches and motivated this change.

## 7025abc8aa154dae857770115c4e6442 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Arc-emergence elevated from spec note to Operational Principle. The stance "arcs are emergent, not stored" sits alongside Agent-first quality and pre-delegation settling as a concrete-architecture principle that flows from §Founding principles #1.**

[`d641aaf0`](#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19) settled the arc data-model choice (`Refs:`-connected subgraph, materialized by AI at query time, no first-class arc objects) and pointed to §"WAL access pattern" for the spec addition. On reflection, the rule has two layers: a definition layer (what an arc is) and a stance layer (arcs are emergent rather than stored). The stance layer is principle-shaped — it encodes a deliberate design choice flowing from "loose framework, AI as interpreter" rather than mere terminology — and belongs in §"Operational principles" with the other principles of the same shape ([`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) Agent-first; [`fc3d3c37`](#fc3d3c37688c4391bcd95d8e7787698c--decision--2026-05-18) pre-delegation settling).

**Why:** principles land where the AI encounters them every session (read in `installkit/stoa.md` on every load); spec notes live in reference sections looked up on demand. The arc-emergence stance is a design constraint the AI should honor whenever the question "should I store this structurally?" arises. That's principle-tier visibility, not reference-section visibility.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` §"Operational principles" gains a third principle. Suggested wording:

  > **Arcs are emergent, not stored.** An *arc* is the `Refs:`-connected subgraph terminating at a settled state. Multiple arcs share entries when an inflection touches multiple lines of design. The *decision forest* is the union of all arcs in the WAL. The AI traverses `Refs:` edges to materialize arcs at query time; arcs are not represented as a first-class data shape. This follows §Founding principles #1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter): trust AI to surface structure from the existing graph rather than encoding it in schema. See WAL [`d641aaf0`](context_log.md#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19) and [`7025abc8`](context_log.md#7025abc8aa154dae857770115c4e6442--decision--2026-05-19).

- `d641aaf0`'s "How to apply" pointed to §"WAL access pattern"; treat as superseded for placement only. The decision content of `d641aaf0` is unchanged.

**Refs:** [`d641aaf0`](#d641aaf03caf4930b83946c67362b346--decision--2026-05-19) (original arc-emergence decision; placement now refined here); [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (Agent-first — sibling operational principle); [`fc3d3c37`](#fc3d3c37688c4391bcd95d8e7787698c--decision--2026-05-18) (pre-delegation settling — sibling operational principle); [`c8b4d09`](context_log.md#c8b4d09--decision--2026-05-08) (loose framework, AI as interpreter — founding principle #1, the source).

## a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Autonomous WAL management. AI owns all WAL coherence work (writing, classification, batching, committing); operator owns substance. Propose-confirm gate dissolves.**

Realization of FP4 ([`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19)) applied consistently. Operator brings substance — the conversation, the decisions being made; AI brings coherence — recording, classification, surfacing, reconciliation, supersession. The previous propose-then-confirm-then-append loop asked the operator to do AI's coherence work; empirical beta data showed it degraded to rubber-stamp ([`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19)). Removing the gate aligns the methodology with its own principles.

**What changes operationally:**
- AI judges what gets logged, what type, what granularity, what order, when to commit.
- Operator touchpoints retained: substance (the conversation), explicit-log primitive (*"log this"* / *"WAL it"*), `/stoa coherence <subject>` ask on demand, `/stoa audit`, cadence-#6 Superseding-verdict resolution menus, harness-level commit permission, classification override on surfaced findings.
- Operator no longer touches: whether to log, entry type/order/wording, when to commit, coherence-classification confirmation on routine appends.

**Symmetric H/AI trigger logic.** Settling cues fire on the same rules regardless of which side emits — substance over origin. AI-side auto-refinement cues, operator-side directive/yes/lifecycle cues, structured-selection returns — all promote to T2 by the same AI judgment criteria.

**Why:** the propose-confirm loop violated FP4 (substance/coherence division of labor) and the PNG-bytes framing ([`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) — WAL is AI-format; humans interact with rendered surfaces, not raw entries). Empirical: three live operators rubber-stamped without reading; ceremony does not produce signal.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: rewrite §"`[stoa]` proactive suggestion shape" to remove propose-then-append framing; rewrite cadences #3, #4, #7 procedures; soften §"WAL guardrail" operator-override language (closed further by [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19)).
- Embedded hook block: rewrite Pass A AI-instruction stderr text (draft + append + re-stage + retry, or `--no-verify` + observation on no-decision diff).
- Operator-facing touchpoints listed clearly in the slim section.

**Refs:** [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (FP4 — spine of the shift); [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity as audit; rubber-stamp empirical); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes framing); v0.7.0 batch siblings — [`b90a584f`](#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19), [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19), [`b237c4ea`](#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19), [`92cddf26`](#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19), [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19), [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19), [`33708824`](#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19), [`d7c66232`](#d7c66232ee4a4a97a93ec56342fcc150--table--2026-05-19), [`001ae82f`](#001ae82f78e040ada6e7217bd8cb922d--observation--2026-05-19).

## b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`[stoa-preflight]` and `[stoa-propagation]` visible-output compliance blocks deprecated. Live compliance verification is empirically ceremony; reconstruction-fidelity (post-hoc, beta-calibration) and `/stoa audit` (operator-invoked, session-time) carry audit weight instead.**

The visible-output block pattern (introduced in v0.5.x and v0.6.0 to backstop AI-discipline failures) was an escalation from wording-tightening to visibility per the arc at [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12). Empirical data ([`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19)): three live operators acknowledged the blocks without reading them — the rubber-stamp pattern. Visibility produced ceremony, not signal.

**What stays:**
- `[stoa-init]` boot block on session boundaries — different purpose (install-state probe evidence, not behavioral compliance). Unchanged.
- Informational `[stoa]` chat lines (artifact tracking suggestions, drift signals, chat-anchor on T2 writes per [`33708824`](#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19)). These are AI-rendered surfaces in the PNG-bytes sense ([`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19)); they communicate without gating.

**What goes:**
- `[stoa-preflight]` block at settling cues / phase-settlement offers — removed.
- `[stoa-propagation]` block at pre-commit drift walk — removed. Cadence #1 still runs internally (AI walks tracked artifacts pre-commit); just no visible compliance evidence.

**`/stoa audit` Sweep 2 reframes** from *"compliance verification of visible blocks"* to *"audit AI's autonomous WAL management retroactively"* — missed promotions (decisions visible in code/conversation without T2 entries), over-promotions (T2 entries that look like trajectory texture), miscalibrated coherence findings. Becomes the primary operator-facing audit loop under v0.7.0.

**Why:** the visible-block pattern was load-bearing only as long as the AI behavior it backstopped degraded silently. Under autonomy + AI-managed coherence ([`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19)), the failure modes shift: the question is no longer *"did AI do the discipline?"* but *"did AI's autonomous judgments produce a coherent WAL?"* Live-turn compliance verification doesn't answer the latter; reconstruction-fidelity does, post-hoc.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: delete the `[stoa-preflight]` rule + format + rationale block; delete the `[stoa-propagation]` rule + format + rationale block.
- Cadence #3 procedure removes "emit `[stoa-preflight]`" requirement; runs as internal AI walk.
- Cadence #1 procedure removes "emit `[stoa-propagation]`" requirement; runs as internal AI walk.
- `/stoa audit` dispatcher: Sweep 2 procedure rewrites per the autonomy-audit framing.

## b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Three-tier WAL model. T1: in-memory conversation (mutable). T2: `context_log.md` file (strictly append-only at write-time). T3: git commits (batched at strong cues). T1↔T2 consistency is multi-layered, not pure discipline.**

Architecture under autonomy: WAL operations span three levels with distinct invariants.

- **T1 — in-memory (conversation context).** Where inflections originate and trajectory texture lives. Fully mutable; AI can iterate, summarize, retract. Subject to total loss at `/compact`, `/clear`, host crash — bounded loss per FP2. Trajectory texture (misreadings, exploratory thought, alignment-on-meaning chatter) lives here exclusively.
- **T2 — `context_log.md` file.** Strictly append-only at write-time. No drafting carve-out, no same-turn edits, no body adjustments. AI must get entries right on first write or append a `rollback`. Only structural-integrity repairs allowed (separator insertion; post-pull merge fixes — existing carve-out). The drafting-iteration carve-out collapses into T1 only.
- **T3 — git commits.** AI batches T2 appends and commits at strong cues per [`92cddf26`](#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19). Visible to humans; distributable; the durable record across machines/clones.

**T1↔T2 consistency — multi-layered (operational, not punt-to-audit):**

1. **Active chat anchor at every T2 write** (per [`33708824`](#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19)). Informational `[stoa]` line in same turn — operator notification + AI turn-anchor + structural visibility against silent omission.
2. **Discipline rule.** Once an inflection is in T2, T1 understanding is subordinate. T1 refinements that contradict T2 must promote via WAL types — `rollback` (supersedes), `branch` (forks), or fresh entry with `Refs:` (extends).
3. **Self-coherence at per-T2-write** (per [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19)). AI considers consistency against this session's recent T2 writes (working memory); atomic-pair supersession when detected.
4. **Cadence backstops.** Pre-commit WAL audit (#3 — diff-shaped detection of code-bound supersessions); pre-compact/clear sweep (#4 — promotes T1 realizations before context loss); `/stoa audit` (#5 — retroactive operator-facing).

The layers structurally reinforce the discipline; they do not enforce it (AI is the writer; there's no external gate). The methodology trusts AI's coherence work per FP4 and uses these layers to keep T1↔T2 drift bounded to short windows.

**Bootcheck orphan-T2 probe (new in v0.7.0).** New session start probes for uncommitted T2 appends (T2 ahead of T3 — prior session ended without lifecycle flush). On detect, the `[stoa-init]` block surfaces hex IDs of orphan entries; new AI commits them as-is at next strong cue (T2 immutability means no edits). If new session disagrees with prior session's entries, rollback discipline applies — append a `rollback`, original stays.

**Why:** the prior model conflated *"AI authored"* with *"AI may edit."* The 3-tier split makes the append-only invariant precise: append-only operates at the file-write boundary (T2), not at the git-commit boundary (T3). T1 absorbs drafting iteration; T2 is the WAL's durable shape; T3 is human-visible distribution. The cleaner invariant raises AI's quality bar on T2 writes (no retroactive cleanup), which is the right calibration under autonomy.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: new §"Three-tier WAL model" introducing the tiers + the consistency-layers list + the orphan-T2 probe mention.
- §"WAL guardrail" updates: drafting-iteration carve-out scopes to T1 only; T2-write boundary is the immutability frontier.
- `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`: add the orphan-T2 probe step.

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy shift — context for the model); [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (FP4 — spine); [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19) (two-tier coherence — uses this tier model); [`33708824`](#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19) (chat anchor — Layer 1 mechanism); [`b237c4ea`](#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (T1→T2 promotion target); [`92cddf26`](#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19) (T2→T3 batching).
