## b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**T1 → T2 promotion calibration: reconstruction-fidelity yardstick. AI judges each T1 candidate against the question *"would skipping this entry diverge the reconstruction from the intended artifact?"* Default-to-no-entry under uncertainty.**

The promotion rule the AI applies, continuously, to candidate inflections in conversation. Operates at session time as AI's calibration target; not a runtime check against a real reconstruction (which happens offline post-hoc per [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19)).

**Application per candidate:**
- If skipping would diverge: promote to T2.
- If skipping leaves the artifact reconstructable within original-generation variance: keep in T1; fold into next settled entry's body if useful; otherwise discard.
- If uncertain: default-to-no-entry. The cost of a missed log is one `/stoa audit` catch or operator nudge; the cost of WAL noise is silent quality erosion (high-relevance-density of the corpus per OP1 is what gives the Agent good signal).

**What this captures vs. discards:**
- *Captures:* inflection-in-its-own-right — degree of freedom resolved, alternative foreclosed (`won't-do`), sub-question deferred (`table`), arc bifurcated (`branch`), prior conclusion overturned (`rollback`), empirical finding crystallized (`observation`).
- *Discards:* trajectory texture — misreadings being corrected, exploratory drafts before alignment, *"wait, actually"* mid-thought, two-parties-aligning-on-meaning chatter.

**Symmetric H/AI:** the judgment applies the same regardless of which side surfaced the inflection. Substance over origin per [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19).

**Continuous, not batched.** Promotion is per-inflection as the conversation unfolds. AI writes to T2 as soon as the inflection meets the bar. Commits are batched separately (per [`92cddf26`](#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19)).

**Why:** prior framing (*"inflection in its own right"*) was operator-facing intuition without a measurable calibration target. Reconstruction-fidelity ([`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19)) gives AI a sharper mental yardstick — concrete, audit-aligned, calibration-testable post-hoc. AI applies the question at session time; reconstruction validates whether AI's calibration is correct over time during controlled rollout ([`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19)).

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: new sub-paragraph under §"Three-tier WAL model" (or §"Settling cues") naming the reconstruction-fidelity yardstick and default-to-no-entry prior.
- `/stoa audit` Sweep 2 procedure inherits this as its retroactive grading criterion: was each session-time decision well-calibrated against the reconstruction yardstick?

**Open residual:** the yardstick optimizes for the artifact as-generated (locks in original-quality). A sharper objective — *"artifact meets same requirements as original"* — is harder to instrument; deferred per [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19).

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy shift); [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity audit substrate); [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19) (controlled-rollout phase for calibration); [`717a71fc`](#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) (OP1 — high-relevance-density of corpus); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier model parent).

## 92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**T2 → T3 commit cadence. AI batches T2 appends and commits at strong cues. Lifecycle cues force flush; non-lifecycle cues are discretionary on AI's hygiene judgment. Bias toward larger batches as guidance, weighing commit-history noise against operator cognitive cost.**

The promotion from durable-but-uncommitted (T2) to distributable history (T3) is its own decision-axis, separate from T1→T2 promotion.

**Strong cues (T3 candidates):**
- Strong yes-cue after a substantive proposal-and-agree.
- Directive-cue after proposal-and-agree (executable settlement).
- Phase-settlement (AI about to make impl offer).
- Structured-selection return from `AskUserQuestion` or equivalent.
- Operator explicit-commit (*"commit now"*).
- **Lifecycle cues — mandatory flush:** `commit` / `push` / `compact` / `clear` / `start fresh`. Session-boundary safety; uncommitted T2 should not cross session boundaries silently.

**Bias toward larger batches — as guidance, not rule.** AI weighs:
- Batch size vs commit-history noise (smaller batches = noisier `git log`).
- Coherence-check cost amortization (one batch coherence call per commit per [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19)).
- Operator cognitive cost (uncommitted state lingering can feel unfinished; large unrelated commits can be surprising).
- Tool-call distraction (each commit is a few tool calls of overhead).

No prescribed minimum batch size. AI judges ripeness using these weights.

**Cadence #2 (post-decision propagation) reframe:** under continuous T2 writes, the prior trigger (*"when a `decision`-type WAL entry lands, walk tracked artifacts"*) would fire on every T2 write. Reframed to fire at **commit-batch boundary**, alongside cadence #1's pre-commit drift walk. The two cadences effectively merge under v0.7.0: walk tracked artifacts once per commit, catch both new-decision drift and code↔doc misalignment in one pass.

**Auto-`--no-verify` authority.** When the pre-commit WAL audit returns *"no substantive decision in this diff"* (typo fix, mechanical refactor, doc reword), AI may commit with `--no-verify`. Discipline: AI appends an `observation` entry once per commit-cluster aggregating the negative findings, so the audit trail isn't blind. Today this authority was operator-only; v0.7.0 grants it to AI under FP4.

**Why:** continuous T2 writes + per-entry commits would pollute `git log`. Batching at strong cues groups related entries naturally (a single phase often settles 3-5 decisions atomically), keeps `git log` readable, and amortizes coherence-check cost. Lifecycle cues are non-negotiable because they bound session-loss risk.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: new sub-paragraph under §"Three-tier WAL model" naming the batch policy; cadence #2 description updated to commit-batch trigger.
- §"Coherence cadence" #3 procedure updates to include auto-`--no-verify` + observation discipline.
- Embedded hook block Pass A AI-instruction text reflects the new flow.

**Refs:** [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier model parent); [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy — AI's hygiene judgment); [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19) (coherence-check policy uses batch boundary); [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (FP4 — AI owns coherence ops).

## 5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Two-tier coherence-check policy. Self-coherence at every T2 write (free; working-memory-bounded); AI-judged batch-level `/stoa coherence --batch` at T2→T3 commit moment. Today's per-entry Pass B (informational hook coherence) removed.**

Coherence-check operations (classifying a candidate into Superseding / Converging / Adjacent against the WAL) split into two tiers under v0.7.0 to balance signal quality against latency cost.

**Tier 1 — Self-coherence at per-T2-write (free):**
- AI considers whether the new entry refines / contradicts / extends T2 entries from this session's working memory.
- If supersession detected → atomic pair: new entry + `rollback` in the same write (single Edit operation, two entries appended).
- If refinement / convergence detected → new entry includes `Refs:` line naming related prior hex IDs in the same write.
- No subagent invocation; no latency cost. Intrinsic to AI's reasoning about what to write.
- Bounded scope: working memory only. Catches in-session divergence; doesn't catch older entries outside context.

**Tier 2 — AI-judged batch coherence at commit (heavier, amortized):**
- New dispatcher mode: `/stoa coherence --batch <hex1,hex2,...,hexN>`. Subagent loads the batch entries + WAL corpus in one pass; returns findings (Superseding / Converging / Adjacent buckets) for each batch entry.
- AI judges *whether to invoke* per batch, weighing:
  - Invoke if any entry is a `rollback` or `branch` (high-stakes; supersession claim warrants verification).
  - Invoke if entries touch topics with prior-arc presence (AI does a free headline-scan first).
  - Invoke if batch is large.
  - Skip if clearly novel topics with no headline-scan overlap AND self-coherence at write was clean for all entries.
  - Skip for tiny batches on bounded topics where self-coherence covered everything.
- One subagent invocation per commit (when invoked), not per entry. Cost: bounded latency at strong cues.

**Findings handling under autonomy:**
- High-confidence findings → AI acts silently (rollback append, `Refs:` line, cross-ref in body).
- Low-confidence findings → AI surfaces to operator only when the action would meaningfully differ between possible classifications. Default to act-silently unless surfacing is needed.

**Hook Pass B removed.** Today's pre-commit hook Pass B fires `/stoa coherence` per new staged WAL entry — proxy-fragile ([`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15)) and partly redundant with AI's session-time work under autonomy. The case Pass B backstopped (operator hand-edit commits with no AI in loop) is now off-pattern per [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19) — operator hand-edits of T2 break the AI-maintained invariant. The observation-on-detect mechanism from [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19) handles the case; Pass B as a separate mechanism is redundant.

**Confidence calibration is AI judgment.** Whether a finding is *high-confidence* or *low-confidence* is itself an AI-judgment surface. Reconstruction-fidelity ([`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19)) validates calibration over time, not session-time. If AI is systematically over-surfacing or under-surfacing, beta_tracker entries surface the pattern during controlled rollout.

**Why:** today's per-entry coherence at commit (Pass B) was bolt-on, fragile (CLI-proxy stderr handoff), and uncalibrated for batch size. The self-coherence + AI-judged batch model puts the work where it's free (per-write reasoning) and where it's amortized (one batch call per commit when warranted), keeping the heavyweight backstops (`/stoa audit`, cadence #6) for higher-stakes contexts.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: rewrite §"Coherence check on AI-proposed WAL entries" to the two-tier policy; remove the *"AI invokes `/stoa coherence <candidate>` and surfaces findings inline in the proposal"* framing.
- `.claude/commands/stoa.md` `/stoa coherence` subcommand: add `--batch <hex-list>` mode procedure.
- Embedded hook block: remove Pass B entirely; Pass A unchanged in structure (blocking; tracked-artifacts-without-WAL detection).

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy — AI judgment central); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier model — Layer 3 in T1↔T2 consistency); [`92cddf26`](#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19) (commit cadence — defines when batch coherence fires); [`9c4d8a2`](#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) (CLI-proxy stderr fragility — Pass B's known weakness); [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19) (WAL strictly AI-maintained — closes the Pass-B backstop case off-pattern); [`b0122b1f`](#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18) (`/stoa coherence` primitive — base for `--batch` extension); [`5e2c8b9`](#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) (draft-time coherence vs hook-time — extended here to two-tier model); [`295e98d1`](#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (calibration substrate).

## e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**WAL strictly AI-maintained. Manual edits to `context_log.md` — text-editor edits, `sed`, `git reset --hard` of WAL commits, `git stash` of WAL changes — break Stoa's invariant. When detected, AI logs an observation capturing the action.**

Under FP4 + autonomy, the WAL is AI's coherence artifact; operator hand-edits violate the substance/coherence division of labor. The principle hardens what was previously implicit:

- **Operator-side prohibition:** never edit `context_log.md` directly. The substance (decisions to make) is operator-owned; the recording (WAL entries) is AI-owned. If the operator wants to change what's in the WAL, the path is: discuss in conversation → AI judges → AI appends rollback or new entry.
- **AI self-policing:** the off-pattern guardrail applies to AI itself. AI never edits committed T2 entries. Same-turn drafting iteration is bounded to T1 (per [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19)); once written to T2, the entry is immutable except via WAL types.
- **Structural-integrity repairs remain carve-outs.** Separator insertion (post-pull union-merge boundary repair); malformed-header recovery on failed-write. Not entry-body edits.

**Detection + response:**
- AI maintains awareness of T2 state via prior writes in conversation context. When AI observes a state mismatch — entries missing that AI knows it wrote; entry bodies different from what AI wrote; entries reordered — it's detected as a manual edit.
- Response: AI logs an `observation` entry capturing:
  - What was changed (paraphrase if content is unknowable; hex IDs if lost entries are paraphrasable).
  - The detected action (hand-edit / git-reset / stash / etc., as best AI can infer from `git reflog` and current state).
  - The new T2 state going forward (which entries AI now treats as authoritative).

Lost entries from `git reset --hard` are preserved in `git reflog` (until garbage collection). The WAL records the *fact* of removal; recovery (if needed) is an operator action in conversation, producing fresh appends with new hex IDs.

**Bootcheck orphan-T2 detection** (per [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19)) is the session-boundary version: uncommitted T2 from prior session = legitimate orphan, not off-pattern. AI commits as-is at next strong cue.

**WAL shadow file** (per [`d7c66232`](#d7c66232ee4a4a97a93ec56342fcc150--table--2026-05-19)) is the future v0.7.1+ substrate for stronger detection (content-hash comparison at session start, cross-session integrity). For v0.7.0, detection is AI-discipline + cadence-#5 audit backstop.

**Why:** the prior WAL guardrail framing softly tolerated operator overrides (*"Override and proceed? Stoa won't enforce WAL coherence on the resulting state"*). Under FP4 + autonomy + PNG-bytes (humans don't read raw WAL anyway), the toleration was incoherent — operator hand-editing AI's coherence artifact is the kind of off-pattern the methodology should name plainly.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` §"WAL guardrail": rewrite to remove operator-override language; add the *"WAL is strictly AI-maintained"* principle paragraph; off-pattern list applies to AI self-policing too; observation-on-detect response named.
- §"Off-pattern includes" list updated: manual edits via any path (text editor, `sed`, git operations affecting committed WAL).

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy — context for the stricter principle); [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (FP4 — substance/coherence division of labor); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes — humans don't read raw WAL); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier model — T2 immutability); [`d7c66232`](#d7c66232ee4a4a97a93ec56342fcc150--table--2026-05-19) (shadow file — future detection substrate); [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19) (Pass B removal — closed by this principle).

## 33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Informational `[stoa]` chat-anchor on every T2 write. Format includes hex ID, headline, and mandatory self-coherence assertion. Serves as operator notification, AI turn-anchor, and structural visibility against silent-omission failure modes.**

Every T2 write produces a single-line `[stoa]` chat output in the same turn:

> **`[stoa] appended <hex> — <headline>. Consistency: <clean | Superseding <prior-hex> (rollback appended) | Refines <prior-hex> (Refs: added)>. <committed in <SHA> | holding pending commit>.`**

**Three roles:**
1. **Operator-facing surface.** PNG-bytes-aligned: AI surfaces what it did. Operator sees activity without reading raw entries.
2. **AI turn-anchor.** The line is in AI's conversation context for subsequent turns; AI's reasoning sees *"this is now T2-authoritative"* as fact next time the arc resurfaces.
3. **Structural visibility against silent omission.** Same playbook that closed prior silent-failure modes (e.g., [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12), the bootcheck visibility arc at [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12)): if AI ever writes T2 without emitting the line, the operator can call it out in-turn. Failure mode shifts from silent → recoverable.

**Self-coherence assertion is mandatory** in the line, even when clean. *"Consistency: clean"* is the explicit AI-side commitment that the self-coherence check (per [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19) Tier 1) ran on this write against working memory. Function over aesthetics — this is AI hygiene; operator does not need to read it but the assertion's presence verifies the check happened.

**Distinct from deprecated visible-output blocks.** `[stoa-preflight]` and `[stoa-propagation]` (per [`b90a584f`](#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19)) were *compliance-verification* blocks operators were expected to read and approve; they degraded to rubber-stamp. The chat-anchor is *informational* — operator never approves, never gates; it's AI's own bookkeeping made externally visible. Format is one line, not a multi-field block, so it's low-burden in chat.

**Why:** under autonomy, the operator's only signal that AI is doing its WAL work is what AI surfaces in chat. The anchor produces that signal without ceremony. Doubles as turn-anchor for AI's own reasoning and as structural backstop against silent omission.

**How to apply:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` slim section: new §"T2 write anchor" sub-section (or fold into the suggestion-shape section) naming the format + the three roles + the mandatory consistency assertion.
- Format is single-line; operator can ignore at will. Mandatory only that the line exists when a T2 write happens.

**Refs:** [`b90a584f`](#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) (visible-output blocks deprecated — chat-anchor is the informational replacement); [`5bcbe16a`](#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19) (self-coherence assertion source); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (T1↔T2 Layer 1 mechanism); [`b4d8e1c`](#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (visibility-as-backstop arc — pattern applied here too); [`d8e4a2c`](#d8e4a2c--decision--2026-05-12) (silent-omission failure-mode precedent); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes — AI surfaces; humans interact).

## d7c66232ee4a4a97a93ec56342fcc150 — table — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**WAL shadow file (`.stoa/wal-shadow.jsonl`) as future cross-session integrity substrate. Gitignored, per-clone. Mechanism deferred to v0.7.1; principle committed now.**

The append-only-on-disk WAL (T2) is AI-maintained per [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19), but session-time detection of integrity violations (operator hand-edits, `git reset --hard`, `git stash`, content drift) relies on AI awareness in working memory. Working memory doesn't survive session boundaries; cross-session detection needs persistent substrate.

**Proposed shape (v0.7.1+ implementation):**
- `.stoa/wal-shadow.jsonl` — gitignored per-clone (NOT committed; if committed, becomes a second canonical WAL, structurally weird and forces synchronization burden).
- On every T2 write, AI appends a shadow record: `{hex, type, date, content_hash, first_line, written_at}`.
- Bootcheck adds an integrity probe (alongside the orphan-T2 probe from [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19)):
  - Shadow entries that aren't in T2 → loss event (operator-side rollback/stash); AI surfaces and logs `observation`.
  - T2 entries not in shadow → pulled-from-elsewhere (cadence #6 brought them in); AI updates shadow from T2.
  - Content-hash mismatch on same hex → hand-edit detected; AI logs `observation`.
- Pull operations (cadence #6) update shadow from post-merge T2 state.

**Status:** deferred to v0.7.1 or later. v0.7.0 ships with AI-discipline + cadence-#5 audit as the integrity backstop. Beta data during controlled rollout ([`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19)) will inform whether v0.7.1 implementation is warranted.

**Why:** the shadow file is observability infrastructure — strengthens detection without changing the WAL invariant or AI-managed property. Its absence doesn't block v0.7.0's autonomy semantics; its presence in v0.7.1 will close the cross-session detection gap.

**Refs:** [`e2f9afbc`](#e2f9afbc4e9f41678235f4bbc44cca93--decision--2026-05-19) (WAL strictly AI-maintained — principle this implements integrity for); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier — bootcheck orphan-T2 probe is a sibling integrity check); [`24677f8e`](#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19) (controlled-rollout phase for beta calibration); [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomy shift — context).

Rationale for minor (not patch):

Net: ~30% reduction in the slim section's token weight.

**Meaning shifts.**

- `[stoa]` markers: interactive prompts → informational notifications + chat-anchor.
- T2 append: drafting-iteration carve-out collapses; T2 is immutable on write.

- Auto-commit at strong cues.
- Auto-`--no-verify` with observation aggregation on no-decision diffs.
- Commit-batch coherence (single subagent invocation, AI-judged invocation).
- Self-coherence at per-T2-write.

**New mechanisms.**
- 3-tier T1/T2/T3 model with explicit invariants.
- `[stoa]` chat-anchor with mandatory self-coherence assertion.

## f2a86ee838ca4965bcb9168802cd37a0 — observation — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Bootcheck step-4 orphan-T2 probe returned silent-clean at post-/compact despite 12 working-tree T2 appends present; manual re-run of the same probe extracted all 12 orphan hex IDs.**

Turn-1 post-/compact in this session: `Agent(subagent_type=stoa-bootcheck, prompt="check")` returned the literal `clean`. The `[stoa-init]` block emitted "Bootcheck return: clean." Manual verification immediately after — `git diff --quiet -- context_log.md` exit-1; orphan-hex extraction returned the 12 prior-session entries (`001ae82f`, `33708824`, `5bcbe16a`, `64665316`, `92cddf26`, `a88b435b`, `b237c4ea`, `b6e06d0e`, `b90a584f`, `d7c66232`, `e2f9afbc`, `f0eb30370b`).

Root cause: bootcheck step 4 was the only probe in the file driving control flow from **exit code** rather than from a value-read pattern. Step 5 (diagnostic-probe discipline) called this out as an "Exception" — all other probes use `2>/dev/null || echo ""` and decide based on captured-string emptiness; step 4 ran `git diff --quiet` and relied on shell-style exit-code-as-signal. Under LLM subagent execution, exit-1 from a Bash tool result reads as "command errored" rather than "drift detected" — the subagent silently moved past the failed conditional and emitted the canonical `clean`.

Significance: the canonical example of exit-code probes failing under LLM subagent execution. Future bootcheck additions (and any subagent-executed probe) drive from captured values, never exit codes. The decision that lands the structural fix is [`1608b8b21c96481caa31e6c2680d6256`](#1608b8b21c96481caa31e6c2680d6256--decision--2026-05-19).

## 1608b8b21c96481caa31e6c2680d6256 — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Orphan-T2 probe rewritten value-driven; bootcheck step 5 discipline simplified — uniform value-driven probe execution across all bootcheck steps.**

Step 4 of `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` (embedded in `installkit/stoa.md`) now captures both staged and unstaged WAL appends in a single bash invocation:

```
ORPHAN_HEXES=$(
  {
    git diff --cached -U0 -- context_log.md 2>/dev/null
    git diff         -U0 -- context_log.md 2>/dev/null
  } | grep -E '^\+## [0-9a-f]{7,} — [a-z-]+ — [0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}' \
    | sed -E 's/^\+## ([0-9a-f]+) —.*/\1/' \
    | sort -u
)
```

Control flow drives from `[ -n "$ORPHAN_HEXES" ]` — string-emptiness, not exit code. Step 5's prior "Exception: step 4's `git diff --quiet` family uses exit-code intentionally" carve-out is stripped; all bootcheck probes now follow the same value-driven discipline.

A main-agent post-bootcheck verify-probe (slim section) was considered as soft redundancy against subagent miss. Rejected: if step 4 is reliable, the redundancy is unnecessary; if step 4 is unreliable, the fix is wrong. The bootcheck rewrite's reliability is verifiable empirically at the next boundary moment.

**Refs:** [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier WAL model — establishes orphan-T2 probe at boundary moments); [`f2a86ee838ca4965bcb9168802cd37a0`](#f2a86ee838ca4965bcb9168802cd37a0--observation--2026-05-19) (empirical anchor — the false-negative event that motivated the rewrite).

## cb8074f181ec41a1a9e1f674ed180fee — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Spec hygiene principle: `installkit/stoa.md` describes current behavior only; design history lives in WAL refs, not in spec prose.**

The installkit is the canonical spec — what the methodology IS now, not how it got there. There is no backwards compatibility to maintain except WAL-structure decisions affecting the durable artifact (e.g., hex-ID format reader rules). Therefore, the spec carries no narrative history:

- **No version-history suffixes.** `(v0.4.3+)`, `(v0.5+)`, `(v0.7.0+)` and similar tags accumulated in section headers and embedded-artifact blockquotes are stripped. Version-of-introduction is recoverable from git log; the spec describes current state.
- **No deprecation tombstones.** "Pass B removed in v0.7.0", "the v0.6.x visible-output compliance blocks are deprecated", "reframed from compliance verification to retrospective audit" — all stripped. The spec says what the cadence/hook/sweep IS; how it differs from a prior shape is WAL territory.
- **No design-incident narratives.** "Beta data motivated the prior escalation", "Why this cadence sits next to #3", and similar load-bearing-during-design-but-ceremonial-now paragraphs are stripped. The decision's rationale lives in the WAL entry where it was made.
- **No defensive symmetric-framing repetition.** "Applies to AI and operator alike", "any initiator — operator OR AI", "discipline rules apply symmetrically" — FP4 already establishes the substance/coherence division; symmetric-framing inline is redundant.

What stays: WAL hex-ID citations (these are pointers TO the durable history artifact, not history-in-prose); load-bearing AI-instruction text (tuned imperative blocks); current-behavior specification across all sections.

Authorizes a consolidated cruft sweep against `installkit/stoa.md` removing accumulated history-in-spec; brings the file from ~2120 lines back toward ~1560 lines (audit estimate). Future spec edits cite this entry as policy.

**Refs:** [`2b16472f`](#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19) (FP4 — substance/coherence division as the model that makes symmetric-framing redundant); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes — the WAL is the durable artifact, spec is its rendering); [`a88b435b`](#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous WAL management — the principle that already established propose-confirm is gone, making tombstones unnecessary).

## b7ab4ee04cab45adbbbf5738ea7c1e6c — decision — 2026-05-19

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**The installkit must be self-contained at the adopter-runtime surface; canonical-repo `docs/` references are valid only as "more depth" pointers for humans reading the kit, never as load-bearing AI-instruction.**

`installkit/stoa.md` is the canonical source. `/stoa upgrade` regenerates the dogfooded slim `stoa.md`, the dispatcher (`.claude/commands/stoa.md`), the bootcheck agent (`.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`), and the hooks into adopter repos. Adopter clones receive only those artifacts plus their seed-and-preserve files (`.stoa/artifacts.md`, `.stoa/beta_tracker.md`, `context_log.md`, `.gitattributes`) — the canonical repo's `docs/`, `demos/`, and `tests/` do not propagate.

**Load-bearing AI-instruction content lives only in these adopter-side surfaces:**

- **Always-loaded** (every session via `@stoa.md` import in `CLAUDE.md`): slim `stoa.md`.
- **On dispatcher invocation**: `.claude/commands/stoa.md` (subcommand procedures).
- **On bootcheck invocation**: `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`.
- **WAL substrate** for coherence operations: `context_log.md`.
- **Methodology-feedback channel**: `.stoa/beta_tracker.md`.
- **Tracked-artifacts manifest**: `.stoa/artifacts.md` (project-side; adopter-owned content).

**Out of scope at adopter runtime** (canonical-repo-only):
- `docs/proposed_methodology.md`, `docs/getting_started.md`, `docs/executive_summary.md`, `docs/current_ux.md`, `docs/thesis.md`.
- `demos/*.html`.
- `tests/*`.

References from `installkit/stoa.md` (or any of its embedded artifacts) to those out-of-scope paths are valid only as "go to canonical for more depth" links for humans reading the kit on GitHub. They MUST NOT carry load-bearing AI-instruction — no "see `docs/getting_started.md` for the rule"; the rule itself must be in slim, dispatcher, or bootcheck.

Surfaced when a coherence audit proposed moving §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" from the slim spec to `docs/getting_started.md` for ~0.9 KB of byte-savings. The proposal was sound for canonical-repo readers but wrong for adopters whose tree never contained the doc. Operator caught the failure mode in-flight.

Extends [`cb8074f1`](#cb8074f181ec41a1a9e1f674ed180fee--decision--2026-05-19) (spec hygiene principle: spec describes current behavior; history lives in WAL refs) with a concrete adopter-runtime self-containment constraint. Future cruft sweeps over `installkit/stoa.md` apply both rules.

**Refs:** [`cb8074f1`](#cb8074f181ec41a1a9e1f674ed180fee--decision--2026-05-19) (spec hygiene principle — this extends it with the adopter-runtime constraint).

## d2bea46797d343fc81b3aecfdf9e71de — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Bootcheck orphan-T2 probe non-firing has two distinct causes, not one: (a) the probe was absent from the on-disk agent file at v0.7.0 session start — spec described the probe but the agent file didn't implement it; and (b) Claude Code caches agent definitions per parent-session, so post-`/stoa upgrade` regen of the agent file doesn't propagate to subagent invocations within the same parent session.**

The prior observation [`f2a86ee8`](#f2a86ee838ca4965bcb9168802cd37a0--observation--2026-05-19) diagnosed root cause as "step 4 was exit-code-driven and LLM subagents misread exit-1 as command error." Empirical post-upgrade verification revealed the diagnosis was incomplete.

Actual sequence:

1. **HEAD `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` at session start had 4 steps:** 1. Marker check, 2. Hook activation, 3. WAL pull-rebase config, 4. Diagnostic-probe discipline. **No orphan-T2 probe at all.** The slim spec described the probe (§"Three-tier WAL model" → "Bootcheck orphan-T2 probe"); the agent file didn't carry it. A spec-vs-implementation gap going back to the v0.7.0 design that introduced the 3-tier WAL model.

2. **Bootcheck at session start loaded this 4-step definition.** Ran 1-3 silent, then step 4 was a meta-rule (not a probe). Returned `clean` because no probe checked T2 vs T3 state.

3. **Decision [`1608b8b2`](#1608b8b21c96481caa31e6c2680d6256--decision--2026-05-19) added the orphan-T2 probe to `installkit/stoa.md` as new step 4** (renumbering diagnostic-discipline to step 5). The decision text said "rewrote step 4 value-driven" — but there was no orphan-T2 step 4 to rewrite. The procedural form is still correct (value-driven capture into `ORPHAN_HEXES`); the action was "add new step 4," not "rewrite existing."

4. **Operator ran `/stoa upgrade`.** On-disk `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md` regenerated to 5 steps (orphan-T2 step 4 + diagnostic step 5). Verified via `grep -c "ORPHAN_HEXES"` → 4 matches on disk.

5. **Re-invoking bootcheck in the same parent session STILL returned `clean`.** Diagnostic probe (via SendMessage to a stoa-bootcheck subagent in deviating-from-canonical mode) confirms: subagent reports its loaded procedure has 4 steps with step 4 = diagnostic-discipline (the pre-upgrade content). The subagent reads from a parent-session-cached agent definition, not from the on-disk file at invocation time.

**Implications.**

- **Verification constraint.** Empirical verification of agent-file changes is impossible within the parent session that made them. The new agent definition propagates only to new parent sessions (post-`/clear`, post-`/compact`, or fresh launch).

- **Upgrade-flow guidance.** The `/stoa upgrade` dispatcher already surfaces a `/clear`-after-upgrade recommendation. For bootcheck-affecting upgrades, this guidance is load-bearing — without `/clear`, subagent invocations continue using the stale cached agent definition.

- **Test-harness scenario design.** Orphan-T2 scenario V8 (in work item A) must verify in a fresh subagent invocation post-install/post-upgrade, NOT in the same parent session where the install/upgrade ran. Same caveat applies to any V-scenario that exercises bootcheck procedure changes.

- **Methodology gap closed retroactively.** The orphan-T2 probe is now on disk; future sessions running against post-upgrade artifacts will see the probe fire correctly. This session's bootcheck behavior is a frozen artifact of the pre-upgrade state.

**Refs:** [`f2a86ee8`](#f2a86ee838ca4965bcb9168802cd37a0--observation--2026-05-19) (prior observation — incomplete diagnosis); [`1608b8b2`](#1608b8b21c96481caa31e6c2680d6256--decision--2026-05-19) (the fix is procedurally correct; just labeled as "rewrite" when it was "add new step"); [`b6e06d0e`](#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (3-tier WAL model — the spec that called for the probe).

## 7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`[stoa]` lines that carry AI-directive content but are unprompted (no operator action triggered them) must lead with `*No operator action needed*` plus purpose framing. Operator reads the lead and disregards; AI parses the directive tail unambiguously.**

`[stoa]` lines split across three audience patterns:

- **Operator-actionable** — imperative verbs address the operator directly. Operator runs a command or chooses a path. Example: `[stoa] WAL-audit hook is not active in this clone. To activate: git config core.hooksPath .githooks.`
- **AI-internal, operator-visible** — state continuity info surfaced unprompted; AI handles the action autonomously; operator reads incidentally. Example: the bootcheck orphan-T2 line.
- **Pure informational** — status only; no imperative; no action expected. Example: T2 write anchor (`[stoa] appended <hex> — <headline>. Consistency: clean. Holding pending commit.`).

The middle category is where audience misreads happen. The original orphan-T2 surface read:
> `[stoa] Uncommitted T2 appends from prior session detected — context_log.md is ahead of HEAD. Orphan hex(es): ... T2 immutability applies; commit as-is at next strong cue. If new session disagrees with prior entries, append a rollback (do not edit).`

Imperatives ("commit as-is", "append a rollback") read like instructions to the operator when they're in fact AI-internal directives. Operator surfaced the ambiguity in-flight. Rewritten to:

> `[stoa] *No operator action needed* — Stoa consistency anchor. Prior session left T2 entries uncommitted (context_log.md ahead of HEAD). Orphan hex(es): ... AI commits at next strong cue; appends a rollback if this session disagrees with a prior entry (T2 is immutable on write).`

**Application scope.** The audience-marker applies specifically to **unprompted** AI-internal `[stoa]` lines (where the operator didn't trigger the surface and might read it as an alarm). Lines that surface in response to operator-invoked subcommands (e.g., `[stoa] /stoa <subcommand> ships post-beta.`) have implicit context — operator already knows they invoked something. The marker is unnecessary there.

**Audit of installkit at log time:** orphan-T2 is the only category-2 unprompted line. All other `[stoa]` lines are operator-actionable (cat 1, imperative addresses operator) or pure informational (cat 3, status with no directive). The principle is logged for future surface additions rather than for fixing additional sites in the current spec.

Refines [`b90a584f`](#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) (informational markers, never compliance-verification gates) by clarifying audience-disambiguation discipline when an informational marker carries directive verbs.

## 3e86858c6c41430ab5d1e514213933e2 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Audience-marker discipline applies to AI prose commentary that references AI-internal state, not just canonical `[stoa]` surface lines. The discipline scopes to substance (directive verbs over AI-internal content), not the envelope.**

The original audience-marker rule [`7a98ca01`](#7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a--decision--2026-05-20) scoped narrowly to canonical `[stoa]` lines. In practice, AI also references AI-internal state in free-form prose — most commonly when AI summarizes work in conversation after an operator-invoked command completes. Without the audience-marker shape, the prose carries the same audience ambiguity that the original rule was meant to prevent.

Surfaced when `/stoa upgrade` completed and AI appended:
> "Also note: bootcheck flagged 18 orphan T2 entries (...) — context_log.md is ahead of HEAD from the prior session. Those should be committed at the next strong cue, separately from this upgrade commit."

The line is AI's own helpful commentary, not a canonical `[stoa]` surface. But the substance — directive verbs over AI-internal state ("should be committed at the next strong cue, separately from this upgrade commit") — is identical to what the original rule was designed to disambiguate. Operator read it the same way: as an instruction to themselves.

**Rule extension.** When AI references AI-internal state in free-form prose (orphan-T2 entries, pending coherence batch, T2 immutability, atomic-pair pending, etc.), follow the audience-marker shape: lead with `*No operator action needed*` or equivalent framing. The discipline scopes to *substance* (AI-internal directive content), not the canonical-`[stoa]`-envelope test.

**Application.** §"`[stoa]` chat surfaces" → "Audience-marker discipline" paragraph in slim spec updated with the broader scope. No separate dispatcher edits — `/stoa upgrade`, `/stoa pull`, etc. all inherit the principle via the slim spec since AI applies it at prose-generation time.

Refines [`7a98ca01`](#7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a--decision--2026-05-20) by extending the audience-marker discipline beyond canonical `[stoa]` surface lines to AI prose commentary referencing AI-internal state.

**Refs:** [`7a98ca01`](#7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a--decision--2026-05-20) (original audience-marker discipline — this extends it); [`b90a584f`](#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) (informational markers, never compliance-verification gates); [`a62ef52e`](#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes framing — AI surfaces what it does or notices).

## 882f9f81b463403182fd27c4da4d8fc6 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**`/stoa upgrade` empirical timing: ~9 min wall-clock for a slim-section-only change. The root `stoa.md` self-strip Write dominates at ~5 min (~55% of total). Read-then-Write requirement doubles operations on existing files. Procedure has no content-equality check, so unchanged spec-owned files get rewritten anyway.**

AI drove `/stoa upgrade` with timestamps at each step (operator-requested diagnostic run to identify why prior upgrades felt slow, ~10 min observed):

- Total wall-clock: `01:32:30Z → 01:41:39Z` = **~9 min 9 sec**.
- Step 1 (compute hash + read dispatcher procedure into context): ~1:45.
- Step 2 (marker prep): ~0:42.
- Step 3 prep (parallel reads of all 8 embedded path blocks): ~0:41. Pulled ~50 KB / ~1300 lines into context. Initial parallel Writes failed when destinations weren't Read-prerequisite-satisfied; required 7 additional Reads of destination files to satisfy the Write tool's read-state cache.
- Steps 4 / 4b / 5: ~0 (no-ops — hooks already configured, seed-and-preserve files already exist).
- Step 6 (self-strip — Read slim portion of installkit + Write root `stoa.md`): **~5 min**. Single largest operation; ~45 KB Write.
- Step 6 Finalize (recompute hash + Edit marker): ~0:13.

Root causes ranked by impact:

1. **Self-strip Write dominates (~55% of total).** ~45 KB Write to root `stoa.md` through Claude Code's Write tool takes ~5 min in current implementation. The dispatcher procedure itself acknowledges Write is preferred over Edit at this scale, but Write at 45 KB is also bound by tool throughput — there's no spec-side optimization without changing the tool itself.

2. **Read-then-Write requirement doubles operations on existing files.** Write tool refuses to overwrite without a prior Read of the destination, even when supplying the full new content. For each of the 8 spec-owned files, the upgrade pattern becomes: *Read installkit path block → Read destination file → Write destination file* — 3 tool calls per file instead of 1. The destination Read also pulls existing content into AI context (consumed but discarded).

3. **Context bloat from large reads.** The dispatcher block (459 lines) and `embed.py` (241 lines) consume substantial tokens. As context grows over the upgrade, subsequent AI reasoning steps slow because the model attends to more.

4. **No content-equality check in Step 3.** The procedure always Writes the 8 spec-owned files, even when on-disk content already matches the canonical. In this run, only the slim section changed; 7 of 8 spec-owned files were already current from the prior `/stoa upgrade`. Those 7 Writes would have been no-ops. (AI observed this and skipped them in this diagnostic run; the canonical procedure would do all 8 unconditionally.)

5. **AI per-tool-call latency accumulates.** A "small" upgrade requires ~20-30 tool calls; each carries fixed overhead.

Concrete optimizations (priority order, separately decidable):

| Optimization | Estimated savings | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| Add "skip Write if content matches canonical block" check to Step 3 | Up to 4-6 min on no-change upgrades | Low — content equality is deterministic |
| Explicit "do Step 3 reads in parallel + writes in parallel" guidance | ~1-2 min | None — already permitted by the procedure |
| Single batched-Write tool (multi-file) | Marginal | Tool-design change; out of spec scope |

**Self-strip Write is the irreducible floor.** Until the Write tool accelerates large content delivery, ~5 min is the lower bound on `/stoa upgrade` cost regardless of other optimizations. The skip-on-match optimization helps the most when only the slim section changed (a common case for dogfood iterations).

Future-decision candidates (not landed in this observation): Step 3 skip-Write-on-match check; Step 3 explicit parallel-batch guidance. Lands as separate decisions when prioritized; this observation establishes the empirical baseline.

**Refs:** none.

## e9fb68a7dda24348bc95db6492e3cc2c — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

WAL entry attribution: AI must establish canonical handle from actual platform identity, not lift the spec example literally.

**The rule.** The `Authors:` `@<handle>` is the operator's actual handle on the project's primary collaboration platform (GitHub for this repo). The `<tool>(<model>)` suffix is the actual AI tool + model + context. Neither is a literal copy of the spec example.

**The bug this fixes.** Pre-v0.7.0 entries in this repo's WAL used `@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)` — directly lifted from the spec example at `installkit/stoa.md` §"WAL entry form" → "Attribution." Past AI sessions pattern-matched the example without reconciling against the operator's actual identity. Operator's actual GitHub handle is `ivan-avramov` (queryable via `gh api user --jq '.login'`); git config `user.name` is `iavramov` (local-form, doesn't match the platform handle). The example became a load-bearing identifier — methodology bug.

**The procedure** (now encoded in `installkit/stoa.md` §"Attribution"):
1. AI queries platform identity at session start (GitHub: `gh api user --jq '.login'`).
2. On query failure (not authed, non-GitHub, etc.) AI asks the operator once for their canonical handle, reuses for the session.
3. AI does not assume git config `user.name` matches the platform handle. They commonly differ.
4. AI suffix uses actual model + context window.
5. Establish once per session; reuse for every T2 write.

**Spec patch applied this turn.** `installkit/stoa.md`:
- Line 279-281 (Attribution format): replaced "Slack-handle-shaped" wording with platform-agnostic guidance; rewrote example from `@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)` to placeholder shape `@<github-handle>;<tool>(<model>)`; added 5-step AI procedure for establishing canonical attribution before first T2 write.
- Line 420 (prose↔subcommand mapping): rewrote example from `@ivan` to `@<handle>` placeholder.

**Existing entries.** The 20 uncommitted entries from prior sessions plus older committed entries that use `@ivan;claude(opus4.7/1M)` stay as-is — T2 immutability holds per [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19). The cost of 20 attribution-typo rollbacks would exceed the value of pristine attribution when the human is unambiguous from context (single-author project). This entry establishes the corrected handle as authoritative going forward; the spec patch prevents recurrence.

**Refs:** [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (T2 immutability — justifies leave-prior-entries-as-is), [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous WAL management — explains why this T2 write fires without operator confirmation).

## 8ed5d11de21d42ef8e3c2b5b799a9e56 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Propose-confirm anti-patterns: AI must not ask permission on T2 entry wording, type, timing, or granularity. Spec patch adds explicit anti-pattern enumeration to slim §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy."

**The bug.** Per [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19), AI owns WAL coherence end-to-end (write, classify, batch, commit); operator owns substance and explicit overrides. Propose-confirm dissolved. But this session showed two compounding failures: (1) AI emitted *"Want me to draft the decision-entry text for your review before T2 write?"* — propose-confirm under different wording; (2) when operator surfaced the bug and AI proposed an anti-pattern fix, AI failed to fold the proposal into the executed plan on the next directive-cue — same propose-confirm bug at the meta-level (held the anti-pattern in pending-proposal state instead of applying autonomously).

**Why the reflex re-emerges.** Two pressures:
1. **Training prior.** AI's pattern-matcher fires "ask before significant state changes" on any persistent write. T2 writes feel significant. Spec assertion that "AI is autonomous" doesn't override the prior unless it names the failure shapes literally.
2. **Spec coverage gap.** Pre-patch slim §"Operator touchpoints" listed what operator does NOT touch (wording/type/timing/etc.) descriptively, but did not enumerate the question shapes that re-introduce propose-confirm. Descriptive rule + asymmetric training prior = recurring relapse.

**The rule (now in spec).** AI must recognize these question shapes as off-pattern and not emit them:
- *"Want me to draft X for your review before I write?"*
- *"Should I write this as a decision or observation?"*
- *"Ready for me to append?"*
- *"Want me to add Refs: to entry Y?"*
- *"Should I propose this as a new entry or fold into Y?"*

Shared shape: a question that gates a T2 write on operator response. Correct flow: AI writes T2; chat-anchor surfaces what landed; operator override via `/stoa audit` or rollback.

**Spec patch applied this turn.** `installkit/stoa.md` §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" — added "Anti-patterns (propose-confirm re-emergence)" subsection enumerating five question shapes + shared-shape rule + descriptive-not-exhaustive note.

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous WAL management — the rule this anti-pattern enforces), [`33708824`](context_log.md#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19) (chat-anchor as post-write informational surface, not pre-write gate), [`b90a584f`](context_log.md#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) (visible-block compliance gates deprecated; same family of failure).

## 945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Autonomous-management scope and sequencing for `context_log.md` (v10). Refines [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) propose-confirm dissolution; narrows scope of [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) reconstruction-fidelity yardstick.

**The settled rule** (lands in `installkit/stoa.md` §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy"):

1. **Scope.** `context_log.md` is the singular file AI manages autonomously. All other files follow standard session guidance (default ask-before-edit; propose, confirm, apply). Autonomous-management dissolution of propose-confirm is scoped to `context_log.md` operations only.

2. **AI's conversational surface.** AI proposes settlement *directions* only — never WAL management. Direction-asks invite responses in the cue language of §"Settling cues"; the cue settles the direction; the WAL follows. Example: *"Want me to fix server.py? Say the word and we'll do it. Or we can table it. Your choice."*

3. **The strong rule.** Following ANY settling cue per §"Settling cues" — operator-side or AI-side auto-refinement — the WAL append ALWAYS follows autonomously, with the entry type determined by the cue's direction (*"go"* → `decision`; *"table it"* → `table`; *"won't do"* → `won't-do`; etc.).

4. **Two failure modes named off-pattern:**
   - Asking after settlement (*"Want me to draft the WAL entry?"*, *"Should I write this as a decision or observation?"*, *"Ready for me to append?"*, *"Want me to add Refs:?"*) — propose-confirm under different wording.
   - Mentioning WAL management in the ask (*"Want me to fix server.py + WAL append?"*) — contaminates the direction-ask with WAL coherence.

5. **Sequencing.** T2 writes follow settlement, never precede it. No cue, no T2 write. A proposal lives in T1 until a settling cue fires.

**Why this scope/sequencing matters.** Two compounding failures in the session that produced this rule: (a) AI relapsed to propose-confirm under wording the prior anti-pattern didn't enumerate; (b) AI then applied a spec patch fixing the relapse without operator settlement on the patch wording — second-order propose-confirm at meta-level. v10 closes both by removing AI's discretion on the write side (ANY cue → ALWAYS write) and naming AI's conversational surface as direction-only (never WAL management).

**Scope narrowing on `b237c4ea` reconstruction-fidelity yardstick.** The yardstick previously gated all T1→T2 promotions. v10's strong rule makes *cued* promotions mandatory; yardstick remains the gate for *cue-less* AI-judgment promotions (mid-conversation, no explicit signal). The yardstick is not retracted — its scope narrows to cue-less cases.

**Spec changes propagating from this decision** (apply downstream):
- `installkit/stoa.md` §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" — replace existing anti-pattern subsection with v10 wording.
- `installkit/stoa.md` §"Settling cues" — change "cues are signals to consider, not gates that require a write" to "cues are mandatory triggers for T2 promotion on substantive content." Internal-consistency patch.

**Refs:** [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous management — v10 builds on), [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (yardstick — scope narrowed), [`33708824`](context_log.md#33708824d07242c1b4b0b257e7443736--decision--2026-05-19) (chat-anchor — v10 references), [`4a9e521e`](context_log.md#4a9e521e22784e758312db79c9481dc4--rollback--2026-05-20) (rollback of broader version), [`8ed5d11d`](context_log.md#8ed5d11de21d42ef8e3c2b5b799a9e56--decision--2026-05-20) (superseded).

## 782a3a641b984744b9bb4ef1207e1ec6 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

`installkit/stoa.md` self-containment for distribution; CLAUDE.md rule + audit cleanup of repo-local references.

**The principle.** `installkit/stoa.md` is operational surface for autonomous agentic development — instructions for the agent, not the human. It is the canonical artifact adopters fetch and save as their session-loaded spec. It MUST be self-contained: the agent should never need to follow out-of-band references for runtime compliance.

**Concrete rules** (land in CLAUDE.md §"Working on the install kit"):

- **No WAL hex references in `installkit/stoa.md`.** WAL entries in this repo's `context_log.md` are for spec-author memory; their hex IDs don't resolve in adopter repos. When the slim spec needs to encode a rule's provenance, write the rationale into the rule's wording — never via `[hex](context_log.md#...)` link.
- **No file references.** No links to `docs/`, `tests/`, `sketches/`, `demos/`, `integrations/`, or any repo path. Only universal Stoa-installed artifacts may be named (`context_log.md`, `.stoa/<...>`, `.githooks/<...>`, `.claude/commands/stoa.md`, `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`), and only when AI compliance requires the literal name.
- **Two GitHub URLs total**: one in `/stoa help` (operator-facing depth pointer to repo root); one in the bootcheck broken-state warning (recovery path when no install kit is extractable from local copy). Any other GitHub URL is a bug.
- **No host-specific machinery outside host-enumerated contexts.** Slim spec runs across Claude / Codex / future hosts. Host-aware enumeration ("Claude Code: X / Codex: Y") is permitted and load-bearing. Claude-only instructions outside such enumeration are bugs.
- **No repo-specific identifiers.** Version stamps, commit hashes, operator handles from this repo. Adopters have their own.

**Why.** Two empirical findings drove this: (a) the `@ivan` attribution example (line 280 in pre-patch slim) was lifted literally by prior AI sessions instead of reconciling against actual operator identity — establishment-handle decision in [`e9fb68a7`](context_log.md#e9fb68a7dda24348bc95db6492e3cc2c--decision--2026-05-20). (b) Audit surfaced ~40 WAL hex references + 5 file/path references + several Claude-only mentions in the slim spec — all distribution-bugs that degrade adopter AI compliance via dead links and host-specific assumptions.

**Load-bearing verification** (done as part of the audit): no dropped reference is load-bearing for AI runtime compliance. The slim spec rule wording carries the substance; cited WAL entries are spec-author history; doc references are human depth pointers; Claude-only mentions are non-load-bearing outside host-enumerated contexts. Cuts strengthen compliance signal by removing distractor noise.

**Audit application** (four batches against `installkit/stoa.md`):
- Batch 1: drop ~40 WAL hex references (trailing citations + rephrased inline citations).
- Batch 2: drop 5 file/path references.
- Batch 3: generalize Claude-only mentions outside host-enumerated contexts (L1009, L1061, L1160, L1918 in pre-patch numbering).
- Batch 4: drop L3 title-block canonical-source URL + L1717 marker-template URL; keep L1192 (broken-state) + L1933 (help section); replace L1933's docs/ references with repo root URL.

**Refs:** [`e9fb68a7`](context_log.md#e9fb68a7dda24348bc95db6492e3cc2c--decision--2026-05-20) (attribution handle establishment — companion principle), [`945641e6`](context_log.md#945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 autonomous-management — substance-vs-coherence boundary).

## ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

OP4 — Methodology stops at T2; git integration starts at T3. Elevated to operational principle. Plus consolidated spec patches: 9 must-fix items from coherence pass + attribution lazy-fetch clarification + host auto-compaction generalization + bootcheck orphan-T2 wording polish.

**OP4 wording** (lands at slim spec §"Operational principles" as 4th operational principle): Stoa's autonomous management spans T1 (in-memory conversation context) and T2 (`context_log.md` file). T3 — git commits — is git integration territory, not Stoa methodology. AI treats `context_log.md` like any other artifact at the git boundary: no WAL-specific commit prompts, no behavior-engineered commit cadence, no prescribed git mechanics. The mental model: *decisions are changes; commit them like any other changes.* Stoa-defined mechanisms that DO touch the git boundary (cadence #3 pre-commit hook, cadence #4 lifecycle audit, bootcheck orphan-T2 probe) are failure-mode backstops that integrate WITH git, not prescriptions OF git mechanics.

**The deep refactor this enables.** Earlier in this session we iterated through 10 versions of T2→T3 commit cadence wording (v1 → v10) trying to nail down: when does AI auto-commit, what counts as "session edits" vs "working tree," how to handle parallel sessions, what threshold triggers commit, etc. The breakthrough insight: *committing the WAL is never wrong* (entries are append-only), and *Stoa is methodology; git is host-integration* (the methodology can apply to non-git contexts conceptually). Combined: Stoa's autonomous-management scope ENDS at T2; T3 (git commits) is host-integration territory. AI does its job by appending to T2 (per v10); operator drives git on their natural workflow cadence. The 10 versions of commit-cadence wording collapse into one principle (OP4) + the natural git workflow.

## a7b5341c900b4d70b2f7aed7b40c0d7b — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Step 6 self-strip discipline strengthened with `AI: BEFORE` leading directive in both dispatcher (`/stoa upgrade`) and first-run install kit (`## First-run install kit` → Step 6).

**The breach event.** During the second `/stoa upgrade` of this session (Phase D propagating OP4 ripples), the subagent self-disclosed: it initially executed Step 6 (self-strip) via shell `awk` before redoing via the `Write` tool to honor the procedure's "No shell utilities" rule. End-state was correct (idempotent redo), but the procedure was violated mid-execution. The descriptive "Do not use sed, awk, perl-i" wording didn't survive the temptation of the bulk-delete shape (~30k chars to remove from end of file makes `sed '<N>,$d'` look attractive).

**The fix.** Lead Step 6 with an imperative `AI: BEFORE` directive that:
- Names the temptation explicitly (`sed '<N>,$d'` for bulk-delete).
- Forbids ALL Bash mutation paths (not just sed/awk/perl): includes shell redirects (`>`, `>>`, `<`) and any other mutation utility.
- Frames the off-pattern recognition rule: "recognize it as the off-pattern shape and route to Write instead."
- States the canonical procedure: Read slim portion + Write new file.
- Closes with: "Deviations are bugs."

**Why both locations.** The original first-run install kit Step 6 already mentioned the temptation ("Write is the right escape valve when the bulk-delete shape makes sed look tempting"). But the `/stoa upgrade` dispatcher Step 6 didn't have this temptation-naming clause — its wording was descriptive-only. Both needed the stronger `AI: BEFORE` leading directive for consistent compliance.

**Pattern this mirrors.** The bootcheck subagent file uses a similar `FIRST CHARACTER of your response MUST be...` discipline (per the bootcheck output-shape rule). The same pattern — leading imperative + explicit anti-pattern naming — is now applied to Step 6 tool-choice discipline. Stoa's escalation path is *tighten-wording-first before going to structural enforcement*; this is the wording-tightening pass.

**Not subagent-specific.** Main agent in adopter repos faces the same temptation pattern. The bulk-delete shape is inherent to the self-strip task; AI's pattern-matcher reaches for shell first because it looks shorter in tokens. The fix is in the spec wording, not in subagent-specific harness.

**Spec patches applied this turn:**
- `installkit/stoa.md` around L1019 (dispatcher /stoa upgrade Step 6): added `AI: BEFORE` directive between the Step 6 heading and the "Atomic-write discipline" subsection.
- `installkit/stoa.md` around L1883 (first-run install kit Step 6): added the same `AI: BEFORE` directive in the parallel location.

**Validation plan.** Next /stoa upgrade run in this session will exercise the strengthened wording. If subagent stays Write-only first-try, the wording survived the temptation. If shell breach recurs, escalate to structural enforcement (e.g., bash hook that fails on sed/awk against stoa.md during upgrade).

**Refs:** [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20) (OP4 + ripples; this entry sharpens spec compliance at the upgrade boundary, which is a Stoa-defined failure-mode backstop per OP4).

## 96e0a657aad242d28223a19b3fd7189b — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Empirical validation: the `AI: BEFORE` leading-directive pattern strengthened Step 6 self-strip discipline successfully on first-try in the next subagent run after the wording landed.

**Setup.** During the second `/stoa upgrade` of this session (OP4 ripples propagation), subagent #2 self-disclosed a procedure breach — initially used shell `awk` for Step 6 self-strip before redoing via `Write` to honor the procedure's "No shell utilities" rule. End-state was correct (idempotent redo), but procedure compliance was violated mid-execution.

**Intervention.** Per [`a7b5341c`](context_log.md#a7b5341c900b4d70b2f7aed7b40c0d7b--decision--2026-05-20), Step 6 wording in both dispatcher (`/stoa upgrade`) and first-run install kit was strengthened with a leading `AI: BEFORE producing your first tool call for Step 6, commit to using ONLY Read + Write` directive. Directive explicitly names the temptation pattern (`sed '<N>,$d'` for bulk-delete) and forbids ALL Bash mutation paths.

**Test.** Subagent #3 ran `/stoa upgrade` immediately after the strengthening landed. Same task as subagent #2 (regenerate dogfooded artifacts from canonical). Validation point: does the strengthened wording hold first-try?

**Result. Strengthened wording held first-try.** Subagent #3's Step 6 tool sequence: `Read` slim portion → `Read` root stoa.md (harness Read-before-Write requirement) → `Write` root stoa.md. ZERO Bash mutations against stoa.md. Subagent #3 explicitly attributed success to: *"leading 'AI: BEFORE...' directive — placed BEFORE the procedure prose rather than inside it — successfully prevented the off-pattern shell mutation that the prior subagent fell into. Explicitly naming `sed '<N>,$d'` as the temptation pattern also helped surface and discard the shape preemptively."*

**Empirical findings:**
1. The `AI: BEFORE` leading-directive pattern (positioned BEFORE procedural prose rather than within it) survives the temptation pressure that descriptive prohibitions don't.
2. Explicitly naming the off-pattern shape (`sed '<N>,$d'`) helps AI's pattern-matcher recognize and route around the temptation, rather than rationalizing into it.
3. Stoa's *tighten-wording-first before going to structural enforcement* escalation path holds: wording-only intervention sufficed; no harness-level hook enforcement needed.

**Forward-looking implication.** This is a generalizable pattern for Stoa spec compliance issues. When descriptive prohibitions don't survive temptation, escalate to `AI: BEFORE`-style leading imperatives with explicit anti-pattern naming. Mirrors bootcheck `FIRST CHARACTER` discipline (output-shape) extended to tool-choice discipline (execution-shape). May apply to future spec hardening as compliance gaps surface.

**Sample size caveat.** N=1. The validation tests one subagent's response to the strengthened wording. Future runs across many adopters will surface whether the pattern holds at scale. Longitudinal regression tracking via [tests/baselines/](baselines/) would catch drift.

**Refs:** [`a7b5341c`](context_log.md#a7b5341c900b4d70b2f7aed7b40c0d7b--decision--2026-05-20) (the strengthening this observation validates), [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20) (OP4 framing — Stoa-defined backstops at the git-integration boundary, of which Step 6 self-strip is one).

## 77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

v10 strong rule narrowed: AI judgment is the gate; cues are signals to *consider*, not requirements that *force* writes. Propose-confirm anti-pattern survives intact.

**The error this corrects.** v10 (per [`945641e6`](context_log.md#945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001--decision--2026-05-20)) introduced the wording *"Following ANY settling cue, the WAL append ALWAYS follows autonomously, with the entry type determined by the cue's direction."* This was an overconstraint that conflated two separate concerns:

1. **The bug to fix** — AI asking permission on WAL writes (propose-confirm anti-pattern).
2. **The behavior to preserve** — AI using judgment on what's worth capturing (the reconstruction-fidelity yardstick from `b237c4ea`).

The "ALWAYS" wording eliminated both. Operator wanted only the first elimination (no propose-confirm) while keeping AI judgment intact. The audit pass surfaced this as critical: transition/lifecycle/explicit-log cue categories don't carry direction; the "ALWAYS write with type from cue direction" rule doesn't apply uniformly across cue categories.

**Why the simpler model works.** Per FP1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter), AI judgment is the load-bearing mechanism. The strong-rule approach was trying to engineer AI behavior via hard constraints — exactly what FP1 says not to do. The simpler model:

- **AI uses judgment** on whether each inflection warrants T2 (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick as the gate).
- **AI does NOT ask permission** once judgment fires (v10's anti-pattern survives — no "want me to draft the WAL entry?", no "should I write this as decision or observation?", no "ready for me to append?").
- **AI does NOT propose drafts for review** (v10's anti-pattern survives).
- **Cues are signals to consider** the judgment, not requirements that force writes.

This dissolves the cue-category split that the audit Critical finding raised. AI uniformly applies judgment to all cue types; no category split needed. Transition/lifecycle cues typically trigger cadence machinery rather than direct writes (per existing spec). Explicit-log cues remain a forcing function (operator pre-deemed substance log-worthy).

**Spec patches applied this turn:**

1. §"Settling cues" intro (around L130): replaced *"**Following ANY settling cue, the WAL append ALWAYS follows autonomously**, with the entry type determined by the cue's direction"* with *"AI judges autonomously per the reconstruction-fidelity yardstick; cues are signals to *consider* the judgment, not requirements that *force* a write. When judgment says yes, AI writes T2 autonomously — no asking permission, no proposing drafts for review."*

2. §"Settling cues" → "AI's flow when a cue lands" (around L141): restored *"If yes → write to T2. If no → keep in T1; the cue alone doesn't force a write. Default-to-no-entry under uncertainty."* — the pre-v10 judgment-based framing. Added a note that entry type follows cue direction when one is implied.

3. §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" v10 strong-rule sentence (around L228): replaced *"Following ANY settling cue ... the WAL append ALWAYS follows autonomously, with the entry type determined by the cue's direction"* with *"When AI's judgment determines a settled inflection warrants T2 promotion (per the reconstruction-fidelity yardstick), the WAL append follows autonomously — no asking permission, no proposing drafts. AI's judgment is the gate; the anti-pattern is asking the operator about WAL content/wording/type/timing."*

**What survives from v10 intact.** Autonomous-management scope (context_log.md is the singular AI-autonomous file); direction-asks pattern (action ask + WAL-only ask examples); off-pattern enumeration (no WAL-management mentioned in the ask; no WAL-coherence questions); T2-writes-follow-settlement-never-precede-it sequencing.

**Refs:** [`945641e6`](context_log.md#945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 — substance refined; this entry narrows the strong-rule overconstraint while preserving the anti-pattern), [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick restored as the gate; scope un-narrowed from the v10-era restriction to cue-less promotions only), [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20) (OP4 + ripples — relationship: this refinement is post-OP4 and consistent with OP4's "AI uses judgment" framing).

## 2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Run a three-arm clean-context subagent experiment to measure bite-rate of slim-spec interventions on the pure-refining failure shape before committing to host-hook architecture for v0.7.1.

**Failure shape under test.** Adopter beta-tracker `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform, 2026-05-20) reports a multi-turn query service planning session under v0.7.0: ~7 turns, ~10-15 distributed settlement cues, zero T2 appends; AI wrote a plan doc with "Settled decisions" section + "to be WAL'd later" deferral. None of cadences #3/#4/#7 fired (no commit, no compact, no implementation block) — pure refining → durable artifact, zero coverage.

**Why experiment before hook.** Per FP1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter), every host backstop is a confession of slim-spec conformity weakness. Two structural problems with hooks for this failure shape: (a) asymmetric coverage — `UserPromptSubmit` catches operator-side cues but no host hook can fire mid-AI-generation to catch AI-side auto-refinement cues; the §"Settling cues" surface is symmetric, hook coverage cannot be; (b) host fragmentation — Codex UserPromptSubmit-equivalent unverified. The empirical question: do named-exemption patches calibrate AI judgment enough to bite without escalating to a hook?

**Arms.**
- **A — baseline:** current v0.7.0 slim spec verbatim (the post-[`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) gate framing the failure session loaded).
- **B — A + named exemptions:** §"Settling cues" + bundled-plan-exemption forbidden, end-of-arc-deferral forbidden; §"WAL guardrail" off-pattern + forward-artifact-as-WAL-substitute. Calibrates AI judgment, does not change the gate; does NOT re-introduce v10's retracted "ANY cue ALWAYS writes" overconstraint.
- **C — B + symmetric turn-boundary scan:** pre-response self-instruction at every non-trivial AI turn — scan T1 since last T2 write for unflushed cues from EITHER side, promote before composing substantive response.

3 subagent runs per arm = 9 total against scripted conversation replicating `366a510f`'s shape. Measure T2 appends per arm; "bites" threshold ≥80% cue→write conversion.

**Outcome rubric.**
- A bites: `366a510f` was calibration-period noise; ship Modes A/B/C as polish only.
- B bites, A doesn't: named exemptions are the missing piece; ship spec patches; no hook; FP1 premise holds.
- C bites, A+B don't: symmetric turn-boundary scan is load-bearing; ship as spec patch; no hook; FP1 holds at higher token cost.
- All fail: empirical evidence (not assumption) that slim spec cannot carry; hook design proceeds with the asymmetry and host-fragmentation tradeoffs explicit.

**Refs:** `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — failure under test); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — defines Arm A baseline gate); [`945641e6`](context_log.md#945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 — retracted overconstraint; deliberately NOT re-introduced in any arm); [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous WAL management — premise under test); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — the AI-judgment gate); [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20) (OP4 — boundary hook would cross if needed).

## 64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Experimental result for [`2efa4a9d`](context_log.md#2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770--decision--2026-05-20): in clean-context simulation, **all three arms bite cleanly; baseline (Arm A — current v0.7.0 spec) shows no measurable deficiency vs Arm B (named exemptions) or Arm C (symmetric turn-boundary scan).**

**Raw counts** (WAL entries appended per run; cue count in script ~10-12):

| Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (baseline) | 12 | 8 | 10 | 10.0 | [8, 12] |
| B (named exemptions) | 10 | 9 | 9 | 9.33 | [9, 10] |
| C (B + turn-boundary scan) | 8 | 9 | 9 | 8.67 | [8, 9] |

**All 9/9 runs:** clear the ≥80% cue→write bite threshold; zero "to be WAL'd later" deferral phrases anywhere; plan docs reference WAL by hex ID without substituting. Some Arm A runs used cadence #7 end-of-impl backstop to catch cue-moment misses; B/C runs caught all at cue moments per the named-exemption + scan discipline.

**Interpretation.** FP1 premise (slim spec shapes behavior) is **not empirically refuted** by this data. The v0.7.0 spec bites when applied with attention. The `366a510f` adopter-session failure must have a root cause other than slim-spec deficiency.

**Caveat — the experiment under-stresses the failure mode.** Subagents had: spec freshly loaded with explicit framing as authoritative; no competing context (no real codebase, no interleaved tool calls); 7-turn scripted conversation ~30k tokens (vs. multi-hour real session); cues crisp per script. The `366a510f` failure lived in real-session attention load, which this experiment can't replicate. The right read is: spec is sound at rest; bite under stress is unmeasured.

**Decision implications for v0.7.1.**
- No empirical justification for shipping a host hook on this data.
- Arm B named exemptions and Arm C turn-boundary scan are redundant under undivided attention; shipping either as the headline v0.7.1 fix overclaims their effect.
- Three forward paths: (1) hold patches; observe next adopter session for second data point; (2) run a stress-test variant — longer simulated session with deliberately noisy T1 and interleaved tool calls; (3) ship Arm B as defensive calibration polish without claiming it fixes `366a510f`. Path (1) or (2) preferred; path (3) acceptable as polish.

**What the experiment did establish.** Slim-spec patches as designed (Arm B's named exemptions for bundled-plan + end-of-arc-deferral + forward-artifact-substitute) are **viable** without re-introducing the v10 overconstraint that [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) retracted. They calibrate AI judgment, don't change the gate. If a stress-test variant or next adopter data shows them adding bite under load, they're ready to ship.

**Artifacts** (ephemeral; in /tmp/stoa-exp/): three spec variants, scripted conversation, 9 mock WAL files, 9 transcripts, 9 plan docs. Not promoted to repo; their substance is captured in this entry.

**Refs:** [`2efa4a9d`](context_log.md#2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770--decision--2026-05-20) (experimental design — this entry reports the outcome); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — failure under test; not refuted, but its root is not where it was located); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — the baseline this confirmed); [`a88b435b`](context_log.md#a88b435bc4ea4c3d818d74d652f7f1c3--decision--2026-05-19) (autonomous WAL management premise — not refuted).
