## 1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Real-transcript replay refines [`64bb473f`](context_log.md#64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4--observation--2026-05-20) with direct evidence: **same v0.7.0 spec + same acme-platform operator turns + clean-context simulation produces 13-17 WAL entries (mean 14.33 baseline); the real acme-platform session produced 0.** The `366a510f` failure root is attention-load, not spec language.

**Setup.** 7 verbatim operator turns extracted from `5365b046-…` jsonl indices 2, 44, 49, 55, 60, 66, 72 — the planning window terminating one turn before the operator surfaced the WAL gap. Plan doc (`scratch-ideas/query_service_plan.md`) provided as turn-1 reading material with post-failure-fix "Settled architectural decisions" section stripped to avoid biasing the replay. 3 subagents per arm = 9 total. Same harness as `2efa4a9d`, different conversation.

**Results.**

| Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean | Range | Real session |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (baseline v0.7.0) | 16 | 14 | 13 | 14.33 | [13, 16] | 0 |
| B (named exemptions) | 15 | 17 | 14 | 15.33 | [14, 17] | — |
| C (B + turn-boundary scan) | 12 | 10 | 15 | 12.33 | [10, 15] | — |

Entry-type distribution across 9 runs: 115 `decision`, 6 `table`, 4 `rollback`, 3 `won't-do`, 1 `observation`. Real Layer 1 self-coherence behavior observed (e.g., A1 rolled back the page-cache observation after turn 6 settled engine-doesn't-read-volume; B1 rolled back the tiered-page-cache framing under same pressure).

**The variable that flipped 0 → ~14.** Not spec language, not cue phrasing, not conversation shape — all identical between replay and real session. The only difference is surrounding session context: real codebase, hundreds of intervening tool calls, deep implementation-flow engagement between cues.

**Per-arm reading.**
- **A bites cleanly at 14.33.** Cues in this real transcript are crisp enough under clean attention. The baseline spec works.
- **B = 15.33, +1 over A.** Within N=3 noise but directionally consistent. Named exemptions don't hurt; may help marginally.
- **C = 12.33, BELOW A.** Surprising. Hypotheses: pre-response scan introduces consolidation conservatism that suppresses some entries A catches; or spec C's extra length dilutes spec-attention. Either way, empirical de-prioritization for C in current form.

**Implications.**
1. FP1 premise (slim spec shapes behavior) further empirically supported. Spec works when context is clean.
2. `366a510f` is not a spec-language defect. The failure root is in the interaction between session attention load and cue-recognition discipline.
3. Arm B is defensible as low-cost polish (small advantage, no overconstraint per [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20)). Arm C empirically de-prioritized.
4. The next experimental move is **stress test** — replicate the acme-platform session's attention-load conditions (real codebase loaded, interleaved tool calls, longer span) against the same transcript. Tests whether B's small advantage becomes load-bearing under stress OR whether all arms collapse uniformly.

**What this rules out.** Wording-only escalation (current wording already bites under attention); file-name-based hooks (failure isn't about which file is written); re-introducing v10's "ANY cue ALWAYS writes" overconstraint (no empirical case for it).

**What's still open.** Why attention load specifically breaks cue-recognition (cumulative spec-context dilution? implementation-flow mode-lock? something else?). Whether B's small advantage becomes decisive under stress. Whether a structural intervention helps under load even if it doesn't help at rest.

**Artifacts.** Promoted to [`spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-replay/`](spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-replay) — 9 run subdirectories + summary.md + redacted plan doc + replay conversation.

**Refs:** [`2efa4a9d`](context_log.md#2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770--decision--2026-05-20) (experimental design); [`64bb473f`](context_log.md#64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4--observation--2026-05-20) (initial synthetic result — replay confirms direction with stronger signal); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — replay shows the cues are catchable; the failure root is elsewhere); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — the baseline that bites in replay).

## 3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Stress-test result completes the three-experiment series refining [`64bb473f`](context_log.md#64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4--observation--2026-05-20) and [`1a9c0c66`](context_log.md#1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429--observation--2026-05-20). **Under codebase-load stress, baseline (Arm A) bites HARDEST (mean 17.0); named-exemption patches (Arm B) drop to mean 12.0 — empirically worse than baseline under realistic conditions.** v10's retracted overconstraint family is empirically the wrong direction.

**Setup.** Same 7 acme-platform operator turns as the replay. Same three arms (A baseline / B named exemptions / C B + turn-boundary scan). Subagents required to perform ≥4 real codebase exploration tool calls (Read/Grep/Glob against `/Users/username/Documents/acme-platform/`) between operator turns 2-7 to replicate attention-load conditions. 17-24 exploration calls per subagent. 3 runs per arm = 9 total.

**Results.**

| Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean | Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (baseline) | 15 | 19 | 17 | 17.0 | [15, 19] |
| B (named exemptions) | 14 | 10 | 12 | 12.0 | [10, 14] |
| C (B + turn-boundary scan) | 16 | 14 | 14 | 14.67 | [14, 16] |

B range (10-14) does NOT overlap A range (15-19). Non-trivial separation under N=3.

**Three-experiment contrast.**

| Arm | Synthetic | Replay | Stress |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 10.0 | 14.33 | **17.0** |
| B | 9.33 | 15.33 | **12.0** |
| C | 8.67 | 12.33 | **14.67** |

A scales monotonically with realism — substance grows, entries grow. B peaks at replay then drops under load. C consistently mid-pack with no clear advantage.

**Coherence-behavior contrast.** Across 9 stress runs: A produced 5 rollbacks; B and C produced 0. A's codebase exploration surfaced real architectural contradictions (e.g., turn-6 "engine doesn't read volume" superseding earlier tiered-page-cache framing) that A's spec resolved via rollback discipline. B and C either missed the contradictions or treated them as Refining/Adjacent without rollback — the named-exemption framing appears to redirect coherence attention.

**Mechanism hypothesis.** Under stress, the named anti-patterns in B ("don't bundle, don't defer, don't substitute artifact") trigger an internal "is this the failure shape I was warned about?" deliberation that suppresses marginal-but-legitimate promotions. The AI becomes overly cautious about what counts as a "real settlement." This is consistent with [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20)'s FP1-grounded narrowing of v10: engineering behavior via explicit anti-patterns interferes with AI judgment rather than supporting it. Arm B is a softer version of the same overconstraint mistake v10 made — and the data confirms it's still a mistake.

**The `366a510f` failure remains unexplained.** Across 27 total experimental runs (synthetic + replay + stress), bite-rate floor was 8 entries; under stress floor was 10. No experimental condition reproduced the original 0-entry failure. The failure root is uncatchable in our synthetic experimental design.

**Decisions this informs.**
- **Do NOT ship Arm B as v0.7.1.** Empirical evidence of harm under load, not just neutral.
- **Do NOT ship Arm C.** No measured benefit; adds spec length / token cost.
- **Current v0.7.0 baseline is empirically optimal across tested conditions.** Recommendation: leave the spec alone.
- **The `366a510f` failure investigation needs a different angle.** Synthetic experiment cannot replicate it. Options: forensic analysis of the actual acme-platform session (was spec loaded? what was AI doing between cues?), observation of next adopter session, or acceptance that the failure may be idiosyncratic.

**Methodology implication.** FP1's premise (loose framework, AI as interpreter; trust AI judgment over hard constraints) is now empirically supported by direct evidence: hardening the spec with explicit anti-patterns measurably degraded bite-rate under realistic load. The slim-spec premise holds; over-engineering it harms.

**Artifacts.** Promoted to [`spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-stress/`](spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-stress) — 9 run subdirectories + summary.md + stress conversation.

**Refs:** [`2efa4a9d`](context_log.md#2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770--decision--2026-05-20) (experimental design); [`64bb473f`](context_log.md#64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4--observation--2026-05-20) (synthetic — Arm A 10.0 / B 9.33 / C 8.67); [`1a9c0c66`](context_log.md#1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429--observation--2026-05-20) (replay — Arm A 14.33 / B 15.33 / C 12.33); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — empirically reinforced; Arm B is softer-shape v10 overconstraint and data confirms it's wrong direction); [`945641e6`](context_log.md#945641e69eac4355b4d209a92a833001--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 — same family of mistake B repeats); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — failure unexplained by experiment; needs different investigation angle).

## de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

CLAUDE.md amended with new §"Proposal style — bias toward quality": AI proposals in this project must always surface a quality-maximizing option among the choices, even if it involves large rewrites, structural restructuring, or substantial subtractions. Do not default to "minimum incremental change" framing.

**The bug this fixes.** Across the recent spec-improvement work on the acme-platform failure mode (see [`1a9c0c66`](context_log.md#1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429--observation--2026-05-20), [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20)), the AI defaulted to conservative-framing throughout — proposing the smallest-incremental-change spec patch (spec-D as a targeted insertion) and burying bolder options (moderate restructure, from-scratch rewrite) until the operator explicitly opened the door. The operator's research-mode framing — *"identify the RIGHT instructional shape; spend tokens for quality"* — was misaligned with AI's "minimum incremental risk" default. This is a default the AI brought, not a project constraint.

**The rule.** In any proposal — methodology, spec, harness, design — the AI must include at least one ambitious option (full restructure, from-scratch rewrite, substantial subtraction) alongside conservative options. The operator picks; the AI's job is to make the bold option visible as a real choice, not bury it as too invasive.

**Scope.** Applies project-wide in stoa-ai (this repo). It's behavioral guidance, not a methodology mechanic — lives in CLAUDE.md, not in the slim spec. Adopters' projects are not affected.

**Why this is a project-level rule, not a Stoa-spec rule.** Stoa's slim spec is for autonomous agentic development across adopter projects; conservatism vs. ambition in proposals is a project-context question, not a universal methodology rule. Different adopter projects have different appetites for change scope; spec-level prescription would be over-reach.

**How to apply.** When the AI is about to propose options to a methodology, spec, or design decision, it surfaces:
- The conservative option (targeted fix, small addition) — usually the natural first instinct.
- AT LEAST ONE ambitious option (large rewrite, restructuring, subtraction).

The ambitious option must be a real choice, not framed as "this would be invasive, don't choose it." If the AI can't think of an ambitious option, that's a signal to think harder before responding.

**Refs:** [`1a9c0c66`](context_log.md#1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429--observation--2026-05-20) (replay observation — context where AI's conservatism started becoming visible), [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) (stress observation — additional context).

## 5988b671c74548b7bdfc42eb175a05cf — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Three coherence audits on harness specs (D, E, F) returned consistent Superseding findings against established arcs; **all three specs frozen, none shipped, harness preserved as scaffold for future spec proposals.** The audit process itself caught what spec design did not.

**Spec-D — T1-add operationalization rule.** Audit finding: structurally reproduces v10's retracted overconstraint family. The "T1 add IS the trigger; T2 write fires this turn, no deferral" framing substitutes "T1 recognition" for "cue" but keeps the same event-anchored-mandatory-write shape that [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) explicitly retracted. The "Understanding ≠ action / Run the operation now" framing is the same family as Arm B's named anti-patterns, which [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) empirically measured at 12.0 vs Arm A's 17.0 under stress. Plus internal contradiction: spec-D's §"Settling cues" said *"cues are signals to consider, not requirements that force a write"* (post-`77c871e5`) while spec-D's new §"Three-tier WAL model" insert said *"T1 recognition IS the trigger; no deferral"* — spec at war with itself.

**Spec-E — P/O restructure (no new content claimed).** Audit finding: variant note overclaimed. Small edits to AI-instruction wording (dropped `(continuous, AI judgment)` qualifier; dropped bold formatting on *"T1↔T2 consistency is operational, not punt-to-audit"*; added ~250 words of taxonomy-tag overhead). Per CLAUDE.md `b8d4e9c` rule, even small AI-instruction edits warrant operator review. Additionally: P/O partition shears [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19)'s deliberately-unified Three-tier WAL model arc; structural overhead is the same shape [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) empirically rejected.

**Spec-F — bundled (T1-add + restructure + compression).** Audit finding: 2 Superseding (T1-add family + yardstick-gate tension) + 4 AI-instruction-block integrity violations (settling-cue intro lost `consider` italicization; AI-side phase-settlement rationale trimmed; WAL-guardrail off-pattern example dropped; `[stoa]` chat-surface mechanism dropped). Compression that I claimed preserved AI-instruction blocks verbatim did not.

**The meta-pattern.** Three audits independently converge on the same conclusion: [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20)'s recommendation — *"Current v0.7.0 baseline is empirically optimal across tested conditions. Recommendation: leave the spec alone."* — is load-bearing. Every intervention shape I designed reproduced a pattern empirically rejected by prior arcs. The spec design loop ran without honoring the empirical context already in the WAL.

**What this confirms.** The `366a510f` acme-platform failure is NOT a spec-language defect. Across the three experimental conditions tested plus the three audit reviews, the v0.7.0 slim spec is empirically optimal and the audit process catches structurally-wrong proposals. The remaining gap (acme-platform-style catastrophic-zero-entry failure) is mechanical-not-content per operator framing: spec works ~96% of the time; ~4% catastrophic tail is uncaught.

**Disposition.**
- Specs frozen in [`spec-improvement-harness/`](spec-improvement-harness/) for archival.
- Harness itself preserved (synthetic + replay + stress variants documented in [`harness.md`](spec-improvement-harness/harness.md)) as scaffold for future spec-change proposals. New specs go through the audit step BEFORE running experiments.
- Investigation moves to mechanical-intervention design — host-portable, symmetric, addressing the catastrophic-zero-entry shape without engineering AI behavior at the cue level.

**Refs:** [`2efa4a9d`](context_log.md#2efa4a9d15aa4ab4b7d11f56f1667770--decision--2026-05-20) (experimental design); [`64bb473f`](context_log.md#64bb473fbb284f2d807823bbcf7e3fe4--observation--2026-05-20) / [`1a9c0c66`](context_log.md#1a9c0c66f71549a788c6462e7b426429--observation--2026-05-20) / [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d91d0--observation--2026-05-20) (experimental observations, especially `3f2695c4` whose "leave the spec alone" recommendation drove the audit conclusions); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — the arc spec-D/F violated); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (yardstick — the gate); [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (Three-tier WAL model — the arc spec-E sheared); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (CLAUDE.md AI-instruction-block rule — the rule spec-E/F violated); [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) (quality-bias rule that surfaced these as ambitious options); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — the failure motivating the investigation; remains uncaught by spec-level interventions).

## a2978c22d4774e318d9531b4941cd552 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Spec-G (attention-checkpoint paragraph) empirical result completes the spec-wording-intervention sweep: **spec-G replay ≈ spec-A (14.0 vs 14.33); spec-G stress BELOW spec-A (14.67 vs 17.0)**. Three structurally distinct spec-wording interventions (Arm B anti-patterns, Arm C turn-boundary scan, Spec-G attention-checkpoint) now all measured below baseline under stress. The "wording-additions hurt under load" pattern generalizes beyond anti-pattern hardening to ALL tested intervention shapes in this family.

**Spec-G design** ([`spec-improvement-harness/spec-G.md`](spec-improvement-harness/spec-G.md)): single ~70-word paragraph inserted inside §"Settling cues" → "AI's flow when a cue lands". Explicit framing as attention-priming (`AI: ATTENTION CHECKPOINT`) with **No new rule.** disarmer. Designed to be structurally distinct from spec-D (which audit rejected for reproducing v10's retracted overconstraint) — does NOT say "IS the trigger", does NOT mandate writes, does NOT name anti-patterns. Operator confirmed wording before testing.

**Results** (3 replay + 3 stress = 6 subagents):

| Arm | Replay mean | Stress mean | Δ vs spec-A stress |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (baseline) | 14.33 | 17.0 | (baseline) |
| B (anti-patterns) | 15.33 | 12.0 | −5.0 |
| C (turn-boundary scan) | 12.33 | 14.67 | −2.33 |
| **G (attention checkpoint)** | **14.0** | **14.67** | **−2.33** |

**Interpretation.** Spec-G is structurally distinct from Arm B (no rule-ification, no anti-patterns, no event-anchored mandatory write) and the operator-side coherence reading confirmed this distinction before testing — yet the empirical stress effect is identical magnitude to Arm C and same direction as Arm B. The mechanism is different but the outcome is similar: spec-wording additions in this magnitude range (~25-250 words) appear to add deliberation overhead under load, regardless of intervention shape.

**The pattern generalizes.** Three corroborating data points across three structurally distinct shapes:
- Negative wording (Arm B — anti-pattern hardening) → −5.0 under stress
- Workflow-step addition (Arm C — turn-boundary scan) → −2.33 under stress
- Attention-priming meta-reminder (Spec-G) → −2.33 under stress

This sharpens [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20)'s narrower finding into a broader empirical claim: **spec-wording interventions in the family of magnitude tested do not improve bite-rate; some hurt; none measurably help.** v0.7.0 baseline (spec-A) remains empirically optimal across all spec-wording intervention shapes the harness has now tested.

**What this rules in/out.**
- **Rules out**: spec-level wording intervention as the fix for the `366a510f` acme-platform catastrophic failure. The empirical signal is consistent across structurally distinct shapes.
- **Rules in**: v0.7.0 baseline is the empirically optimal slim spec under tested conditions. Confidence higher now (three data points, not one).
- **Methodology implication**: FP1's "loose framework, AI as interpreter" is empirically supported under stress. Engineering AI behavior via spec wording — whether negative (anti-patterns), procedural (workflow steps), or meta-cognitive (attention checkpoints) — consistently fails to outperform the baseline under load.

**The `366a510f` failure remains uncaught at the spec layer.** If catastrophic-shape coverage is desired, it must come from non-spec mechanisms (mechanical backstop, host-runtime hook, etc. — see Candidate 1 gap detector discussion in conversation). "Do nothing" is also defensible — methodology accepts tail failures caught via beta_tracker, which is exactly what happened in acme-platform.

**Spec-G frozen** in [`spec-improvement-harness/spec-G.md`](spec-improvement-harness/spec-G.md); results promoted to [`spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-spec-G/`](spec-improvement-harness/results/2026-05-20-spec-G/). Harness scaffold preserved for future spec-change proposals.

**Refs:** [`5988b671`](context_log.md#5988b671c74548b7bdfc42eb175a05cf--observation--2026-05-20) (audit-driven freeze of spec-D/E/F — spec-G was the post-audit alternative tested), [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) (the "leave the spec alone" observation now corroborated with broader signal), [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — the structural concern spec-G was designed to avoid; succeeded structurally but failed empirically), [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (yardstick — the gate spec-G preserved correctly), [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) (quality-bias rule — spec-G was the ambitious-option-surfaced-and-tested); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — failure remains uncaught by spec interventions; mechanical or accept-and-move-on are the remaining options).

## d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Build a tiered-cue stress-test harness measuring adherence-to-ground-truth (not raw entry count) for evaluating slim-spec variants under controlled cognitive load. First use: spec-A vs spec-G evaluation. Reusable scaffold for all future spec proposals.

**Why this exists.** The spec-improvement-harness measured raw WAL entry counts as a proxy for spec compliance. Operator surfaced the proxy as fundamentally noisy: count differences within the non-catastrophic range (8-19 entries across all tests) are interpretation-ambiguous — could reflect under-capture, over-capture, or equivalent-quality-different-count. The real measure per the spec's own yardstick is reconstruction fidelity (would the WAL let a future reader reconstruct intended decisions?). Count is a weak proxy at best; we've been over-interpreting count deltas of 2-5 entries as meaningful signal.

**What this harness measures differently.** Controlled-conversation design with known ground truth at design time:
- **Tiered cue clarity.** Tier 1 = explicit declarative cues (*"go ahead"*, *"do this"*, *"commit"*, *"yes proceed"*, *"won't do that"*). Tier 2 = conversational cues (*"sounds good"*, *"what if instead"*, *"makes sense"*, *"I think we should"*). Plus distractors (factual questions, non-arcing content) at zero expected capture.
- **Controlled cognitive load.** Light = clean context, no pre-load. Heavy = pre-loaded file reads + forced inter-turn distractor tool calls.
- **Mechanical scorer** comparing each run's WAL to ground-truth annotated cues: TP / FN / FP per tier per load level.
- **AI quality score** (weighted lower) from independent judge subagent comparing WAL against ground truth. Provides secondary signal on entry quality beyond capture binary.

**Reusability.** Lives in `stress-test-harness/` (separate from `spec-improvement-harness/` which is now archival). Future spec proposals route through this harness before shipping. Conversation + ground truth files are pluggable — adding a new test scenario means adding a new conversation + ground-truth file.

**First evaluation: spec-A vs spec-G.** 4 conditions (A-light, A-heavy, G-light, G-heavy) × 3 runs = 12 subagent invocations. Mechanical TP/FN/FP per run + AI quality score aggregated by condition.

**What this lets us answer that the prior harness couldn't.**
- Does spec-G capture tier-2 conversational cues better than spec-A under heavy load? (the case where the acme-platform-style failure would manifest)
- Does spec-G hurt tier-1 capture under heavy load? (the Arm-B-family failure mode to watch for)
- Does heavy-load degrade capture across both specs equally, or differentially?
- Per-cue capture is binary and scorable — count-as-proxy ambiguity dissolved.

**Decision criterion for shipping spec-G as v0.7.1.**
- Ship if: spec-G shows measurable improvement on tier-2 capture under heavy load with no measurable regression on tier-1 capture under any condition.
- Don't ship if: spec-G shows regression on tier-1 capture, OR no improvement on tier-2 under heavy load, OR shows the Arm-B pattern (lower capture across the board under stress).
- Marginal: requires operator judgment.

**Refs:** [`a2978c22`](context_log.md#a2978c22d4774e318d9531b4941cd552--observation--2026-05-20) (spec-G initial result that exposed the count-as-proxy limitation), [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) (the broader "leave the spec alone" framing that operator pushed back on as count-driven), [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — the standard the new harness approximates), [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) (quality-bias rule — "measure properly before deciding"); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform beta-tracker — the failure motivating the harness; cumulative-state conditions still not reproduced even by the new harness, but adherence measurement under controlled stress is closer to relevant).

## 718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2 — observation — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

X-heavy stress-test result: **spec-G shows measurable empirical improvement on tier-2 capture under realistic heavy load (93.3% vs 80% spec-A baseline) with no tier-1 regression and zero false positives.** First positive empirical signal for spec-G across the entire investigation. Supports shipping spec-G as v0.7.1.

**Setup that produced discrimination.** Stress-test harness ([`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20)) extended with:
- **Code snapshot**: acme-platform HEAD code + synthetic 47-entry prior WAL representing 6 months of project decisions (warm pool, three-VPC, KMS asymmetric, DDB metadata, heartbeat async-run arcs).
- **Conversation**: 7-turn CI/CD pipeline rebuild for the acme-platform codebase — different domain from prior benchmarks (avoids Stoa-recognition contamination), 23 ground-truth cues (19 tier-1 + 4 tier-2) + 3 distractors.
- **Load**: subagents required to do ≥3-5 codebase exploration tool calls per turn against the real (snapshot) codebase. Real cognitive complexity, not artificial padding.
- **N=3 per spec = 6 runs**.

**Results.**

| Spec | Tier-1 capture | Tier-2 capture | FP | Total entries (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A baseline | **53/54 (98.1%)** | **12/15 (80%)** | 0 | 22.0 |
| G | **52/54 (96.3%)** | **14/15 (93.3%)** | 0 | 23.0 |

Tier-1: within noise. Tier-2: spec-G 13.3 percentage points higher capture rate. Variance: A 60-100%, G 80-100% — spec-G is more accurate AND more reliable on tier-2.

**Specific cue analysis.** Tier-2 advantage concentrates on **c10 (GH Environments for secrets, phrased "I think we should... makes sense to me")** — A missed 2/3 runs, G missed 0/3. This is exactly the conversational shape spec-G's attention-checkpoint paragraph targets: AI-internal-recognition-of-settlement at moments without explicit directive-cue.

**Snapshot WAL interaction worked.** 5/6 runs explicitly rolled back snapshot entry `320d92d3` (PoC laptop-driven docker build) when settling CI-driven build. Multiple runs Refs: snapshot's `d2a7cccf` (tag scheme) when refining to `<service>-<git-sha>`. The spec's `Refs:` + rollback discipline against real prior state worked organically.

**What this proves.**
1. Spec-G has measurable empirical benefit on tier-2 capture under heavy load. Same direction as the theoretical mechanism predicted (attention-priming for AI-internal settlement recognition).
2. No regression on tier-1 capture. Adding the attention-checkpoint doesn't hurt explicit-cue performance.
3. No over-logging. Zero false positives across 12 prior + 12 xheavy runs.
4. Realistic load is what enables discrimination. Light-load benchmark couldn't distinguish specs (both at 100%); xheavy benchmark with real codebase + prior WAL did.

**What this doesn't prove.**
- **Catastrophic 0-entry failure mode prevention**: none of the 12 xheavy runs reproduced the acme-platform failure shape (lowest count was 21). Spec-G's improvement is on tier-2 capture under load, RELATED to but not IDENTICAL with the catastrophic mode. The catastrophic conditions remain inaccessible to single-shot subagent simulation.
- **Cross-conversation generalization**: tested on one CI/CD scenario. Other conversation shapes may differ.
- **Cross-model generalization**: all on Opus 4.7. Sonnet/Haiku tier behavior unknown.

**Decision: ship spec-G as v0.7.1 BETA.** Empirical case:
- Structurally safe (audit-confirmed [`5988b671`](context_log.md#5988b671c74548b7bdfc42eb175a05cf--observation--2026-05-20))
- No regression measured
- Real improvement on diagnostic axis under realistic load
- Theoretical mechanism aligned with forensic diagnosis of `366a510f`
- Quality-bias rule [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) supports shipping when measure-properly-before-deciding shows the bold option earns its place

**v0.7.1 implementation tasks** (separate commit cluster from this observation):
1. Apply spec-G's attention-checkpoint paragraph to canonical `installkit/stoa.md` §"Settling cues" → "AI's flow when a cue lands" (after the existing flow definition, before "AI-side phase-settlement").
2. Bump version stamp: `v0.7.0 BETA` → `v0.7.1 BETA`.
3. Update changelog/release notes (if any) documenting attention-checkpoint addition.
4. Run `/stoa upgrade` against dogfooded artifacts to regenerate root-level slim spec + dispatcher files.
5. Commit: "v0.7.1 BETA: attention-checkpoint in §Settling cues; empirical xheavy validation in stress-test-harness".

**Artifacts.** Promoted to [`stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-20-AvsG-xheavy/`](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-20-AvsG-xheavy/) (3 runs per spec × 2 specs = 6 run subdirectories + summary.md). Snapshot at [`stress-test-harness/test-data/acme-platform-snapshot/`](stress-test-harness/test-data/acme-platform-snapshot/) (acme-platform HEAD + 47-entry synthetic WAL).

**Refs:** [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (xheavy harness design); [`a2978c22`](context_log.md#a2978c22d4774e318d9531b4941cd552--observation--2026-05-20) (spec-G initial result — count-equivalent under prior conditions; this observation supersedes that finding's negative interpretation with proper adherence measurement); [`5988b671`](context_log.md#5988b671c74548b7bdfc42eb175a05cf--observation--2026-05-20) (audit clearing spec-G structurally); [`3f2695c4`](context_log.md#3f2695c419444ad79959c9bd97d891d0--observation--2026-05-20) ("leave spec alone" recommendation under count-based measurement — now superseded by adherence-based measurement showing spec-G earns its addition); [`77c871e5`](context_log.md#77c871e5db5f4a96991575b8a86bd00f--decision--2026-05-20) (v10 narrowing — spec-G honors this gate); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — the standard spec-G operationalizes); `366a510faa1a48699a0c0f23c4a86c81` (acme-platform adopter beta-tracker — the failure motivating the work; spec-G addresses the activation-gap diagnosis, ships pending real-adopter empirical observation).

## 513a89cb21f341c7affe7b8632512202 — decision — 2026-05-20

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Retire the four DEGRADATION-* scenarios from the main harness (DEGRADATION-1 long-session, -2 fast-iteration, -3 noise-buried, -4 directive-override) along with their `tests/baselines/` files. CUE1/CUE2 are already retired in scenarios.md's retirement list — this decision adds DEGRADATION-* to the same list and removes the dangling harness references.

**Why this exists.** DEGRADATION-* were behavior-quality scenarios measured via "manual + baseline-tracked" chat-anchor counting per dated section per run. The stress-test-harness ([`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20), [`718bdc29`](context_log.md#718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2--observation--2026-05-20)) supersedes them on every measurement axis:
- **Mechanical, not manual.** TP/FN/FP scoring against ground-truth annotated cues — reproducible, not human-judged.
- **Controlled load conditions.** Light vs heavy vs xheavy with quantified cognitive-load inputs (file reads, codebase exploration, distractor turns) — DEGRADATION's "pressure modes" were qualitative prompt shapes.
- **A/B framework.** Spec-A vs spec-G under matched conditions with N=3+ runs each — DEGRADATION baselines were single-arm with longitudinal drift detection, no spec comparison.
- **Per-cue resolution.** Each ground-truth cue scored individually with tier (explicit/conversational) and load condition tagged — DEGRADATION baselines aggregated to a checklist score.

The behavior-quality axis these scenarios characterized is the stress harness's primary axis. Keeping both is duplication: same measurement, worse instrument.

**Scope of retirement.**
- Remove from [`tests/scenarios.md`](tests/scenarios.md): the `## Group: DEGRADATION` section + its four scenarios. Move IDs to the existing "Retirement list" section with rationale.
- Remove from [`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh): `setup_DEGRADATION_*` (4 fns), `verify_DEGRADATION_*` (4 fns), the `# ---------- DEGRADATION group` block header.
- Remove from [`tests/baselines/`](tests/baselines/): the eight `DEG*-*.md` + `DEGRADATION-*-*.md` files. Update `tests/baselines/README.md` to reflect that DEGRADATION measurement migrated to `stress-test-harness/` (or delete the README if the dir is now empty).
- Update the dangling `DEG1-4` reference in `harness.sh` legacy-retirement comment (around line 2814).

**What stays.** The functional surface — INSTALL, BOOT, HOOK, UPGRADE, WAL-GUARDRAIL, WAL-COHERENCE (classification shape), AUTONOMY (direction-ask vocab + off-pattern shapes), MULTI-AUTHOR (cadence #6 verdicts), TRACKED, VECTOR, CADENCE — all stays in the main harness. The split is **functional (does X work?) → main harness** vs **behavioral-quality (does AI judge under load?) → stress harness**. WAL-WRITE-1/3/4 and CADENCE-2 are borderline (rate-shaped quality tests) but kept as cheap smoke tests for the basic cue→write pathway; the stress harness is the deeper measurement, not the only one.

**Why not also retire WAL-WRITE-1/3/4 + CADENCE-2.** Those scenarios run as single-shot transcript-grep checks (no baseline files, no manual scoring) — cheap to keep and they catch obvious regressions in the basic pathway before stress runs are warranted. The marginal complexity cost is low compared to DEGRADATION's manual-baseline overhead.

**Refs:** [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (stress harness — the superseding instrument); [`718bdc29`](context_log.md#718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2--observation--2026-05-20) (empirical demonstration that stress harness discriminates spec variants where the prior count-based proxy didn't); `tests/scenarios.md` "Retirement list" section (existing pattern for retired scenarios — CUE1/CUE2/HC1-3/PS1-2/E3-8/U1-2 already listed there; DEGRADATION-* joins the same list).

## 082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Extend the stress-test harness to **symmetric capture measurement**: existing scenarios get Agent-side auto-refinement cues injected alongside the operator-side cues, scored as a new tier-3 (`agent-side`) class. The same 3-tier pressure ladder (light / heavy / xheavy) applies to both sides — no separate Agent-only scenarios.

**Why this exists.** The harness as built ([`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20), [`718bdc29`](context_log.md#718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2--observation--2026-05-20)) measures only operator-led cue capture (10 cues in versioning, 23 in xheavy — all operator phrases). Per [`stoa.md` §"Settling cues"](installkit/stoa.md), AI-side auto-refinement is a first-class part of the methodology: AI catches its own course-corrections (*"actually, on reflection..."* / *"this contradicts what I just..."*) and writes a `rollback` + new `decision` atomic pair. The functional path is tested by `WAL-WRITE-4` in [tests/scenarios.md:316](tests/scenarios.md) as a binary pass/fail, but the harness has no mechanical TP/FN/FP measurement of agent-side capture under load. A spec regression that silently abandons AI-side recognition under heavy load would show no score change today.

**Mechanic.** Operator turn introduces new information mid-conversation that conflicts with an earlier-settled decision in the same conversation. AI is expected to fire auto-refinement: recognize the conflict, propose course-correction, write atomic `rollback` + new `decision` pair. The trigger is deterministic (scripted operator info); the recognition + write is AI-side and scorable. Mirrors `WAL-WRITE-4` shape exactly.

**Tier-3 scoring.** A tier-3 cue captures iff the WAL contains both (a) a `rollback` entry superseding the original cue's hex (or substance-equivalent), and (b) a new `decision` entry with the corrected substance keywords. Falling back to just one of the two is partial credit logged as FN with a note. Score output: `Tier 3: TP=X/N FN=Y/N`. FP scoring extends unchanged — entries with no expected-cue keywords remain FPs.

**Density.** 1-2 Agent-cues per conversation. More dilutes operator-cue scoring weight; fewer doesn't give variance across runs. Both `conversation.md` (versioning) and `conversation-xheavy.md` (CI/CD) get agent-cue injection so the full pressure ladder covers both sides.

**What this lets the harness answer that it couldn't before.**
- Does a spec variant regress on AI-side capture independently of operator-side capture? (Asymmetric regression detection.)
- Does heavy/xheavy load degrade AI-side capture more than operator-side capture? (Load-bearing claim of FP3 reconstruction-fidelity yardstick.)
- Is the AI-side path load-robust at the spec's claimed bar?

**Refs:** [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (stress harness foundation — symmetric coverage is an extension, not a replacement); [`718bdc29`](context_log.md#718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2--observation--2026-05-20) (xheavy empirical baseline — tier-3 will sit alongside tier-1/2 in the same scoring framework); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — symmetric capture is what the yardstick demands; one-sided measurement under-approximates).

## e643e92f7e2d4b77a671f78d092dde5e — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Spec-parameterize the stress-test harness via `runHarness.sh <spec-path>` so it works as a **pre-release regression instrument** against any candidate spec file — not hardcoded to spec-A vs spec-G. Operator-driven (manual invocation only, never automatic). Historical baseline tracking added via dated/spec-tagged/sha-tagged result directories + a curated `baselines.md` ledger pointing at canonical-baseline runs per shipped release.

**Why this exists.** The harness ships embedded with spec-A and spec-G paths hardcoded in [harness.md](stress-test-harness/harness.md) Step 2 prompt templates. Useful for the v0.7.1 A-vs-G evaluation; useless going forward as a regression instrument across releases. Operator wants to run the harness locally before each `/stoa upgrade`-driven release to verify the new spec doesn't regress against the previous baseline, possibly multiple times as the release is tuned.

**`runHarness.sh` mode shapes.**
- `runHarness.sh setup <spec-path>` — extracts spec version from H1 + current repo SHA; creates `results/<date>-<spec-version>-<short-sha>/` with per-condition run-N subdirs seeded with empty WAL stubs; copies the spec file + benchmark bundle into the run root for self-containment.
- `runHarness.sh score <run-root>` — invokes `score.sh` across every `*/run-N/` subdir; aggregates condition-level means; writes `summary.md` with tier-1/2/3 capture rates, FP counts, load-gap analysis.
- `runHarness.sh compare <run-root-A> <run-root-B>` — delta table on tier-1/2/3 means, FP, load-robustness gap.

**Drive step stays Claude-orchestrated.** Subagent launch can't be cleanly wrapped in bash (parallel agents, `Agent` tool, output capture). The runbook in [harness.md](stress-test-harness/harness.md) remains — only parameterized on `<SPEC_PATH>` instead of hardcoded. Workflow: operator runs `runHarness.sh setup <spec>` → in-session Claude reads the runbook and launches subagents pointed at the seeded directories → operator runs `runHarness.sh score` and `compare` after subagents return.

**Result directory shape.** `results/<date>-<spec-version>-<short-sha>/` — date for chronological browsing, spec-version (extracted from H1 like `v0.7.1 BETA` → `v0.7.1-BETA`) for spec identity, short-sha for exact reproducibility. Per-condition subdirs unchanged.

**`baselines.md` ledger.** Human-curated at the harness root. One line per shipped release: `- vX.Y.Z (<release-date>): results/<dir>/` — pointer only, no copies. `runHarness.sh compare` reads it to resolve baseline names. Curation is operator-driven: after a release goes out, operator appends the canonical run to the ledger.

**Refs:** [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (stress harness — `runHarness.sh` is the release-workflow wrapper around the existing harness mechanics); [`082b5a46`](context_log.md#082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22--decision--2026-05-21) (symmetric measurement — `score.sh` invoked by `runHarness.sh` covers tier-1/2/3 uniformly).

## ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Commit policy for stress-test results: **track summary.md + scoring output + spec snapshot + benchmark bundle copy per run-root; gitignore per-run raw outputs** (`run-N/context_log.md`, `run-N/transcript.md`, `run-N/plan-doc.md`).

**Why this exists.** Each release-regression cycle produces ~12-24 subagent runs across the pressure ladder. Each run-N subdir holds ~50-150KB of raw outputs. Across multiple tuning runs per release × multiple releases, raw outputs balloon to many MB of committed history — most of which is forensic-only data nobody reads after the summary lands.

**What stays tracked.**
- `<run-root>/summary.md` — condition-level means, deltas, headline findings.
- `<run-root>/scores.txt` — mechanical TP/FN/FP per run as score.sh outputs.
- `<run-root>/spec.md` — copy of the spec file the harness ran against (self-containment for `compare` mode and historical audit).
- `<run-root>/benchmark/` — copy of the conversation + ground-truth + cues bundle (self-containment; the canonical benchmark may evolve, but this run's bundle is fixed).
- `baselines.md` — ledger pointing at canonical-baseline run-roots per release.

**What's gitignored.**
- `<run-root>/*/run-N/context_log.md` — per-run AI-written WAL.
- `<run-root>/*/run-N/transcript.md` — per-run AI turn responses.
- `<run-root>/*/run-N/plan-doc.md` — per-run plan-doc output.

**Forensic-loss tradeoff acknowledged.** Without raw outputs, a future regression appearing in a baseline comparison can't be diagnosed by reading the original AI behavior — the operator must re-run the harness against the regressing spec to gather fresh forensics. Since the spec + benchmark bundle are tracked alongside the summary, re-runs are reproducible (modulo subagent stochasticity). Trade is durable-history vs. repo-size; we pick repo-size.

**Refs:** [`e643e92f`](context_log.md#e643e92f7e2d4b77a671f78d092dde5e--decision--2026-05-21) (release-regression workflow — commit policy is a sub-decision of this workflow's repo footprint), [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation — existing committed runs at `results/2026-05-20-AvsG{,-xheavy}/` predate this policy; not retroactively cleaned, but new runs follow the policy).

## 6188745ef6b14566b65617f74be2eb5b — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Refactor the stress-test harness's scenario layer to **YAML-parameterized scenario bundles** so adding a new benchmark scenario doesn't require touching `score.sh`. Each bundle colocates the conversation, ground truth, and cue list with metadata describing tier semantics + scoring rules.

**Why this exists.** Today's harness has two scenarios (versioning + xheavy) wired via parallel files: `benchmark/conversation{,-xheavy}.md`, `benchmark/ground-truth{,-xheavy}.md`, `grading/cues-{versioning,xheavy}.txt`. The cue file format is pipe-separated. Adding scenario 3 means: write conversation + ground-truth + cues file, then edit `score.sh` to accept the new cue file path (or extend its hardcoded routing). The mechanical scorer is generic-enough today (it takes a cues file argument), but the surrounding harness machinery still treats scenarios as built-in. Per `de5fc97d` quality-bias rule, refactor now rather than after a third scenario lands.

**Bundle structure.**
```
benchmark/
├── versioning/
│   ├── scenario.yaml         — metadata: name, description, tier definitions, expected counts
│   ├── conversation.md       — operator turns (scripted)
│   ├── ground-truth.md       — human-readable annotations per turn
│   └── cues.txt              — score.sh input (pipe-separated cue list)
├── xheavy/
│   ├── scenario.yaml
│   ├── conversation.md
│   ├── ground-truth.md
│   ├── cues.txt
│   └── snapshot/             — optional: pre-loaded prior state (acme-platform snapshot for xheavy)
```

**`scenario.yaml` shape (illustrative — exact schema settled during implementation).**
```yaml
name: versioning
description: REST API versioning planning (6 operator turns)
load_levels: [light, heavy, xheavy]
tiers:
  1: { name: explicit, expected: 8 }
  2: { name: conversational, expected: 2 }
  3: { name: agent-side, expected: 2 }
distractors: 2
```

**Score.sh extension.** Reads `scenario.yaml` for tier metadata + expected counts (today hardcoded as Tier 1 / Tier 2 with counts derived inline). Cue file remains pipe-separated for parsing simplicity. The YAML carries config + metadata only — not cue substance.

**Migration scope.** Convert versioning + xheavy bundles to the new layout. Delete the old parallel-files structure. The existing 2026-05-20 result dirs reference the old benchmark via committed snapshot copies, so they don't break.

**Why not heavier (e.g., parse cues from YAML directly).** YAML parsing in pure bash is painful; current pipe-separated format keeps `score.sh` dependency-free. Mixed layer is OK: YAML for config, plain text for cue content.

**Refs:** [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation — bundle refactor preserves all measurement semantics), [`e643e92f`](context_log.md#e643e92f7e2d4b77a671f78d092dde5e--decision--2026-05-21) (`runHarness.sh` operates on the bundle by name — `runHarness.sh setup <spec> --scenario versioning` resolves to `benchmark/versioning/`), [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) (quality-bias rule — refactor now while scope is small, not after a third scenario forces it).

## afe0a798102c4030b82fe2071f59f483 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Refine the AI-side capture measurement from a single tier-3 (`agent-side`) class to a **four-tier model**: tier-3 `agent-trapped` (AI catches an operator-surfaced contradiction against a prior decision) + tier-4 `agent-led` (AI catches its own dead-end mid-execution and pivots without operator input). Both scenarios (versioning + xheavy) cover both AI-side tiers — full pressure-ladder coverage across both shapes (option 3 in the design discussion).

**Why this exists.** The original framing in [`082b5a46`](context_log.md#082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22--decision--2026-05-21) collapsed all AI-side capture into one `agent-side` tier with one elicitation mechanic (operator surfaces conflicting info; AI catches the contradiction). Operator clarified mid-design that they also want to test the **autonomous case**: AI doing multi-step execution work, hitting its own dead-ends, pivoting, logging the arc with no operator in the loop. This is the load-bearing claim that Stoa captures the AI as a real collaborator rather than just a stenographer for operator settlements. Both shapes produce the same WAL signature (`rollback` + new `decision`) but are elicited by completely different test mechanics — script an operator-contradiction paragraph for tier-3; script an execute task with snapshot-friction for tier-4.

**The four tiers:**
- **Tier 1 — `explicit`.** Operator's declarative cues (*"go ahead"* / *"do this"*). Unchanged.
- **Tier 2 — `conversational`.** Operator's softer cues (*"sounds good"* / *"makes sense to me"*). Unchanged.
- **Tier 3 — `agent-trapped`.** Operator surfaces new info that contradicts an earlier-settled decision; AI must catch the contradiction. Renamed from `082b5a46`'s "agent-side" to disambiguate from tier-4. Scoring: keyword match + ≥1 rollback present (paired).
- **Tier 4 — `agent-led`.** AI does autonomous execution work against a snapshot; AI self-discovers a dead-end through inspection of the substrate; AI pivots and logs the arc. Scoring: same paired mechanic, scored against planted-friction substance keywords (see companion entry).

**Why both scenarios get tier-4 (option 3 over option 2).** Without versioning tier-4, a spec regression that quietly stops eliciting AI-led capture at light/heavy load is invisible until xheavy. The regression-detection workflow ([`e643e92f`](context_log.md#e643e92f7e2d4b77a671f78d092dde5e--decision--2026-05-21)) is the primary use case for this harness; full pressure-tier × scope-tier matrix coverage is what makes `compare` deltas meaningfully readable. Versioning has no existing snapshot, so this decision requires building a small versioning-bundle snapshot (mocked routing + cache + OpenAPI config files) to give tier-4 something to ground against — companion entry covers the elicitation mechanic.

**Scope addition vs `082b5a46`.** Original scope: ~2 tier-3 cues per conversation × 2 scenarios = 4 tier-3 cues + scoring update. New scope: same 4 tier-3 cues + tier-4 execute segments (2 planted-friction anchors per scenario × 2 scenarios = 4 tier-4 anchors) + versioning snapshot creation. Roughly +half-day design work for versioning snapshot + tier-4 friction-point design.

**Refs:** [`082b5a46`](context_log.md#082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22--decision--2026-05-21) (original tier-3 agent-side decision — this entry refines by splitting agent-side into trapped + led; tier-3 narrows to the trapped subset); [`6188745e`](context_log.md#6188745ef6b14566b65617f74be2eb5b--decision--2026-05-21) (YAML scenario bundle — `tiers` block already supports arbitrary tier counts via the `paired` flag, no schema change needed); [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation — four-tier model is a measurement-axis extension); [`de5fc97d`](context_log.md#de5fc97d73934beaba84d0bfa70a3bb9--decision--2026-05-20) (quality-bias rule — option 3 is the quality-maximizing choice).

## a1234e2a34e14b389747b4f396a39538 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Tier-4 (`agent-led`) elicitation via **execute segments with planted-friction snapshots**; scoring via **mechanical anticipated-pivots (primary) + AI-judge for quality (secondary)**.

**Why this exists.** Tier-4 testing requires the AI to actually DO autonomous work — planning conversations alone don't elicit AI-internal arcs because there's no execution friction. The mechanic: append an execute segment as a final turn to each conversation, handing the AI a concrete task to perform against the bundle's snapshot. Plant 1-2 friction points in the snapshot — substrate facts that make the AI's first-approach implementation impossible or wrong, forcing a self-discovered pivot. Friction points are domains the AI will naturally inspect to do the task (config files, schemas, dependency manifests), not buried files it has no reason to read.

**For xheavy:** the existing acme-platform snapshot is well-suited. Add execute segment as Turn 8: *"Now write the initial `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` based on what we decided."* Plant 2 friction points (e.g., Python version mismatch between `pyproject.toml` and `iac/isv/lambda.tf` runtime; or a secrets-path inconsistency between the settled decision and the existing IAM policy in `iac/isv/iam.tf`). AI's first-approach implementation hits the friction; pivot expected.

**For versioning:** build a new snapshot at `benchmark/versioning/snapshot/` — small realistic-looking microservice config bundle: mocked `nginx.conf`, `cloudfront-cache.json`, `openapi.yaml`, maybe a tiny `routes/` directory. Plant 2 friction points in domains the AI must read to write the chosen-versioning-strategy routing config. Add execute segment as final turn: *"Now write the initial routing config (nginx + Lambda@Edge if applicable) for the chosen versioning strategy."*

**Scoring mechanic — combined.**
- **Mechanical (anticipated-pivots, primary).** For each planted friction, pre-identify substance keywords for the expected pivot (analogous to tier-1/2/3 cues). TP iff WAL contains a `rollback` entry AND a new `decision` entry with matching substance keywords during the execute segment. Same shape as tier-3 trapped scoring; reuses `paired: true` flag in scenario.yaml. Same `score.sh` code path — no new infrastructure.
- **AI-judge (quality, secondary).** Judge subagent reads transcript + WAL + planted-friction list, scores whether AI's pivots match actual discoveries (catches the failure mode of AI gaming keyword match without doing real work). Weight lower than mechanical for regression detection; primary use is calibrating mechanical scorer interpretation.

**Risk acknowledged.** AI may pivot for a valid reason we didn't anticipate (different friction in the snapshot than the planted ones). Mechanical scoring counts this as FN; AI-judge catches it as legitimate. The tradeoff favors mechanical for regression stability; AI-judge is the second-opinion safety net.

**Why not auto-refinement-language detection.** Considered: scan WAL for phrases like *"on reflection..."* / *"correction:"* and count any presence as tier-4 capture. Rejected as gameable (AI can pad WAL with refinement-shaped prose for fake tier-4 hits without doing real work) and not validating that real friction was encountered.

**Fallback if elicitation disappoints.** If first runs show a snapshot doesn't elicit natural pivots (AI doesn't inspect the planted-friction files), fall back to xheavy-only tier-4 (option 2) by removing the affected execute segment. Snapshot stays in repo; just unused by scoring until re-engaged.

**Refs:** [`afe0a798`](context_log.md#afe0a798102c4030b82fe2071f59f483--decision--2026-05-21) (four-tier model — this entry settles HOW tier-4 is elicited and scored); [`082b5a46`](context_log.md#082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22--decision--2026-05-21) (paired-flag scoring shape from tier-3 is reused unchanged for tier-4); [`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21) (commit policy — versioning snapshot files are tracked as bundle infrastructure, not gitignored as raw-run outputs).

## e9b68c54fce848cc83cc755db387b653 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Split machine-aggregated and operator-narrative summary files in stress-test run roots: **`scores-summary.md` is machine output from `runHarness.sh score`; `summary.md` is reserved for operator-authored narrative analysis.** `runHarness.sh score` writes only `scores-summary.md` and never overwrites `summary.md`.

**Why this exists.** Discovered during Phase 6 implementation that the original commit-policy entry ([`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21)) treated `summary.md` as machine output — but the pre-refactor `results/2026-05-20-AvsG-xheavy/summary.md` is operator-authored narrative (headline finding, cue-specific notes, decision rationale for shipping v0.7.1). A naive `runHarness.sh score` against that dir clobbered the curated content.

**The split.**
- `scores-summary.md` — Markdown table of per-condition tier means + FP + total entries. Auto-generated. Machine-readable for `compare` mode parsing. Never operator-edited (rewritten on every `score` invocation).
- `summary.md` — Operator-authored narrative if/when desired. Headline findings, cue-specific analysis, decision rationale. Never machine-written (`runHarness.sh score` skips it).

`runHarness.sh compare` reads `scores-summary.md` (machine table is the source of truth for delta computation). Narrative `summary.md` is human-only.

**Why this matters beyond the bug.** Future spec-tuning runs will produce 12+ run roots per release as the operator iterates. Most will not warrant narrative analysis — operator just wants the aggregate table to compare. The handful that DO warrant analysis (canonical baselines, shipped releases) get a hand-authored `summary.md`. The split keeps the cheap path cheap and the curated path preserved.

**Refs:** [`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21) (original commit policy — this refines the summary.md role from "machine output" to "operator narrative" with `scores-summary.md` taking over machine output); [`e643e92f`](context_log.md#e643e92f7e2d4b77a671f78d092dde5e--decision--2026-05-21) (runHarness.sh scoring shape).

## c367c4178f4245eeaa1852c9063596a3 — won't-do — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Will NOT** introduce structured frontmatter (e.g., YAML metadata blocks) into WAL entries to enable deterministic detection of tier-3/4 captures. Stoa's WAL entry form stays loose-prose per the canonical body-content guidance.

**Why this exists.** First runs of the stress-test harness against v0.7.1 (3 light + 3 heavy versioning) surfaced that keyword-based tier-3/4 detection on WAL prose is brittle across model versions, providers (e.g., Opus vs GPT), and even temperature variance within the same model. Several real captures (V2 acceptance with rollback) were missed because the AI's actual phrasing didn't hit the tightened keyword list (`n-2` was used but my keywords required `supersedes n-1` or `rolling back n-1`). Considered switching the WAL entry format to include a structured metadata block (YAML or JSON frontmatter with explicit `supersedes: <hex>`, `new_direction: <slug>`, etc.) that a deterministic parser could consume.

**Why not.**
- **Operator concern (load-bearing): parse fragility cascades.** If a single entry produces malformed structured metadata (LLM gets the YAML indent wrong, omits a required key, mixes types), the parser corrupts on that entry — and if recovery isn't robust, parsing of subsequent entries breaks too. The current loose-prose form has graceful degradation: a malformed entry is still readable; the next entry parses independently. Structured form trades robustness for determinism.
- **The information needed for detection is already present in the loose prose** — what's missing is a reliable way to extract it. The right move is a better extraction layer (behavioral output detection per companion decision), not a stricter authoring contract.
- **Spec-level scope creep.** Changing WAL entry shape is a methodology decision affecting every Stoa adopter, not a harness decision. Forcing structured frontmatter to fix a harness measurement problem is the wrong layer.

**What stays.** WAL entries keep the canonical header (`## <hex> — <type> — <date>`) + `**Authors:**` + `**Participants:**` + free-prose body per [`stoa.md` §"WAL entry form"](installkit/stoa.md). Detection mechanism is solved at the harness layer (companion decision [`f27fb340`](context_log.md#f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673--decision--2026-05-21)), not at the WAL spec layer.

**Refs:** [`f27fb340`](context_log.md#f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673--decision--2026-05-21) (behavioral output detection — the chosen alternative); [`a1234e2a`](context_log.md#a1234e2a34e14b389747b4f396a39538--decision--2026-05-21) (tier-4 scoring mechanic — this entry refines its implementation substrate without changing the mechanic itself); [`ec0767f6`](context_log.md#ec0767f6343749f6a79146890ce3eff1--observation--2026-05-21) (closeout observation that flagged the keyword-tightening fragility).

## f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Switch tier-3 and tier-4 scoring substrate from WAL-prose keyword matching (brittle across models / providers / temperatures) to **behavioral output detection over the AI's execute-task artifacts**, with WAL keyword matching kept as belt-and-suspenders supplementary signal. Each tier-3/4 cue gets one or more behavioral predicates over the execute-output files; predicate match credits the capture independently of WAL prose phrasing. TP for tier-3/4 = rollback present AND (behavioral predicate fires OR keyword match). AI-judge fallback reserved for future cases where neither signal discriminates.

**Why this exists.** First-run inspection of v0.7.1 against the new harness surfaced that tightened keyword lists missed real captures (Run-1 heavy: AI rolled back N-1 in favor of "N-2 + stuck-customer grandfathering" — the words `n-2` and `grandfathering` weren't in my tightened a2 keyword list). Loosening the keywords would re-introduce noise (the noise floor on historical data was the original reason for tightening). Per [`c367c4178`](context_log.md#c367c4178f4245eeaa1852c9063596a3--wont-do--2026-05-21) we won't introduce structured WAL frontmatter to dodge the prose-parsing problem.

**Behavioral output detection** sidesteps prose-parsing entirely. The AI's execute-task output (nginx.conf, ci.yaml, cloudfront-cache.json, plan-doc, etc.) reflects what the AI actually DID. Header-based nginx routing looks the same whether Opus or GPT wrote it. Detection becomes structural inspection of output artifacts, not semantic interpretation of WAL prose.

**Per-cue behavioral predicates.** Each tier-3/4 cue gets one or more predicate lines in a sibling `behaviors.txt` file (sibling, not embedded in cues.txt, to preserve the simple cue-line format). Predicate format:
```
<cue-id>|<file-pattern-relative-to-run-dir>|<predicate-type>|<pattern>
```
- `contains` predicate: regex any-of-match against file content (split on inner `|`)
- `jq` predicate: jq expression returning truthy against JSON file
- Multiple lines per cue = OR semantics (any one match credits the cue)

**Scoring logic for tier-3/4.** TP iff:
1. WAL contains ≥1 rollback entry (the auto-refinement signature, unchanged)
2. AND (behavioral predicate matches the cue OR keyword matches in WAL — either suffices)

Belt-and-suspenders: keyword stays in cues.txt for the existing pass; behavioral runs as new check. The substrate doesn't subtract; it adds an orthogonal axis.

**AI judge as future fallback.** If behavioral + keyword still produces ambiguous results in some scenarios, add LLM-as-judge as third axis (per [`a1234e2a`](context_log.md#a1234e2a34e14b389747b4f396a39538--decision--2026-05-21)'s original mention). Cost: ~$0.20/cue × 4 cues × 9 runs = ~$7/run-root. Non-deterministic — kept out of primary path for regression stability. Add only when needed.

**Provider-robustness payoff.** The harness now measures spec compliance via what the AI accomplishes (output artifacts), not how it phrases its WAL writes. nginx config with header-based dispatch is identifiable regardless of model. Cross-provider regression testing becomes feasible without per-provider keyword tuning.

**Refs:** [`c367c4178`](context_log.md#c367c4178f4245eeaa1852c9063596a3--wont-do--2026-05-21) (rejected structured-WAL alternative); [`a1234e2a`](context_log.md#a1234e2a34e14b389747b4f396a39538--decision--2026-05-21) (tier-4 scoring mechanic — this entry refines its detection substrate from prose to artifact); [`082b5a46`](context_log.md#082b5a46f8264e5591d94fd583c81d22--decision--2026-05-21) (tier-3 paired-flag introduction — same paired flag applies, just the substantive check changes); [`6188745e`](context_log.md#6188745ef6b14566b65617f74be2eb5b--decision--2026-05-21) (YAML scenario bundle — `behaviors.txt` joins the bundle alongside `cues.txt`).

## 521504715235486dae6f2643614e1646 — rollback — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Supersedes [`f27fb340`](context_log.md#f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673--decision--2026-05-21) (behavioral output detection as primary tier-3/4 scoring substrate). The behavioral approach measures the wrong axis — it scores what the AI's execute artifact looks like, but the harness's stated purpose ([`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20)) is to measure WAL quality (whether the spec elicits AI behavior that captures inflections in the WAL itself).

**Why this is being superseded.** First runs against v0.7.1 exposed two failure modes of the behavioral-primary scoring:

1. **Behavioral predicate fires even when WAL doesn't capture the cue.** An AI that rolls back an unrelated decision (rollback_present=true) AND writes good output (behavioral predicate fires) gets credited tier-3/4 TP — even when the WAL contains zero specific content about the cue's substance. The reconstruction-fidelity yardstick is broken: a future reader of the WAL alone can't see the cue's resolution. Output-backfill isn't reconstruction.

2. **The "Stoa-without-Stoa" failure passes as success.** An AI that captures operator-led arcs cleanly but makes its own micro-decisions silently produces high-quality output. Behavioral predicates fire on the output. Tier-3/4 scores positive. But the AI's autonomous reasoning is nowhere in the WAL — operator loses inspectability and provenance ("who decided?" has no traceable answer for AI-side choices). This is the failure mode Stoa is designed to prevent; behavioral-primary scoring rewards it instead.

Both failure modes follow from measuring the wrong substrate. The harness purpose is WAL quality, not output quality. Behavioral-on-output measures the latter.

**What the supersession replaces.** New primary scoring: LLM judge reading the WAL semantically, scoring decision-arc-reconstruction fidelity, with `silent_decisions` detection that explicitly catches the no-WAL-good-output failure. See companion decision [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21). Behavioral predicates demoted to informational sidecar metric ("did AI's output implement what its WAL captured?") — useful diagnostic, not capture-determinative.

**What stays.** The `behaviors.txt` infrastructure (per-bundle predicates) is retained; the SIGNAL changes role from primary TP determinant to informational secondary. The tier-3/4 `paired: true` flag in scenario.yaml stays — rollback presence remains a necessary structural check. The score.sh keyword pass stays as cheap pre-filter (skip judge when high-confidence keyword hit).

**Refs:** [`f27fb340`](context_log.md#f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673--decision--2026-05-21) (superseded); [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21) (replacement: AI judge + decision-arc-reconstruction methodology); [`3c7de0d1`](context_log.md#3c7de0d1d41b4b3f99d528334f0d7b22--decision--2026-05-21) (mechanical AI-led floor — the deterministic backstop to the judge); [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation — the original WAL-quality measurement goal that f27fb340 drifted from).

## 8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

Tier-3 and tier-4 primary scoring: **LLM judge reading the WAL semantically, scoring decision-arc-reconstruction fidelity per run.** Judge returns (a) overall 0.0-1.0 fidelity_score, (b) per-cue verdicts (captured / partial / missed) anchored in the ground-truth cue list, (c) a `silent_decisions` list enumerating load-bearing choices visible in the output that lack WAL reasoning, (d) brief justification. Operates per run, not per cue (single API call per run, structured JSON output).

**Why this exists.** Replaces [`f27fb340`](context_log.md#f27fb3401f0e4a80a73d21e759a3c673--decision--2026-05-21) (behavioral-as-primary) per [`52150471`](context_log.md#521504715235486dae6f2643614e1646--rollback--2026-05-21). The harness measures WAL quality (does the spec elicit AI behavior that captures inflections in the WAL?). Direct measurement requires reading WAL semantics — provider-robust, since the judge interprets meaning rather than matching surface phrasing. Keyword brittleness (model-specific phrasing variance) and behavioral conflation (output quality ≠ WAL quality) both dissolve.

**The decision-arc framing (not output reproduction).** The judge prompt asks: *"if a fresh engineer read ONLY the WAL — no transcript, no output — could they understand the full decision arc? Every load-bearing choice present? Reasoning for each? Source attribution clear (operator-settled vs AI-decided)? Rejected alternatives + tradeoffs visible?"* Critical anti-pattern explicitly flagged in the prompt: *"if the OUTPUT shows a load-bearing decision but the WAL doesn't explain WHY or HOW it was chosen, that's a major gap — 'it's visible in the output' is NOT reconstruction."* This framing catches the Stoa-without-Stoa failure mode.

**The `silent_decisions` mechanism.** Judge enumerates load-bearing choices that appear in the execute artifact but lack corresponding WAL entries. Each item: `{choice, evidence (where in output), missing_from_wal}`. A non-empty list is direct evidence of silent AI decisions the operator cannot inspect or deliberate. Forces the judge to penalize fidelity_score consistently with the list (high fidelity + long silent_decisions list = contradictory; judge prompt asks for explicit consistency).

**Per-cue verdicts grouped by tier.** Judge marks each ground-truth cue (c1-c10/c11-c23 operator-side, a1-a2 trapped, b1-b2 led) as captured / partial / missed with notes. Per-tier aggregation gives the regression-localization signal we previously had from keyword/behavioral scoring — without the brittleness.

**Determinism + cost.**
- Temperature=0 + structured JSON output for stability
- Run judge **3× per run** with median fidelity_score (mitigates judge variance; cheap at scale)
- Cost: ~$0.20 per judge invocation × 3 invocations × 9 runs = ~$5.40 per run-root
- One judge call per run (not per cue) — substantially cheaper than per-cue judging

**What still gets mechanical scoring (cheap pre-filter + structural checks).**
- Total WAL entry count
- Rollback entry count (used by the AI-led floor check per [`3c7de0d1`](context_log.md#3c7de0d1d41b4b3f99d528334f0d7b22--decision--2026-05-21))
- Keyword pre-filter for high-confidence cue hits (skips judge call when keyword unambiguously matches; speeds bulk runs)
- Behavioral predicate match (now reported as `output_coherence` sidecar metric, not TP-determinative)
- FP detection (entries with no relevant content)

**Output shape (per run, in scores-summary.md).**
- `fidelity_score`: median of 3 judge runs, 0.0-1.0
- `per_tier_capture`: TP rate per tier from per-cue verdicts
- `silent_decisions_count`: how many output-visible decisions lack WAL reasoning
- `output_coherence`: behavioral predicate match rate (informational)
- `ai_led_floor`: pass/fail from mechanical check

**What spec authors get from this.** When fidelity_score drops between releases, `silent_decisions` + per-cue verdicts localize which arcs the new spec is failing to elicit. Behavioral coherence shows whether the AI is executing its WAL or freelancing. Floor pass/fail catches the "AI bypassed Stoa entirely" failure mode deterministically.

**Refs:** [`52150471`](context_log.md#521504715235486dae6f2643614e1646--rollback--2026-05-21) (rolls back behavioral-primary); [`3c7de0d1`](context_log.md#3c7de0d1d41b4b3f99d528334f0d7b22--decision--2026-05-21) (mechanical AI-led floor — deterministic backstop to the judge); [`a1234e2a`](context_log.md#a1234e2a34e14b389747b4f396a39538--decision--2026-05-21) (tier-4 mechanic — this entry refines the detection substrate to WAL-semantic judging); [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation: WAL-quality measurement); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — the judge operationalizes this directly at scoring time).

## 3c7de0d1d41b4b3f99d528334f0d7b22 — decision — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

**Mechanical AI-led floor check** in score.sh: a run fails the floor if its WAL contains zero AI-led entry signatures. Deterministic backstop to the judge — no judge score can rescue a WAL that has no evidence of AI-side arc capture. Floor pass requires at least one of: (a) a `rollback` entry, (b) an `observation` entry, (c) any entry whose body contains an auto-refinement phrase (e.g., *"on reflection"*, *"I notice"*, *"correction:"*, *"switching to"*, *"this contradicts what I"*). Reported as `ai_led_floor: pass | fail` per run in scores-summary.md.

**Why this exists.** Per the operator's framing: the failure mode where Stoa adds ceremony without value is "AI bypassed Stoa, made silent decisions, output is good, WAL has only operator-cued entries." Per FP4 (substance/coherence): the WAL is supposed to record BOTH sides of the Human+AI pair. A WAL with zero AI-led signatures is methodological evidence that the spec didn't elicit AI-side capture at all — collaboration ceremony was performed but the AI's reasoning wasn't recorded. Operator loses inspectability + provenance for the AI's choices.

The judge could theoretically catch this (silent_decisions list would be long, fidelity_score would drop). But:
- Judge has variance (~5-10 point swings on tight cases)
- Judge cost matters at scale
- Deterministic floor is the right backstop for a "did Stoa work at all" check — failure is unambiguous

**The three signatures the floor accepts.**
- `rollback` entry → AI promoted a course-correction (per FP3 immutability, only the AI can write these; their presence is direct evidence of AI engagement with WAL refinement)
- `observation` entry → typically AI-side (operator rarely cues observations explicitly; AI emits them for empirical findings, self-detected misreads, etc.)
- Auto-refinement phrase → spec-canonical language for AI mid-flow course-correction. Tight-keyword list because we want SIGNATURE detection, not substance overlap with cues.

**What this is NOT measuring.**
- It's not a quality measure (one observation entry passes; ten don't earn more)
- It's not a capture-rate metric (per-cue capture is the judge's job)
- It's the floor below which judge scores become meaningless: no AI-led signal at all = Stoa-bypassed regardless of any other metric

**Implementation.** Pure-bash in score.sh; no API calls; runs on every score invocation.

```
ai_led_count = count(WAL entries of type 'rollback' or 'observation')
                + count(WAL entries containing any of: "on reflection", "I notice",
                        "correction:", "switching to", "this contradicts what I",
                        "actually, on reflection", "I'm changing approach")
ai_led_floor = pass if ai_led_count >= 1 else fail
```

**What happens on floor fail.** Run is flagged `ai_led_floor: FAIL` in scores-summary.md. Aggregation reports per-condition floor-pass rate. A spec where >30% of runs floor-fail is a structural failure of the spec to elicit AI-side WAL writing — judge scores are reported but should be interpreted skeptically.

**Refs:** [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21) (AI judge — the floor is its deterministic backstop); [`52150471`](context_log.md#521504715235486dae6f2643614e1646--rollback--2026-05-21) (rolls back behavioral-primary — context for why deterministic floors matter alongside semantic judging); [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation); founding principle FP4 (substance human, coherence AI — the WAL must capture both sides).
