## ea30b5907e8d49d6b19bdc45cc15226e — observation — 2026-05-21

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)]

First end-to-end judge run against v0.7.1 BETA establishes empirical baseline + validates the decision-arc-reconstruction methodology. **Median judge fidelity_score per condition: versioning-light 0.72, versioning-heavy 0.72, xheavy 0.82.** All 9 runs pass the mechanical AI-led floor. Full report at [`stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-21-v0.7.1-BETA-a5135d9/summary.md`](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-21-v0.7.1-BETA-a5135d9/summary.md).

**Methodology validation.** The judge surfaced specific WAL completeness gaps that the prior mechanical scoring credited as success — particularly the "silent pushback rationale" failure mode in versioning a1 (AI correctly rejected operator's CDN-cost trap by inspecting cloudfront-cache.json snapshot evidence, but the rejection reasoning lives only in plan-doc/config-comment text, not the WAL). The `silent_decisions` mechanism worked exactly as designed: enumerated specific output-visible choices that lack WAL reasoning, with concrete evidence pointers. The judge's per-cue verdicts also preserved diagnostic locality (which arc broke, not just an aggregate score). Per-run variance is meaningful (0.55-0.82 within one condition) — supports the case for 3× median in sensitive regression runs.

**Spec strengths confirmed empirically.**
- **Operator-side capture is robust** across all 3 load conditions. Tier-1 at 98-100%, tier-2 at 83-100%. Spec reliably elicits WAL entries for explicit + conversational operator cues with rationale + tradeoffs preserved.
- **Hard-trap tier-3 capture is strong in xheavy.** Both xheavy traps (X1 GH-Envs vs infosec, X2 sub-5min vs 8min wall time) have valid premises AI can't refute. Spec elicits proper rollback+decision pairs every run.
- **AI-led arc capture works for blocking friction.** xheavy b1 (Python runtime mismatch — lambda.tf says 3.10, Dockerfiles say 3.12) fires consistently as AI is writing the CI matrix and must pick a version. Captured as auto-refinement observation/decision in all 3 xheavy runs.

**Spec weaknesses surfaced empirically (candidate inputs for next-iteration spec design).**

1. **Soft-trap pushback reasoning gap** — versioning a1 across all 6 versioning runs. When AI correctly rejects an operator-surfaced contradiction (premise is wrong against substrate), the spec elicits the substantive correct behavior (push back, hold the prior decision) but does NOT elicit a WAL entry recording WHY the rejection. Future readers see the decision unchanged with no record of the challenge or rebuttal. Candidate spec addition: AI obligation to WAL the *reasoning* for declining an operator-surfaced contradiction, not just the action. Currently spec addresses "accept and rollback" path; doesn't address "reject with substrate evidence" path. Mean silent_decisions: versioning-light 3.3, versioning-heavy 0.7 (heavy lower because traps had stronger premises that got accepted).

2. **Non-blocking tier-4 friction is missed** — xheavy b2 (Trivy scan redundancy: 4 services share `python:3.12-slim` base, AI writes per-service scans without noting dedup opportunity) missed in 3/3 xheavy runs. b1 fires because AI MUST pick a Python version to write the matrix; b2 doesn't fire because writing per-service scans works fine functionally even if redundant. Suggests the spec's autonomous-discovery behavior is keyed to "AI hits a wall" rather than "AI notices suboptimality." Either: refine planted friction in the harness scenario to be more wall-shaped, OR investigate whether spec should be tuned to surface "noticed but proceeded" decisions.

3. **Observation-vs-decision type drift on tier-4** — xheavy b1 captured as `observation` in some runs (run-2, run-3) while the ci.yaml made a concrete decision (pin Python 3.10). The WAL defers a decision the artifact already made. Per slim spec: observations are "empirical findings, not forward-looking commitments" — but here the AI committed in code without WAL-promoting to decision. Subtle but consequential: a reader of the WAL alone doesn't know what was settled.

**Promotion candidate.** This run-root is recommended for `baselines.md` as the v0.7.1 BETA canonical baseline. Spec changes after this point compare against these fidelity_scores per condition + the specific cue-by-cue patterns. Operator confirms promotion before append.

**Empirical artifacts in this run-root.**
- 9 run-N subdirs with per-run WAL + transcript + execute output (gitignored per [`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21))
- `scores.txt` + `scores-summary.md` (mechanical aggregate)
- `summary.md` (operator-narrative analysis with judge comparison)
- Judge verdicts in this conversation's transcript (not yet persisted to per-run judge-verdict.json — refactor pending per [`0a0b0d15`](context_log.md#0a0b0d158fab4aa4bb0813fa218d3248--observation--2026-05-21))

**Refs:** [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21) (judge methodology — this entry validates empirically); [`3c7de0d1`](context_log.md#3c7de0d1d41b4b3f99d528334f0d7b22--decision--2026-05-21) (floor check — all 9 passed); [`0a0b0d15`](context_log.md#0a0b0d158fab4aa4bb0813fa218d3248--observation--2026-05-21) (subagent mechanism — used here for first time); [`d23fd224`](context_log.md#d23fd2247d624d17b786e75958c79c84--decision--2026-05-20) (harness foundation — this run validates the v2 harness end-to-end); [`b237c4ea`](context_log.md#b237c4ea1f014ff387b90fa324ec53fb--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity yardstick — the judge operationalizes this and produces measurable per-condition scores).

## 5e8e675930f74c5e90fa5e39998380ca — observation — 2026-05-23

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Extended deliberation arc (~15 turns) across two related questions: (1) should Stoa introduce a "temporary session DAF" tier for staging in-flight deliberation arcs, and (2) does autonomous WAL management create a privacy/embarrassment exposure risk requiring operator-controlled review?

**Outcome: no new structure warranted.** Both proposed mechanisms dissolve under the editorial test from the proposed declarative-vs-imperative meta-principle (see [`sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md`](sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md)). The substance of the dissolution:

**On temp DAFs for privacy:** the original framing (operator-managed staging tier; T2-local; explicit publish step) was over-engineering — it re-introduced operator-review load at the merge boundary, which is exactly the autonomous-management friction Stoa is designed to eliminate. Re-introducing operator-controlled exposure via tiering would collapse Stoa's ambiance property.

**On embarrassment / content-appropriateness:** empirically observed N=many sessions across multiple frontier models (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Gemma) without a single instance of AI capturing embarrassing content into produced artifacts. Frontier-model training/RLHF + Stoa's existing entry format (question/alternatives/path/rationale shapes naturally professional prose) handle the concern empirically. The body-content guidance addition I initially proposed (`"WAL entries become part of the project's shared, durable record — write them as such"`) fails the editorial test's second criterion — the declarative form has not been observed to fail; the imperative addition is premature.

**On calibration drift across model generations:** also dissolves. If a future model regression introduced embarrassment-leakage behavior, the signal would surface across all AI-mediated artifacts (code-gen, doc-gen, image-gen) and get caught by the broader AI market faster than any Stoa-specific audit hook. This is an AI-ecosystem problem, not a Stoa-specific problem.

**On trajectory preservation across `/clear`:** real felt gap (sketches preserve outcomes, not the trajectory that produced them), but the cost of dedicated infrastructure (temp-DAF tier with branch / merge / discard semantics) exceeds the value given current empirical evidence. Existing cadence #4 affordance (AI may append optional broader-shape observation pre-compact/clear) is sufficient; AI can be more generous with that affordance when trajectories are valuable.

**Net result of this deliberation:**
- No new sketch (the temp-DAF sketch is not written).
- No spec change.
- No new audit dimensions.
- Adopter-facing advisory worth considering: *adopters can trial-test their model's output discipline on representative prompts before relying on Stoa for sensitive work*. Possibly added to [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md); decision deferred to operator.

**Why this entry exists.** The deliberation was non-trivial (multiple substantive reframings; one AI off-pattern slip documented in beta-tracker [`609c3085`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md#609c3085cf24425c9e40e0f193e3e732--2026-05-23); a meta-principle surfaced via [`sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md`](sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md)). Without this entry, future-us would re-traverse the same arcs when temp DAFs or content-appropriateness machinery are re-proposed. The entry's purpose is reconstruction-fidelity: when this design space is revisited, the reasoning chain (operator-management friction; empirical AI discipline; editorial test against premature imperatives; AI-ecosystem-vs-Stoa scoping) should be recoverable. This is itself a worked example of the body-content discipline applied to a deliberation that concluded "no new content needed."

**Refs:** [`sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md`](sketches/declarative-vs-imperative.md) (the meta-principle this deliberation exercises); [`.stoa/beta_tracker.md`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) entry `609c3085` (off-pattern slip discovered within this deliberation arc).

## 4b3c686be138451e8c8af026a5f1aa1d — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Added a project-level rule to [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — *"Bias toward declarative over imperative"* — and refactored the in-flight sketch material to disambiguate two altitudes that had been conflated during the 2026-05-23/24 deliberation.

**The rule (verbatim, as it landed in CLAUDE.md):**

> When proposing AI behaviors, spec additions, or methodology rules, prefer declarative descriptions of desired outcomes over imperative if/else rules. Imperative rules accumulate and create rule-tension; promote to imperative only when empirical failure justifies it.

Slots in immediately after the existing *"Proposal style — bias toward quality"* section; same shape (biasing AI's proposals in a particular direction).

**Why now.** Throughout this session the operator repeatedly surfaced the declarative-over-imperative discipline as a meta-principle the AI kept needing reminded of (cf. multiple turns of "remember declarative > imperative"). Making it project-active via CLAUDE.md eliminates the per-session reminder load. The rule biases future spec work and AI behavior proposals declarative-by-default; imperative additions earn their keep only via the empirical-failure criterion. Empirical substrate for the criterion: existing imperative backstops that earned their place (cadence #3 Pass A hook, the WAL guardrail off-pattern list, the v0.7.1 attention-checkpoint, the §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" off-pattern enumeration from [`8ed5d11d`](context_log.md#8ed5d11de21d42ef8e3c2b5b799a9e56--decision--2026-05-20)).

**The altitude split.** The original sketch `declarative-vs-imperative.md` conflated two distinct concerns: (a) the general declarative-over-imperative principle for spec authoring (now in CLAUDE.md), and (b) the agent-rule-tuning discipline — specifically, that when fixing observed AI behavioral failures, behavior declarations generalize across variants better than procedural enumeration of forbidden phrasings. Operator caught the conflation late in the session. Resolution: the sketch is renamed to `behavior-not-procedure.md` and refocused narrowly on (b); the meta-principle (a) moves to CLAUDE.md as a project rule.

**Empirical grounding for the agent-rule-tuning altitude.** Beta-tracker entries [`5c2e3ff1`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) and [`609c3085`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) document the propose-confirm reflex and its substance-uncertainty variant relapse despite the off-pattern enumeration. The relapse demonstrated that procedural enumeration catches specific phrasings but doesn't generalize across variants the enumeration didn't anticipate. The renamed [`sketches/behavior-not-procedure.md`](sketches/behavior-not-procedure.md) captures the proposed refinement — adding a behavior declaration alongside the existing enumeration in §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" — plus the six-question editorial test for when procedural enumeration earns its keep over behavior declaration.

**Scope.** CLAUDE.md is project-active for this repo's sessions; not adopter-facing (adopters have their own CLAUDE.md). The principle is consistent with FP1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter) and serves as editorial discipline for future spec work. The rule is itself declarative — no imperative enforcement; AI applies it as judgment during proposal work.

**Refs:** [`5e8e6759`](context_log.md#5e8e675930f74c5e90fa5e39998380ca--observation--2026-05-23) (today's broader dissolution context — temp-DAF / privacy / trajectory concerns that this principle's editorial test helped dissolve); [`8ed5d11d`](context_log.md#8ed5d11de21d42ef8e3c2b5b799a9e56--decision--2026-05-20) (the off-pattern enumeration that the renamed sketch proposes refining); [`.stoa/beta_tracker.md`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) entries `5c2e3ff1` and `609c3085` (empirical substrate); [`sketches/behavior-not-procedure.md`](sketches/behavior-not-procedure.md) (the agent-rule-tuning sketch, post-rename); [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](sketches/wal-grounding.md), [`sketches/experiment-vs-feature.md`](sketches/experiment-vs-feature.md), [`sketches/daf-attachment.md`](sketches/daf-attachment.md) (sibling sketches from this deliberation that exemplify the declarative-default discipline).

## 7c784c7072e5411c8be1c213f24be739 — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Added a project-level rule to [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — *"Slim section content is strictly AI-directive"* — as a new bullet in §"Working on the install kit", positioned after the existing *"AI-facing instructions in `installkit/stoa.md` are code, not prose"* bullet.

**The rule (verbatim, as it landed in CLAUDE.md):**

> Every line in `installkit/stoa.md` above `## First-run install kit` loads into every Stoa session. Content there must shape AI behavior — directives, rules, recognition tables, format specs, surface strings. Rationale for why a rule is shaped a certain way (*"this is free"*, *"preserves X property"*, *"works without Y"*), reassurance prose (*"naturally handles Z"*, *"falls through to cadence backstops"*), and meta-explanation of rule-overlap belong in WAL entries and proposal docs, not slim. When editing slim, audit each clause: does this clause change AI behavior? If no, cut.

**Why now.** Surfaced during the slim-section audit (Phase 0 of slim-compaction work). Operator caught multiple rationale-leak instances in proposed slim edits (*"no subagent invocation; no latency cost"*, *"naturally handles model changes"*, *"works without it"*) — content explaining *why* a rule has its shape rather than *what* the rule directs. Such content wastes session context every load and risks AI treating reassurance prose as if it were a rule. The rule provides an editing discipline (clause-by-clause audit: *does this clause change AI behavior?*) that catches the anti-pattern.

**Relationship to existing rules.** Sibling of *"AI-facing instructions are code, not prose"* ([`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15)): that rule says *don't casually rewrite tuned AI-instruction blocks*; this rule says *don't write non-directive content into slim in the first place.* Together they bound slim-section editing on both sides — preserve tuned content; reject untuned/non-directive content.

**Scope.** CLAUDE.md is project-active for this repo's sessions; not adopter-facing. Applies to all edits to `installkit/stoa.md` above the `## First-run install kit` boundary.

**Refs:** [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instructions-are-code rule, sibling); [`56ebaca7`](context_log.md#56ebaca7dd66474b9e7de144c962ae38--decision--2026-05-24) (sibling CLAUDE.md meta-rule landing in this same audit phase).

## 84a167f5e26045928a2fd29e41bce5b0 — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Reframed how the thesis ([docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md)) presents the capacity-asymmetry case that motivates Stoa's "AI as maintainer" pairing. The naive framing — *"AI keeps more decision arcs in working context than humans"* — gets superseded by a two-sided reframe grounded in literature on both sides.

**Human side.** Capacity numbers stay as load-bearing anchor: Cowan (2001, 2010) puts focused-attention capacity at 3-5 chunks unscaffolded; Miller (1956) is historical baseline; Engle/Kane/Conway program on WMC-as-executive-attention is the most directly relevant body for goal-maintenance-under-interference (which is what arc-tracking demands); Sweller's CLT explains why decision arcs specifically (high element-interactivity) are hard to hold in parallel without schema or external scaffolding. Chunking literature (Chase & Simon 1973; Gobet & Simon 1996; Ericsson & Kintsch 1995) and Klein's RPD model complicate raw-capacity by showing expert templates expand effective capacity in familiar territory — but Stoa's target use case (novel architecture, multi-author coordination) is exactly where templates haven't formed.

To this, the reframe adds a **shape-of-data argument**: traditional externalization (code, current-state design docs, runbooks) preserves the *what* — the present state of the world — but loses the *why* (alternatives considered, decisions rejected, dependencies between commitments). Parnas & Clements (1986) is the canonical SE statement that rationale documentation must be faked because real processes don't produce it; LaToza et al. 2006 documents engineers expensively reconstructing design rationale from code re-reads and teammate-interruptions; Ko & Myers (Whyline, ICSE 2008) is the cleanest quantitative anchor — rationale-shaped access yielded 3× success and 2× speed on debugging. The right framing then becomes: humans can't hold the arcs in head (Cowan numbers), traditional artifacts lose the arc shape (Parnas, LaToza, Ko & Myers), and Stoa's WAL is both first-class scaffolding *and* the right shape of data (arcs, not just state).

**AI side.** Published long-context literature establishes that frontier LLMs degrade well below nominal context for reasoning tasks. Anchors: Liu et al. 2023 (Lost in the Middle, positional U-curve); Hsieh et al. 2024 RULER (effective context typically 25-50% of nominal on multi-hop tracing; aggregation is the weakest task family across all tested models); Kuratov et al. 2024 BABILong (popular LLMs use only 10-20% of advertised context for multi-fact reasoning); Goyal et al. 2025 EMNLP-F (reasoning degrades 13.9-85% even when retrieval is held at ceiling — the cleanest mechanical separation); Hong et al. 2025 Chroma "Context Rot" (every one of 18 tested frontier models degrades at every input-length increment); Bai et al. 2024 LongBench v2; Modarressi et al. 2025 NoLiMa.

**The unstudied configuration.** Every published benchmark uses the *signal-in-noise* paradigm: a small amount of relevant content embedded in distractor text. Stoa's substrate is the opposite shape — curated, high-relevance-density (every entry is signal), with explicit cross-references (`Refs:`), and the task is classification (Adjacent / Converging / Superseding / Unrelated) against the corpus, not QA over it. No published benchmark covers this configuration. This cuts in opposing directions: optimistic (no distractor cost → degradation later than published numbers predict) vs. pessimistic (every entry is a potential confounder; classification is finer-grained than QA). Which dominates is unknown — justifying a Stoa-specific benchmark that produces genuinely novel data, not a translation of published curves.

**Thesis-positioning consequence.** Published AI long-context lit becomes *backdrop establishing the question is worth asking*, not a direct comparison set. The thesis's capacity-comparison claim lands as `unscaffolded human` vs. `AI + Stoa-style scaffolding` — both sides of the comparison are working-memory bound; both are scaffolding-bound; the question is whether the scaffolding can be made first-class and machine-consumable, and the benchmark below ([`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24)) measures whether it works in Stoa's actual configuration.

**Alternatives considered.** Keeping the naive "AI > human" framing (rejected — empirically weak; Hutchins' distributed-cognition correction makes it a category error; the right comparison is scaffolded-vs-scaffolded). Dropping the human-side numbers entirely in favor of just the shape-of-data argument (rejected — numbers are load-bearing; they establish *how small* unaided capacity is, which is the visceral case for needing scaffolding at all). Citing published AI long-context numbers as direct comparison (rejected — substrate shape is not comparable; would mislead readers).

**Refs:** [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24) (benchmark design v1 — operationalizes the AI-side claim made here).

## 425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Settled the design of the AI coherence-degradation benchmark v1 — the experiment that quantifies at what corpus size frontier LLM coherence-classification on Stoa-shaped substrate starts to degrade. Findings target the thesis ([docs/thesis.md](docs/thesis.md)).

**Substrate.** Synthetic corpora of WAL-shaped entries on neutral topics (not Stoa-domain content — testing a general problem-solving capacity claim, not a domain-specific one). Each entry follows canonical Stoa WAL form (header `## <hex> — <type> — <date>`, Authors line, prose body, optional `Refs:`). **`Refs:` are realistic and load-bearing — entries genuinely reference other entries in the corpus.** Without explicit cross-references, the benchmark wouldn't be testing the right input: arcs *are* the `Refs:`-connected subgraphs in the WAL.

**Task.** Given a held-out candidate entry, classify its relationship to the corpus into one of four classes: Adjacent (related, not contradicting), Converging (independent same-conclusion), Superseding (contradicts a prior entry; rollback recommended), Unrelated (no semantic connection to any prior). This is the same taxonomy the spec's two-layer coherence-check operates on.

**Adaptive sampling on N.** Start with sparse points — **N = 50, 100, 500** — and infill where degradation actually appears. Rationale: published lit (RULER multi-hop, BABILong, Chroma) suggests the interesting transition for frontier models on item-dense reasoning lands somewhere in the low hundreds; N = 50 is "in the clear," N = 100 is at the published edge, N = 500 is well past. Branch rules: all three near-perfect → push to N = 1000, 2500; degradation appears at 500 only → infill 250, 750; degradation at 100 → infill 75, 150, 200 (the most interesting case for the thesis); degradation at 50 → re-examine corpus difficulty (degradation that early likely means the corpus is too hard, not that capacity is 50).

**Difficulty levels.** Two corpora generated at each N — *easy* (relationships are semantically distant, lexical overlap on ground-truth pairs) and *hard* (relationships require inference, no lexical handles). The gap between the two curves is itself a finding. Difficulty is the dominant confound per RULER/BABILong methodology notes.

**Statistical power.** **3-5 independent corpora per (N, difficulty) cell.** Synthetic-corpus variance can swamp signal at smaller N; one corpus per cell would conflate capacity findings with corpus-luck. The corpus generator is the bottleneck once; runs are cheap.

**Position variants.** End-of-corpus placement of would-be-conflicting ground-truth entries by default; one mid-corpus spot-check at the largest N to detect whether Liu et al. 2023's "lost in the middle" dominates capacity effects. Cheap, high-information.

**Ablations** (run at N values where the main curve shows something interesting, not at every N):
- **`Refs:` shuffle / strip** — same corpus, but with reference edges randomized or removed. Does the model use the explicit graph, or is it deriving relationships from content alone? Bears on whether the `Refs:` discipline carries weight beyond cognitive scaffolding for humans.
- **Body-stripped / headline-only** — same corpus, headers only. Does coherence-classification work on dense summaries alone? Bears on the slurp-vs-RAG threshold question in OP1.

**Model and condition.** `claude-opus-4-7[1m]`, thinking effort **xhigh**. Single model/condition, fixed. The justification: this is the operator's actual usage mode; results land as Stoa-configuration-specific data, not as a model-comparison study. Documented honestly when written up: no other model tested; "claude-opus-4-7 / xhigh / 1M-context" is the specific configuration measured.

**Metrics.** Precision/recall per class (Adjacent / Converging / Superseding / Unrelated). **Headline metric: Superseding-recall** (missed-conflict rate), the most expensive failure mode for Stoa — published RULER/BABILong/Chroma agree that the "compare multiple corpus items to detect contradiction" class degrades earliest and steepest. Per-run cost and latency captured (informs the slurp-vs-RAG threshold discussion in OP1).

**Per-N candidate count.** ~50 candidate-classifications per (N, difficulty, corpus) cell — enough for stable precision/recall numbers; not so many that compute dominates.

**Alternatives considered.** Multi-model matrix (Sonnet 4.6 + Opus 4.7 + Haiku 4.5; rejected — would dilute focus, and the operator's actual usage is the relevant configuration); dogfooding real `context_log.md` entries paraphrased for ground-truth control (rejected — neutral synthetic topics keep the claim general; real Stoa entries would risk Stoa-specific contamination); skipping ablations to keep matrix small (rejected — `Refs:`-strip and headline-only directly test load-bearing claims about why Stoa's substrate works); one corpus per cell (rejected — corpus-luck would swamp signal at smaller N).

**Implementation deferred.** Corpus generator, ground-truth labelling discipline, run-orchestration, and result-storage shape are next-session work. The design here settles *what* the experiment measures; *how* it's implemented is downstream.

**Refs:** [`84a167f5`](context_log.md#84a167f5e26045928a2fd29e41bce5b0--decision--2026-05-24) (thesis capacity-comparison reframe — establishes the framing this benchmark serves).

## b9fc227821f245618f81696d7858987a — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Extended the `stoa-bootcheck` subagent to query the operator's canonical platform handle at session start, return it in a new trailing `Attribution: ...` line, and have the main agent cache `@<handle>` for the session's T2 writes. Replaced the slim §"WAL entry form" → §Attribution 5-step procedure with a 2-clause rule: handle-establishment (read from bootcheck's `[stoa-init]` block; fallback to operator ask) and per-write composition (compose `@<cached-handle>;<current-tool>(<current-model>)` on every T2 write, recomputing the tool/model suffix from session metadata).

**Why now.** Per the Phase 0 slim-strictly-AI-directive rule ([`7c784c70`](context_log.md#7c784c7072e5411c8be1c213f24be739--decision--2026-05-24)): the 5-step attribution procedure was procedural detail that fired once per session at first T2 write. Moving the platform-identity query into bootcheck (which already runs at the boundary moment) consolidates — one subagent invocation establishes both install-state AND attribution; main agent caches both from the same `[stoa-init]` block. Slim now describes only the cache-and-recompose discipline AI follows at each write — fewer steps, simpler runtime rule-ladder.

**Mid-session model changes naturally handled.** The per-write composition rule recomputes `<tool>(<model>)` from session metadata at write time. Operators changing model mid-session see the new model suffix in subsequent T2 entries without any explicit re-bootcheck.

**Failure mode preserved.** If `gh api user` fails or the remote isn't GitHub-hosted, bootcheck returns `Attribution: needs-operator (reason: <not-authed | non-github-remote | gh-not-installed | query-failed>)`. Main agent surfaces this in the `[stoa-init]` block; first-message operator response provides the handle; main agent caches for the rest of the session.

**Changes (slim):**
- §"Session boot check": (a) probe-list expanded to mention canonical platform handle; (b) status-return summary clarified as *"status return"* (separate from the new trailing Attribution); (c) `[stoa-init]` block format adds `Attribution: ...` field; (d) *"If the return is X"* → *"If the status return is X"* for disambiguation.
- §"WAL entry form" → §Attribution: 5-step procedure + *"Mid-session safety"* paragraph replaced by 2-clause handle-establishment + per-write composition rule.

**Changes (bootcheck embedded artifact, `.claude/agents/stoa-bootcheck.md`):**
- §"Output discipline (read FIRST)": output contract extended to *"status line(s) followed by trailing Attribution: line"*; mandate language strengthened.
- §"Procedure": new Step 5 — Attribution probe (GitHub remote detection + `gh api user --jq .login`; cause-tagged failure modes). Step 6 renumbered (was Step 5: diagnostic-probe discipline).
- §"Output": restructured into *"Status line(s)"* + *"Trailing line"* subsections; WRONG/RIGHT examples updated to include the Attribution line; new RIGHT example for the failure case.

**AI-instruction-block discipline acknowledged.** This commit touches multiple AI-instruction blocks (Session boot check directive, the bootcheck subagent's output discipline + procedure + output sections, and the Attribution rule). Per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15): wording is what it is because it was tuned; deviations are bugs unless explicitly retuned. This entry IS the retuning record — the compliance shift is documented here for future audits.

**Net effect on AI runtime rule-ladder.** Removes one session-time procedure (the 5-step *"establish canonical attribution at first T2 write"* flow that AI had to execute mid-session). Replaces with two cache-rule lookups: once at session start (read bootcheck's `Attribution:` line), and once per T2 write (recompose `<tool>(<model>)` suffix from session metadata). Simpler ladder; lower per-write cognitive load.

**Refs:** [`7c784c70`](context_log.md#7c784c7072e5411c8be1c213f24be739--decision--2026-05-24) (slim-strictly-AI-directive rule); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instructions-are-code rule — this entry IS the explicit retuning record).

## 5dc9e930cd8a41908b7877419862204b — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Adopted `experiments/` as the canonical top-level directory for per-measurement narrative docs. Each empirical instrument Stoa carries (stress-test of arc capture, coherence-classification capacity benchmark, future tracking-drift harness, future reconstruction-fidelity instrument) gets one narrative doc here.

**Three-doc role split.** Each empirical instrument has up to three artifacts, each with a distinct audience:

| Doc | Audience | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `experiments/<measurement>.md` | Thesis readers, evaluators, future selves | Goal + methodology summary + results history (append-only) + limitations + thesis-citation summary |
| `<harness>/README.md` | Operators running the harness | How to use it: usage, layout, tracked-vs-gitignored — pure runbook |
| `<harness>/results/<run>/summary.md` | Forensic readers of a specific run | Per-run depth: headline numbers, per-condition breakdown, methodology validation, recommendations |

The experiments doc carries the *audience-facing narrative* — what the measurement is for, what's been learned across releases. The harness README carries the *operational runbook* — how to actually run it. The per-run summary carries *the forensic detail of one run*.

**Naming by what's measured, not by harness mechanism.** Thesis readers care about the empirical question (arc capture, coherence classification, drift detection, reconstruction fidelity), not the implementation (stress-test-harness, tracking-harness, etc.). So: `arc-capture-quality.md` not `stress-test.md`; `coherence-classification-capacity.md` (planned) not `coherence-benchmark.md`. Decouples narrative from implementation; supports multiple harnesses for one measurement or one-shot measurements without harnesses.

**Per-doc structure** (six sections, consistent across the program):
1. **Goal** — empirical question + which thesis bet it speaks to
2. **Methodology** — substrate, conditions, scoring approach
3. **Results history** — append-only; newer at top, prior runs flagged as not-directly-comparable when methodology changed
4. **Limitations and confounds** — honest scoping; cumulative-state proxies, cross-scenario thinness, cross-model untested, etc.
5. **Runnable harness** — link to harness dir + WAL provenance hex IDs
6. **Thesis-citation summary** — single quotable paragraph the thesis paraphrases verbatim; stable block lives next to its source

**Thesis-citation summary is the load-bearing element of the pattern.** Without it, the thesis would either paraphrase from scratch each citation (drift risk) or lift full results tables (bloat). With it, the thesis carries headline summaries; depth is one click away. The thesis's §Experiments section becomes a curated index — one short paragraph per experiment plus link.

**First instance.** `experiments/arc-capture-quality.md` — migrated narrative content from `stress-test-harness/` (README.md's *"Why this exists"* + baselines.md framing + results/2026-05-21-v0.7.1-BETA-a5135d9/summary.md headlines + harness's *"What it does NOT measure"*). The harness README + baselines.md were trimmed to point at the experiments doc for narrative; harness retains its operational content.

**Sketch / experiments-doc maturity ladder.** Sketches in `sketches/` are seed material, not source of truth (WAL + harness implementation carry authority). When a sketch's measurement matures into reality (e.g., `sketches/tracking-harness.md` → built harness), the canonical home is the experiments doc, and the sketch gets deleted. Maturity ladder: sketch → WAL settlement → harness implementation → `experiments/<name>.md`.

**Alternatives considered.** Bolting per-experiment writeups directly into the thesis as inline sections (rejected — bloat as the experiment program grows; thesis is one of multiple audience-facing docs and shouldn't carry forensic detail). Splitting "theory" from "experiments" into two parallel top-level docs (rejected — fragments the thesis argument; readers would bounce between docs to follow Bet 1's evidence). Co-locating narrative inside each harness dir as `<harness>/EXPERIMENT.md` (rejected — measurement may have multiple harnesses or no harness; co-location couples narrative to implementation in the wrong direction). Single `docs/experiments.md` indexing all measurements (rejected — doesn't scale beyond ~3 experiments; each measurement deserves its own doc with version history).

**Why now.** Three experiments are in flight or planned (stress-test of arc capture exists; coherence-classification-capacity is being designed; tracking-drift-detection is sketched). With more planned, the pattern is worth settling once, validated against a known instance (arc-capture-quality migration), then applied to the new ones.

**Refs:** [`84a167f5`](context_log.md#84a167f5e26045928a2fd29e41bce5b0--decision--2026-05-24) (thesis capacity-comparison reframe — establishes the framing experiments docs serve); [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24) (coherence-classification benchmark design — the second experiments-doc instance, to be drafted next).

## 9e28ada9c16543f3b665d1a911d45bfc — decision — 2026-05-24

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

Settled the dual-layer pattern for integrating `experiments/` content into [`docs/thesis.md`](docs/thesis.md): inline **Empirical anchor** callouts at the Claim / Bet sections where evidence is locally needed, plus a centralized §Experiments section serving as program-overview and index.

**The pattern.**
- **Inline callouts** — labeled blockquotes (`> **Empirical anchor — [<experiment>](...):** ...`) inserted in Claim / Bet / §Capacity-asymmetry sections where the local argument benefits from evidence-pointing. 2-4 lines: experiment link + headline finding paraphrased for the local argument + implicit pointer to the experiments doc for depth. Visually distinct from regular thesis prose (the thesis already uses blockquotes for cited-canon, so the callout label is what distinguishes Stoa-internal measurement from external canon).
- **Centralized §Experiments section** — the empirical-program-at-a-glance, with one short paragraph per experiment (empirical question, current status, headline-or-pending, link, cross-links to which Claim/Bet sections carry its callouts). Re-quotes from each experiments doc's §Thesis-citation summary; updates flow forward by re-quotation, not independent restatement.

**Three reading paths.**
1. Top-to-bottom prose readers encounter inline callouts at the relevant arguments and click through if curious.
2. Skimmers go straight to §Experiments to see the empirical program.
3. Depth readers go to `experiments/<name>.md`.

All three are consistent — same content, three levels of granularity.

**Label = "Empirical anchor".** Distinguishes Stoa-internal measurement from external cited canon. Considered alternatives: *Empirical*, *Evidence*, *See*, *Experiment*. *Empirical anchor* won — *Empirical* alone reads as a stub; *Evidence* overloads with cited-opposing-canon framing; *See* is too generic; *Experiment* over-elevates a single instance. *Empirical anchor* names what the block does (anchors the local argument in Stoa-internal measurement) without over-promising.

**Pre-results vs. results-landed callout format.** For experiments with results, callouts carry a one-line headline finding. For experiments in design / pre-results (e.g., [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24)'s coherence-classification benchmark), callouts are *only added after results land* — design-phase callouts add no information beyond what the §Experiments index already carries. The §Experiments section index can carry pre-results entries (status = "in active design"); inline callouts wait for findings.

**Workflow when a new run lands.**
1. Update `experiments/<name>.md` §Results history + §Thesis-citation summary.
2. Re-quote the updated §Thesis-citation summary into the thesis §Experiments index entry.
3. Update the inline callouts that cite this experiment (typically 1-3 of them).

Three narrow edits per run. No prose restructuring required.

**First instance.** Two `arc-capture-quality` callouts being added immediately to validate the pattern with real numbers (v0.7.1 BETA baseline) before scaling to the new §Capacity asymmetry + §Experiments + Bets-reframe restructure. Callout locations: Claim 1 (forest is canonical — does the WAL actually capture inflections in practice?) and Bet 1 (settlement-cue recognition is a load-bearing slice of the calibration bet).

**Alternatives considered.** Inline-citations-only (rejected — no program-overview entry point for skimmers; readers can't see all empirical work at a glance). Centralized-section-only (rejected — fragments the thesis argument from its evidence; readers have to bounce to find what's measured against each claim). Footnotes / endnotes (rejected — interrupts prose flow without the visual distinction of blockquotes; thesis already uses blockquotes consistently). Embedded results tables in the Claim sections (rejected — bloats prose; defeats the purpose of separating depth into experiments docs).

**Refs:** [`5dc9e930`](context_log.md#5dc9e930cd8a41908b7877419862204b--decision--2026-05-24) (experiments-doc pattern — the upstream structural decision this callout pattern integrates with the thesis).

## 4d2cc9d496824db4b8701424ff9a3f85 — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Introduce entry-class axis: EC:STRONG / EC:DEFERRED / EC:WEAK. Type→class mapping deterministic; class fixed at write-time so spec rules become mechanical lookups instead of fresh AI judgment per fire.**

Three classes alongside the existing entry types: `EC:STRONG` (forward commitment — types: `decision`, `won't-do`, `rollback`); `EC:DEFERRED` (opinionated parking — types: `table`); `EC:WEAK` (recorded observation; no forward commitment — types: `observation`).

Pick the type, the class follows. Class labels appear in spec rule text only; WAL entry headers carry the type. Several rules across slim previously conditioned on commitment-strength implicitly (L97 broad-class scope, Layer 2 batch invoke/skip, cadence #5 missed-promotion). EC makes the dimension explicit and shared; rules become mechanical lookups instead of re-deriving commitment-strength per fire. A healthy refining-session WAL has `EC:WEAK` at parity with or exceeding `EC:STRONG` — observations along the way outnumber the punctuation settlements they support.

**Refs:** [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (three-tier WAL model — adjacent foundation).

## ac607b4e642a4755b42aa934194b970a — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Remove `branch` as an entry type. Fork patterns emerge as observations with incoming `Refs:` from later sub-arc entries. Five entry types remain.**

The 6-type set reduces to 5 (`decision`, `won't-do`, `table`, `rollback`, `observation`). Branches are not a type — they're an emergent pattern in the `Refs:` graph. When refining produces a multi-option moment, record an observation; sub-arc settlements later reference it via `Refs:`. This follows OP3 (arcs are emergent, not stored): trust AI to traverse `Refs:` at query time rather than encoding fork-structure in entry-type schema.

Empirical justification: `branch` accumulated near-zero use in v0.2+ — only two entries used it in early v0.1, both in the pre-canonical header format. The write-time judgment ("is this fork-y enough?") repeatedly produced miscategorization. Three live tensions resolve cleanly: (1) "can't tell a-priori it's a branch" — no longer a write-time problem since it's not a type; (2) linguistic collision with "git branch" — qualified-when-needed throughout the spec ("WAL-arc branch" vs "git branch / canonical branch"); (3) unjoined sub-arc forks — same as before, just open arcs in the forest. Historical `branch` entries stay valid as-is (append-only invariant preserved).

**Refs:** [`4d2cc9d4`](context_log.md#4d2cc9d496824db4b8701424ff9a3f85--decision--2026-05-25) (EC axis — fork moments map to EC:WEAK observations).

## c95a8889f3844f7592fd1590b9fbd173 — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**T1 model under autonomy: mutable T1 + class-based yardstick + reconciliation rules + flush triggers. Class-based replaces reconstruction-fidelity as the session-time yardstick (reconstruction-fidelity survives as offline calibration).**

AI evaluates each potential inflection against type-fit ("would this fit one of the entry types?") rather than reconstruction-fidelity at session-time. The fidelity yardstick remains valid as the offline calibration target (validating long-term over the WAL corpus) — what changes is what AI applies live. Class-based captures `EC:WEAK` observations on their own terms, resolving the under-capture failure mode where fidelity rarely depended on any single observation and the yardstick said "no" to most.

T1 stays mutable per [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19). Within session, AI may refine candidate content as understanding clarifies, demote a candidate that turns out to be trajectory texture, or preserve-the-arc when a misinterpretation→correction sequence carries provenance value (capture both as paired entries). Flush triggers T1→T2: (1) STRONG identification → immediate flush; (2) mutating tool call → flush all pending T1 of any class; (3) cadence boundaries → flush as backstop. Stale-cache rejection at T2 write layers on top to handle the post-merge case (catchup before append).

**Refs:** [`b6e06d0e`](context_log.md#b6e06d0ec18d4622961b9184e492aaf5--decision--2026-05-19) (T1 mutable foundation — preserved); [`295e98d1`](context_log.md#295e98d1e0df441bbc7a6de60c5662ef--decision--2026-05-19) (reconstruction-fidelity — survives as offline audit, replaced as session-time yardstick); [`4d2cc9d4`](context_log.md#4d2cc9d496824db4b8701424ff9a3f85--decision--2026-05-25) (class-based yardstick uses EC axis).

## 53ecae58776743eda61fd5ca70db1b2a — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**L97 T1↔T2 discipline rule broadens to any class. Promotion via `rollback` for direct supersession; fresh entry with `Refs:` for related-but-non-contradicting. No `branch` mechanism (branch is no longer a type).**

The discipline rule previously read narrowly as supersession-only with mechanism options including a now-removed `branch` type. The rewrite broadens to any class: when T1 thinking evolves to contradict a committed T2 entry, AI promotes via the appropriate type — `rollback` for direct supersession; fresh entry with `Refs:` for related-but-non-contradicting. The mechanism wasn't class-conditioned in the first place; narrow framing was an artifact of the prior `branch`/`split` enumeration. Broad framing matches the rule's actual scope.

## 2c8d2136f5a94409808e2c07d673bf3d — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**T2 write anchor collapses to binary: `Consistency: clean | Superseding <hex> (rollback appended)`. Commit-state field dropped per OP4. Adjacent/Converging classifications flow through `Refs:` in entry body, not the anchor.**

The previous anchor enumerated multiple states (clean / Superseding / Refines) and carried a commit-state field. Two simplifications: (1) anchor states collapse to binary — only Superseding (which produces an atomic rollback) needs anchor surfacing; Adjacent/Converging add `Refs:` lines in the entry body and don't change anchor semantics. (2) Commit-state field drops — per OP4, T3 is git integration territory, not Stoa-prescribed. The anchor reports the T2 write, not the eventual commit. Whether the entry is "holding pending commit" or "committed in <SHA>" is git-domain information AI has no commitment to track at WAL-write time. Reduces ceremony; removes the coupling between WAL operations and git mechanics OP4 explicitly disclaims.

## d961de2ce2f54fcc96d070ca33bf21e0 — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Layer 2 batch coherence at commit: invoke if batch contains any EC:STRONG entry; skip if only EC:WEAK and EC:DEFERRED with clean Layer 1. EC axis replaces heuristic enumeration (rollback/branch flags, headline-scan topic overlap, batch size).**

Previously Layer 2 invoke/skip used a heuristic list (presence of rollback/branch, topic-overlap headline-scan, batch size). Replaced by mechanical EC lookup. The heuristic-versus-mechanical tradeoff falls to mechanical because the EC class already captures the stake-asymmetry the heuristics approximated: `EC:STRONG` entries warrant the heavier full-WAL coherence sweep; `EC:WEAK` and `EC:DEFERRED` entries with clean Layer 1 don't. Topic-overlap headline-scans and batch-size heuristics drop. Cadence #6 internal-conflict sweep and `/stoa audit` remain as on-demand backstops for whatever Layer 2 skip misses.

## f284d28250164f3f944bf77116fcee87 — decision — 2026-05-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Cadence #6 restructures around post-merge git hook as primary mechanism. `/stoa pull` becomes optional UX. Stale-cache rejection (in-session pull) + bootcheck probe (out-of-session pull + new session) drive catchup. Semantic-merge audit substance preserved; mechanism shifts.**

Previous mechanism (cadence #6 firing via pre-pull `/stoa pull` invocation routed from operator-prose cues) was empirically unreliable — operator-driven `/stoa pull` is easy to miss; AI-side `git fetch`-before-push detection is a thin discipline that routinely failed in practice. Restructured: a deterministic post-merge git hook updates `.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit` with merge SHA(s) after any merge/rebase touching `context_log.md`. The hook is proxy-immune.

Catchup fires via three paths:

- **Stale-cache rejection** on next T2 write (in-session pull case): AI re-reads, identifies new entries, runs `/stoa coherence --internal-sweep` on them, then proceeds with the original append.
- **Bootcheck probe** on next session start (out-of-session pull + new session): AI surfaces a `[stoa] N merges pending audit` line; operator triggers `/stoa audit`.
- **Operator-driven `/stoa pull`** (optional UX): pre-merge audit before pulling; not load-bearing — the post-merge hook handles all paths.

## fc35308051a440be924807cc57f53046 — decision — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Cadence #6 mechanism implements as TWO deterministic git hooks: `post-merge` for merges and fast-forward pulls; `post-rewrite` for rebases. Both write `.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit`. Spec wording corrected from singular "post-merge git hook" to dual-hook coverage. Bootcheck Step 4b probe reads the marker; main agent auto-runs catchup on detect (per L34 callout).**

The `f284d282` settlement specified "post-merge git hook" as the cadence #6 mechanical primary. Implementation review surfaced a reliability gap: `git pull --rebase` (the canonical pull behavior under `branch.<main>.rebase=true`, which is the cadence #6 substrate) does NOT fire `post-merge` when an actual rebase occurs — it fires `post-rewrite` instead. `post-merge` only fires on fast-forward pulls and three-way merges. The multi-author scenario "operator has local commits, pulls upstream commits including WAL changes" — exactly the case cadence #6 exists for — would have produced no marker write under single-hook coverage.

**Both hooks ship.** Same filter (context_log.md touched in the recent merge/rebase relative to `ORIG_HEAD`); same marker write (`git rev-parse HEAD >> .stoa/state/merge-pending-audit`). `post-rewrite` adds a `rebase`-vs-`amend` arg check (commit-amend doesn't touch upstream history; not cadence-#6 territory). Both wrap a Phase-1 chain (`.git/hooks/<name>.stoa-backup`) so pre-existing operator hooks keep firing — same pattern as `.githooks/pre-commit`. Step 5 hook-wiring logic skips delegator generation for `post-merge` and `post-rewrite` alongside `pre-commit` (the canonical Stoa hook handles its own Phase 1 chain).

**Marker file.** `.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit` — newline-separated post-operation HEAD SHAs, per-clone runtime state. `.stoa/state/.gitignore` excludes the marker (and any future runtime-state files) from version control while preserving the directory's presence via the `.gitignore` itself.

**Bootcheck Step 4b.** Read-only probe reads `.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit`; if non-empty, surfaces `[stoa] *No operator action needed* — N merge(s)/rebase(s) pending cadence-#6 audit; main agent will run /stoa coherence --internal-sweep on the unaudited entries.` Main agent auto-runs catchup per the slim §"Session boot check" L34 callout — bootcheck stays read-only; main agent acts on the findings. The slim §"Bootcheck post-merge audit probe" wording (L172) is corrected to match: "Main agent runs /stoa coherence --internal-sweep" replaces the operator-triggered framing from draft v2 (L172/L34 coherence fix).

**Refs:** [`f284d282`](context_log.md#f284d28250164f3f944bf77116fcee87--decision--2026-05-25) (cadence #6 post-merge primary — mechanism refined here from singular to dual-hook; substance preserved); [`019d0aff`](context_log.md#019d0aff04524191aed79734366f3e43--decision--2026-05-25) (§"AI behavior in deliberation" — surfacing this gap before silent resolution).

## caab91ea57ee433a82199dce086f8788 — won't-do — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Won't ship strict-fail WAL merge gates (custom merge driver + pre-rebase hook that fail WAL merges outside Stoa sessions). The backstop pattern (post-merge / post-rewrite hooks + bootcheck Step 4b + stale-cache rejection) is cadence #6's mechanism, not a gap to close with prevention.**

Considered during commit-2 deliberation: a custom merge driver (`.gitattributes: context_log.md merge=stoa-wal-fail`) + `.githooks/pre-rebase` that fail WAL merges outside a Stoa session. AI-mediated pulls would bypass via per-invocation `git -c stoa.session-active=true pull`; operator-side terminal `git pull` would hit the gate with divergent commits. Closes the "merge-but-not-yet-audited" temporal gap by preventing the merge.

Rejected for four reasons:

1. **FP1 direct conflict.** "Rigid validators have repeatedly failed because engineers route around them." A merge driver that exits 1 by default IS the canonical rigid validator. Strict-fail will predictably route around itself — CI pipelines, automation, `--no-verify`-equivalent escape hatches, `git config --local --unset core.hooksPath`.
2. **OP4 boundary crossing.** "Stoa-defined mechanisms that DO touch the git boundary are failure-mode backstops that integrate WITH git, not prescriptions OF git mechanics." A custom merge driver that always-fails is unambiguously prescribing git mechanics. A pre-rebase hook that exits 1 is the same shape.
3. **False-confidence trade.** Strict-fail catches well-meaning operators who didn't realize they should be in a Stoa session. It doesn't catch deliberate bypasses. The post-strict-fail claim "WAL merges go through audit" is weaker in practice than the backstop pattern (which doesn't claim prevention) because the bypass paths exist and are invisible to Stoa.
4. **Pattern coherence.** Every other cadence (#3, #4, #5, #7) is a retroactive catch-up. Making cadence #6 a gate breaks the pattern and pulls consistency-pressure toward making them all gates — which is exactly the rigid-validator failure mode FP1 names.

What the backstop pattern accepts: a procedural (not corrupting) temporal gap between unaudited merge and audited audit, bounded by next-session catch-up via bootcheck Step 4b + stale-cache rejection at T2 write. The WAL during the gap is well-formed (append-only intact, all entries syntactically valid) — just unclassified pending Refs-link work. The catch-up converts pending → classified; nothing has been corrupted.

The discomfort the strict-fail proposal sought to resolve is real (Stoa claims AI-managed coherence; git can merge WAL without AI). Resolving by hard prevention trades a philosophical inconsistency for an operational one — and the operational one (CI fails, automation fails, fresh-clone pulls fail, multi-terminal workflows fail) is worse, especially for Stoa-adoption in mixed-tooling environments.

**Refs:** [`fc353080`](context_log.md#fc35308051a440be924807cc57f53046--decision--2026-05-26) (dual-hook mechanism that ships in cadence #6's place); [`92cbef74`](context_log.md#92cbef74e6d24d218d6fdd3f890447a8--decision--2026-05-26) (catchup-surface fidelity — the design dimension this won't-do leaves intact); [`019d0aff`](context_log.md#019d0aff04524191aed79734366f3e43--decision--2026-05-25) (off-pattern detection dropped — sibling retreat from the prevention pattern).

- **Defer pending Codex subagent API research** — third-party marketing comparison (Morph LLM, 2026-03-14) reports Codex shipped subagents to GA, describing a manager-worker pattern with explorer/worker/default agent types in cloud sandboxes. Addresses pending-items entry H4 deeper (architectural deepening Phase 2.C). The cadence #3 wording at slim L451 carried stale text from [`92cddf26`](context_log.md#92cddf26b85447debe962064fcb5bfbb--decision--2026-05-19) (the original commit-batching cadence which was rolled back by [`1a87b34e`](context_log.md#1a87b34ee857448592974a52c7339536--rollback--2026-05-20) under OP4 [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20), but with "the auto-`--no-verify` + aggregated-observation mechanic in cadence #3 wording" explicitly preserved). Per librarian audit, the wording drifted from current practice:

- *Origin reading (Reading A):* commit with `--no-verify`; observation lands in a SEPARATE commit. Implemented once in the wild ([`9cbf7bc2`](context_log.md#9cbf7bc26a8f4903a266354885a83b33--observation--2026-05-20), Phase E test-harness commit).
- *Recent practice (Reading B):* bundle the observation in the SAME commit; `context_log.md` is staged; Pass A passes naturally without `--no-verify`. Implemented twice in the wild ([`60762ce3`](context_log.md#60762ce3d56744eebc16967efc2adfc0--observation--2026-05-26) Phase 1.2 commit 3; [`386f5a78`](context_log.md#386f5a787644429e98508cbf79d145df--observation--2026-05-26) Phase 2.A commit 2).

Reading B is mechanically simpler (no hook bypass needed) and has converged in practice. The fix aligns spec wording with Reading B.

**Cluster semantics.** The phrase "per commit-cluster" was never defined in the WAL — `92cddf26`'s parenthetical hinted at phase-scope but the substance was about batch ripeness, not the zero-finding rule. Practice has converged on cluster = single commit (every in-the-wild aggregated observation has been per-single-commit). Wording updated to "per commit" — explicit, simpler, matches practice.

**`--no-verify` AI scope (load-bearing implication).** This fix removes the ONLY spec-licensed AI-side `--no-verify` path. After this entry lands, AI has no spec-documented autonomous license to skip hooks. The cases remain:
- *Operator explicit authorization* — operator types "commit with --no-verify" or "skip hooks": licenses one specific use per the general harness rule.
- *Hook source comment at line 695* (`# Per-commit override: git commit --no-verify`) — operator-facing escape-hatch documentation; not part of any AI-instruction rule.
- *Hook failures (non-Stoa reasons):* AI investigates root cause per general harness rule; doesn't bypass.
- *Hook failures (Stoa Pass A blocking):* AI follows the hook's surfaced recovery instructions (now: "append observation and re-stage"); doesn't bypass.

Strengthens discipline by removing ambiguity at the only locus where AI was tempted toward bypass. Aligns with the general harness rule from the system prompt: *"Never skip hooks (--no-verify) unless the user has explicitly asked for it."*

**Three loci edited (must stay in sync).**

- **Slim L451** (cadence #3 rule): "If T1 is empty after class-based audit, AI may commit with `--no-verify` plus one aggregated `observation` entry per commit-cluster capturing the negative findings." → "If T1 is empty after class-based audit, AI may commit with one aggregated `observation` entry per commit capturing the negative findings."
- **Slim L487** (zero-finding cross-reference): drops "(auto-`--no-verify` path)" parenthetical and "commit-cluster" → "per commit".
- **Install-kit L764-765** (pre-commit hook output message): "commit with --no-verify and append one aggregated observation entry per commit-cluster" → "append one aggregated observation entry to `context_log.md` and re-stage". Operator-facing recovery instruction now matches the slim rule.

L695 (per-commit override comment in hook source code) **unchanged** — general escape-hatch documentation, independent of the cadence-#3 rule's wording.

**Mechanism note.** Three-locus edit, all in `installkit/stoa.md`. Two loci are slim AI-instruction blocks (subject to [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15)); one is install-kit-embedded artifact (the pre-commit hook). Single WAL entry covers all three because they're the same rule surfaced at three loci; granularity-wise they're an atomic unit (can't split a rollback meaningfully).

## 1dcaa464c9c44ce69085dfb5e6e21604 — decision — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Cadence #2 (post-decision propagation pass) gets a deterministic backstop: Pass C added to `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`. Triggers when staged diff bumps the SemVer in `installkit/stoa.md` or `stoa.md`; checks each path in `.stoa/artifacts.md` for SemVer mismatches; blocks the commit on drift. Sibling to cadence #3's Pass A. Slim §"Coherence cadence" #2 wording sharpened to name the three drift event-shapes (rename, version bump, cadence-rule reword) and acknowledge Pass C as the deterministic backstop for the version-bump case. Mechanical detection for rename and cadence-reword propagation stays out of scope — discipline is the load-bearing mitigation for the residual.**

Addresses the recurring cadence-#1+#2 miss documented across three beta-tracker instances (`d4f9a13` v0.3.6→v0.3.7, `b485bbf9` v0.4.3→v0.5.1, today's Phase 2.D). Per [`e358ce94`](context_log.md#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17) (the WAL entry capturing the two prior instances and enumerating mitigation options): option (a) visible-output block was deployed for v0.5.2 and **subsequently deprecated** by [`b90a584f`](context_log.md#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) as ceremony / rubber-stamp; option (b) tie-to-`/stoa upgrade` was rejected upfront because it misses ad-hoc inline edits (the v0.5.1 failure mode); option (c) **deterministic pre-commit hook was flagged as "the v0.6+ escalation candidate if (a) also degrades."** (a) HAS degraded — both via deprecation and via today's recurrence. This entry ships (c).

**Layer 1 — Pass C deterministic hook.** Added to `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` alongside Pass A. Trigger gating: only fires when staged diff modifies a SemVer line in `installkit/stoa.md` or `stoa.md`. Unrelated commits (no version-stamp change) silently skip the check. When triggered, walks `.stoa/artifacts.md`, checks each tracked path's current SemVer (prefers `git show :path` for staged content; falls back to working-tree); collects mismatches; blocks with exit-1 if any. Surface format: `[stoa] **wal-audit:version-stamp-drift** detected — ...` + AI-instruction line + path list with current vs expected stamps. Sibling to Pass A's shape; same operator override path (`git commit --no-verify`).

**Layer 2 — Cadence #2 discipline sharpening.** Slim §"Coherence cadence" #2 gains explicit enumeration of three drift event-shapes: **rename in slim spec** (walk for OLD term), **version bumped** (walk for stamps not matching the new version — Pass C is the deterministic backstop), **cadence-rule reworded** (walk for references to the OLD framing). Layer 2 is buying time for the rename and reframing cases where mechanical detection was rejected as overengineering early in Stoa (the `1034`-era mapping-table won't-do); Layer 1 closes the dominant catchable case. The `b4d8e1c` arc predicts further escalation if data warrants — likely scope-expansion of Pass C to additional catchable patterns rather than fresh discipline rules.

**Why this shape (block over warn).** Pass A blocks per [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) + [`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11); Pass C follows the same shape for UX consistency. Block fires only on version-stamp-touching commits; the "I'll do it later" pattern remains accessible via `--no-verify` (operator escape hatch; same as Pass A). The block IS the forcing function — surfaces drift at commit boundary at every attempt until resolved. Operator can bundle drift cleanup in the bump commit (recommended) or override one-shot.

**BETA-tag exclusion.** Per the sibling decision [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) (just below), the SemVer regex in Pass C is `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` only — BETA suffix is NOT part of detection. Aligns with the existing bootcheck Step 1 SemVer-prefix-only comparison.

**Surface format note.** Pass C uses the `[stoa] **wal-audit:<check>**` kept-side pattern (per [`a62ef52e`](context_log.md#a62ef52e--decision--2026-05-19)). Pass A's existing `[stoa-wal-audit]` single-bracket form is older shape; unifying both to the new pattern is worth a follow-up commit but not bundled here.

**Mechanism note.** Three loci edited in this commit:
- `installkit/stoa.md` §"Coherence cadence" #2 — Layer 2 wording (slim AI-directive block; subject to `b8d4e9c`).
- `installkit/stoa.md` `#### path: .stoa/hooks/wal-audit` block — Pass C bash logic + spec-owned-blurb update naming both Pass A and Pass C.
- The local `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` will refresh on next `/stoa upgrade`.

Tests for Pass C ship in the adjacent-propagation commit (sibling pattern to Phase 2.A's two-commit structure).

**Refs:** [`e358ce94`](context_log.md#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17) (direct parent — prescribed (c) as v0.6+ escalation if (a) degraded); [`b90a584f`](context_log.md#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) ((a) deprecation that opened the gap this entry closes); [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (pure-discipline-degradation arc — this is the predicted next-altitude move for cadence #2); [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11), [`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11) (cadence #3 Pass A precedent — UX shape Pass C follows); [`a62ef52e`](context_log.md#a62ef52e--decision--2026-05-19) (kept-side `[stoa]` surface pattern for the new check's stderr format); [`9f70a1f3`](context_log.md#9f70a1f3b299483cad04fd2bb6382e44--decision--2026-05-19), [`758dde1d`](context_log.md#758dde1d62234bacb8cd9d24f0624f66--decision--2026-05-17) (tracked-artifacts list role — the substrate Pass C reads); [`c91b07e`](context_log.md#c91b07e--decision--2026-05-10) (spec-owned classification — hook script refresh-on-upgrade); [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) (sibling BETA-tag-isolation rule — Pass C regex follows it); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline).

## ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3 — decision — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Add CLAUDE.md rule: the "BETA" suffix on Stoa version stamps is for human tracking only — never include "BETA" (or future variants like "RC", "GA") in spec logic, checks, regex patterns, or operational surfaces. Version comparison and detection operates on the SemVer prefix (`v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`) only; the suffix is human-visible decoration that may evolve without affecting any code path.**

Surfaced during the cadence #2 Pass C design (sibling decision [`1dcaa464`](context_log.md#1dcaa464c9c44ce69085dfb5e6e21604--decision--2026-05-26)): initial regex draft was `v\d+\.\d+\.\d+ BETA`. Operator flagged that BETA shouldn't be part of any detection or check — it's meta-status (where Stoa is in its development cycle), not version content. Once Stoa ships a non-BETA release (or evolves the suffix), regex with BETA in it would silently break.

**Rule shape.** Declarative, not imperative. Documents the principle; doesn't enumerate every locus. Existing bootcheck Step 1 already respects this (`grep -oE 'v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'` strips the suffix); Pass C follows the same pattern. Future spec-owned code adding version-aware logic should default to the SemVer-only regex.

**Why CLAUDE.md not slim spec.** CLAUDE.md is operator + AI guidance for this repo (spec-author work); slim spec is operational surface for AI sessions across adopters. The BETA-tag-isolation rule is about how the spec-author writes detection code — meta-discipline, not session-time AI behavior. CLAUDE.md is the right altitude. The rule lands as a top-level section similar to the other bias rules (declarative-over-imperative, philosophical-over-mechanical).

**Why now.** Three instances of cadence-#2 miss across version bumps (per beta-tracker `d4f9a13`, `b485bbf9`, today's Phase 2.D); the Pass C hook design surfaced the BETA-in-regex temptation; documenting it as a discipline rule prevents recurrence at the locus where it would land (any future spec-owned version-aware code).

**Mechanism note.** Single section addition to CLAUDE.md, placed near the other bias rules. No slim spec change. No adopter-distribution surface change (CLAUDE.md is spec-author-only).

**Refs:** [`1dcaa464`](context_log.md#1dcaa464c9c44ce69085dfb5e6e21604--decision--2026-05-26) (sibling Pass C design — surfaced this rule's need); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline — note that THIS entry edits CLAUDE.md not slim, so b8d4e9c doesn't strictly apply, but documenting the rule's substance-impact via WAL entry follows the same shape).

## 22b364acec524f4e8eeaa52a40d78500 — rollback — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Rollback of [`1dcaa464`](context_log.md#1dcaa464c9c44ce69085dfb5e6e21604--decision--2026-05-26) (Pass C v1 cadence #2 deterministic backstop hook). Design error in mechanism scope: Pass C v1 was built for Stoa-internal dogfooding (this repo's tracked methodology docs vs Stoa's own version stamp) but shipped via the install kit to all adopters, where its "any SemVer in tracked artifact" heuristic would false-positive on adopter content (product versions, library versions, unrelated SemVer in their project docs). Pass C v1 fired in production on the v0.8.0 → v0.9.0 bump commit, flagging 18 tracked artifacts as "stale" — the vast majority were false positives (historical narrative references; frozen baselines).**

The recurring cadence #2 miss documented in [`d4f9a13`](../.stoa/beta_tracker.md) (v0.3.7), [`b485bbf9`](../.stoa/beta_tracker.md), and the 2026-05-26 instance was real. The escalation candidate `e358ce94` enumerated was real. But Pass C v1's specific MECHANISM was wrong-scope. Per CLAUDE.md §"Multi-adopter framing for install-kit analysis": *"frame analysis across the multi-adopter distribution surface — never narrowed to single-adopter assumptions based on this repo's dogfooded install."* AI's design didn't apply this discipline to the mechanism, only to the abstract escalation choice.

**What this rollback reverses:**

- Pass C hook block in `installkit/stoa.md` `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit` — removed; restored to single-Pass-A form.
- Slim §"Coherence cadence" #2 reference to Pass C as deterministic backstop — removed; cadence #2 returns to discipline-only.
- The spec-owned-blurb naming both Pass A and Pass C — reverted to Pass-A-only wording.

**What stays:**

- [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) — BETA-tag isolation rule in CLAUDE.md. Justified independently of Pass C; surfaced during Pass C design but doesn't depend on it.
- [`0780b922`](context_log.md#0780b922117545158beab900eb4cd23c--decision--2026-05-26) — Cadence #3 wording cleanup (no relation to Pass C).
- All Phase 2.A/2.B/2.C/2.D work — independent.

**What replaces Pass C v1 (in a sibling commit, not this one):**

- Sibling rollback [`d0b0adac`](context_log.md#d0b0adac4d7f4614a3d91856d99a13cf--rollback--2026-05-26) reverts [`cee78c99`](context_log.md#cee78c997cc54d1ea9b000c5113676fa--observation--2026-05-26) (Pass C tests aggregated observation), since the test scenarios themselves are being removed.
- Sibling decision [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26) lands the CLAUDE.md adopter-applicability discipline rule capturing the design-discipline lesson.
- Cadence #7 artifact-coherence nudge (planned, separate commit) — fills the discipline-side gap that Pass C v1 tried to mechanize.
- Wal-grounding rule (planned, separate session — see [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](../sketches/wal-grounding.md)) — Layer 1 of the two-layer reframing.

**Beta-tracker entry capturing the design lesson:** `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` entry `04e12001` (same hex as the CLAUDE.md decision since both lessons land together).

**What's accepted (the trade):**

- Cadence #2 has no deterministic backstop. Recurrence expected per [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) arc. Cadence #5 retrospective `/stoa audit` is the failure-recovery.
- The escalation ladder for cadence #2 stops at "AI discipline + nudge" rather than mechanical block. Not all cadences benefit from mechanical backstops; cadence #2 turns out to be one where the discipline IS the load-bearing mechanism.

**Refs:** [`1dcaa464`](context_log.md#1dcaa464c9c44ce69085dfb5e6e21604--decision--2026-05-26) (the entry this rolls back); [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) (sibling that survives); [`d0b0adac`](context_log.md#d0b0adac4d7f4614a3d91856d99a13cf--rollback--2026-05-26) (sibling test-observation rollback); [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26) (CLAUDE.md adopter-applicability discipline rule capturing the lesson); [`e358ce94`](context_log.md#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17) (the WAL-prescribed escalation that the v1 design honored at the choice-level but failed at the mechanism-level); [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (arc that predicts continued cadence #2 miss recurrence under discipline-only treatment); CLAUDE.md §"Multi-adopter framing for install-kit analysis" (the discipline AI failed to apply to the mechanism).

## 04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d — decision — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Add CLAUDE.md section: "Adopter-applicability discipline for mechanism design." Before landing any mechanism that ships to adopters via the install kit (hook scripts, dispatcher procedures, subagent probes, automatic checks, deterministic backstops), validate that the mechanism is defensible for typical adopter use — not just for the dogfood scenario in this repo. Enumerates four checks before landing: behavior in fresh adopter repo; behavior with unrelated adopter content; false-positive surface; whether the failure mode actually occurs in adopter usage.**

Surfaced by the Pass C v1 design error documented in beta-tracker entry `04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d` (same hex by deliberate choice — the rule-decision and the beta-tracker entry share scope). Pass C v1 passed Stoa-internal validation (WAL audit found `e358ce94`'s prescription; mechanism implemented correctly for dogfood case) but failed adopter framing — the "any SemVer in tracked artifact" heuristic produced false positives on adopter content (product versions, library versions, unrelated SemVer).

**Why CLAUDE.md, not slim spec.** CLAUDE.md is spec-author guidance — meta-discipline for editing the spec. Slim spec is operational surface for AI sessions across adopters. The adopter-applicability check is about HOW spec authors design mechanisms; it's not session-time AI behavior. CLAUDE.md is the right altitude. Sibling shape to §"Multi-adopter framing for install-kit analysis" — that section is about analyzing changes; this section is about designing mechanisms.

**Composition with existing disciplines.** Three disciplines apply to install-kit-shipped mechanism design; none subsumes the others:
- **WAL-grounding** (sketched in [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](../sketches/wal-grounding.md); ready to promote) — has AI consulted prior WAL decisions? Catches "did we already settle this?"
- **Multi-adopter framing** (existing CLAUDE.md section) — does analysis consider distribution surface? Catches "did we narrow to single-adopter framing?"
- **Adopter-applicability** (this entry's new section) — does the MECHANISM work in adopter context? Catches "does the implementation false-positive at adopter sites?"

Pass C v1 passed the first two and failed the third. All three required.

**Mechanism note.** New section in CLAUDE.md inserted between §"BETA tag is human-only" and §"Multi-adopter framing for install-kit analysis" — sibling placement, declarative-rule shape.

**Refs:** [`22b364ac`](context_log.md#22b364acec524f4e8eeaa52a40d78500--rollback--2026-05-26) (Pass C v1 design rollback that surfaced this lesson); [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) (BETA-tag rule, sibling CLAUDE.md addition; closed Pass C v1's only mechanical discriminator option and forced the design error to be structural); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline — note this entry edits CLAUDE.md not slim, so `b8d4e9c` doesn't strictly apply; the WAL entry shape is the same).
