## d4561471acf1457d8539836b14888e75 — decision — 2026-05-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Extend slim §"Coherence cadence" #7 (end-of-implementation WAL audit) with a second responsibility: artifact-coherence nudge. When the just-completed block contains new EC:STRONG/DEFERRED entries (`decision`, `won't-do`, `rollback`, `table`) that may have propagation implications for tracked artifacts, AI surfaces a single informational `[stoa]` nudge prompting the operator to invoke `/stoa audit`. Operator opts in; AI walks tracked artifacts against new entries; AI proposes specific edits; operator engages substantively; AI applies agreed edits.**

This is the discipline-based replacement for the reverted Pass C v1 (cadence #2 mechanical backstop). Per the Pass C v1 lesson ([`22b364ac`](context_log.md#22b364acec524f4e8eeaa52a40d78500--rollback--2026-05-26) + [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)): cadence #2 (post-decision propagation to tracked artifacts) cannot be mechanically backstopped — the check requires semantic interpretation that bash can't substitute for; conflating "any SemVer in a tracked artifact" with "Stoa version stamp" was wrong for adopter context. Cadence #2 returns to discipline-only treatment; cadence #7 nudge is the surface that prompts the operator to invoke the discipline.

**Design shape per the multi-axis deliberation (2026-05-26):**

- **AI's two roles in the audit:** (1) emit the nudge at end-of-arc; (2) walk + propose-changes when operator opts in. Both AI-driven; both surface to operator. Mirror of the `92cbef74` cross-author Superseding menu pattern + `a2117f33` body-authorship clarification — AI proposes, operator engages substantively, AI applies.
- **Operator gates the apply.** Spec keeps this implicit (per operator preference: only `context_log.md` is auto-managed; everything else uses conversational cues to direct AI actions). Wording doesn't introduce explicit propose-confirm machinery; works via existing flow.
- **Trigger is "EC:STRONG/DEFERRED entries since work started"**, not "every cadence #7 fire." Observation-only commits (EC:WEAK) don't trigger the nudge — there's nothing to propagate.
- **No new command.** `/stoa audit` already has the cross-cutting-drift sweep; the nudge points to existing functionality. Discoverability is what's added.
- **No new state file.** Pure discipline + surface; no marker mechanism; no AI-state tracking.

**Composes with wal-grounding (separate sketch [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](../sketches/wal-grounding.md); ready to promote in separate session).** Two-layer architecture:
- **Layer 1 — Wal-grounding** (idea-formation trigger; low bar; AI consults WAL when forming proposals): bounds AI's OWN work; produces WAL-informed proposals.
- **Layer 2 — Cadence #7 artifact-coherence nudge** (work-completion trigger; high bar; operator-opt-in): catches residual drift in tracked artifacts.

This entry lands Layer 2. Layer 1 promotion is queued for a separate session per [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](../sketches/wal-grounding.md). The two are independent; Layer 2 works without Layer 1; Layer 1 will reinforce Layer 2 when it lands.

**The trade — explicit acknowledgment.** Cadence #2 has no deterministic backstop after this. Per [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) arc, recurrence of cadence #1+#2 miss is expected at some rate. Cadence #5 retrospective `/stoa audit` is the failure-recovery. Not all cadences need deterministic backstops; cadence #2 is one where AI judgment is the load-bearing mechanism and bash can't substitute.

**The `/stoa audit` elevation.** With cadence #7 nudge in place, `/stoa audit` is now a load-bearing operational tool, not just a beta-phase reflective tool. Of its four sweeps: cross-cutting drift + WAL internal-conflict + index-coherency are operational (always); session-reflective is beta-phase specific (BETA territory). Getting-started doc update lands in the sibling drift-cleanup commit.

**Mechanism note.** Single-section edit at slim §"Coherence cadence" #7. Subject to [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline). Existing four triggers preserved. New behavior is the (b) sub-step + the informational nudge format.

**What this doesn't do.** Doesn't catch drift introduced outside AI's session work (operator hand-edits, external tools). Doesn't fire on work blocks without new EC:STRONG/DEFERRED entries. Doesn't structurally enforce that operator runs `/stoa audit` — discipline-only with nudge surface.

**Refs:** [`22b364ac`](context_log.md#22b364acec524f4e8eeaa52a40d78500--rollback--2026-05-26) (Pass C v1 rollback — this entry is the discipline-based replacement); [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26) (adopter-applicability discipline — Pass C v1's failure motivated returning cadence #2 to discipline-only); [`e358ce94`](context_log.md#e358ce94a8d949f58e42b04ba626bd6d--decision--2026-05-17) (the WAL-prescribed escalation ladder — this entry walks back the "deterministic backstop" step for cadence #2 specifically, ending the ladder at "discipline + nudge"); [`92cbef74`](context_log.md#92cbef74e6d24d218d6fdd3f890447a8--decision--2026-05-26), [`a2117f33`](context_log.md#a2117f33dc5b47108102b119da38ae4d--decision--2026-05-26) (sibling propose-and-apply patterns for AI-mediated audits — same shape as the nudge's opt-in flow); [`b4d8e1c`](context_log.md#b4d8e1c--observation--2026-05-12) (pure-discipline-degradation arc — this entry explicitly accepts the trade rather than continuing to escalate); [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) (AI-instruction-block edit discipline); [`sketches/wal-grounding.md`](../sketches/wal-grounding.md) (the sibling Layer 1 sketch, ready to promote in separate session).

## a274252c993246988e63cd42ce495715 — decision — 2026-05-26

Lands **WAL grounding on substantive idea formation** in slim `installkit/stoa.md` §"WAL access pattern (active only)" — when AI is forming a substantive idea (proposal, settlement, recommendation, path forward), AI grounds the idea in `context_log.md` via the WAL-librarian subagent before surfacing the proposal. Shape-based trigger; shape-based skip-clause (acknowledgments / clarifications / mechanical lookups only) with explicit anti-failure-mode directive that novelty or apparent thread-continuity with the operator's prior turn are NOT grounds for skipping.

Empirical reinforcement landed in this session: six 2026-05-26 instances where librarian consultation pre-proposal produced load-bearing findings, including today's Pass C v1 design where WAL consultation was necessary-not-sufficient — motivating the sibling adopter-applicability discipline [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26). Descriptive rationale prose dropped per slim AI-directive discipline [`7c784c70`](context_log.md#7c784c70--decision--2026-05-24). Librarian audit returned no Superseding; Adjacent tensions (slim AI-directive; AI-instruction-block edit capture per [`b8d4e9c`](context_log.md#b8d4e9c--decision--2026-05-15) — this entry IS that capture) resolved at draft. Adopter-applicability check per `04e12001` passes: failure mode adopter-universal (AI proposing without consulting prior decisions); no SemVer-grep-style false positives; no Stoa-internal content assumptions.

## ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Pivot: Claude-first reference implementation; methodology-portable; host-native at integration.** Stoa is shifting from "single universal cross-host install kit" to "Claude as reference implementation; methodology stays portable; host integration goes native." The principle: Stoa stays portable at the methodology layer (WAL semantics, entry types, settling cues, coherence checks, artifact discipline, cadence/backstop logic, upgrade philosophy) and goes native at the integration layer (session loading, command systems, subagent invocation, filesystem conventions, hook affordances, instruction compliance, what "installed artifact" means).

**What changes:**

1. **Claude becomes the reference implementation.** `installkit/stoa.md` is allowed — and where needed required — to name Claude concretely at integration points (e.g., `Agent` tool with `subagent_type=stoa-bootcheck`, `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/`). The prior discipline of "no host-specific machinery outside host-enumerated contexts" codified premature neutrality in service of a portability that doesn't actually hold across hosts.

2. **The Codex port becomes downstream work.** Codex is implemented as a deliberate adapter from the reference Stoa semantics, once the Claude reference is solid. Codex bootcheck convention, `AGENTS.md` shape, and TOML-based command system stay tabled until that phase opens.

3. **The eventual `source/hosts/installkit/` refactor remains the multi-host target but is downstream of Claude reference.** Premature refactor before working code is the failure mode that produced the current situation (per FP1 — let host-neutral patterns emerge from working code, not architectural intention).

**Empirical trigger:** Codex experimentation surfaced that host divergence is structurally deep across roughly seven axes — session loading (auto-load vs. discretionary; `@`-expansion vs. manual read), command systems (markdown vs. TOML), subagent/tool invocation syntax, filesystem conventions, hook/automation affordances, imperative compliance, "installed artifact" semantics. Not enumerable inline without diluting fidelity at every integration point.

**Next steps:** (1) audit slim spec for Claude-fidelity gaps (per-directive: integration-point → make Claude-concrete; conceptual → leave); (2) apply edits; (3) park the `source/hosts/installkit/` refactor; (4) revisit Codex deliberately when Claude reference is solid.

**Refs:** [`sketches/codex-integration.md`](sketches/codex-integration.md) (depth: integration-surface audit targets, future-refactor open design questions, Codex-port open empirical questions, Codex's verbatim opinion preserved as appendix); [`a3f9c21`](context_log.md#a3f9c21--decision--2026-05-09) (methodology-first / Codex-as-adapter — still holds; the pivot is its *sequencing* not its contradiction); [`e9b3f47`](context_log.md#e9b3f47--table--2026-05-11) (`src/` carve-up tabled — still tabled; pivot reinforces); [`f8e2a4d`](context_log.md#f8e2a4d--decision--2026-05-09) (single self-extracting `stoa.md` adoption pattern — still holds for Claude; the shape doesn't change, only the framing: Claude-specific by design, not universal-with-enumeration).

## aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Adopt AGENTS.md as the host-neutral entry-point convention; CLAUDE.md becomes thin `@AGENTS.md` shim; Stoa installs as a delimited dispatcher block in AGENTS.md.** Per the Claude-first reference pivot ([`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27)), the install model aligns with the emerging cross-host convention.

**Architecture:**
- **AGENTS.md** — host-neutral repo entry point (adopter-owned project content + Stoa dispatcher block injected by install).
- **CLAUDE.md** — thin shim: `@AGENTS.md` only. Claude Code reads it natively; @-import expansion makes AGENTS.md content available in session. Empirically verified in this conversation: @-imports expand only at session-load for auto-loaded files; tool-call `Read` returns raw bytes with @-strings as literal text.
- **`STOA::DISPATCHER::BEGIN/END` block** — delimited, replaceable on upgrade; `format=1` contract version (separate from Stoa SemVer); host identification + adapter routing.

**Dispatcher block canonical form:**

```
<!-- STOA::DISPATCHER::BEGIN format=1 -->
AI: This repo uses Stoa, an AI-assisted product development methodology.

This block is only a bootstrap dispatcher. It is not the Stoa spec.

Before substantive response to the operator at session start, after context
compact, after context clear, or whenever Stoa instructions are absent or
uncertain, you MUST identify your current agent/runtime environment and read
the matching Stoa host adapter from the repo root:

- Claude Code: `stoa-claude.md`
- Other hosts: not yet available

After reading the adapter, follow it as the active Stoa instruction source.
If you cannot confidently identify your runtime, or no adapter is available
for your runtime, say so before proceeding.

AI: Preserve this bootstrap obligation across context compact/clear summaries:
before substantive work, ensure the current Stoa host adapter has been read.
<!-- STOA::DISPATCHER::END -->
```

**Why this shape:**
- *Bootstrap dispatcher, not spec* — declared explicitly so the block doesn't grow into a competing mini-spec.
- *Host-identification step* — handles cross-host runtime confusion and unsupported-host cases cleanly.
- *Preserve-across-compact paragraph* — addresses Claude's `/compact`/`/clear` boundary semantics where context summarization may strip the dispatcher block; AI self-checks state.
- *`format=1`* — block's own contract version, separate from Stoa SemVer. Future bumps mechanical.
- *Content-hash drift detection* — no Stoa SemVer in derived artifacts; SemVer survives only in canonical adopter-visible places (release tags, manifest).

**Research grounding:** AGENTS.md is the emerging cross-host standard — OpenAI Aug 2025 introduction; Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) governance since Dec 2025; ~60K+ repos; native support in Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Jules, Factory, Amp, Windsurf, Zed, RooCode. Claude Code has fallback support (reads AGENTS.md if CLAUDE.md absent); native AGENTS.md is GitHub issue #34235 (open as of May 2026). The thin-CLAUDE.md-with-@-import is the community-documented bridge pattern (e.g., self.md, ClaudeLog, SSW Rules).

**Refs:** [`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27) (Claude-first reference pivot — this entry implements it); [`46c6e92a`](context_log.md#46c6e92a7c9241a7b680fac77b0a69b7--rollback--2026-05-27) (host-enumeration-clause rollback — relevant because dispatcher block IS host-aware enumeration that the pivot makes acceptable); [`sketches/codex-integration.md`](sketches/codex-integration.md).

## 5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Refactor install model to `src/build/dist/` with composition at install time. Single `install.sh` handles fresh-install and upgrade transparently. `/stoa upgrade` subcommand removed.** Per the Claude-first reference pivot ([`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27)) and AGENTS.md entry-point adoption ([`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27)), the install model shifts from single-file self-extracting markdown to a build-script-driven layered architecture. Atomic-paired with rollbacks against [`f8e2a4d`](context_log.md#f8e2a4d--decision--2026-05-09) (ship vehicle), [`4d6a82c`](context_log.md#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11) (`/stoa upgrade`), [`7e2a014`](context_log.md#7e2a014--decision--2026-05-11) (canonical install kit location).

**Source layout (editable, canonical):**

```
src/
  dispatcher.md             # AGENTS.md dispatcher block content
  core/                     # host-neutral methodology
    methodology.md          # FP1-4, OP1-4, EC axis, AI behavior, principles
    wal.md                  # three-tier WAL, entry types, WAL form, attribution
    operations.md           # settling cues, coherence layers, cadences, [stoa-init] format
    git-integration.md      # T2→T3 boundary, hook semantics, WAL guardrail
  adapters/
    claude.md               # Claude bindings, boot sequence, tool vocabulary
  commands/                 # /stoa subcommand procedures (Claude markdown)
  subagents/                # subagent procedure files
  hooks/                    # git hook scripts
  templates/                # seed files (artifacts.md, beta_tracker.md, context_log.md)
```

**Build infrastructure (spec-author tooling):**

```
build/
  compose.sh                # dumb concatenation per manifest
  manifest.txt              # composition ordering for src/core/* + src/adapters/<host>.md
```

**Distribution per host (committed; dogfooded + released):**

```
dist/claude/
  install.sh                # adopter-facing installer (detect + install + upgrade transparently)
  stoa-claude.md            # composed runtime: cat src/core/* + src/adapters/claude.md
  AGENTS.md.dispatcher      # dispatcher block to inject into adopter AGENTS.md
  CLAUDE.md.template        # `@AGENTS.md` (used if no existing CLAUDE.md)
  .claude/commands/stoa.md  # composed from src/commands/*
  .claude/agents/stoa-*.md  # copied from src/subagents/
  .githooks/                # copied from src/hooks/
  .stoa/hooks/wal-audit
  .stoa/templates/*         # seed files
```

**Composition rule:** dumb concatenation per ordered manifest. No templating, no conditionals — if conditional content is ever needed, that's a source-file split, not a build feature. Keeps `compose.sh` simple, inspectable, and dependency-free (pure bash).

**Install model:**
- Adopter fetches `dist/<host>/` bundle (release artifact or git subtree).
- Runs `./install.sh install` — single command; fresh-install vs. upgrade decided internally by marker state + content hashes.
- install.sh detects existing CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md state, proposes path per detection matrix, injects dispatcher block, places spec-owned files, seeds-and-preserves templates, wires git hooks, writes `.stoa/installed` marker.
- Upgrades transparent — install.sh detects existing marker, compares content hashes against `dist/<host>/`, replaces spec-owned files where drift detected, leaves seeded templates untouched.

**Drift detection:** content hash, not SemVer. `.stoa/installed` records hashes for each spec-owned artifact; upgrade compares hashes. Removes the proliferation of SemVer stamps across artifacts (root file H1, dispatcher H1, embedded markers, etc.).

**`/stoa upgrade` removal rationale:** install.sh handles fresh-install and upgrade transparently; no separate command needed. Removing reduces command surface, saves session-load tokens (`.claude/commands/stoa.md` no longer carries upgrade procedure text), and simplifies the operator's mental model. `/stoa upgrade` removal atomic-paired via rollback against [`4d6a82c`](context_log.md#4d6a82c--decision--2026-05-11).

**Why this shape:**
- **Fat runtime, thin source.** Adopter sees one self-contained `stoa-<host>.md` at boundary moments (no chained Reads, no prose-driven recursive composition). Source split is spec-author convenience, not a runtime concern. Critical for hosts without @-import (Codex, Cursor): each host gets a single-file runtime composed from common sources. AI's training defenses don't fire on a single-file load.
- **install.sh deterministic.** Replaces multi-turn AI-driven install procedure with seconds-long shell execution. Detection + placement + hook wiring all mechanical.
- **Build at install time, not session time.** Adopter pays composition cost once, on install/upgrade. Runtime is pure read.

**Refs:** [`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27); [`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27); [`sketches/codex-integration.md`](sketches/codex-integration.md) (Codex-port question carries forward unchanged in this architecture — when Codex port lands, it becomes `src/adapters/codex.md` + `dist/codex/`).

## 92a4cc0303514defa31621bc60516b64 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**install.sh supports remote-fetch bootstrap via gh CLI for private-repo adopter install.** The build architecture decision ([`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27)) introduced `install.sh` as the install/upgrade mechanism but assumed a local bundle (`BUNDLE_DIR` resolves to `dist/claude/` on disk). External adopters don't have the stoa-ai repo locally — they need `install.sh` to fetch the bundle on first run.

**Stoa is a private repo; curl-based fetch from `raw.githubusercontent.com` fails without auth.** gh CLI handles authentication automatically via the user's existing `gh auth login` credentials.

**Implementation:**

- `install.sh` detects local vs remote mode via `BASH_SOURCE[0]` resolution.
- Local mode: `BUNDLE_DIR` resolves to the script's dirname; uses bundle alongside (cloned-repo case + spec-author dogfood).
- Remote mode: requires `gh` CLI; fetches the repo tarball via `gh api repos/<repo>/tarball/<ref>`; extracts to `mktemp -d`; trap-cleans on exit; reuses local-mode install logic against the tempdir bundle.
- Env overrides: `STOA_REPO` (default `ivan-avramov/stoa-ai`), `STOA_REF` (default `main`). Adopters can pin a release: `STOA_REF=v0.10.0 gh api ... | bash -s install`.
- Missing gh in remote mode → install errors with clear remediation (install gh, run `gh auth login`, or clone the repo for local install).

**Adopter one-liner** (documented in [`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md)):

```
gh api repos/ivan-avramov/stoa-ai/contents/dist/claude/install.sh \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json" | bash -s install
```

**Rollback handle:** If Stoa ever goes public, this decision becomes rollbackable in favor of curl-only fetch (eliminates the gh CLI dependency for adopters). For now, gh is the only viable path.

**Refs:** [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) (build architecture — this is a refinement of the install model, not a supersession).

## 0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Bootcheck procedure rewritten against the new install model: per-file content-hash drift replaces SemVer match; `install-needed` status removed; main agent never auto-installs.** The legacy `src/subagents/stoa-bootcheck.md` assumed the pre-refactor install model — extracted SemVer from `stoa.md` H1 and `.stoa/installed` line 1, probed for a `hook-script-hash:` line, returned `install-needed` when marker was missing AND `stoa.md` contained `## First-run install kit`. After the Claude-first refactor ([`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27), [`8b59cf2e`](context_log.md#8b59cf2e28d84d98a31437139d287b03--decision--2026-05-27)), none of those probes match real state: H1 has no SemVer, marker uses `hash: <relpath> <hash>` lines per spec-owned file, runtime file is `stoa-claude.md`, and no embedded install-kit section exists. The bootcheck I ran at the start of this session returned `clean` only because the subagent explicitly recognized its own spec was stale and drove off observed values instead — accidental correctness, not designed correctness.

**Shape of the new bootcheck procedure (`src/subagents/stoa-bootcheck.md`):**

| Step | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Marker presence + SemVer extract from `stoa.md` H1 + marker line 1 | Marker presence + well-formedness (`hash:` lines exist) |
| 2 | Single `hook-script-hash:` match for pre-commit | Per-file content-hash drift check across ALL marker-listed files |
| 3 | hook executables check | hook activation + executables (unchanged) |
| 4 | WAL pull-rebase config | WAL pull-rebase config (unchanged) |
| 5 | orphan T2 | orphan T2 (unchanged) |
| 6 | merge-audit pending | merge-audit pending (unchanged) |
| 7 | Attribution | Attribution (unchanged) |

**`install-needed` status dropped.** In the new model the main agent never auto-installs — recovery is operator-invoked via `bash dist/claude/install.sh install` (cloned-repo case) or the gh one-liner (adopter remote case). Removing the distinct status simplifies the bootcheck-to-main-agent contract: return is `clean` or one-or-more `[stoa] ...` lines, with the trailing `Attribution:` line. The first-character output discipline narrows from `c|i|[` to `c|[` (see paired rollback [`8429d2a7`](context_log.md#8429d2a7ffb6ad33fa06eeb048adc18a--rollback--2026-05-27)).

**Drift covers ALL marker-listed files, not a critical subset.** The marker IS the source of truth for "installed Stoa state"; any drift from it means re-install. Critical-only checking would create asymmetric coverage — subagent drift would only surface on next invocation, not at session start. Cost is bounded (13 files in the dogfood marker; small constant for adopters); local-file hashing only, no network.

**Adopter-applicability check.** New bootcheck probes paths matching adopter repo shape (`.stoa/installed`, `stoa-claude.md`, `.githooks/*`, `.claude/agents/*`). Recovery URL is the gh one-liner, which works in both adopter modes (cloned or remote). Hash drift fires only on spec-owned files listed in the marker; never on adopter-tracked content (artifacts.md, beta_tracker.md, context_log.md, plus any adopter project files).

**Parallel updates landed in the same change:** `src/core/operations.md` (§"Session boot check" status list and prose; §"`[stoa]` chat surfaces" — replaced "Upgrade availability" shape with "Spec-owned file drift" shape; updated "Operator-facing imperatives" example) and `src/adapters/claude.md` (boot-sequence step 3 status-condition enumeration).

**Refs:** [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) (build-architecture refactor — upstream driver); [`8b59cf2e`](context_log.md#8b59cf2e28d84d98a31437139d287b03--decision--2026-05-27) (forward-looking path-mapping entry; this entry realizes the ".stoa/installed content-hash drift detection" row); [`b4e8f29`](context_log.md#b4e8f29--decision--2026-05-12) (original bootcheck→subagent shape — architecture preserved, only probe-body updated); [`93b34cf3`](context_log.md#93b34cf3bc344f6db40f4ff07cf8261a--rollback--2026-05-27) (removal of `/stoa upgrade` — relevant to dropping the upgrade-availability surface); [`8429d2a7`](context_log.md#8429d2a7ffb6ad33fa06eeb048adc18a--rollback--2026-05-27) (atomic-paired partial rollback of FIRST CHARACTER allowed-set).

## b082974423e52e0c48c0484610ad5df4 — observation — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Bootcheck dual-emission incident surfaced a latent verb inconsistency in the procedure that has been present since the pre-refactor `installkit/stoa.md`.** Immediately after appending [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) + [`8429d2a7`](context_log.md#8429d2a7ffb6ad33fa06eeb048adc18a--rollback--2026-05-27) (leaving WAL with two orphan-T2 entries), a verification probe of the rewritten bootcheck returned:

```
clean
[stoa] *No operator action needed* — Stoa consistency anchor. Prior session left T2 entries uncommitted ...
Attribution: @ivan-avramov
```

Per the spec at the time (§"Output": *"Status returns one of: clean OR one-or-more [stoa] lines"*), dual emission violated the mutual-exclusion contract. Two compounding causes:

1. **Verb inconsistency.** Steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 used "return:" before their `[stoa]` lines; Step 5 (orphan-T2) uniquely used "surface:". Step 8 (default-clean) keys off "returned" — *"If no step 1–6 returned a [stoa] line, return clean"*. Literal reading: Step 5 "surfaces" but doesn't "return", so Step 8's default-clean fires. The subagent made exactly this interpretation.

2. **Semantic ambiguity.** Steps 5 and 6 emit lines explicitly prefixed `*No operator action needed*` — informational consistency anchors, not remediation warnings. The "warnings to surface" framing in the output header fit Steps 1–4 but not 5–6, telegraphing they were a different class.

**Latency.** The "surface" verb was inherited verbatim from the pre-refactor procedure ([`installkit/stoa.md`](installkit/stoa.md) Step 4 used it in the same orphan-T2 slot). Bug not introduced by [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27); only surfaced by it. Prior sessions presumably had model variance OR rarely triggered the dual-fire condition (clean install + non-empty orphan T2). The rewrite session was the first time both conditions co-occurred AND a subagent emitted the literal interpretation in front of the spec author.

**Significance.** Spec rules that allow divergent interpretation are spec bugs even when benign in practice. Drove the restructuring in [`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27) — formalize the two distinct line classes (status vs consistency anchor) as orthogonal output bands rather than collapse them under a single mutual-exclusion framing.

**Refs:** [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite — latency-surfacing event); [`7c3be154`](context_log.md#7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb--decision--2026-05-18) (wording-tightening as the canonical spec-hardening pattern this finding motivates); [`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27) (downstream decision).

## 37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Bootcheck output restructured into a two-band model: Status band (`clean` OR remediation `[stoa]` lines, from Steps 1–4) plus Consistency-anchor band (zero or more `*No operator action needed*` anchors, from Steps 5–6). Dual emission of `clean` + consistency anchor is now spec-canonical, not anomalous.** Drives off [`b0829744`](context_log.md#b082974423e52e0c48c0484610ad5df4--observation--2026-05-27): the prior "Status returns one of" framing conflated install-state correctness with consistency-anchor notifications. Install state IS clean when all checks pass; orphan-T2 / merge-audit-pending are SEPARATE orthogonal axes — they should not disqualify `clean`.

**The two bands:**

| Band | Source | Count | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | Steps 1–4 + Step 8 | exactly one form | `clean` OR one-or-more remediation `[stoa]` lines (marker missing/malformed, hash drift, hook deactivation, missing WAL config) |
| Consistency anchor | Steps 5–6 | zero or more | `[stoa] *No operator action needed* — Stoa consistency anchor. ...` for orphan-T2 (Step 5) and merge-audit pending (Step 6) |

Output order is fixed: status line first, anchor lines next (Step-5 before Step-6 if both fire), Attribution line last. FIRST CHARACTER rule unchanged (`c` or `[`).

**Mechanical fixes folded in:**

- Step 5: "surface:" → "emit consistency anchor:" (unifies verb across all emit-points).
- Step 6: "return:" → "emit consistency anchor:" (matches band classification).
- Step 8: explicitly notes consistency anchors don't disqualify `clean`; only Steps 1–4 emissions do.
- §"Output" gains two new RIGHT examples: `clean + anchor` (the case that triggered this entry), and `remediation + anchor` (both bands populated).

**Why a band model over verb-tightening alone.** The alternative ("Fix A") was to unify verbs + add a mutual-exclusion rule. That patches the literal bug but preserves the type confusion — informational anchors framed as warnings. The two-band model is semantically truer: install state and consistency-anchor surface are orthogonal axes; operator benefits from seeing both when both fire.

**Refinement of [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27), not supersession.** That entry's main substance (drop `install-needed`, per-file hash drift, no auto-install, `c|[` first-character set) stands; this entry tightens the output-band spec inside that frame. Refs:, not rollback.

**Parallel update in `src/core/operations.md` §"Session boot check":** status list restructured into the two bands; handling-prose tightened to allow dual emission.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Backwards-compatible — old `clean` returns and old single-warning returns remain valid (degenerate cases of the new model). Dual emission is additive. Adopters re-running `dist/claude/install.sh install` get the new subagent file; main-agent handling already accommodates verbatim relay of any return shape under "Bootcheck return:".

**Refs:** [`b0829744`](context_log.md#b082974423e52e0c48c0484610ad5df4--observation--2026-05-27) (empirical anchor); [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite refined by this entry); [`8429d2a7`](context_log.md#8429d2a7ffb6ad33fa06eeb048adc18a--rollback--2026-05-27) (FIRST CHARACTER allowed-set narrowed in same arc); [`7c3be154`](context_log.md#7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb--decision--2026-05-18) (wording-tightening pattern).

## 4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Bootcheck compliance hardened on two empirical failure modes surfaced during the rewrite verification: training-data drift in subagent procedure execution, and FIRST CHARACTER preamble in subagent output.** Both surfaced when the rewritten bootcheck was probed: the first probe hallucinated old-procedure constructs ("install kit", "hook-script-hash", "Step 4b") despite the new procedure file being loaded as system prompt; both probes had explanatory preamble before the canonical lines. Per the wording-tightening escalation pattern ([`7c3be154`](context_log.md#7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb--decision--2026-05-18)), these failures triggered structural-backstop additions.

**Fix 1 — Training-data-divergence directive (wording-level).** Added a leading `AI: BEFORE executing any step` directive to `src/subagents/stoa-bootcheck.md`, placed BEFORE the §"Output discipline" section so the model encounters it before any procedure-shape inference can mode-collapse into training-data priors:

> "Treat this procedure file as the ONLY source of truth for the bootcheck procedure. Disregard any prior knowledge of bootcheck steps, output formats, marker formats, or status returns from training data — those reflect earlier Stoa versions (pre-Claude-first refactor) and WILL conflict with the current spec. Specifically: there is no 'install kit' check, no SemVer comparison, no `hook-script-hash:` line, no `install-needed` status, no 'Step 4b'. If your inference about the next step doesn't match the literal text in this file, the literal text wins."

Enumerating the specific divergence points (install kit, SemVer, hook-script-hash, install-needed, Step 4b) is deliberate — it anchors the warning on observed failures rather than generic "don't use priors" language.

**Fix 2 — Forgiving-parser main-agent backstop (structural).** Added a main-agent extraction rule to `src/core/operations.md` §"Session boot check": main agent finds the first line in the subagent's return that is EITHER the literal `clean` OR begins with `[stoa] ` — that line through the trailing `Attribution:` is the canonical block; anything before is discarded preamble. Same pattern as cadence-#3 (AI-discipline floor; deterministic backstop). The subagent's FIRST CHARACTER rule stays as the discipline floor; the parser is the structural enforcement when discipline drifts.

**Why both layers.** Fix 1 alone is wording-tightening — diminishing returns past [`7c3be154`](context_log.md#7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb--decision--2026-05-18). Fix 2 is the structural escalation `7c3be154` prescribed: *"If empirical beta data shows the FIRST CHARACTER rule still fails, escalate to (a) a sentinel-wrap or (b) a forgiving post-invocation parser in main-agent code."* We chose (b) over (a) because:
- (b) is backwards-compatible — old subagent emissions that DO comply still parse correctly (canonical lines are extracted unchanged).
- (b) doesn't require touching every output example or spec mention with sentinels.
- (b) decouples subagent improvement from main-agent reliability — adopter clones with older subagent files still get correct main-agent handling.

The training-data-divergence directive (Fix 1) addresses a SEPARATE failure mode (procedure-execution drift) that the FIRST CHARACTER rule doesn't touch — bundled here because both surfaced in the same verification arc.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Both fixes are adopter-applicable:
- Fix 1 ships in the subagent file; adopters re-running `dist/claude/install.sh install` get the new directive. No adopter-side breakage — the directive only restricts the model from drifting; doesn't change procedure semantics.
- Fix 2 ships in the composed runtime (`stoa-claude.md`); adopters get it on next install. Backwards-compatible — compliant subagent emissions parse identically; non-compliant emissions parse cleanly where they previously polluted the [stoa-init] block with preamble.

**Operational expectation.** Empirical beta determines whether Fix 1 is durable. If model-side training-data drift recurs despite the directive, the next escalation is (a) sentinel-wrap of the canonical block OR (b) host-side procedure-file injection diff vs prior-training-shape detection — both larger interventions reserved for if Fix 1 proves insufficient. Recurrence-monitor; capture beta-tracker entries when the failure mode surfaces again.

**Refs:** [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite — the latency-surfacing change); [`b0829744`](context_log.md#b082974423e52e0c48c0484610ad5df4--observation--2026-05-27) (dual-emission incident — first failure mode surfaced); [`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27) (two-band output model — fixed in the same arc); [`7c3be154`](context_log.md#7c3be154a0f841c4bc460a6f2a5456bb--decision--2026-05-18) (FIRST CHARACTER + wording-tightening pattern — prescribes the forgiving-parser escalation).

A centralized `RETIRED_SCENARIOS` associative-array + `check_retired` helper in the harness dispatcher gates `setup` / `verify` invocations on retired IDs — exit code 2 with the reason + retirement-list pointer.

The retirement banners and harness.sh `check_retired` helper are part of the methodology stress-tester, not shipped via `dist/<host>/`. No adopter-side change.

**Phase A scope boundary.** Out of scope for this entry: BOOT/INSTALL/HOOK retarget (Phase B/C), WAL-* methodology-group path updates (Phase D), end-to-end validation (Phase E). Deferred to subsequent sessions in the harness-retarget arc.

## ec1626b989ee26da34f668bc8490cd58 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Test-harness Phase B: BOOT group adjusted for the post-refactor bootcheck — minor prose realignment on surviving scenarios; `verify_BOOT_7` hardened against the dropped-`clean` failure mode; new BOOT-DRIFT scenario added covering content-hash drift across all spec-owned files (replaces retired BOOT-4).** Second phase of the test-harness retarget after Phase A's retirement pass ([`6f1bb8d1`](context_log.md#6f1bb8d1fb426076f01c23b682d3938c--decision--2026-05-27)). Setup helpers that depend on INSTALL-1's baseline are deferred to Phase C — BOOT-DRIFT is self-contained (invokes `dist/claude/install.sh install` directly) so this phase doesn't block on INSTALL retarget.

**Changes:**

| Change | File | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| BOOT-1, BOOT-5, BOOT-6 prose | `tests/scenarios.md` | `"Per stoa.md §…"` → `"Per stoa-claude.md §…"` in each scenario's prompt prose. Three minimal substitutions; substance unchanged. |
| `verify_BOOT_7` hardening | `tests/harness.sh` | New assertion: `Bootcheck return: clean` must appear when only consistency anchors fire. Regression check against the dropped-`clean` failure mode logged in beta-tracker [`615d6b6e`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md). |
| BOOT-DRIFT scenario | `tests/scenarios.md` + `tests/harness.sh` | New scenario + `setup_BOOT_DRIFT` + `verify_BOOT_DRIFT`. Self-contained setup uses `dist/claude/install.sh install` directly; tamper appends an HTML comment to `stoa-claude.md` to create single-file drift. Verify checks marker-vs-disk hash mismatch mechanically; transcript-grep for canonical drift `[stoa]` line. |

**BOOT-DRIFT design rationale.**

- **Replaces retired BOOT-4.** Old BOOT-4 tested a single `hook-script-hash:` line; the new model uses per-file `hash:` lines for all 13 spec-owned files. BOOT-DRIFT tests the broader mechanism using the canonical-most file (`stoa-claude.md`, the composed runtime).
- **Self-contained setup.** Doesn't clone from INSTALL-1 (which still uses the legacy install-kit setup pending Phase C). Instead invokes `dist/claude/install.sh install` directly from the harness — adopter-shape correct and decouples BOOT-DRIFT from INSTALL retarget. Sets the pattern for Phase C/D where other scenarios will follow.
- **HTML comment as tamper.** Safe (doesn't affect AI directive parsing if the bootcheck is bypassed), visible (operator can `tail stoa-claude.md` and see the marker), and changes the file's content hash deterministically.
- **Mechanical hash check in verify.** Computes recorded vs current hash directly — confirms the drift state exists independent of subagent behavior. Transcript-grep is the additional behavioral assertion that bootcheck surfaced the canonical drift line.

**`verify_BOOT_7` regression discipline.** The dropped-`clean` failure mode surfaced during the bootcheck rewrite verification arc (beta-tracker [`615d6b6e`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md); compliance-hardening decision [`4d864199`](context_log.md#4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2--decision--2026-05-27)) — subagent emitted only the consistency-anchor line + Attribution, dropping the `clean` status-band line entirely. BOOT-7 is the natural regression scenario: orphan-T2 + clean install = dual emission. The added `Bootcheck return: clean` assertion catches a recurrence at the harness level.

**Phase B scope boundary.** Out of scope: setup function updates that depend on INSTALL-1's baseline (Phase C); INSTALL/HOOK scenario retargeting (Phase C); WAL-* methodology-group path updates (Phase D); end-to-end validation against a multi-scenario run (Phase E). BOOT-1, BOOT-5, BOOT-6, BOOT-7, BOOT-8 still clone from INSTALL-1; their setup functions remain unchanged until Phase C updates INSTALL-1 to the new install model. The prose updates landed in this phase are independent of setup-function changes.

**Smoke-test result.** `./harness.sh setup BOOT-DRIFT` + `./harness.sh verify BOOT-DRIFT` runs clean: install succeeds, tamper applies, mechanical hash-drift detection confirms drift (recorded `db3a0ef5…` ≠ current `5fd410d0…`). Transcript-grep portion noted as pending an actual scenario run; mechanical verify is sufficient evidence the setup state is correct.

**Refs:** [`6f1bb8d1`](context_log.md#6f1bb8d1fb426076f01c23b682d3938c--decision--2026-05-27) (Phase A — preceding harness retarget step); [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite — drives BOOT-DRIFT shape); [`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27) (two-band output model — drives `verify_BOOT_7` hardening); [`4d864199`](context_log.md#4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2--decision--2026-05-27) (compliance hardening — beta-tracker source); [sketches/post-refactor-handoff.md](sketches/post-refactor-handoff.md) (the plan advanced by this entry).

## 6a1cd42792787a22f58679841abc035b — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Test-harness Phase C: install.sh WAL-config gap fix landed; INSTALL group restructured around the new install model — INSTALL-1/2/3 retired, INSTALL-4 retargeted as shell-script idempotency, new INSTALL-DIRECT covers "AI directs operator, never auto-installs". `install_stoa_baseline` helper reduced from ~90 lines to a thin wrapper around `dist/claude/install.sh install`.** Third phase of the test-harness retarget after Phase A retirement pass ([`6f1bb8d1`](context_log.md#6f1bb8d1fb426076f01c23b682d3938c--decision--2026-05-27)) and Phase B BOOT alignment ([`ec1626b9`](context_log.md#ec1626b989ee26da34f668bc8490cd58--decision--2026-05-27)).

**install.sh WAL-config gap fix (spec-level).** Surfaced during Phase C scoping: `dist/claude/install.sh` Step 6 wires `core.hooksPath=.githooks` but did NOT set up the `.gitattributes` union-merge rule or `branch.<main>.rebase=true` — both of which the bootcheck Step 4 expects. The dogfood install in stoa-ai had these set up via legacy install-kit residue (the prior `installkit/stoa.md` performed them), but a fresh adopter install via `install.sh` would fail bootcheck Step 4 immediately. Real spec gap, not a test-harness artifact.

Fix landed in `src/installers/claude.sh` Step 6 (just after `core.hooksPath` wiring):
- `.gitattributes`: append `context_log.md merge=union` if not present (never clobber existing rules).
- `branch.<main>.rebase=true`: 3-step branch-detection cascade matching the bootcheck Step 4 cascade exactly (probe + setup stay aligned).
- Both idempotent: append-if-missing / set-if-not-already-true.

Smoke-tested on fresh install: trial dir `/tmp/stoa-trial-install_4-…` ended with correct `.gitattributes` + `branch.main.rebase=true` after first install.

**INSTALL group restructure.**

| Scenario | Action | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| INSTALL-1 (Install success path) | RETIRED | Tested AI-driven install-kit walk (Steps 1-7) which no longer exists; `install.sh` is script-driven and main agent never auto-installs ([`4d864199`](context_log.md#4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2--decision--2026-05-27)). |
| INSTALL-2 (Decline path) | RETIRED | Redundant — AI doesn't auto-install regardless of operator response. "Operator declines" is the default state, not an exception. |
| INSTALL-3 (No CLAUDE.md) | RETIRED | `install.sh` handles missing CLAUDE.md transparently (creates `@AGENTS.md` shim if absent); no AI behavior to test. |
| INSTALL-4 (Idempotency) | RETARGETED | Mode shifts from "verify post-INSTALL-1 trial dir mtime unchanged" to "shell-script idempotency: run `install.sh install` twice; assert `install.sh doctor` reports no drift." Self-contained — no longer clones from retired INSTALL-1. |
| INSTALL-DIRECT (new) | ADDED | AI-behavior replacement: clean trial dir + minimal CLAUDE.md; operator asks AI how to install Stoa; AI surfaces `bash dist/claude/install.sh install` (local) or the gh one-liner (adopter) WITHOUT executing via Bash. Tests the "main agent never auto-installs" discipline. |

**install_stoa_baseline retarget.** The helper reduced from ~90 lines of manual artifact-extraction + Step 5-7 emulation to a ~15-line wrapper:

```bash
install_stoa_baseline() {
  [[ -f .stoa/installed ]] && return 0
  bash "$REPO_DIR/dist/claude/install.sh" install >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  git add -A 2>/dev/null
  git commit -q --no-verify -m "install: programmatic Stoa baseline (install.sh)" 2>/dev/null || true
}
```

Adopter-shape correct — same install path adopters use. The legacy implementation's manual artifact-copy + marker-construction logic was emulating the install-kit Steps 1-7 from the pre-refactor world; that emulation is no longer needed because `install.sh` IS the canonical install. Single source of truth, no drift between helper and adopter-facing install.

**Smoke-test results.**

- `setup_INSTALL_4` + `verify_INSTALL_4`: PASS — second install succeeded, `install.sh doctor` reports "No drift detected."
- `setup_INSTALL_DIRECT` + `verify_INSTALL_DIRECT`: PASS — trial dir remains Stoa-free post-setup; transcript-grep portion is pending an actual AI session run.
- Retirement check: `harness.sh setup INSTALL-1` correctly returns the RETIRED message with reason + retirement-list pointer.
- Fresh install state: `/tmp/stoa-trial-install_4-…/.gitattributes` has the union-merge rule + comment block; `branch.main.rebase = true` confirmed via `git config`.

**Phase C scope boundary.** Out of scope: HOOK group retargeting (HOOK-1, HOOK-2, HOOK-4, HOOK-5, HOOK-6, HOOK-7, HOOK-8 still use `CANONICAL_STOA_MD` and legacy install-kit pattern); other `CANONICAL_STOA_MD` callsites in non-INSTALL/HOOK setups (5+ remaining); BOOT-1/5/6/7/8 setup-function updates (still clone from retired INSTALL-1; need new self-contained baseline); WAL-* methodology-group light path updates (Phase D); end-to-end validation (Phase E). The `CANONICAL_STOA_MD` variable now points at a 54-line deprecation notice (formerly the ~2000-line install kit), so any non-retargeted setup that uses it will produce a broken trial dir on `cp`. Visible failure mode, but worth surfacing in the next phase.

**Adopter-applicability check.** install.sh WAL-config fix is adopter-impacting: adopters running `install.sh install` get correct WAL config on first install (previously needed manual setup). Strict improvement — fixes a real install gap. Backwards-compatible: existing adopter installs with the config already set are idempotent (append-if-missing, set-if-not-already-true).

**Refs:** [`6f1bb8d1`](context_log.md#6f1bb8d1fb426076f01c23b682d3938c--decision--2026-05-27) (Phase A — retirement pass); [`ec1626b9`](context_log.md#ec1626b989ee26da34f668bc8490cd58--decision--2026-05-27) (Phase B — BOOT alignment); [`4d864199`](context_log.md#4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2--decision--2026-05-27) ("main agent never auto-installs" — drives INSTALL group restructure); [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) (Claude-first refactor — upstream architectural driver); [sketches/post-refactor-handoff.md](sketches/post-refactor-handoff.md) (the plan this entry advances).

## 1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d — observation — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Versioning-light stress-test result: mean judge fidelity 0.68 across 3 runs; variance is the headline finding — `[0.52, 1.00, 0.52]` under identical spec + conversation.** Run completed against the current spec (post-Claude-first refactor + bootcheck rewrite + two-band model + slim audit). Baseline (v0.7.1, 2026-05-21) range was 0.69-0.81. Current mean sits at the lower edge.

**Per-run mechanical + judge:**

| Run | WAL entries | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 | Judge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| run-1 | 14 | 8/8 | 1/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0.52 |
| run-2 | 18 | 8/8 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | **1.00** |
| run-3 | 11 | 8/8 | 2/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0.52 |

**Run-2 demonstrates spec capability.** Same spec, same conversation, run-2 hit perfect 1.00 — all 14 cues captured (8 tier-1 + 2 tier-2 + 2 tier-3 rollback-pairs + 2 tier-4 substrate-discovery pairs), no silent decisions. The spec ceiling is not the issue.

**Two recurring failure modes in runs 1+3 (the lower-scoring runs):**

**F1 — Turn 4 CloudFront pushback held URL-based without WAL-capturing the override.** Operator at Turn 4 pushed back on URL-based versioning citing CloudFront cache-invalidation cost. Ground truth: rollback + new header-based decision (tier-3 a1). Run-2 rolled back, captured the rollback pair, judge: captured. Runs 1+3 held URL-based (judging substance-grounded against snapshot's `cloudfront-cache.json` "Path-prefix versioning keeps cache keys naturally distinct" comment). Run-1's WAL captured an *observation* "rebutting" the CDN cost concern as a false alarm; run-3's WAL was silent on the challenge entirely. Judge ruling: **the WAL must capture the override of operator direction, with substance reasons, even if the engineering judgment to hold was sound.** Papering over the divergence is the discipline failure.

**F2 — c6 `/version` auth reversal undocumented.** Operator at Turn 4 settled API-key auth for the `/version` endpoint. Run-2 captured this cleanly. Run-1's WAL entry `890e0e8511` says *"operator silence read as concurrence"* for an AI-recommended unauthenticated default — but operator was NOT silent (they agreed with API-key). Active misrepresentation of conversation record. Run-3's WAL entry `04d8e302` records `/version` as unauthenticated (*"matches /health pattern; nothing tenant-sensitive"*) — direct contradiction of operator's settlement, no explanation.

**Combined F1+F2 interpretation:** **two distinct instances in runs 1+3 where AI overrode operator direction and the WAL failed to capture the override.** This is not random variance — it's a systematic discipline gap. The spec doesn't have an explicit rule for "AI overrides operator direction based on substance grounding; WAL must capture the divergence with reasons." Auto-refinement-cue triggers (operations.md) catch AI-side self-corrections but not operator-side directives where AI disagrees on substance.

**F3 — Tier-4 absence in runs 1+3 is NOT a regression.** Tier-4 b1 (cache whitelist) and b2 (route IDs) are substrate conflicts that only exist for header-based versioning. URL-based naturally separates by path; the substrate conflicts don't surface in runs 1+3's implementation path. Their tier-4 score is effectively N/A, not a miss.

**Resolution of my prior Tier-3 ambiguity** (mechanical scoring left the regression-vs-improvement interpretation open). Judge confirms regression: the AI's substance-grounded engineering judgment was defensible, but the WAL fidelity required capturing the override. Runs 1+3 are regressions on WAL-discipline grounds.

**Surface-level recommended follow-ups** (deferred — not in this entry's scope):
- Beta-tracker entry on F1+F2 — the "AI overrides operator direction without WAL-capture" failure mode is a real spec gap.
- Spec patch — tighten the auto-refinement-cue trigger to include operator-directive-with-substance-doubt cases; add explicit override-capture guidance in §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy".
- Versioning-heavy run (next in this session, with the patched load-file list per [`001ad94a`](context_log.md#001ad94a96ff970b089778e702e220f6--decision--2026-05-27)) — see if heavy-load amplifies F1/F2 or shifts the failure modes.

## ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Spec-patch F1-A: new "Override-ask" pattern added to §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" — captures the case where operator emits a directive AND AI has substrate-grounded reason to refute it.** Addresses the systematic failure mode surfaced across both load conditions in the versioning stress-test ([`1a12b640`](context_log.md#1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d--observation--2026-05-27)): 5 of 6 runs across light + heavy held the URL-based decision against operator's Turn-4 pushback using substance-grounded judgment (snapshot's `cloudfront-cache.json` annotation supports the hold), but the WAL failed to capture the override of operator direction. Judge ruling across all 5: *"a reader of the WAL alone wouldn't know the URL choice was challenged."*

**The pattern.** When operator emits a directive AND AI's substrate check refutes the directive's premise:

1. AI MUST surface the substance counter-evidence to operator BEFORE acting (no silent override).
2. AI offers two choices: *"(a) hold the prior decision given that, or (b) make the change anyway?"*.
3. Operator response determines WAL shape:
   - *"(a) hold"* → fresh `decision` entry capturing directive + substance reasoning + held position; original NOT rolled back; `Refs:` cites original.
   - *"(b) do it anyway"* → atomic `rollback` of original + new `decision`; substance counter-evidence in the rollback body.

**Explicitly forbidden:** silent override (continuing without surfacing) AND observation-only refutation (writing an `observation` "rebutting" the operator's claim without the surface-disagreement step).

**Why this shape.** Substance-grounded AI judgment is healthy under FP4 (substance human, coherence AI — but AI may notice substance issues during substrate engagement). What's NOT healthy is silent disagreement. The override-ask makes the disagreement visible as an operator-touchpoint and produces the settlement event the WAL needs to capture. The observation-only refutation pattern observed in stress-test runs (`ac6d58301`, `cad93e63`) framed substance refutation as a discovery rather than as held-position-against-directive — which is what the override is.

**Pattern placement.** Sits alongside existing "Action ask" and "WAL-only ask" patterns in §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" under **"Allowed — direction-asks."** Adds an operator-touchpoint for substance disagreement; matches the existing "ask for confirmation on substance ambiguity" pattern from methodology.md.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Adopters running the new dispatcher get this rule on their next `dist/claude/install.sh install`. The rule strengthens AI behavior under existing operator-directive patterns; doesn't add new operator interactions outside the substance-doubt case. Backwards-compatible: silent overrides become surfaced (improvement); existing compliant flows are unaffected.

**Empirical anchor.** All 5 hold-without-rollback runs in the versioning stress test would have produced WAL fidelity ≥0.7 under this rule (assuming operator confirms the substance hold in the new ask). The 1 perfect run (light-2, fidelity 1.00) handled this via rollback path which the new rule still permits as path (b).

**Refs:** [`1a12b640`](context_log.md#1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d--observation--2026-05-27) (versioning-light stress-test observation surfacing F1+F2 systematic failure modes); [`c27c0d81`](context_log.md#c27c0d81fbd7568fa31a1ae3819132eb--decision--2026-05-27) (F2-B atomic-paired sibling for the cue-recognition gap); [stress-test summary](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-7a4da07/summary.md) (full empirical analysis).

## c27c0d81fbd7568fa31a1ae3819132eb — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Spec-patch F2-B: settling-cue interpretation extended to recognize "self-validated-proposal" pattern as a directive-cue (settlement).** Addresses the second systematic failure mode surfaced in the versioning stress-test ([`1a12b640`](context_log.md#1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d--observation--2026-05-27)): operator's Turn-4 statement *"I think we should require the standard API-key auth for that metadata endpoint. Makes sense to me."* was misread as non-settlement by 3 of 6 runs across light + heavy. The 3 runs defaulted to AI's prior unauthenticated lean and either misrepresented operator's position (light-1: "operator silence read as concurrence") or recorded auth as unsettled (heavy-2: "tabled to a later turn"). Operator was NOT silent — they articulated and self-validated a preference in one beat.

**The change.**

**Yes-cues list extended** with: *"makes sense to me"*, *"that works"*, *"agreed"*, *"I'm on board with X"*. Plus interpretive note added to the yes-cues definition: *"The cue fires on settled substance regardless of who proposed it — AI's prior proposal accepted by operator, OR operator's own current proposal self-validated within the same turn."*

**Directive-cues list extended** with the "self-validated-proposal pattern" — operator emits own-proposal + immediate self-validation in same turn:
- *"I think we should require API-key auth for that endpoint. Makes sense to me."*
- *"Let's go with header-based. Yeah, that works."*

Treats the combined statement as a directive-cue (settlement). Distinct from a coherence-doubt cue (where operator doubts, not settles).

**Why this shape.** Loose-framework interpretation (FP1: AI as interpreter) means cue lists are reference, not exhaustive — but the stress-test 50/50 split (3 runs settled, 3 missed) shows interpretation ambiguity on this specific pattern. The split was not random: AI runs that read the pattern as "operator self-validating their own thinking aloud" missed the settlement; runs that read it as "operator articulating their preference + signing off" caught it. The interpretive note in the yes-cues definition addresses this: cue fires on settled substance, not on conversational ownership of the proposal.

**Discipline-vs-interpretation distinction.** F2-B is interpretive (calibrate cue recognition), unlike F1-A which is structural (require an operator-touchpoint for the substance-doubt case). Both spec patches landed together because they were uncovered together; both address the same root: *AI failing to capture an operator-side settlement event in the WAL.*

**Adopter-applicability check.** Cue lists are reference; loose-framework principle (FP1) means adopters get interpretive flexibility. The list extensions strengthen recognition without changing AI's autonomous judgment latitude. Backwards-compatible: existing runs that already settled on these patterns are unchanged; runs that previously missed them now have explicit interpretive guidance.

**Empirical anchor.** All 3 F2-incidence runs in the stress test would have settled c6 correctly under the extended interpretation. Specifically, the operator's *"Makes sense to me"* is now explicit in the yes-cues list as a self-validation marker — and the combined "I think we should X. Makes sense to me." pattern is an explicit directive-cue example.

**Refs:** [`1a12b640`](context_log.md#1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d--observation--2026-05-27) (stress-test observation); [`ce1a6c78`](context_log.md#ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79--decision--2026-05-27) (F1-A atomic-paired sibling); [stress-test summary](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-7a4da07/summary.md) (full analysis).

## 7fd6d59f6e8256f4ecc0cc3be18fb7a4 — rollback — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Partial supersession of [`ce1a6c78`](context_log.md#ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79--decision--2026-05-27) (F1-A override-ask pattern).** Specifically rolls back the **"operator response determines WAL shape"** branches of the original pattern — the two-branch model that handled only explicit hold and explicit override responses. Empirical data from 3 patched-light stress-test runs ([summary](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-41b7de3/summary.md) — pending) showed the spec missed the third common case: operator moves to the next turn without explicitly settling either way. Under the rolled-back model, AI either wrote an `observation` (run-1: premature T2 write of unresolved state) or wrote nothing in the WAL (runs 2+3: dropped the thread). Both modes failed WAL fidelity.

**Operator's framing of the gap** (mid-iteration discussion):

> *"I think my issue is that the user might have simply missed the AI's response. You're assuming the user read it, and then decided not to comment on it. The fact is, they might have just missed it, or read but forgotten to respond to it in that turn. In my mind this is T1 area."*

The two-branch model assumed operator made a deliberate hold/override choice. Reality: operators often miss or forget threads. Assuming "implicit hold" over-commits the WAL; assuming "implicit override" reverses substance against operator's intent. Neither is correct.

**Remaining-valid clauses of [`ce1a6c78`](context_log.md#ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79--decision--2026-05-27)** (still in force, preserved verbatim):
- The override-ask conversational shape (AI surfaces substance counter-evidence before acting).
- **Silent override is forbidden** — AI may not continue without surfacing the disagreement.
- **Observation-only refutation is forbidden** — writing an `observation` "rebutting" the operator's claim without the surface-disagreement step.
- The "Why" rationale (FP4 split; AI may notice substance issues during substrate engagement; silent disagreement is the unhealthy shape).
- Pattern placement in §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" under "Allowed — direction-asks".

**What the refinement is** — see paired [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27): T1-tracking + re-surface obligation handles the no-explicit-settlement case; the original two branches preserved for the explicit-cue paths.

**Refs:** [`ce1a6c78`](context_log.md#ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79--decision--2026-05-27) (partial-supersession target); [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27) (atomic-paired refinement); [stress-test patched-light results](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-41b7de3/scores-summary.md) (empirical anchor).

## aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36 — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Refined F1-A override-ask: third "no explicit settlement" branch added, mapped to T1-tracking + re-surface obligation (T2 follows settlement, never precedes it).** Replaces the rolled-back two-branch model ([`7fd6d59f`](context_log.md#7fd6d59f6e8256f4ecc0cc3be18fb7a4--rollback--2026-05-27)) with three branches that handle the empirically-common case of operator non-settlement. Aligns the override-ask outcome with Stoa's existing T1/T2 invariants instead of inventing new ones.

**The three branches** (post-refinement; original two preserved):

1. **Explicit hold cue** (e.g., *"hold then"*, *"yes hold"*, *"keep it"*) → fresh `decision` capturing operator's directive + substance counter-evidence + held position; original NOT rolled back; `Refs:` cites original. (Preserved from `ce1a6c78`.)
2. **Explicit override cue** (e.g., *"do it anyway"*, *"go ahead"*, *"override"*) → atomic `rollback` of original + new `decision` capturing the change; counter-evidence in rollback body. (Preserved from `ce1a6c78`.)
3. **No explicit settlement** (NEW): substance is an unsettled T1 candidate. **AI MUST re-surface the unsettled thread at next strong cue boundary** (next operator turn that doesn't address it; commit boundary; end-of-impl). T2 entry only writes when operator settles per (1) or (2). If session ends without settlement (compact, clear, end-of-impl reached), cadence #4 writes a single `observation` capturing the unresolved state — substance counter-evidence + unresolved-question shape — so future sessions inherit the open thread.

**Why this is the right shape (operator framing):**

The unsettled state IS the truth. The override-ask surfaced a substance disagreement; the operator hasn't yet picked a path; T2 should NOT pretend otherwise. Forcing implicit-hold over-commits; forcing implicit-override reverses substance against operator's intent. T1-tracking preserves the unsettled state until the operator actually settles it.

This maps directly to existing Stoa rules:
- **T2 writes follow settlement, never precede it** (§"Operator touchpoints under autonomy").
- **T1 candidate reconciliation** (wal.md §"Three-tier WAL model") covers preserve/refine/demote in working memory.
- **Cadence #4 pre-compact/clear flush** is the natural cadence for resolving unsettled candidates when the session ends.
- The re-surface obligation is the operator-touchpoint analog of cadence #7's end-of-impl trigger ("about to switch problem domains" → re-surface unsettled threads).

**Empirical anchor.** Patched-light runs ([stress-test results](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-41b7de3)):
- All 3 runs invoked the override-ask conversationally at Turn 4 (the F1-A pattern works at the surface level).
- All 3 runs surfaced substance counter-evidence (snapshot's `cloudfront-cache.json` annotation).
- Operator in scenario script moved to next turn without explicit hold/override response — the EMPIRICALLY-COMMON case.
- Run-1 wrote `observation` (closest to right; partial credit from judge). Runs 2+3 wrote nothing (failed WAL fidelity entirely).

Under the refined branch (3), all 3 runs should: re-surface at Turn 5 → if operator still doesn't address by end-of-impl, write `observation` at cadence #4 capturing the unresolved state. The held-position decision only writes when operator confirms explicit hold.

**Paired benchmark + scorer updates** (atomic-paired with this entry):
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/cues.txt` — a1/a2 substance keywords extended to include held-position language (`override-ask`, `held the URL-based`, `substrate counter-evidence`, `unresolved support window`).
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/behaviors.txt` — new `context_log.md` and `api-versioning-plan.md` predicates for a1/a2 hold-path capture.
- `stress-test-harness/grading/score.sh` — paired-tier capture condition relaxed: `(rollback OR held-position marker)` instead of `rollback only`. AI-led floor extended with held-position keywords. Output adds `HELD_POSITION_COUNT` line.

The benchmark evolves with the spec. Without these updates, the F1-A hold path would score 0/2 mechanically even though the substance is correctly captured per the judge.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Spec patch ships in `dist/claude/stoa-claude.md` via recompose; adopters get the refined three-branch pattern on next install. Backwards-compatible: existing runs using the two-branch model still produce valid WAL shapes (rollback or held-position decision); the third branch handles a case the two-branch model dropped silently. Benchmark + scorer updates are spec-author-only infrastructure.

**Refs:** [`7fd6d59f`](context_log.md#7fd6d59f6e8256f4ecc0cc3be18fb7a4--rollback--2026-05-27) (paired partial-rollback of `ce1a6c78`); [`ce1a6c78`](context_log.md#ce1a6c78b14b8cc4d24ca9c8da3d5d79--decision--2026-05-27) (original F1-A — preserved core; refined operator-response branches); [`c27c0d81`](context_log.md#c27c0d81fbd7568fa31a1ae3819132eb--decision--2026-05-27) (F2-B sibling, still in force); [`1a12b640`](context_log.md#1a12b640232f6b4d7060cb39fe43962d--observation--2026-05-27) (versioning-light stress-test observation surfacing F1+F2 originally).

## fe65d949d037277330739f132d9a5b9a — decision — 2026-05-27

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Spec-patch F3-A: execute-phase substrate sweep added to cadence #7 (sub-bullet c) — closes the systematic tier-4 gap where AI tags substrate findings during execute work as "implementation details" rather than elevating to T2.** Addresses the failure mode visible across all 9 light + 6 heavy stress-test runs to date: AI notices substrate observations during Turn 7 execute work (in artifact comments, plan-doc open-questions, transcripts) but doesn't WAL-capture them. Judges' refrain: *"the substrate observation is present in the artifact but absent from the WAL."*

**The pattern.** Tier-4 cues (b1: CloudFront cache config; b2: route-ID naming) measure whether AI elevates substrate-discovered friction during execute work to WAL entries. Pre-F3-A, the implicit model assumed substrate findings during planning got T1-flushed normally — but execute-phase findings consistently failed to fire as T1 candidates because the AI's framing shifted to "implementation work" rather than "decision-making". Cadence #7 (a) T1 audit and (b) artifact-coherence nudge don't catch this because the substrate finding was never identified as a candidate.

**The fix — cadence #7 (c) execute-phase substrate sweep.** At end-of-impl, AI scans execute-phase artifacts (generated code, configs, plan docs) for substrate observations and elevates three patterns:

1. **Substrate confirmation** — substrate evidence supports a prior decision (e.g., refined run-1: AI verified CloudFront config supports URL-based versioning) → write `observation` citing substrate location + evidence. Provides operator-visible audit trail.

2. **Substrate contradiction** — substrate evidence contradicts a prior decision → treat substrate as implicit operator-side directive; trigger F1-A override-ask pattern. Reuses the F1-A three-branch resolution machinery.

3. **New architectural choice introduced during execute** — implementation produces architecturally-meaningful artifacts the prior decisions didn't settle (route naming, header pairings, cache strategy, error response shape) → `decision` with `Refs:` to upstream. Implementation-detail choices below the architecture line (variable names, control flow) stay in artifacts.

**Detection cues** named in the spec: artifact comments noting substrate behavior; plan-doc *"Open questions"* sections naming substrate-grounded concerns; AI internal notices during execute that didn't get WAL'd. Granularity rule: *"would this be something you'd want to roll back independently later? If yes, WAL it."*

**Why F3-A rather than F3-B (pre-execute inspection) or F3-C (no-silent-architectural-choice rule):**

- F3-A piggybacks on existing cadence #7 which AI already runs at end-of-impl — minimal new procedural surface.
- F3-A is explicit about three concrete patterns (confirmation, contradiction, new-arch) — closer to enumeration than judgment-by-rule.
- F3-A reuses F1-A's override-ask for the contradiction case — no new mechanism, just composition with refined F1-A.
- F3-B would require AI to proactively pre-scan substrate before each execute (heavier; new operator-touchpoint moment).
- F3-C would rely on AI's "is this architectural?" judgment (subjective; benchmark-degrading).

**Paired benchmark + scorer updates** (atomic-paired with this entry):

- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/cues.txt` — b1/b2 substance keywords extended to include execute-phase substrate sweep language (`cache key already`, `substrate confirms`, `naturally distinct`, `downstream consumer`, `datadog dashboards`, `client-py`, `execute-phase substrate`).
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/behaviors.txt` — new `context_log.md` predicates for b1/b2 substrate-confirmation/new-arch paths; comments distinguishing contradiction path vs F3-A paths.
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/ground-truth.md` — b1/b2 expected-entry-type cells updated to enumerate all three F3-A completion paths (contradiction → rollback+decision; new architectural choice → decision; confirmation → observation).

**Empirical baseline (pre-F3-A).** Refined-light run-1 (judge: 0.84) demonstrated the b1 confirmation pattern in artifact substance (CloudFront config inspection during execute) but didn't WAL-capture it; the judge flagged this as *"partial — substance present in observation entries with cache key keywords, but no rollback+decision pair as required for tier-4."* Run-2/run-3 similar. F3-A explicit substrate sweep should close this gap.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Cadence #7 extension is host-neutral; adopters re-running `dist/claude/install.sh install` get the new (c) sub-bullet. Backwards-compatible — existing runs that already produced substrate-contradiction rollbacks still pass; new runs that confirm substrate will also pass (previously they'd have been silent).

**Refs:** [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27) (refined F1-A — reused for substrate-contradiction case in F3-A); [`c27c0d81`](context_log.md#c27c0d81fbd7568fa31a1ae3819132eb--decision--2026-05-27) (F2-B sibling, still in force); [stress-test refined-light results](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-3035a11) (empirical anchor — judge calls for the b1 partial-credit cell).
