## 0c0508c6d4dbdd298b544d3f925f0c96 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Spec-patch F3-D: sharpens F3-A cadence #7(c) pattern 3 with explicit "default-shift rule" — if AI is documenting a substrate finding in a code comment or plan-doc note, the WAL-elevation step is automatic, not a separate judgment call.** Addresses the inter-run variance observed in F3-A versioning-light (mean 0.90, range 0.85-0.97): all 3 runs noticed substrate findings during execute work; all 3 generated correct artifacts; but only run-3 elevated all findings to WAL. Runs 1+2 documented some findings in artifact comments + plan-doc "Open Questions" sections without WAL'ing them — same substrate, same noticing, different judgment about WAL-worthiness.

**Empirical anchor — the b2 case** ([F3-A run-1 + run-2 transcripts](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-e70c818)):

The `v1-routes.yaml` snapshot file in the versioning bundle has an explicit header docstring naming three downstream consumers (Datadog dashboards, paystream-client-py, customer-facing migration runbooks) that are coupled to route IDs. *"Adding a new version requires touching all three downstream consumers. Hand-edited."* The AI in all 3 runs read this header, used it to inform v2-routes.yaml generation (chose `route-v2-*` IDs mirroring v1 for parallel-update flow), and noted it in the v2-routes.yaml header comment plus the plan-doc. Run-3 also wrote `decision e2561278` capturing the parallel-naming choice with Refs to upstream. Runs 1+2 stopped at the artifact comments. Same finding, same evidence, different WAL-elevation judgment.

**The default-shift rule** added to cadence #7(c) pattern 3:

> If AI is documenting a substrate finding inside a code comment, an artifact header, or a plan-doc "Open questions" / "Notes on substrate" section — AI has ALREADY crossed the "this is worth noting" threshold. The next step is automatic: write the WAL entry too. The artifact-or-plan-doc note is AI's own evidence that the finding cleared the substrate-finding bar; the WAL-elevation step is not a separate judgment call.

**Architecture-line carve-out** preserved and sharpened:

- Carve-out applies ONLY to: variable names, control-flow style, equivalent syntactic forms, formatting choices.
- Substrate-derived choices ABOVE that line — naming conventions (route IDs, header pairings, error codes), contract surfaces (API responses, downstream consumer impacts, integration points), substrate-derived configs (cache strategies, retry policies, timeout values), and substrate findings supporting or refuting prior decisions — **ALWAYS elevate**.
- Default is `observation` when AI is unsure between observation and skip. Overcapture cost is one WAL line; undercapture cost is reconstruction-fidelity loss.

**Why this is a refinement (not supersession) of [`fe65d949`](context_log.md#fe65d949d037277330739f132d9a5b9a--decision--2026-05-27).** The F3-A three-pattern structure stands; F3-D only sharpens pattern 3's judgment-call ambiguity by adding the default-shift rule. Pattern 1 (substrate confirmation → observation) and pattern 2 (substrate contradiction → F1-A trigger) operate identically. The architecture-line carve-out from F3-A is preserved; F3-D adds explicit enumeration of what's above vs below the line.

**Why F3-D over F3-B (sweep-exhaustiveness rule) or F3-C (procedural inventory):** F3-B's structural rule needed the same carve-out F3-D uses, so it doesn't actually close the judgment gap. F3-C added ceremony with a new operator-touchpoint that wasn't load-bearing. F3-D is the smallest change that targets the empirical failure mode directly — runs already document the finding; F3-D makes elevation automatic from documentation rather than a separate decision.

**Predicted impact.** Runs 1+2-style misses (substrate documented in artifact-or-plan-doc but not WAL'd) should now elevate by default. Expected tier-4 mechanical capture: 100% (vs current 67%). Expected mean fidelity: 0.92-0.95 range (vs current 0.90). The default-shift removes the judgment-variance source identified across the 3 F3-A runs.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Refinement ships in `dist/claude/stoa-claude.md`; adopters get it on next install. Backwards-compatible: existing runs that already followed the default-shift produce identical WAL shapes; runs that didn't now have explicit rule to follow. The shift is conservative — defaults toward more WAL entries (observation overcapture), which is the cheap side of the error.

**Refs:** [`fe65d949`](context_log.md#fe65d949d037277330739f132d9a5b9a--decision--2026-05-27) (F3-A — refined by this entry); [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27) (refined F1-A — F3-D pattern 2 still triggers F1-A for substrate-contradiction); [`c27c0d81`](context_log.md#c27c0d81fbd7568fa31a1ae3819132eb--decision--2026-05-27) (F2-B — independent spec patch, still in force); [F3-A run results](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-27-unknown-version-e70c818) (empirical anchor — b2 variance pattern).

## e3d01921559d4e09b441c5ca24c99475 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Stress-test mechanical scorer refactored to track judge verdicts more faithfully.** Three issues surfaced when comparing mechanical scores against the F3-D heavy-run judge verdicts (means 0.78-0.82, 13/14 cues captured per judge):

1. **Global paired-AI-signature gate cross-contaminated cues.** Score.sh required `rollback OR held-position marker` *anywhere in the WAL* for paired-tier cue capture. Once a1's WAL entry contained `override-ask` / `substrate counter-evidence`, a2's capture credited too — even when a2 had no F1-A entry. Heavy run-2 and run-3 over-credited a2 this way (judge marked both as missed; mechanical marked both as captured).

2. **`grep -qF` fixed-string keyword matching defeated regex-shaped cue patterns.** Patterns like `cache.*naturally distinct` in `cues.txt` were never firing because `.*` was matched literally. Switched cue matching to `grep -qiE` (case-insensitive regex). Existing literal patterns (`6-month`, `n-1`, `/v1`) work unchanged under regex; the previously-broken `.*` patterns now fire as intended.

3. **Cross-cue contamination at the keyword level.** Generic F1-A signature phrases (`override-ask`, `substrate counter-evidence`, `execute-phase substrate`) appeared in multiple cues' patterns. Whole-WAL grep + shared phrasing → one cue's entry credited a sibling cue. Patterns are now topic-anchored (URL / N-1 / cache / route) so each cue's substance test disambiguates.

**Plus a separate sub-issue:** execute-output and plan-doc behavior lines for paired-tier cues let mechanical credit "AI did some work" even when the work landed only in `api-versioning-plan.md` or `execute-output/nginx.conf`. That's exactly the silent-decision failure mode the judge catches via WAL-stands-alone scoring. For mechanical to track judge, paired-tier `behaviors.txt` is now WAL-only.

**Changes landed:**

- `stress-test-harness/grading/score.sh` — dropped global paired-AI-signature gate from per-cue capture; switched cue keyword matching from `grep -qF` to `grep -qiE`; broadened the AI-led-floor held-position regex to catch observed phrasings (`(url-based|n-1|header-based).*(is|was) held`, `held against`, `refuted by .*snapshot`, `substrate.*refute`).
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/cues.txt` — topic-anchored a1/a2/b1/b2 cue patterns; dropped non-disambiguating generic markers (`override-ask`, `substrate counter-evidence` as standalone phrases); replaced bare `n-2` (which incidentally matched c4 trade-off prose) with verb-bound forms (`extend.*n-2`, `n-2.*extend`).
- `stress-test-harness/benchmark/versioning/behaviors.txt` — paired-tier rows are now WAL-only (no execute-output, no plan-doc); patterns topic-anchored.

**Verification.** Re-scored `2026-05-28-unknown-version-09c077a` heavy runs against judge verdicts:

| Run | Mechanical (pre-fix) | Mechanical (post-fix) | Judge | Agreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Heavy-1 | a1✗ a2✗ b1✗ b2✗ | a1✓ a2✓ b1✓ b2✓ | a1✓ a2✓ b1 partial b2✓ | high (b1 minor over-credit) |
| Heavy-2 | a1✓ a2✓ b1✗ b2✓ | a1✓ a2✗ b1✓ b2✓ | a1✓ a2✗ b1✓ b2✓ | full ✓ |
| Heavy-3 | a1✓ a2✓ b1✗ b2✓ | a1✓ a2✗ b1✓ b2✓ | a1✓ a2✗ b1✓ b2✓ | full ✓ |

Heavy aggregate post-fix: T1=100% T2=100% T3=67% T4=100% (matches judge: 13/14 cues mean per run). Light aggregate unchanged at 100% across all tiers — light runs already had WAL traces for every cue.

**The remaining mechanical-vs-judge gap (heavy run-1's b1)** is stylistic, not substantive: judge calls b1 partial because the cache-substrate substance lives in the planning-phase entry `6ad996a9` (which also carries the a1 hold) rather than a standalone execute-phase observation. Mechanical credits the substance regardless of which entry it lives in. Defensible — mechanical errs toward giving substance credit; judge enforces shape discipline. The judge is primary; mechanical is sidecar.

**Why this is the right scope of fix.** The original mechanical scorer added a global rollback/held requirement on top of per-cue behavior patterns, assuming the per-cue patterns weren't specific enough. The opposite was true: per-cue patterns ARE specific enough when topic-anchored, and the global gate causes cross-contamination. Trusting per-cue patterns is both simpler and more accurate. The AI-led floor remains as a separate aggregate signal — "WAL has at least one AI-side signature anywhere" is still meaningful regardless of per-cue capture.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Stress-test infrastructure lives in `stress-test-harness/`, which is `.gitignore`d from `dist/` and never ships to adopters. Spec-author-only work. No adopter-applicability concerns.

**Refs:** [`0c0508c6`](context_log.md#0c0508c6d4dbdd298b544d3f925f0c96--decision--2026-05-28) (F3-D default-shift); [`013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba`](context_log.md#013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba--decision--2026-05-28) (F3-D baseline establishment, where this gap surfaced); [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27) (F1-A refined — three completion shapes the mechanical scorer must recognize per-cue).

## 6db947a2cdfb408d9b26708120bf06c0 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**F1-E: plan-doc default-shift rule added to F1-A no-settlement branch.** Extends the F3-D default-shift principle ([`0c0508c6`](context_log.md#0c0508c6d4dbdd298b544d3f925f0c96--decision--2026-05-28)) from cadence #7(c) substrate findings to F1-A no-settlement unresolved-state material. The rule lands inline in the F1-A no-settlement bullet (operations.md §"Operator touchpoints under autonomy" → "Override-ask"):

> **Plan-doc default-shift.** If AI is documenting the unresolved-state substance (substrate counter-evidence, proposed alternatives, held position) inside a non-WAL artifact — plan-doc *"Open questions"* / *"Open threads"* / *"Unsettled"* section, code comment marking the held state, or similar surface — AI has ALREADY crossed the *"worth noting"* threshold. **Write the WAL observation too**, at the moment of writing the artifact substance, not deferred to session end. The artifact note is AI's own evidence that the finding cleared the threshold; the WAL-elevation step is not a separate judgment call.

**Why this matters.** The F3-D post-judge analysis ([`013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba`](context_log.md#013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba--decision--2026-05-28); summary.md in the run-root) surfaced a new failure mode in 2 of 3 heavy runs: when operator surfaced contradicting evidence mid-conversation (Turn 5 — three top-10 customers still on v0; the settled N-1 support window would break them on v3 ship), the AI did substantive F1-A no-settlement work — proposed three resolution alternatives, marked the original N-1 decision as provisionally held — but recorded ALL of it in the plan-doc's *"Open Question 2"* / *"Thread 2"* section. Zero WAL entries.

The judges both flagged this as the canonical tier-3 miss: a reader of the WAL alone cannot see that the decision was challenged, that alternatives were proposed, or that the support window is contested. The plan-doc has the substance; the WAL is silent. Same shape as the F3-D pre-patch substrate-finding failure mode (substance lived in artifact comments, not WAL), now applied to F1-A no-settlement → plan-doc.

**Why this is the right shape of patch.** Three reasons:

1. **Empirical evidence of the failure mode.** Heavy run-1 escaped the failure (wrote `e0c969ef` observation correctly); heavy runs 2 and 3 deflected into plan-doc. 2 of 3 isn't sampling noise — it's a recurrent gap the spec doesn't currently close.

2. **F3-D demonstrated the default-shift mechanism works.** Pre-F3-D, AI was missing substrate elevations in 33% of cases; post-F3-D light went from 33% T4 → 100% T4. Same mechanism applied to the new failure mode should produce similar gains.

3. **Minimum disruption.** Adds one paragraph inline in the F1-A no-settlement bullet rather than restructuring the F1-A pattern or promoting default-shift to a top-level principle. The principle generalizes (any AI substance written into a non-WAL artifact crosses the WAL-elevation threshold), but explicit per-pattern instances are easier for the AI to reach in-session than abstract principles. Generalization can come later if more recurrences land.

**Backstop relationship to cadence #4.** Cadence #4's end-of-session observation remains the catchup for the case where AI didn't write substance into either the artifact OR the WAL during the session. F1-E closes the case where AI wrote substance into the artifact but not the WAL. The two are complementary: F1-E fires at the moment of artifact-writing during the session; cadence #4 fires at session end as the last-chance backstop.

**Predicted impact.** Heavy condition's a2 miss rate (2 of 3 runs) should drop. Expected heavy mean fidelity: 0.85-0.90 range (vs current 0.807). Light condition shouldn't change much since light already had 100% T3 capture — F1-E targets the specific failure mode that heavy load surfaced.

**Adopter-applicability check.** Refinement ships in `dist/claude/stoa-claude.md`; adopters get it on next install. Backwards-compatible: existing runs that already followed the principle (heavy run-1, all light runs) produce identical WAL shapes; runs that deflected into plan-doc now have explicit rule to follow. Conservative — defaults toward more WAL entries (observation overcapture), the cheap side of the error.

**Refs:** [`0c0508c6`](context_log.md#0c0508c6d4dbdd298b544d3f925f0c96--decision--2026-05-28) (F3-D — the analogous default-shift rule for substrate findings; this entry extends the principle); [`aaf9a6bd`](context_log.md#aaf9a6bd44e50055d576e4b59eb65a36--decision--2026-05-27) (F1-A refined — the 3-branch structure being refined here); [`013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba`](context_log.md#013016197e909b0b4ca1674099623dba--decision--2026-05-28) (F3-D run-root + summary.md flagging this failure mode); [stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-28-unknown-version-09c077a/summary.md](stress-test-harness/results/2026-05-28-unknown-version-09c077a/summary.md) (empirical anchor — F1-A no-settlement → plan-doc-only pattern in heavy runs 2+3).

## 099ebe90ff954011bdf595f25a8efd58 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-7,1M)]

**Stress-test harness attribution string made dynamic (orchestrator-resolved) instead of hardcoded.** `stress-test-harness/harness.md` Step 2's light-load drive-prompt template carried a literal `Attribution: @ivan-avramov;claude(opus4.7/1M)` line. Heavy and xheavy templates inherit it ("same as light"). Every drive subagent across every run this session copied that literal — so every run-root's WAL self-labels as `opus4.7` regardless of the model that actually produced it.

This was latent until Opus 4.8 entered the picture (operator exposed `claude-opus-4-8[1m]` via the Zed ACP server). The moment a model-comparison run becomes possible — hold the spec constant, vary only the drive model — a hardcoded attribution silently mislabels the 4.8 run's artifacts as 4.7, defeating the entire point of the comparison.

**Fix.** Replaced the literal with a `<ATTRIBUTION>` parameter, added to the Step 2 parameterization list alongside `<SPEC_PATH>` / `<RUN_DIR>` / `<SCENARIO_DIR>`. The orchestrating agent (the parent Claude driving the harness) resolves it live from its own session-environment model and substitutes it when constructing each subagent prompt — exactly the pattern already used for the other parameters. Format unchanged: `@ivan-avramov;claude(<model>/<context>)` where `<model>/<context>` is the live driving model (`opus4.8/1M`, `opus4.7/1M`, `sonnet4.6/1M`, etc.).

**Why orchestrator-resolved and not script-resolved.** `runHarness.sh setup` is a shell script with no reliable way to know the model that will drive the run (the model is resolved by the harness/ACP layer at agent-spawn time, after setup runs). The orchestrating agent DOES know its model — it's in the session environment block. The harness is explicitly Claude-orchestrated, so parameterizing on an agent-resolved value is consistent with the existing design rather than a new mechanism.

**Adopter-applicability check.** `stress-test-harness/` is gitignored from `dist/` and never ships to adopters — spec-author-only tooling. No adopter-applicability concerns. (Filed as a WAL entry anyway per the every-behavior-change rule and because cadence #3 requires `context_log.md` staged with the change.)

**Note on existing run-roots.** Prior run-roots (F3-D `09c077a`, F1-E `3836bcb`, the xheavy `a603196`) retain their `opus4.7` attribution in committed WAL artifacts. Those runs WERE driven on 4.7 (this session's environment), so the labels are accurate — not retroactively wrong. The fix only affects runs driven from here forward, where the model may differ.

**Refs:** [`e3d01921`](context_log.md#e3d01921559d4e09b441c5ca24c99475--decision--2026-05-28) (prior harness-tooling change this session — scoring refactor; same spec-author-only / gitignored-from-dist applicability posture).

## 10cf67c9547e4952a6ef49b2eed0bf27 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Stress-test drive templates now pin execute-turn output to `<RUN_DIR>` (parallel-run isolation), closing the shared-`/tmp` collision latent gap.** The Step-2 drive-prompt templates told the subagent where to write its WAL and transcript (`<RUN_DIR>/context_log.md`, `<RUN_DIR>/transcript.md`) but said nothing about the execute-turn output location — and the scenario `conversation.md` Turn-7 prose points at `/tmp/versioning-routing/` + `/tmp/api-versioning-plan.md`. With one subagent that is harmless; with N runs driven in parallel (the model-comparison case), every run would write execute config + plan writeup to the SAME `/tmp` paths and clobber each other, and would risk editing the shared `<run-root>/benchmark/<scenario>/snapshot/` in place. The 4.8 model-comparison run surfaced this: the orchestrator had to hand-augment all 6 subagent prompts with explicit output routing to produce the per-run `execute-output/` layout the scorer/judge expect.

**Fix.** Same shape as the [`099ebe90`](context_log.md#099ebe90ff954011bdf595f25a8efd58--decision--2026-05-28) attribution-param fix — move the run-time clarification into the template so the orchestrator does not re-derive it each run. Added an "Execute-turn output routing (REQUIRED — run isolation)" block to the light template (heavy inherits it; an explicit note added to the xheavy paragraph): treat `<SCENARIO_DIR>/snapshot/` as read-only; write execute-phase output files into `<RUN_DIR>/execute-output/`; write the plan writeup into `<RUN_DIR>/`; ignore the conversation's `/tmp` paths and use the run-specific path (the conversation already offers "or your run-specific path"). Tightened the `<RUN_DIR>` parameter description to name the `execute-output/` subdir + plan-doc convention.

**Why template-level and not fixture-level.** The collision risk is an orchestration concern (parallel runs sharing a filesystem), not a scenario-design concern. Leaving `conversation.md`'s Turn-7 prose untouched keeps the scenario fixture and its tier-4 cue substance stable; routing is handled purely at the drive-prompt layer where `<RUN_DIR>` is known.

## 5000066d891f4969bededf4ce080b0f0 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Re-establish Stoa SemVer at v0.10.0 — single source (`VERSION` file) assembled into the composed fat spec's H1, exactly once.** Version stamping was deliberately removed in the refactor ([`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27): content-hash drift, not SemVer; killed per-artifact stamp proliferation + SemVer-based drift detection), with the stated intent that version "survive only in canonical adopter-visible places" ([`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27)). That home was never built — Stoa ran version-less since `v0.9.1` ([`4179d5be`](context_log.md#4179d5befa45426e885ac22dd79caa83--observation--2026-05-27)), and the stress-test harness emitted `unknown-version` run-roots. This closes the gap.

**Mechanism.** A root `VERSION` file holds bare SemVer (`0.10.0`) — the single thing bumped. `build/compose.sh` reads it and prepends `# Stoa v<VERSION>` as the fat spec's H1 (the spec previously had no H1, opening at `## What Stoa is`). The version renders **exactly once**, in H1. No version in the marker, dispatcher, or surface output — content hashes still own drift detection; version is identification, not logic. Coherent with `5a1835bb`/`aeec6b10`: a single source + single compose-assembled display is neither the proliferation nor the version-as-logic the refactor opposed, and the fat spec is the most canonical adopter-visible artifact (the thing adopters fetch and load). Operator corrected an early framing that treated "derived/build artifact" and "carries a version" as exclusive — they are not.

**No BETA suffix.** Per SemVer convention `0.x.y` is pre-stable by definition; an explicit `(beta)`/`BETA` tag is redundant and would re-introduce the human-only-suffix handling ([`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26)). Pure SemVer, nothing to strip.

**Coincident fixes.** (a) The bootcheck-failure line listed `version-match` among unverified state, but [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) removed version-matching from the bootcheck entirely — stale token, removed from the enumeration. (b) The harness `extract_spec_version` already reads H1 for `v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`; the versioned H1 makes it resolve `v0.10.0` automatically — no harness edit, `unknown-version` self-heals.

**Refs:** [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) (removed SemVer proliferation + SemVer-drift-detection; this re-adds version as identification-only, honoring that), [`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27) (version belongs in canonical adopter-visible places — realized here as the fat spec H1), [`ee1906ca`](context_log.md#ee1906caaad94eb89d5f34e2abb491f3--decision--2026-05-26) (BETA human-only — satisfied trivially by carrying no suffix), [`0ef83389`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite removed version-match; stale token fixed here), [`4179d5be`](context_log.md#4179d5befa45426e885ac22dd79caa83--observation--2026-05-27) (last stamped version v0.9.1, before the version-less gap this closes).

## 185c83a3f22147f3b6619808a6981aa2 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Bootcheck reliability redesign: probe logic extracted to a single shipped script invoked as ONE Bash call, and the subagent made fail-closed.** Operator hit ~7 tool errors at session-start bootcheck — one `Tool permission request failed: Error: Internal error` plus a cascade of `Cancelled: parallel tool call` siblings — yet the bootcheck still returned `clean`. Two root causes: (1) the subagent fanned its install-state probes out as multiple parallel `Bash` calls; none were allowlisted, so each raised a permission prompt, one internal-errored, and the harness cancelled the whole parallel batch; (2) Step 8 "default-clean" emitted `clean` whenever no remediation line was produced — making a cancelled/errored probe (never ran) indistinguishable from a passing probe (ran, found nothing). Fail-open: a single transient permission glitch could suppress every probe and still report healthy.

**Chosen (Option 2 of the offered set).** New spec-owned `src/hooks/bootcheck-probe` runs all probes (marker, drift, hooks, pull-rebase config, orphan-T2, merge-audit, attribution) sequentially and emits a `key=value` report terminated by `probe_status=complete`. The subagent now invokes exactly `bash .stoa/hooks/bootcheck-probe` (one call, never parallel) and maps fields to the unchanged canonical `[stoa]` lines. Two guaranteed properties: **one permission request / one tool call** (trivially allowlistable; cannot cascade-cancel — kills both the trigger and the amplifier), and **fail-closed** (`clean` only when the `probe_status=complete` terminator is observed; a missing terminator emits a new `probe-incomplete` remediation line reporting install-state UNVERIFIED, never `clean`). The complex regex/heredoc/substitution now live inside the script file, invisible to the permission parser. Bonus: the probe is now unit-testable.

**Alternative considered.** Option 1 (minimal): keep inline probes but mandate a single sequential Bash call + add the fail-closed gate in wording — no new file, but the probe stays a large model-rewritten one-liner (this session the model had added its own `printf` diagnostics) and stays untestable. Rejected for the quality-maximizing path per the repo's bias-toward-quality posture.

**Wiring.** `build/compose.sh` and `src/installers/claude.sh` (placement, marker `hash:` enumeration, `doctor` check) updated to ship + hash-track the new script alongside `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`; drift detection (compose step 8 `find .stoa/hooks`) covers it automatically. Adopter-applicable: one short allowlistable command + fewer prompts is strictly better for adopters, and fail-closed never false-positives on adopter content. Output discipline (FIRST CHARACTER rule, training-data directive, forgiving-extraction backstop) preserved unchanged.

**Refs:** [`4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2`](context_log.md#4d8641994c932852c90512ded80228e2--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck forgiving-extraction backstop — same subagent, output-discipline axis; preserved here), [`0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af`](context_log.md#0ef83389f603bdff07c31af822b283af--decision--2026-05-27) (bootcheck rewrite that set the current probe set), [`5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) (Claude-first refactor establishing the dist/install model this ships through).

## cd2bd2513fe04f318fbf1900644ac312 — decision — 2026-05-28

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Bootcheck moves from a subagent to a main-agent probe script; the `stoa-bootcheck` subagent is retired (Option 1).** Root cause found after [`185c83a3`](context_log.md#185c83a3f22147f3b6619808a6981aa2--decision--2026-05-28)'s fix shipped: the residual `Tool permission request failed: Error: Internal error` was not parallelism (only an amplifier) but that **a subagent cannot reliably surface an interactive permission prompt** — so the subagent's Bash call to the probe errored whenever the command wasn't pre-approved. stoa-ai masked it via a gitignored `settings.local.json` allowlist (which never ships); acme-platform, with none, hit it on a fresh session. 185c83a3's fail-closed property worked there — it reported `probe-incomplete` (UNVERIFIED), not a false `clean` — confirming the safety net while exposing the deeper trigger.

**Chosen.** The main agent runs `bash .stoa/hooks/bootcheck-probe` as its first boundary-moment action (it prompts normally → allow once). The script now emits the FINAL canonical lines (status + anchors + `Attribution:` + `probe_status=complete` terminator); the agent relays them into `[stoa-init]`, mapping nothing. This eliminates the subagent-can't-prompt failure class structurally, keeps the slim small (no mapping logic loaded into every session), removes the FIRST-CHARACTER / forgiving-extraction machinery (it existed only to parse a subagent's text return), and improves cross-host robustness — Codex subagent spawning is fragile (beta_tracker `ae6e0b97`); a host-neutral script the main agent runs sidesteps it.

**Scope.** Supersedes the *subagent-execution* aspect of [`185c83a3`](context_log.md#185c83a3f22147f3b6619808a6981aa2--decision--2026-05-28) only — its script-extraction + fail-closed properties carry forward (this is a refinement, not a rollback). `src/subagents/stoa-bootcheck.md` deleted (+ its README entry); `operations.md` §"Session boot check", `adapters/claude.md`, the probe script, and the test rewritten; `installers/claude.sh` now sheds retired `stoa-*` agents on reinstall (removes repo `.claude/agents/stoa-*.md` absent from the bundle) so existing adopters self-clean. Docs `current_ux.md` + `getting_started.md` synced (cadence #1/#2); `proposed_methodology.md` (version history) and the deferred-retarget `tests/harness.sh` / `tests/scenarios.md` left. The [`92bdc3cd`](context_log.md#92bdc3cd3961446991625b9cd97cba3e--decision--2026-05-28) "Bootcheck surfaced attribution:" label is preserved.

**Process note.** 185c83a3 was an incomplete first fix — the first diagnosis pinned the amplifier (parallel batching) rather than the root cause (the subagent permission-prompt limitation). The fail-closed-then-root-cause arc is the methodology working as intended: the safety net surfaced the residual failure honestly instead of hiding it behind a false `clean`.

**Refs:** [`185c83a3f22147f3b6619808a6981aa2`](context_log.md#185c83a3f22147f3b6619808a6981aa2--decision--2026-05-28), [`92bdc3cd3961446991625b9cd97cba3e`](context_log.md#92bdc3cd3961446991625b9cd97cba3e--decision--2026-05-28).

## e4c1a2d8320f490c8c24d6bc77bc0978 — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Dispatcher block gets its own `## Stoa bootstrap dispatcher` H2 heading, placed inside the markers.** The block is heading-less and comment-delimited, and `inject_stoa_block` appends it to end-of-file when no marker exists yet — so it lands under whatever the file's last H2 is (in this repo's `AGENTS.md`, `## Deferred items`) and reads as subordinate to that unrelated section. Operator flagged the false grouping. Fix: add `## Stoa bootstrap dispatcher` as the first line after the `BEGIN` marker, making the block a peer section instead of nested content.

**Why this shape.** Heading goes *inside* the `BEGIN`/`END` markers (in `src/dispatcher.md`) so the installer's marker-replace carries it to existing adopters on their next reinstall — a heading above the marker would never reach them. Kept the append-at-end injection unchanged: the whole `AGENTS.md` loads into the system prompt at once, so in-file position gives the AI no functional priority; prepending would be invasive for adopters (shoves their own title/intro down) and would add insert-after-intro injection complexity. `H2`, not `H1` — adopter `AGENTS.md` files carry a single `H1` title, a second `H1` is structurally wrong, and `H1` would over-elevate a block whose charter is explicitly "not the spec." `format=1` retained: the format version tracks the machine contract (the marker-locatable region), which a human-facing heading inside the region does not change.

**AI-instruction-block note.** The dispatcher is an AI-instruction block; this is a presentation-only change (heading added; no directive wording altered), reconsidered with the operator before landing per AGENTS.md's AI-instruction-block discipline.

## 1da2f2fc9ea84bcdb5567fd8fcd78264 — observation — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**`.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit` is a local best-effort promptness nudge, not a coherence-debt ledger — its lossiness is by-design, not a gap.** Operator asked whether the marker should be checked in so unaudited merges stay visible to other clones. It should not. The marker records post-operation HEAD SHAs of *this clone's* merge/rebase operations — a local process event, distinct from the *coherence debt* (unreconciled entries in WAL content). The debt lives in WAL content, which propagates via git; its durable guarantee is the internal-conflict sweep (`/stoa coherence --internal-sweep`) — the SAME detector runs at merge-time catchup (cadence #6), at next-touch (Layer-2 batch compares new EC:STRONG entries against the full WAL), and on demand (`/stoa audit`). So a lost or un-propagated marker costs only *when* the sweep fires, never detection power: a latent conflict surfaces the moment anyone builds on the arc. The marker being per-clone, gitignored, lossy, and non-gating is therefore correct. Checking it in would also misfire mechanically — it churns on every merge/clear, and clearing becomes a cross-clone coordination point (conflicts on the state file itself).

**Refs:** [`019d0aff04524191aed79734366f3e43`](context_log.md#019d0aff04524191aed79734366f3e43--decision--2026-05-25) (marker = per-clone runtime state; `.gitignore` excludes it), [`f284d28250164f3f944bf77116fcee87`](context_log.md#f284d28250164f3f944bf77116fcee87--decision--2026-05-25) (cadence #6 post-merge primary mechanism).

## 7bce9ab691924ad5bc4c996368e3fe8f — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Boot-check rule carves out the mandatory adapter read as the one permitted precursor to the probe — removes a guaranteed false-breach.** §"Session boot check" said the first tool call MUST be the probe with "no other tool call precedes the probe," and the self-monitoring breach rule flagged any non-probe first tool call. But the adapter (`stoa-claude.md`) is not auto-loaded — `CLAUDE.md` is just `@AGENTS.md`, and the dispatcher instructs the AI to *read* the adapter — so a single Read of it necessarily precedes the probe on every cold session. The absolute rule was therefore unsatisfiable and the breach rule a guaranteed false-positive (the bootcheck is reliably done, just after the adapter read). Fix: the rule now names the adapter read as the sole permitted precursor; the breach rule exempts it. Real intent preserved (probe before any substantive engagement). Surfaced by the `/stoa audit` session-reflective sweep ([`287f47c7`](context_log.md#287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f--observation--2026-05-29), candidate b).

**AI-instruction-block note.** §"Session boot check" is a tuned AI-instruction block; operator-directed change, reconsidered before landing per AGENTS.md. Wording shift only — no change to what the probe does or when it must run relative to substantive work.

## 6bd9b62dc3a846b1b844f48d2fb1005b — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Layer-2 coherence: the invoke/skip decision is gated on entry class alone — never on perceived processing cost. The main agent delegates; the WAL-librarian subagent owns path selection and bears the cost.** Root cause of the missed adjacencies the audit caught ([`287f47c7`](context_log.md#287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f--observation--2026-05-29)): this session's commit batch contained `EC:STRONG` entries (Layer-2 default = *invoke*), but the main agent skipped Layer-2, reasoning it would be a "heavy" full-WAL slurp not worth it for low-stakes install entries. That conflated two separate decisions — **whether** to invoke (main agent, gated on EC:STRONG) vs **how** to process (the librarian's discretion: slurp / index-retrieval / fallback per §"WAL access pattern", which it optimizes and whose cost it bears). Using how-layer cost to justify a whether-skip usurps the librarian and violates "when in doubt, delegate — invocations are cheap to the parent." The spec's own `(heavier, amortized)` descriptor primed the cost-weighing.

**Fix (b+c).** Reworded §"Two-layer coherence check": STRONG-in-batch → invoke, **not skippable on cost grounds**; the gate is entry-class-only; the main agent delegates and the librarian owns path selection; dropped the `(heavier)` framing. The cheap index path was never missing — it already lives in the librarian's repertoire; the bug was the parent pre-simulating its cost. Failure mode recorded in [`.stoa/beta_tracker.md`](.stoa/beta_tracker.md) `87e602b0`.

**AI-instruction-block note.** §"Two-layer coherence check" is a tuned AI-instruction block; operator-directed (b+c), reconsidered before landing per AGENTS.md.

**Refs:** [`287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f`](context_log.md#287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f--observation--2026-05-29) (the audit whose two missed adjacencies traced to this skip); [`782e0ec9fd514abea90ff5f4c6501016`](context_log.md#782e0ec9fd514abea90ff5f4c6501016--decision--2026-05-29) (retrieval-side twin: offering to ground is off-pattern because grounding is AI-owned procedure — this is the batch-coherence cost-side analog; neither is downgradable by main-agent discretion).

## 27ca469ce7494e769201cf5ef47f3f25 — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Settle the Layer-2 append-only tension (Option B): a link Layer-2 surfaces on an already-written batch entry is recorded on a forward `observation`, never by editing the sealed entry.** Resolves the open question raised in [`e16f4534`](context_log.md#e16f4534109c487bba2beff51ddfc02a--observation--2026-05-29) (first surfaced at [`287f47c7`](context_log.md#287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f--observation--2026-05-29)). The old Layer-2 action clause read "act silently (rollback append, `Refs:` line, cross-ref)", whose "`Refs:` line" implied an in-place edit contradicting the strict T2 append-only rule ("no same-turn edits"). Reworded §"Two-layer coherence check": Superseding → `rollback`; Adjacent/Converging on an already-written entry → forward `observation` citing both; never an in-place edit.

**Why B over the carve-out (Option A — a pre-commit `Refs:`-fold exception).** Keeps FP3 un-poked — no "mutable-while-uncommitted" T2 sub-state. And the forward entry is *higher-fidelity provenance*: it records that the link was found after the fact, where an in-place edit would retroactively make the entry look prescient. Append-only is a fidelity feature (the WAL records what was known *when*), not merely a constraint. Trade-off accepted: a 2-hop cross-ref via the observation instead of a direct edge, and one observation per Layer-2 catch — bounded, since a healthy Layer-1 makes Layer-2 misses rare; frequent catches would signal Layer-1 needs work, not that the record should be mutable. This canonizes the shape `287f47c7` and `e16f4534` already used.

**AI-instruction-block note.** §"Two-layer coherence check" is a tuned AI-instruction block; operator-directed (Option B), reconsidered before landing per AGENTS.md. Runtime clause kept strictly directive — this rationale lives here, not in the composed spec.

**Refs:** [`e16f4534109c487bba2beff51ddfc02a`](context_log.md#e16f4534109c487bba2beff51ddfc02a--observation--2026-05-29) (the open question this settles), [`6bd9b62dc3a846b1b844f48d2fb1005b`](context_log.md#6bd9b62dc3a846b1b844f48d2fb1005b--decision--2026-05-29) (the b+c Layer-2 change this completes), [`287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f`](context_log.md#287f47c73c4342a6960f96c7a9f1756f--observation--2026-05-29) (first instance of the tension).

## 193ae0a77637487480b72f4da713fa48 — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**The `[stoa]` badge is Stoa's voice only. The AI's own verdict on a surfaced item — overriding a finding, declining/deferring a flag, deprioritizing — is the agent's voice and is emitted unbadged.** Operator caught the defect on an artifact-coherence nudge: Stoa's flag (a tracked-doc drift signal — legitimately `[stoa]`) carried *my* deferral decision ("Deferred broader-doc-sweep") under the same badge, so AI judgment wore the methodology's uniform. The operator's distinction is the fix's spine: deciding *how to drive* on Stoa's output is the AI's job and is welcome; *presenting that decision as Stoa's* is the bug. Worse, the deferral wasn't even mine to announce — the nudge already hands the operator the opt-in.

**Directive added** to §"[stoa] chat surfaces": a `[stoa]` line carries only what the methodology produces (records, classifications, flags, remediation, process-state — rendered faithfully, shape-2 AI-state references included); the AI's discretionary verdict on a surface goes **unbadged**, in plain prose. The AI acts freely on Stoa's output; it never signs that decision with the badge. **Why:** a mixed line erodes the badge's meaning — `[stoa]` must reliably read as *"the methodology surfaced this,"* never *"the AI decided this."* The boundary is render-vs-verdict: faithfully reporting Stoa's mechanism-state (incl. shape 2) stays badged; the agent's choice about what to do with it does not.

**AI-instruction-block note.** §"[stoa] chat surfaces" is a tuned AI-instruction block; operator-directed, reconsidered before landing per AGENTS.md. Rationale kept here, out of the directive-only runtime clause.

**Refs:** [`a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737`](context_log.md#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19) (PNG-bytes / "AI-rendered surfaces" — this refines what *AI-rendered* may carry), [`7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a`](context_log.md#7a98ca01cfe442988d9b543775fb034a--decision--2026-05-20) (the `*No operator action needed*` audience-marker — sibling cut distinguishing AI-state *reporting* within the badge; this is the next cut: AI *verdict* outside it), [`b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b`](context_log.md#b90a584fb50742178c6a0d117fe5749b--decision--2026-05-19) (informational-markers principle).

## 3686a3f15f464db2aaa50ded0fafb71c — decision — 2026-05-29

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Before any `EC:STRONG` T2 write, a WAL-librarian grounding pass (not a parent grep) is mandatory — making Layer-1 comprehensive for STRONG, and demoting Layer-2 to a thin backstop (option 1b).** Settles the open thread in [`ce6f228b`](context_log.md#ce6f228bc6ab4522829be821ce28d129--observation--2026-05-29): Layer-2 caught a missed `Refs:` on three straight commits this session — a ~100% rate that meant Layer-1 was systematically under-linking, not that Layer-2 is a rare backstop. Root cause: Layer-1's Refs come from working memory only ([`5bcbe16a`](context_log.md#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19)), and the agent had been populating that memory via shallow parent greps that fragment an entry's body from its hex header → mis-attributed or missed the link. (Same root as the b+c skip: under-delegating WAL reach to the parent.)

**Fix = the librarian-call *and* the tidy (1b, not a half-measure).** The write-time librarian pass becomes the **primary** comprehensive coherence/Refs step for STRONG; Layer-1's working-memory cut is explicitly best-effort; Layer-2 stays invoked-for-STRONG ([`6bd9b62d`](context_log.md#6bd9b62dc3a846b1b844f48d2fb1005b--decision--2026-05-29) — class-gated, never cost) but **demotes from primary to backstop**, expected usually-clean since write-time grounding precedes it (it catches only the residual: skipped/degraded write-time grounding, or cross-entry interactions post-dating an entry's pass). This is the reallocation `ce6f228b`'s option (ii) invited — not silent overlap with Layer-2. It also shrinks the Option-B ([`27ca469c`](context_log.md#27ca469ce7494e769201cf5ef47f3f25--decision--2026-05-29)) forward-observation overhead: `Refs:` now land pre-seal, so the post-write forward-observation fires only on the rare residual. Defensible per [`8c65450c`](context_log.md#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18) (the librarian owns path + cost; the parent must not pre-simulate that cost to skip), and parallels the grounding-before-surfacing rule ([`a274252c`](context_log.md#a274252c993246988e63cd42ce495715--decision--2026-05-26)) on the write side (ground-before-surfacing : retrieval :: ground-before-sealing-Refs : write).

**AI-instruction-block note.** §"Two-layer coherence check" is a tuned AI-instruction block; operator-directed (1b), reconsidered before landing per AGENTS.md. Dogfood: this entry's own Refs were produced by a librarian grounding pass — the very mechanism it mandates.

## dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Escalate the session-boot bootcheck from an AI-discipline rule to a deterministic host SessionStart hook.** Five same-shape boot-discipline breaches in the acme-platform adopter (the probe was not the AI's first tool call — most recently a `git status` was batched ahead of it) cleared the escalation bar set by [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) (≥4 recurrences; wording + visibility + self-monitoring all tried and degrading). The fix: a host SessionStart hook auto-runs `bash .stoa/hooks/bootcheck-probe` and injects its output as session context; the agent renders the `[stoa-init]` block from that injection rather than making the probe its first tool call.

This un-defers the escalation queued in [`12106bc0`](context_log.md#12106bc006234e68a461128dbc149fc6--decision--2026-05-26). The host-neutrality objection that deferred it three times ([`e8c2a14`](context_log.md#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10), [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11), [`12106bc0`](context_log.md#12106bc006234e68a461128dbc149fc6--decision--2026-05-26) — *"Codex has no equivalent"*) is dissolved: the operator verified Codex supports the same `SessionStart` hook event via committed `.codex/hooks.json` + `.codex/config.toml`, same one-time-local-trust model. Unlike the commit boundary — where a host-neutral git hook existed, so [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11) chose it over a Claude `PreToolUse` hook — the session-start boundary has no host-neutral mechanism (it is inherently per-harness); the correct shape is per-host triggers over one shared host-neutral probe, matching Stoa's adapter model. The probe script stays host-neutral; only the trigger is per-host. The retained AI-discipline floor (compose-not-duplicate, [`3e8b5c9`](context_log.md#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11)) covers the trust window. Claude is the first/dogfood target; the Codex binding is deferred to a host bring-up.

**Refs:** [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11), [`12106bc0`](context_log.md#12106bc006234e68a461128dbc149fc6--decision--2026-05-26), [`e8c2a14`](context_log.md#e8c2a14--decision--2026-05-10), [`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11), [`3e8b5c9`](context_log.md#3e8b5c9--decision--2026-05-11)

## 0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**New install-ownership category: merge-and-coexist, for shared host-config files.** Adopting the SessionStart hook ([`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30)) makes `.claude/settings.json` the first file Stoa writes into that it does not fully own — a third category beyond spec-owned (hash-checked, overwritten on reinstall) and seed-and-preserve (templated once). Stoa owns exactly one array entry — the SessionStart hook keyed by the command string `bash .stoa/hooks/session-bootstrap` — while the adopter owns the file.

Lifecycle: install = idempotent merge preserving all other keys/hooks (via `python3` + the `json` module — no new dependency, since `python3` is already required for hex-ID generation; deliberately not `jq`); drift detection = entry-presence check, never a whole-file hash (a hash would false-positive on every adopter edit); uninstall = surgical delete of the matching entry. The committed `.claude/settings.json` (not `.claude/settings.local.json`) is the target so the hook travels with the repo like the rest of Stoa's committed install.

**Refs:** [`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27)

## 5cad02d74678427c9b9e89c0a3e59635 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Slim §"Session boot check" to the hook-injection model plus a ~2-line degradation floor.** With the probe now run by the host SessionStart hook ([`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30)), the always-loaded discipline scaffolding is dead weight. Removed: the *"your FIRST tool call MUST be the bootcheck probe"* imperative, the *"no obviously-Stoa-aware operator exemption"* hardening, the adapter-read carve-out, and the entire *"Self-monitoring on boot-discipline breach"* subsection (retroactive-probe + `beta_tracker` breach logging). Kept (functional, not discipline): the `[stoa-init]` block format, two-band return semantics, terminator/fail-closed handling, decline-decision overlay, fidelity-scaling, merge-audit catchup, attribution caching.

New floor: *if the probe output was not injected this session (hook absent / not yet trusted / policy-disabled / missing terminator), run the probe yourself before substantive work.* The floor changes the failure mode from a tool-call-ordering breach (which kept failing) to a presence-check. The self-monitoring rule's data-capture purpose ([`12106bc0`](context_log.md#12106bc006234e68a461128dbc149fc6--decision--2026-05-26)) is complete — the five acme-platform breach entries delivered the evidence; the rule is superseded, not merely trimmed (a rollback of `12106bc0` follows).

## adc55f758d414c5abc9eda5968111a30 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**First-class `install.sh uninstall`.** Once Stoa owns an entry inside the adopter's shared `.claude/settings.json` ([`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30)), "remove the `.stoa/` folder" no longer cleanly uninstalls. `uninstall` must be surgical and non-clobbering: delete only Stoa's SessionStart entry (matched by the `session-bootstrap` command string; leave all other hooks/keys), unset `core.hooksPath` only if it equals `.githooks` (ours), remove the spec-owned files (`stoa-claude.md`, `.claude/commands/stoa.md`, `.claude/agents/stoa-*.md`, `.githooks/*`, `.stoa/hooks/*`, `.stoa/installed`), and strip the dispatcher block from `AGENTS.md`. Preserve and report operator data — `context_log.md` (the decision record), `.stoa/artifacts.md`, `.stoa/beta_tracker.md` — never delete it. Idempotent and safe to re-run.

**Refs:** [`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30), [`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30)

## 314a397eaa8b422e90fdb990ae4e7470 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Non-clobber `core.hooksPath` activation (corrects an existing clobber bug).** The installer set `core.hooksPath=.githooks` whenever the current value was not `.githooks` — silently overwriting an adopter's Husky/Lefthook path. Corrected: set only when unset; if it points elsewhere, leave it and emit a notice that Stoa's git backstops are inactive until the adopter integrates `.githooks/*` or unsets the path. Refines [`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11)'s hook wiring without overturning it.

## f44f00df64a0444fb0b4cfd442b77c40 — observation — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Two open threads carried forward from the SessionStart-hook adoption.** (1) *Cold-clone trust timing is unverified.* Both Claude and Codex gate repo-provided hooks behind one-time per-machine trust, so on a brand-new clone the SessionStart hook may not run until trust is granted. Unverified: whether it fires within the first trusted session or only the next. This calibrates how prominent the degradation floor's wording should be and whether the hook can be advertised as self-healing a fresh clone (no `install.sh` needed). Resolve via a genuine fresh-checkout test; the dogfood reinstall only exercises the already-trusted upgrade path. (2) *Codex host bring-up deferred.* This change ships the Claude binding only; a real Codex binding needs a new host end-to-end (manifest entry, compose target, `src/installers/codex.sh`, `dist/codex/`). The host-neutral spec and the `session-bootstrap` wrapper are written Codex-ready (plain-stdout injection works for both hosts); the Codex adapter/installer is the next host-bring-up effort.

## 05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2 — observation — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Codex's extensibility surface dissolves the subagent-model risk and corrects four bring-up assumptions.** Research against current OpenAI Codex docs (for the [`f44f00df`](context_log.md#f44f00df64a0444fb0b4cfd442b77c40--observation--2026-05-30) thread-2 bring-up) found the integration surface richer than the deferral feared:

- **Native subagents** exist — TOML defs in `.codex/agents/*.toml` (`name`/`description`/`developer_instructions`), gated by `features.multi_agent`, explicit-spawn, default `agents.max_depth = 1` (no nested spawning). A clean analog to Claude's `Agent`/`subagent_type`; the feared "no equivalent → design an inline fallback" case does not obtain.
- **SessionStart** fires on all four matchers (`startup|resume|clear|compact`) and **injects stdout as developer context** — the shared [`session-bootstrap`](src/hooks/session-bootstrap) wrapper ports unchanged, and the degradation floor need not carry clear/compact on Codex.
- The hook feature flag is **`features.hooks`**, not `codex_hooks` (deprecated alias) — the sketch assumption was stale.
- **Custom prompts are user-global + deprecated**; the repo-committable successor is **skills** at `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (markdown + `name`/`description` frontmatter; triggered by name or description-match, not slash-command semantics). The Claude `/stoa` slash dispatcher has no 1:1 Codex slash analog.

Grounds the two binding decisions that follow ([`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`0f646266`](context_log.md#0f646266133a4b9487ad048ca04db303--decision--2026-05-30)). Live-env-gated residue (cold-clone trust timing; repo-local `.codex/config.toml` hook-firing per openai/codex#17532/#19199; `multi_agent` default; exact `.agents/skills/` path + stdout rendering) is captured in `tests/codex-smoke-test.md`.

## 0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Codex subagent binding: native Codex subagents (`.codex/agents/*.toml`), nested calls run inline, inline-only as the degradation floor.** Per OP2, settled before writing `src/adapters/codex.md`. Given native subagents exist ([`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30)), Stoa binds the main-agent-level delegations — WAL-librarian, `coherence --batch`, `coherence --internal-sweep` — to `.codex/agents/stoa-*.toml`, and the installer enables `features.multi_agent`. The two calls Claude runs as sub-subagents — `query` (inside the librarian) and `coherence --pairwise` (inside a coherence agent) — **run inline within the calling subagent on Codex**, staying under Codex's default `agents.max_depth = 1` rather than requiring a raised depth. Rejected as primary binding: inline-only (no delegation) — it permanently violates "never slurp the WAL into parent context" and loses context isolation; it survives only as the **documented degradation floor** when `multi_agent` is unavailable/untrusted (mirrors the bootcheck floor). The `src/subagents/*.md` files (YAML frontmatter + body) transform to TOML at compose (`name`/`description` → keys, body → `developer_instructions`). Adopter-applicability ([`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)): `stoa-`-namespaced agent files, no collision; the floor covers force-disabled `multi_agent`.

**Refs:** [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30), [`f44f00df`](context_log.md#f44f00df64a0444fb0b4cfd442b77c40--observation--2026-05-30), [`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27), [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)

## 0f646266133a4b9487ad048ca04db303 — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Codex `/stoa` dispatcher binding: a single umbrella Codex skill at `.agents/skills/stoa/SKILL.md`.** Per OP2, settled before writing `src/adapters/codex.md`. Codex has no slash-command analog and its custom prompts are user-global + deprecated ([`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30)); the repo-committable mechanism is skills. Chosen: one umbrella skill holding the whole dispatcher (compose-transformed from the same `src/commands/*` sources as Claude's `.claude/commands/stoa.md`, swapping the Claude-specific `$ARGUMENTS` header for a Codex skill header + frontmatter), mirroring Claude's single-dispatcher structure. Rationale: the **primary dispatch path is the always-loaded runtime's prose↔intent routing table** (host-neutral, in `src/core`), so Codex's per-skill description-matching is not needed for reliable triggering; and several subcommands are not operator-facing skills (`query`/`coherence` → subagents per [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30); `index-*` → infra). Rejected: per-command skills (Codex's own suggestion) — better native trigger granularity but duplicates the runtime routing table and fragments a cohesive dispatcher across ~8 dirs. The AGENTS.md dispatcher block + entry point stay shared/host-neutral ([`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27)); only `src/dispatcher.md` gains a `Codex: stoa-codex.md` routing line.

**Refs:** [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30), [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27), [`ccfd9dc7`](context_log.md#ccfd9dc78b314b8abf3d84881cd1e509--decision--2026-05-27), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27)

## e32625de4f43464caf2a8cf74e8524cd — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**The shared `bootcheck-probe` derives its install-recovery host from a `host:` marker field, so remediation strings point at the right `dist/<host>/install.sh`.** Surfaced during the Codex build: the host-neutral probe (shipped to both hosts) hardcoded `dist/claude/install.sh` (and `build/compose.sh claude`) in its `[stoa]` remediation strings — wrong for Codex adopters. Chosen mechanism: installers write `host: <host>` into `.stoa/installed`; the probe reads it into `DIST_HOST` (default `claude` for back-compat with pre-field markers and the marker-missing case, where host is unknowable) and substitutes `dist/${DIST_HOST}/` throughout. One probe script, single-source, host-correct. Verified: a `host: codex` marker renders `dist/codex/install.sh`. Rejected: per-host probe copies (defeats the shared-probe design); a `session-bootstrap` host arg (the path-correctness need is in the probe's own output, not the wrapper). Back-compat: `claude.sh` now writes `host: claude`; old markers without the field still resolve to `claude`, so existing Claude adopters see no change. The 4 Claude-hardcoded paths that live in always-loaded spec text (`src/core/operations.md` §"Session boot check" / §"`[stoa]` chat surfaces") are NOT touched here — they are AI-instruction blocks (see [`984c6316`](context_log.md#984c63161a9748eaa9f659f5a3f6829c--observation--2026-05-30)).

**Refs:** [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`0f646266`](context_log.md#0f646266133a4b9487ad048ca04db303--decision--2026-05-30), [`314a397e`](context_log.md#314a397eaa8b422e90fdb990ae4e7470--decision--2026-05-30), [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)

Surfaced to the operator as an open thread: host-neutralize the four strings (e.g. `dist/<host>/install.sh` with the agent rendering its loaded-adapter host) and WAL the compliance shift, or accept the gap. Minor sibling finding (non-blocking): the per-subcommand HTML comments in `src/commands/*.md` ("Composed into dist/<host>/.claude/commands/stoa.md …") ride into the composed Codex `SKILL.md` verbatim, naming the Claude path; pre-existing, cosmetic, host-neutralizable in the same pass.

## a826f4cc335d41708e9c5d07be4a6bef — decision — 2026-05-30

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Host-neutralize the four Claude-hardcoded install-path surface strings in `src/core/operations.md` via a `<host>` placeholder.** Resolves the open thread from [`984c6316`](context_log.md#984c63161a9748eaa9f659f5a3f6829c--observation--2026-05-30): the §"Session boot check" status-band recovery note + probe-incomplete message, and §"`[stoa]` chat surfaces" operator-imperative example + spec-owned-drift surface, all read `dist/claude/install.sh` / `build/compose.sh claude` — wrong host in the composed `stoa-codex.md`. Settled (operator-confirmed, satisfying the AGENTS.md "reconsider AI-instruction-block edits with the operator first" gate): replace with `dist/<host>/` / `build/compose.sh <host>`, plus a one-line clarifier so the agent resolves `<host>` to its loaded adapter host (`claude`/`codex`). **Compose-time `<host>`→`$HOST` substitution was rejected** — it would introduce templating into `build/compose.sh`, which [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) holds to dumb concatenation; the literal placeholder + clarifier keeps compose dumb and the agent already knows its host. This is the AI-instruction-block compliance shift the rule requires a WAL entry for: the surface strings change wording (Claude-literal → host-parametric) without changing the surface's behavior. The probe SCRIPT path was already fixed separately ([`e32625de`](context_log.md#e32625de4f43464caf2a8cf74e8524cd--decision--2026-05-30)); the same pass host-neutralizes the cosmetic `src/commands/*.md` HTML-comment leak.

## 77cf42bbbcfa4da099902e2e81131783 — observation — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**First live Codex run: the SessionStart hook fires but Codex rejected our stdout — the directive's leading `[` tripped Codex's JSON detection; the degradation floor then rendered `[stoa-init]` correctly.** Operator-driven real Codex CLI run of the shipped bundle. After folder-trust + hook-review approval, Codex ran `session-bootstrap` and failed it: `hook returned invalid session start JSON output`. Root cause (source-verified against openai/codex `codex-rs/hooks`): Codex's SessionStart parser treats stdout whose first non-whitespace char is `{` or `[` as JSON and hard-fails (`deny_unknown_fields`) if it won't deserialize; our directive begins `[stoa session-boot] …`, so the leading `[` triggered JSON parsing of plain prose. **This corrects [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30)'s "injects stdout as developer context" claim:** Codex DOES inject plain stdout, but ONLY when it does not look like JSON (no leading `{`/`[`); Claude has no such heuristic, which is why the same wrapper worked on Claude ([`ed66428c`](context_log.md#ed66428c977b4b56bab92626509e7ec4--observation--2026-05-30)). The degradation floor held: the agent saw the hook fail, ran `bash .stoa/hooks/bootcheck-probe` itself, read `stoa-codex.md`, and rendered a correct `[stoa-init]` block — validating the belt-and-suspenders design under a real injection failure. Incidental (not bugs): the repo's `PreToolUse hook (failed)` lines are a non-Stoa global hook; `branch.master.rebase`/`needs-operator` are clone-local git state. Fixed in [`870e8923`](context_log.md#870e8923106147928988af89fb4ca361--decision--2026-05-31).

## d1693ec18fc14873a84e7e016ad0a460 — decision — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Installer topology: ONE unified `install.sh` that always installs every supported host; retire the per-host installers.** Settled (operator chose Option A over the B/`--host`-selection and C/keep-separate alternatives). The dispatcher is already multi-host (AGENTS.md routes by runtime), but the installers were per-host (`claude.sh`, `codex.sh`), which the dual-install sandbox proved broken: single-host marker (last-write-wins drops the other host's drift-check), mutually-destructive uninstall (codex uninstall rips the shared `.githooks/`, `.stoa/hooks/`, AGENTS.md dispatcher block out from under a co-installed Claude), and ~95% duplicated installer code. Chosen: a single `src/installers/install.sh` → `dist/install.sh` that lays the host-neutral machinery once + every host's runtime/surface/subagents/hook-wiring, records all hosts in one marker, and uninstalls everything (preserving operator data). No `--host` selection (B rejected): "always all hosts, no per-host management" per operator. A Claude-only adopter also gets dormant `.codex/` wiring — acceptable; it only activates if someone opens Codex, and it matches the dispatcher's "the repo supports every host" philosophy. **Consequence (supersedes today's host-parameterization):** with one installer, the install-recovery command is uniformly `bash dist/install.sh install`, so the probe's `host:`-marker→`dist/<host>/` resolution ([`e32625de`](context_log.md#e32625de4f43464caf2a8cf74e8524cd--decision--2026-05-30)) and the operations.md `<host>` placeholder ([`a826f4cc`](context_log.md#a826f4cc335d41708e9c5d07be4a6bef--decision--2026-05-30)) both collapse to a single `dist/install.sh`; rollbacks for those land with the build. The operations.md surface-string change is an always-loaded AI-instruction-block edit, so it lands only with operator sign-off. The dogfood reinstall will add Codex artifacts (`stoa-codex.md`, `.codex/`, `.agents/skills/`) to this repo — it would dogfood both hosts.

**Refs:** [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`0f646266`](context_log.md#0f646266133a4b9487ad048ca04db303--decision--2026-05-30), [`e32625de`](context_log.md#e32625de4f43464caf2a8cf74e8524cd--decision--2026-05-30), [`a826f4cc`](context_log.md#a826f4cc335d41708e9c5d07be4a6bef--decision--2026-05-30), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27)

## ba80f84e28fa415b8217a5e14f7acbe6 — decision — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(opus-4-8,1M)]

**Canonical-branch detection uses `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` instead of `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`, so it resolves the real branch on an unborn repo.** Surfaced by the live Codex re-test ([`12fc206f`](context_log.md#12fc206fe9334322b85c025ea9d95eef--observation--2026-05-31), finding B): installing into a freshly `git init`'d repo with no commits and no remote made the cascade's middle step return the literal `HEAD`, so it set the useless `branch.HEAD.rebase=true` and the probe then flagged the real branch's rebase config as missing. `symbolic-ref --short HEAD` returns the actual branch name even when unborn (reads `.git/HEAD`), and errors to empty on a detached HEAD (falling through to the `main` default). Applied identically in `install.sh` (`wire_git`) and `bootcheck-probe` (Step 4) so probe and setup stay aligned. Verified: fresh-init repo now gets `branch.master.rebase=true` (default branch resolved), `branch.HEAD.rebase` unset, no spurious probe remediation. Adopter-applicable: anyone who installs before their first commit.

**Refs:** [`12fc206f`](context_log.md#12fc206fe9334322b85c025ea9d95eef--observation--2026-05-31), [`314a397e`](context_log.md#314a397eaa8b422e90fdb990ae4e7470--decision--2026-05-30)

The pairwise tiebreaker and the `MULTI-AUTHOR-MT-*` test verifies were updated to be order-agnostic. ## b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800 — decision — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**PR-merge-gap resolution — accept the inconsistency (Option 1), backstop it with a committed audit-cache certificate log; CI hard-prevention stays opt-in advice.** A server-side PR merge (or a fresh clone) integrates WAL entries with no Stoa session present, so two concurrently-authored entries can land mutually-unaudited — Alice's `a1` and Bob's `b1` each checked against the old corpus, never against each other. We accept the post-merge inconsistency (Option 1: no merge gate — consistent with the WAL-as-CRDT/advisory stance and `caab91ea`'s rejection of client fail-drivers) and close the *silent* part with a content-based backstop: a new committed, `union`-merged `.stoa/audit-cache` — an append-only log of coherence **certificates**. A certificate records a *set* of entries checked mutually-coherent; a pair `(X,Y)` is covered iff some certificate contains both, so concurrent partial certs can never `union` into a fabricated joint coverage (the exact failure that killed the earlier covered-set idea). Certificates are single-parent base-chained deltas (`base:<cert>` + `delta:<hexes>`) — order-free and date-inert, causality in the base pointer the way the WAL's lives in `Refs:` — read via a cover-or-gap scan (audit `WAL − covered` against the full WAL, append the reconciling cert) and compacted via `/stoa audit` snapshots. Emitted by every coherence check over committed entries (commit-time Layer 2; cadence-#6 catchup; boot scan; `/stoa audit`), audit in a subagent and the one-line append in-context. A certificate is a supersedable cache, not gospel — a deeper check or newer model can overturn one (append a corrected snapshot; resolve the real conflict via `rollback`); every cache failure degrades to a re-audit, never to false coverage. Orthogonal to `9b2c8e4`'s `.stoa/index/audit-state` watermark (that tracks vector-index staleness against merges; this tracks WAL-coherence coverage — different objects that coexist). Ships v0.11.0; spec §"Audit cache".

**Refs:** [`caab91ea`](context_log.md#caab91ea57ee433a82199dce086f8788--wont-do--2026-05-26), [`1da2f2fc`](context_log.md#1da2f2fc9ea84bcdb5567fd8fcd78264--observation--2026-05-29), [`92cbef74`](context_log.md#92cbef74e6d24d218d6fdd3f890447a8--decision--2026-05-26), [`9b2c8e4`](context_log.md#9b2c8e4--decision--2026-05-17)

## 7ef53bed88454af5a947e59659a9ee82 — decision — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Cadence #6 becomes content-triggered (the audit-cache coverage delta); the `post-merge`/`post-rewrite` git hooks and the `.stoa/state/merge-pending-audit` marker are retired.** With the committed certificate log in place ([`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31)), the cadence-#6 catchup trigger moves from "a local git hook fired" to "the WAL gained entries not yet certified-together" (`WAL − covered`). The content trigger strictly subsumes the hooks: it catches the server-side PR merge and the fresh clone — neither of which fires a local hook — as well as every local merge/rebase the hooks caught. The bootcheck probe's coverage check replaces its old marker read; the in-session path stays the stale-cache rejection at next T2 write (`c95a8889`). This preserves the proxy-immune, anti-gate stance of `caab91ea` — we replace one backstop *mechanism* (deterministic hook + marker) with another (content-triggered coverage over the cert log), not reopen the strict-fail question — and is exactly what `1da2f2fc` anticipated (detection power lives in the sweep, not the marker, so the marker and the hooks that feed it are dispensable). `.stoa/state/.gitignore` stays for any future per-clone runtime state; the installer removes the orphaned root hooks on upgrade.

**Refs:** [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31), [`caab91ea`](context_log.md#caab91ea57ee433a82199dce086f8788--wont-do--2026-05-26), [`1da2f2fc`](context_log.md#1da2f2fc9ea84bcdb5567fd8fcd78264--observation--2026-05-29), [`c95a8889`](context_log.md#c95a8889f3844f7592fd1590b9fbd173--decision--2026-05-25)

**Cadence-#6 pairwise supersession-direction flips to `Refs:`-edge-first; the date header is demoted to a rough tiebreak only.** The `/stoa coherence --pairwise` subagent decided which of two contradicting entries is "newer" (the rollback target) by date header first, `Refs:` edge second — making a *strict causal* call rest primarily on a coarse timestamp, and contradicting `4a7e6c0`, which already declared the date authoritative for *authorship* only, not integration/causal order. Extends the §Ordering / causality-in-`Refs:` arc ([`4a7e6c0`](context_log.md#4a7e6c0--decision--2026-05-12), [`2e8f3a1`](context_log.md#2e8f3a1--decision--2026-05-12), OP3 [`5bcbe16a`](context_log.md#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19)) into the pairwise verdict ([`b0122b1f`](context_log.md#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18)).

## 4c21933944b14ab7a1e3442c724c1ab4 — decision — 2026-05-31

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Bootcheck coverage check computes `covered()` precisely per leaf, not via a leaf-count shortcut — fixes a false-pending after reconciliation.** The v0.11.0 probe ([`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31)) used a cheap heuristic: clean iff every WAL hex appears in the cache AND there is exactly one leaf certificate. The two-clone divergence test surfaced the flaw — after a divergence is reconciled, the reconciling cert covers the whole WAL but the subsumed divergent cert remains a *dead leaf*, so the chain has ≥2 leaves and the heuristic falsely reports coverage-pending until the next `/stoa audit` prunes it (the whack-a-mole the design set out to kill). Replaced Step 6 with the precise §"Audit cache" reader: clean iff SOME leaf certificate's `covered`-set (its delta accumulated along the base chain to root) ⊇ the WAL hex-set. Divergence detection stays correct (two divergent leaves, neither covering all → pending); the post-reconciliation false flag is gone (the reconciling leaf covers all → clean, dead leaf ignored). Fail-closed to pending. The spec's reader semantics were already precise — only the probe's shortcut diverged, now aligned. Regression-locked by `tests/bootcheck-probe-test.sh` Cases 13–14 and the real two-clone `tests/audit-cache-divergence-test.sh`. No version bump — v0.11.0 is unpushed, so this corrects it pre-release.

**Refs:** [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31)

## 3a5583d8af64433e995c4a2b3cf22fdd — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Codex adapter gets an autonomous-spawn directive: spawning native subagents is the expected default, not gated on an explicit operator delegation request.** Added to [`src/adapters/codex.md`](src/adapters/codex.md) §"Subagent invocation": a non-trivial WAL query routes to the WAL-librarian on AI judgment per §"WAL access pattern", with no operator-permission step; if the host ever surfaces a spawn-approval prompt it is not grounds to decline — proceed; staying inline to avoid spawning is a discipline breach, not a safe default. Also tightened the degradation floor to be the ONLY inline case (multi_agent unavailable OR `.codex/` untrusted) and added a carve-out: in inline mode, read the relevant WAL region into main context and reason there — the never-slurp-into-parent rule presupposes a subagent doing the slurp, so grep-slicing is not the inline path.

Motivated by the soft-stop finding ([`fc6ce18e`](context_log.md#fc6ce18e458f479aa5791ea8ec6465ed--observation--2026-06-01)): the Codex subagent binding ([`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30)) and the access-pattern intent ([`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30)) always intended autonomous delegation — the WAL is silent on any operator-opt-in gate — but the adapter's only non-spawn guidance was the "degradation floor," which the agent read as license to default inline. Claude Code is unaffected (its Agent-tool delegation already fires autonomously); Codex-adapter-only sharpening. Verification still open: an autonomous re-run (non-trivial WAL query with NO delegation instruction) to confirm the directive flips the default.

**Refs:** [`fc6ce18e`](context_log.md#fc6ce18e458f479aa5791ea8ec6465ed--observation--2026-06-01), [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30)

## 362070e755474ce5b14e9ac8266e5789 — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Boot cover-or-gap scan: the main agent computes the gap from WAL headers and delegates the body audit — never Reads the WAL into main context.** Clarified §"Session boot check" and the cadence-#6 "Bootcheck coverage scan" bullet in [`src/core/operations.md`](src/core/operations.md) to align the main-agent-facing wording with §"Audit cache" → "Audit in subagent": on a coverage-pending anchor, the main agent computes the gap as a hex-set diff (`WAL − covered`) from a header grep — headers only, never Reading `context_log.md` into main context — then delegates the body-level audit of the gap to the `/stoa coherence --internal-sweep` subagent (which slurps in its own context) and appends the returned certificate. Host-neutral (`src/core`), so it lands for every adopter — the boot-scan over-read scaled with WAL size and was the cost trap behind the spend-cap hit ([`96347675`](context_log.md#96347675bff8412c9bd1e7e256b3f543--observation--2026-06-01)).
