## 1377aa2fff644771ad29c741579e5e64 — observation — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**WAL-retrieval mechanics are under-propagated across the four `src/subagents/` procedure files — not over-duplicated. `stoa-coherence-batch` carries a dangling cross-reference; `batch` and `internal-sweep` lack the librarian's degraded-path fallback.** The full slurp/retrieve/grep ladder + slurp threshold lives only in [`stoa-wal-librarian.md`](src/subagents/stoa-wal-librarian.md). `stoa-coherence-batch.md` says *"slurp if feasible — see thresholds in stoa-wal-librarian.md"* — a cross-reference the running subagent CANNOT follow, since subagents load only their own procedure file (siblings are not co-loaded). That is a self-containment violation: the agent should never need an out-of-band reference for runtime compliance. `stoa-coherence-internal-sweep.md` carries only *"slurp if feasible"* — no threshold, no fallback. So `batch` and `internal-sweep`, which face the SAME scale problem as the librarian, do not inherit its degraded-path handling: at adopter scale, if the WAL outgrows slurp-feasibility, they have no documented behavior and would improvise or silently truncate. Dogfood-invisible (this WAL slurps fine, so the threshold is moot and the dangling ref cosmetic); it bites adopters with large WALs. The shape is the inverse of "same logic pasted 4×" — it is single-sourced-but-under-propagated, with one unreachable pointer. `stoa-coherence-pairwise` is the genuine exception (greps two named hexes by design; correctly opts out of slurp). Motivates the refactor in [`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01) / [`adb5d4e8`](context_log.md#adb5d4e8b7ba4346a0f470b555784feb--decision--2026-06-01).

## 5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653 — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Extract WAL-retrieval primitives into a shared `src/subagents/_wal-tools.md`, concatenated at build-time into the three slurp-composing subagents; `stoa-coherence-pairwise` stays standalone.** To kill the drift surface behind [`1377aa2f`](context_log.md#1377aa2fff644771ad29c741579e5e64--observation--2026-06-01), the slurp / grep / semantic primitives + the slurp-feasibility threshold (~30% of context, ≈9000 lines) move to one shared source file holding tool DEFINITIONS ONLY — no path-selection policy (policy in the shared file would rebuild the bug elsewhere). `build/compose.sh` concatenates it into the three consumers that compose the tools — `stoa-wal-librarian`, `stoa-coherence-batch`, `stoa-coherence-internal-sweep` — via an explicit consumer list, skipping `_`-prefixed files as standalone agents (the convention `compose_dispatcher` already uses for commands). Placement is tools-first (the composition logic depends on the primitives — topological order + instructional priming); under the frontmatter-must-lead constraint this requires a head/tail split of each consumer (frontmatter+Purpose → toolbox → composition+Output). This is single-source-in-`src/` + self-contained-output-in-`dist/`: the toolbox text is physically present in each composed agent — subagents do not co-load, so a runtime reference would re-introduce the self-containment violation, and build-time concatenation is the only way to get both single-source authoring and self-contained output. **Pure concatenation, NOT templating** — consistent with how `compose_runtime` already assembles the runtime from manifest pieces, preserving the composer's dumb-concatenation property. `pairwise` is EXCLUDED: its obligation (two named hexes) is met entirely by grep, so the slurp/semantic primitives would be dead context; it keeps its one-line grep inline. **Rejected alternatives:** (1) runtime delegation (coherence subagents calling the librarian) — blocked: the librarian returns ANSWERS (hex+headline+summary), not the raw corpus that classification needs in its own context, and subagents cannot spawn subagents; (2) consolidating the coherence trio into one mode-branched subagent — mode-branching dilutes per-invocation prompt crispness and only de-dupes batch↔sweep while leaving the librarian's copy, missing the actual drift target; (3) inline copies + sync comment — silent drift has no observable trigger (miss a file and nothing signals it — the failure that produced [`1377aa2f`](context_log.md#1377aa2fff644771ad29c741579e5e64--observation--2026-06-01)), so hand-sync is the bet that already lost. EXTENDS the triple-mode-primitive unification ([`b0122b1f`](context_log.md#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18)) and the agent-first/slurp access pattern down to the subagent-file layer that [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) created.

**Refs:** [`1377aa2f`](context_log.md#1377aa2fff644771ad29c741579e5e64--observation--2026-06-01), [`b0122b1f`](context_log.md#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`8c65450c`](context_log.md#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18), [`89370375`](context_log.md#89370375f20943ba8d06a319a429ed08--decision--2026-05-18), [`a8a0b715`](context_log.md#a8a0b7155913467b9c1ab1cbc027437a--decision--2026-05-18), [`5bcbe16a`](context_log.md#5bcbe16a06db47f6a6b009296478f07c--decision--2026-05-19), [`fc3d3c37`](context_log.md#fc3d3c37688c4391bcd95d8e7787698c--decision--2026-05-18), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27)

## adb5d4e8b7ba4346a0f470b555784feb — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Reframe subagent WAL-retrieval from imperative cascade to declarative: coverage obligation + composable tools + absolute under-claim invariant; composition objective is expected quality of meeting the obligation, NOT cost.** Each toolbox-consuming subagent ([`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01)) declares a COVERAGE OBLIGATION (librarian: enough relevant entries to answer — relevance-bounded coverage acceptable; batch: every prior entry a new entry could contradict; internal-sweep: every pair in the audited set — all-pairs / gap×full) and then COMPOSES slurp/grep/semantic however its judgment says best meets that obligation on the actual WAL — including partial combinations (e.g. slurp the recent slice + semantic the tail), not a fixed pick-one cascade. The cascade ("slurp ELSE semantic ELSE grep") was imperative-creep that foreclosed composition and could not express obligation-dependent strategy; the declarative form is both more correct and shorter. Two things stay strict: (1) the **under-claim invariant** — certify/assert only the coverage actually achieved; surface the gap; at the limit refuse to certify rather than over-claim. This is the load-bearing safety property: it bounds incomplete coverage to honest under-certification, never a false "clean," which is what makes loose composition safe. (2) the slurp-feasibility threshold survives as a tool PROPERTY (a fact about slurp), not a branch condition. **Objective = expected quality of meeting the obligation, not least cost.** "Least cost" was ambiguous (tokens? time? context?) and off-philosophy: the Layer-2 rule already gates coherence on entry class *"never on processing cost,"* and OP1 makes agent capability the primary quality lever — a quality objective rides model/context improvements (slurp-complete stays feasible at larger WALs; the dilution penalty shrinks), a cost objective fights them. Context-pollution folds INTO quality (loading obligation-irrelevant entries dilutes reasoning → worse answer), so a one-line declarative PROPERTY note on slurp ("completeness and focus both bear on quality; more context is not automatically better") prevents the degenerate always-slurp-the-max read without reintroducing cost. **Accepted residual:** a pure-quality objective sometimes slurps more than strictly necessary for an identical answer (bounded token waste) — accepted deliberately; gating it with imperative cost language would degrade quality under context pressure (rigid rules are what a squeezed agent sacrifices first) and forfeit the compounding property. Instance of the declarative-over-imperative bias ([`4b3c686b`](context_log.md#4b3c686be138451e8c8af026a5f1aa1d--decision--2026-05-24)) and FP1 (loose framework, AI as interpreter); the quality objective grounds in agent-first quality ([`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18)).

**Refs:** [`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01), [`1377aa2f`](context_log.md#1377aa2fff644771ad29c741579e5e64--observation--2026-06-01), [`4b3c686b`](context_log.md#4b3c686be138451e8c8af026a5f1aa1d--decision--2026-05-24), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`89370375`](context_log.md#89370375f20943ba8d06a319a429ed08--decision--2026-05-18), [`a8a0b715`](context_log.md#a8a0b7155913467b9c1ab1cbc027437a--decision--2026-05-18), [`fc3d3c37`](context_log.md#fc3d3c37688c4391bcd95d8e7787698c--decision--2026-05-18)

## bea7ae7d2f974d218eab8e170a235ac1 — observation — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**The audit-cache showed a per-session certification treadmill, rooted in an undesigned commit-time/boot delta asymmetry.** Surfaced from a acme-platform adopter report and confirmed in this repo's own cache. Sessions characteristically end with an EC:WEAK observation (cadence #4 pre-compact/clear, or end-of-impl). An EC:WEAK-only commit skips Layer 2 ([`d961de2c`](context_log.md#d961de2ce2f54fcc96d070ca33bf21e0--decision--2026-05-25)), so it emits no certificate; the bootcheck coverage delta ([`7ef53bed`](context_log.md#7ef53bed88454af5a947e59659a9ee82--decision--2026-05-31)) is **class-blind**, so it flags that uncertified WEAK tail at every next session start, and the boot cover-or-gap scan certifies it — a standalone `.stoa/audit-cache` append decoupled from any real work, plus an internal-sweep subagent spawn, every session, over a ~1-entry WEAK gap. Concrete instance: commit `a088f85` appended only cert `16cb73ea` to certify three EC:WEAK sketch-hygiene observations (`3ec03a26`, `a924431b`, `878451f6`) that were committed weak-only in `3c9d8b4`. Two undesigned facts behind the treadmill: (1) commit-time Layer 2 certifies `delta:` = "this commit's entries", not the coverage gap, so a separately-committed WEAK tail is **never swept by a later STRONG commit** — it persists until `/stoa audit`; (2) the coverage delta + boot scan are class-blind while commit-time Layer 2 is class-aware (it skips EC:WEAK-only) — an asymmetry never reasoned about. The cert-log ([`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31)) was designed for the PR-merge-gap / fresh-clone case; the WEAK-tail certification consequence is incidental. Resolved by [`c891f009`](context_log.md#c891f009969841aea0c74aed34ca7d90--decision--2026-06-01).

**Refs:** [`d961de2c`](context_log.md#d961de2ce2f54fcc96d070ca33bf21e0--decision--2026-05-25), [`7ef53bed`](context_log.md#7ef53bed88454af5a947e59659a9ee82--decision--2026-05-31), [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31), [`c891f009`](context_log.md#c891f009969841aea0c74aed34ca7d90--decision--2026-06-01)

## c891f009969841aea0c74aed34ca7d90 — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Unify certificate emission on one rule: a certificate covers the full coverage gap `W − covered(prior leaf)` and is emitted by the automatic paths only when that gap contains an EC:STRONG entry.** Resolves the treadmill + asymmetry in [`bea7ae7d`](context_log.md#bea7ae7d2f974d218eab8e170a235ac1--observation--2026-06-01). Two coupled changes to the automatic cert paths (commit-time Layer 2 + boot cover-or-gap scan): **(1) delta = gap.** A certificate covers the entire uncertified gap, not just the triggering commit batch — one cert sweeps any earlier EC:WEAK/DEFERRED tail along with this work, across however many commit batches the gap spans (`covered` reaches the current full WAL at emission). This replaces commit-time Layer 2's `delta:<this commit's entries>`. **(2) EC:STRONG-gap trigger.** Emission fires only when the gap holds an EC:STRONG entry (`decision`/`won't-do`/`rollback`); a gap that is exclusively EC:WEAK/DEFERRED (`observation`/`table`) emits no certificate at commit or boot. Generalizes the commit-time EC:WEAK-only Layer-2 skip ([`d961de2c`](context_log.md#d961de2ce2f54fcc96d070ca33bf21e0--decision--2026-05-25)) to the gap and extends the same class-awareness to the boot scan and to the bootcheck probe's coverage check, which now keys `clean`/`pending` on whether any EC:STRONG hex is uncovered (not on full-WAL coverage). **Invariant:** EC:STRONG entries are always certified-together; EC:WEAK/DEFERRED entries are certified lazily — swept into a certificate by the next STRONG-triggered gap audit (along with the work, or at boot recovery if the commit-time check was missed); the EC:WEAK/DEFERRED tail trailing the last EC:STRONG entry is intentionally left uncertified (under-claim-safe). Effect: kills the per-session audit-cache churn + boot subagent spawn for the common WEAK-tail case, and makes commit-time and boot the same operation — audit the gap when it holds a STRONG entry. Safe under [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31)'s anti-fabrication invariant (certs stay sets; divergent concurrent partials leave the cross-pair uncovered → reconciled by the next gap audit) and [`7ef53bed`](context_log.md#7ef53bed88454af5a947e59659a9ee82--decision--2026-05-31)'s anti-gate stance (narrows a backstop trigger; the backstop still fires for every STRONG gap — the only case that can carry a Superseding, since EC:WEAK ([`4d2cc9d4`](context_log.md#4d2cc9d496824db4b8701424ff9a3f85--decision--2026-05-25)) cannot supersede a forward commitment). Accepted cost: a cross-author EC:WEAK observation arriving *alone* won't get a boot-scan Adjacent/Converging `Refs:` link (lowest stakes; had no Layer-1 pass anyway; `/stoa audit` backstops; any WEAK arriving alongside a STRONG is still swept). **`/stoa audit` is unchanged** — it remains the explicit full-coverage reset and snapshots everything it re-verifies (open operator's-call point: whether it too should skip the trailing WEAK tail for strict uniformity — left full for now). Adopter-applicable: keys off the entry-type header field (controlled vocabulary), never body regex, so no false positives on adopter content; the treadmill hits every adopter (sessions end with observations), so the fix is more valuable to adopters than to the dogfood.

**Refs:** [`bea7ae7d`](context_log.md#bea7ae7d2f974d218eab8e170a235ac1--observation--2026-06-01), [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31), [`7ef53bed`](context_log.md#7ef53bed88454af5a947e59659a9ee82--decision--2026-05-31), [`d961de2c`](context_log.md#d961de2ce2f54fcc96d070ca33bf21e0--decision--2026-05-25), [`4d2cc9d4`](context_log.md#4d2cc9d496824db4b8701424ff9a3f85--decision--2026-05-25), [`362070e7`](context_log.md#362070e755474ce5b14e9ac8266e5789--decision--2026-06-01)

## 8439b81979e74fe3944a5cff82953f37 — decision — 2026-06-01

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Aligned the runtime §"WAL access pattern" with the declarative subagent reframe — removed the subagent-internal retrieval detail from the runtime, and reframed main-agent routing from a trivial/non-trivial taxonomy to the parent-context-lean principle. Resolves the parked [`c5f3b146`](context_log.md#c5f3b146654f4e5fb954c94222dd697b--table--2026-06-01).** Two moves in [`src/core/wal.md`](src/core/wal.md) (+ a sibling touch in [`src/core/operations.md`](src/core/operations.md) and the librarian's orientation line). **(1) Option B — runtime stops describing the librarian's internal retrieval.** The old §"WAL access pattern" enumerated the subagent's retrieval as a pick-one cascade (Slurp path / Retrieval path / Fallback + threshold + the `/stoa query` T1/T2 note); that detail is now owned solely by the subagent files ([`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01) `_wal-tools.md` + tails). The runtime keeps only main-agent-facing content (ground via the librarian, never-slurp-into-parent, routing, what the librarian returns, scope discipline, pairwise routing). Same single-source lesson as the toolbox refactor, applied to the runtime↔subagent boundary; also trims every-session runtime context per the AGENTS.md rule *"does this clause change [main-agent] behavior? if no, cut"* — the main agent never executes those paths, the subagent does. The `operations.md` Layer 2 parenthetical `(slurp / index-retrieval / fallback per §"WAL access pattern")` likewise collapsed to `owns its retrieval (per §"WAL access pattern")`. **(2) Reframed main-agent routing from taxonomy to principle.** The trivial/non-trivial split was the last imperative artifact in the section — a two-bucket label defined by an example list, when whether a query floods parent context is not intrinsic to the query but relative to whether *this* agent can name+target the entries it needs (operator's catch: the classification "depends on what's in the agent"). Replaced with the principle it was a proxy for, grounded in the already-present never-slurp rule: **handle in parent what you can name and fetch with a bounded targeted read; delegate anything that requires surveying entries you can't enumerate up front.** Examples retained as illustrations; *"when in doubt, delegate"* folded in as the safe-direction tiebreaker. Safety mirrors the toolbox's under-claim invariant: looser routing fails toward delegation (cheap), and the hard never-slurp-into-parent rule ([`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#e7c4b29--observation--2026-05-10), [`8c65450c`](context_log.md#8c65450caa024834886df98f5844900e--decision--2026-05-18)) stays as backstop. **Scope:** OP1 in [`src/core/methodology.md`](src/core/methodology.md) reviewed and left as-is (principle-level, already consistent); the Codex adapter's *"non-trivial WAL query"* autonomous-spawn references left untouched — plain-English descriptors in a separately-tuned block, still valid under the reframe. Instance of declarative-over-imperative ([`4b3c686b`](context_log.md#4b3c686be138451e8c8af026a5f1aa1d--decision--2026-05-24)) extending the subagent reframe ([`adb5d4e8`](context_log.md#adb5d4e8b7ba4346a0f470b555784feb--decision--2026-06-01)) up into the runtime.

Removed from the dispatcher: the "subagent picks the retrieval path — Slurp / Retrieval / Fallback" cascade; the "retrieval scopes within whichever path" enumeration (in-flight is the runtime's Layer 1 rule, the staleness gate is `/stoa query`'s, indexed retrieval is the subagent's — none is the dispatcher's to describe); and the 4-rung fidelity ladder — all subagent-internal composition now single-sourced ([`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01)) and declarative ([`adb5d4e8`](context_log.md#adb5d4e8b7ba4346a0f470b555784feb--decision--2026-06-01)). The dispatcher now states only WHAT coherence does (delegate → classify → surface → read-only); the coherence subagent owns HOW it retrieves ("composes its retrieval to meet its coverage obligation; the dispatcher consumes the result, not the path"), mirroring the runtime move ([`8439b819`](context_log.md#8439b81979e74fe3944a5cff82953f37--decision--2026-06-01)). ## dd5143fd9be14e4fa425b164f835e60a — observation — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Confirmed: the subagent "semantic" retrieval primitive (`/stoa query`) is un-runnable from subagent context — it is a slash command, but Stoa subagents have no Skill tool.** Surfaced from an adopter session in the acme-platform repo: the `stoa-wal-librarian`, prescribed `/stoa query "<intent>"` as its semantic primitive and holding only `Read, Bash, Grep`, shelled it via Bash → `no such file or directory: /stoa` → silently fell back to slurp+grep. Reproduced live this session (the librarian dispatched here hit the same error). Root cause: the primitive traces to the dispatcher-era `/stoa query` interface ([`5eceaacc`](context_log.md#5eceaacc55c543129b15f508001a3e7a--decision--2026-05-24), [`b0122b1f`](context_log.md#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18)) and was carried wholesale into the single-sourced subagent toolbox ([`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01)) without re-examination against subagent execution context — slash commands need the Skill tool the main agent has and subagents lack.

Blast radius (all spec-owned, ships to every adopter): [`src/subagents/_wal-tools.md`](src/subagents/_wal-tools.md) (shared `semantic` primitive), [`src/subagents/stoa-wal-librarian.tail.md`](src/subagents/stoa-wal-librarian.tail.md) ("lead with semantic (`/stoa query`)"), and [`src/adapters/codex.md`](src/adapters/codex.md) (the `/stoa query` "run inline as a nested sub-subagent" row + depth rule — built on the false premise that `query` is a *spawnable subagent*; it is a Bash-runnable script, `.stoa/index/query.py`). Severity is low today and rises only at scale: per the Agent-first posture ([`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`d45489b7`](context_log.md#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18)) slurp is the primary path and the index is opt-in ([`d5b9df87`](context_log.md#d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af--decision--2026-05-18)); semantic only "leads" in the slurp-infeasible regime, which is precisely where an un-runnable primitive degrades retrieval to lexical-only grep silently. Two adjacent findings: the `Read,Bash,Grep` subagent tool grant is itself undocumented in the WAL, and the `/stoa coherence --pairwise` "the subagent invokes" prose in [`src/core/wal.md`](src/core/wal.md) is the same class of misframe (no live bug — the pairwise subagent only Read+greps). Fix in [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03).

**Refs:** [`5ef60619`](context_log.md#5ef60619146c487eab2645c2a89be653--decision--2026-06-01), [`5eceaacc`](context_log.md#5eceaacc55c543129b15f508001a3e7a--decision--2026-05-24), [`b0122b1f`](context_log.md#b0122b1facf5413eaaf25896fbc0c706--decision--2026-05-18), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`d45489b7`](context_log.md#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18), [`d5b9df87`](context_log.md#d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af--decision--2026-05-18)

## f16a414274554962a92fdf50470f1777 — rollback — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Rolls back [`d5b9df87`](context_log.md#d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af--decision--2026-05-18) — the vector index is no longer opt-in. It ships and installs by default; the opt-in / scale-triggered install posture is retired.** `d5b9df87` made install opt-in on cost grounds (~600MB / Python / model "friction without payoff" for adopters below slurp-infeasible scale). Two things overturn that: (1) the footprint is accepted — cost is no longer the deciding constraint; (2) the slurp-infeasible regime is **not hypothetical** — Stoa's own WAL is 11,035 lines / ~342k tokens, past the ~30% / ≈9000-line slurp threshold for *every* agent. A standard-context subagent cannot fit it at all (both subagents dispatched this session declared it "too large to slurp" and used the installed index); even a 1M-context agent sits at ~34%, over the line. A serious, long-lived project crosses this threshold — Stoa did. Always-installed is also operationally cleaner than threshold-triggered install (front-loads cost to install-time rather than stalling mid-session at scale; no fuzzy per-agent threshold detection) and eliminates the conditional-primitive bug class behind [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03).

**The Agent-first USE posture ([`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18)) is unchanged — slurp stays primary; the index remains a fallback in *use*, engaged only beyond slurp. Only install *timing* changes: opt-in → always-install.** This also overtakes the "considered and declined: default-install" aside in [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03) — the A-fix core stands; that scoped-out aside is now settled the other way after continued deliberation this session. New design in [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03).

**Refs:** [`d5b9df87`](context_log.md#d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af--decision--2026-05-18), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03)

## e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf — decision — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Always-ship the vector index, best-effort-install, slurp-primary use — the design replacing the opt-in posture rolled back in [`f16a4142`](context_log.md#f16a414274554962a92fdf50470f1777--rollback--2026-06-03).** Five commitments:

1. **Scripts ship + install unconditionally, spec-owned.** `query.py` / `embed.py` / `.gitignore` move to canonical source (`src/index/`), compose into `dist/.stoa/index/` (shared payload, like `.githooks/`), and `install.sh` places them — hash-tracked in `.stoa/installed`, overwritten on reinstall. This is what fixes the [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03) gap (scripts were committed only to this repo's dogfood `.stoa/index/`, never packaged in `dist/`; the refactors [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27) / [`d1693ec1`](context_log.md#d1693ec18fc14873a84e7e016ad0a460--decision--2026-05-31) orphaned the place-them-unconditionally step `d5b9df87` had specified).

2. **Substrate (venv + model + sqlite) installs by default but BEST-EFFORT, not fail-loud.** `install.sh` attempts the venv/deps/model/initial-embed; if the environment can't support it (no Python 3.9+, insufficient disk, no network) it degrades — Stoa still installs, the index is simply absent, and slurp+grep carries retrieval. This reverses the fail-loud stance of the original baseline-install [`a5e3c92`](context_log.md#a5e3c92--decision--2026-05-17): fail-loud was correct only when the index was the *primary* lookup (pre-Agent-first); once [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18) made it a fallback, graceful degradation follows. Required by the AGENTS.md adopter-applicability discipline — a constrained adopter must not have their whole Stoa install break over an index they may never need.

3. **How-to-fix surfaces live OUT of always-loaded context.** On degrade, `install.sh` prints a clear stdout message (reason + "Stoa is functional on slurp+grep" + the exact later-install command) — terminal-only, zero session-context cost. Optionally a bootcheck remediation line, **gated** on "WAL over slurp-threshold AND index absent" so small-WAL adopters never see it. The always-loaded runtime (`stoa-<host>.md`) carries none of it.

4. **`/stoa index install` becomes the explicit (re)install / repair path** — no longer the only install path (install.sh now does the default attempt); the command force-(re)builds the substrate on demand.

5. **Post-commit refresh hook promoted** dogfood-only `.githooks/post-commit` → `src/hooks/` → `dist/` (design: [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17)), keeping its `[ -x venv ] || exit 0` no-op guard so it's inert when no index is installed. The BGE-base model choice ([`c4f9e87`](context_log.md#c4f9e87--observation--2026-05-17)) is unchanged.

Implementation sequenced as three coherent commits (foundation: source+compose+place; substrate best-effort install; hook + `/stoa index install` rewrite + VECTOR-test rework + degradation tests). The index-vs-slurp-vs-grep quality benchmark on `tests/fixtures/coherence-cases.md` is a separate, non-blocking arc that would give the Agent-first slurp-primacy bet its first empirical test.

**Refs:** [`f16a4142`](context_log.md#f16a414274554962a92fdf50470f1777--rollback--2026-06-03), [`d5b9df87`](context_log.md#d5b9df8715a448ada7e04f6b9aa997af--decision--2026-05-18), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18), [`a5e3c92`](context_log.md#a5e3c92--decision--2026-05-17), [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17), [`c4f9e87`](context_log.md#c4f9e87--observation--2026-05-17), [`ba09921a`](context_log.md#ba09921ae9a54626a7b39c023e47bc31--decision--2026-06-03), [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27), [`d1693ec1`](context_log.md#d1693ec18fc14873a84e7e016ad0a460--decision--2026-05-31)

## aea4063b40d8433e95a751d600fc6b56 — observation — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Dogfood substance-compression early signal: this repo's `context_log.md` is ~1% of the raw main-transcript bytes of the sessions that produced it (~99×), ~0.56% of the full session footprint (~178×).** Measured on this laptop (Stoa developed exclusively here). Denominator scoped to the `stoa-ai` Claude Code project only — its substance distillate IS this WAL; the acme-platform precursor distilled to a *different* artifact (the frozen `design-methodology.md`) so its sessions are excluded to keep the comparison apples-to-apples. Numbers: WAL 1,383,470 B (409 entries); 97 main transcripts 137.3 MB → WAL = 1.01% (98.99% reduction); + subagent transcripts + cached tool-results (1,073 files) → 246.4 MB → WAL = 0.56% (99.44% reduction). Stoa test scaffolds (coldclone/boot) add <0.4 MB, no material change.

**Caveat — this is a volume/read-burden ratio, not a fidelity ratio.** It quantifies how many fewer bytes a reviewer faces vs a "preserve-the-session-log-with-the-PR" approach; it does NOT measure whether the WAL retained the *right* substance (the unmeasured quality-degradation axis). The denominator is also dominated by mechanical content the alternative also preserves (file reads, tool I/O, re-injected `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, system reminders, thinking) — so the headline ratio conflates *overhead elimination* with *decision distillation*. A substance-to-substance cut (WAL vs human+assistant prose only) would land materially lower and is the obvious next refinement. First hard byte-anchor for the value-prop claim; prior entries only framed it conceptually.

## 708f15a5055a489e915f0a3403db447b — observation — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Substance-to-substance refinement of [`aea4063b`](context_log.md#aea4063b40d8433e95a751d600fc6b56--observation--2026-06-03): against conversation prose (not raw bytes), this repo's WAL is a ~3.6× distillation — and against human-typed input alone it is a 2.8× *expansion*.** Method: across all 97 stoa-ai main transcripts, keep only message `text` blocks (assistant prose + genuine human prose); drop `tool_use`/`tool_result`, `attachment` lines (6.86 MB of pasted file-context project-wide), `thinking` (stored as 0-byte signatures), and the injected impostors riding inside user-role messages — compaction summaries, `<task-notification>` events, and `<command-*>`/`<system-reminder>`/hook wrappers (1.41 MB meta + 0.71 MB task-notif that a naive human-prose count would miscredit).

**The ladder** (denominator / WAL, WAL = 1.383 MB): raw transcripts 137.48 MB → **99.4×**; human+assistant prose 5.01 MB (3.64% of raw) → **3.62×** (WAL = 27.6% of all prose exchanged); assistant prose only 4.50 MB → 3.26×; human prose only 0.50 MB → **0.36×** (WAL is 2.8× the bytes the operator ever typed). Reading: the 99× headline is mostly *overhead elimination*; the honest *distillation* number to cite to an evaluator is ~3.6×. The denominator is ~90% assistant-authored — "human+assistant" ≈ "assistant" by volume; relative to human input the WAL is an expansion, i.e. the value-add is capturing AI-elaborated substance from terse cues ("yes, proceed" / "push" / "you drive"), not compressing operator words.

**Caveat unchanged + sharpened:** still a volume ratio, not fidelity. At 3.6× the denominator is genuine deliberation prose, so "did the right ~28% survive?" becomes the sharp, unanswered question — resolvable only by the deferred semantic-quality pass. The prose denominator still carries throwaway (option tables, narration, `[stoa-init]` blocks, restating), so 3.6× *understates* useful-substance distillation; isolating that requires labeling substance, which is the quality job, not a byte job.

## 401c5619de1046deb9d98ad38c6c225b — decision — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Accepted baseline justification for `context_log.md` storage overhead: the byte ratio against whole-session-preservation tools — the WAL is ~0.5–1% of what "keep the entire agent session log per PR" retains, and that fraction shrinks over project lifetime.** Operator-settled framing of the analysis arc: the intended comparison is NOT substance-distillation efficiency, it is *storage overhead vs current solutions that retain the full agent session log*. On that denominator the WAL is 0.56% of the full session footprint (main transcripts + subagent transcripts + tool-result caches, 246.4 MB) and 1.01% of main transcripts only (137.5 MB) — measured in [`aea4063b`](context_log.md#aea4063b40d8433e95a751d600fc6b56--observation--2026-06-03). Conservative, not generous: each session adds MBs of transcript but only KBs of WAL, so the WAL's share of total session volume trends *down* as the project runs — the intuitive "append-only log will balloon" worry is answered (it grows ~200× slower than the thing you'd otherwise be keeping). Supplies the hard byte figure behind the previously-conceptual read-burden→trust-burden framing ([`a62ef52e`](context_log.md#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19)); does NOT supersede the absolute-scaling-cliff analysis ([`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29)), a different axis (AI-context limits, not per-PR storage). Two adjacent benefits stay deliberately unmeasured: substance-fidelity (companion `table` [`28b65944`](context_log.md#28b6594408ba4aeab38917bb984299fd--table--2026-06-03)) and downstream utility — the WAL's believed-positive-but-unsized help to execution churn and cold repo substance-scans. Propagation candidates if this becomes an evaluator-facing claim: `docs/executive_summary.md`, `docs/proposed_methodology.md`, `docs/opus_self_analysis.md` (none currently drifting — none cite the figure yet).

**Refs:** [`aea4063b`](context_log.md#aea4063b40d8433e95a751d600fc6b56--observation--2026-06-03), [`708f15a5`](context_log.md#708f15a5055a489e915f0a3403db447b--observation--2026-06-03), [`a62ef52e`](context_log.md#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19), [`e7c4b29`](context_log.md#2026-05-10--observation--authors-ivanclaudeopus471m--e7c4b29), [`4d7f1a8`](#4d7f1a8)

## 8577896ffaab461491f13e086994dd2e — observation — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Audit-cache coverage has a canonical-header dependency: the bootcheck probe builds its must-cover set (`WAL_STRONG`) by matching only the canonical hex-first header `## <hex> — <type> — <date>`, so this repo's pre-standardization legacy STRONG entries (date-first, backticked-type headers from 2026-05-08/09/10, e.g. `## 2026-05-08 — \`decision\` — … — \`e8d3458\``) are invisible to coverage and were never certified — yet the probe correctly reported `clean`.** Empirically: the probe sees 305 canonical STRONG headers (all covered); ~39 legacy entries (29 STRONG + ~10 WEAK/DEFERRED, incl. one obsolete `branch` type) fail the grep on two counts (`2026-05-08` is not `[0-9a-f]{7,}`; `\`decision\`` ≠ bare `decision`). **Adopter-safe — the blind-spot is stoa-ai-dogfood-only:** adopters generate canonical 32-char hex-first headers per §"WAL entry form", so their WALs are fully visible and `dist/`'s probe is correct for every adopter. **Resolution (operator-directed): accept as benign; do not revise.** Rejected fixes: broadening the probe grep = adopter-irrelevant complexity in a shipped script (fails the adopter-applicability check), nagging perpetually about settled entries; normalizing the legacy headers = in-place rewrite violating T2 append-only immutability (FP3) and breaking anchor links. The 29 legacy STRONG entries are settled foundational history, most superseded by later canonical entries. **Action:** the legacy hexes are backfill-recorded into an audit-cache certificate — a grandfathering bookkeeping cert, NOT a fresh Layer-2 coherence sweep — so a full set-diff gap computation does not resurface them. A separate, adopter-relevant follow-up (probe flags *unrecognized* WAL-shaped headers instead of silently skipping them — malformed-header defense-in-depth) is left as a candidate `/stoa audit` sweep, not actioned here.

**Refs:** [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31) (v0.11.0 audit-cache certificate-log mechanism this characterizes)

## 4e588c3f198a42f8b7d32c3b3dc63e91 — observation — 2026-06-03

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**The legacy coverage-invisibility census in [`8577896`](context_log.md#8577896ffaab461491f13e086994dd2e--observation--2026-06-03) omits an earlier tier: the pre-hex `#NNNN`-numbered bootstrap entries `#0001`–`#0013` (2026-05-08).** These predate hex IDs entirely — identity is the sequential `#NNNN` index per the file preamble (settled by `aa74270` + `e9fa237`) — so their headers carry no extractable hex token at all. Tier composition: **10 EC:STRONG** (9 `decision` + `#0011` `rollback`), 1 retired `branch` type (`#0006`), 2 `observation` (`#0005`, `#0007`). The true legacy non-canonical surface is therefore **52 entries / 39 STRONG** (13 / 10 here + the 39 / 29 date-first tier `8577896` counted), not 39 / 29.

**No certificate applies to this tier — and that is correct, not a gap.** The date-first tier received backfill cert `918d475…` because each of its headers carries a real trailing hex (`… — \`e8d3458\``) that a broad hex-keyed gap computation could extract and resurface as uncovered; the cert is insurance against exactly that. The `#NNNN` tier carries no `[0-9a-f]{7,}` run anywhere in its headers, so it is **unreachable by any hex-keyed must-cover computation** — the probe's `WAL_STRONG` grep, the main-agent header-hex set-diff, and `Refs:`-graph traversal (later entries cite these as `#0001`, never as hex) all skip it, present and future. A certificate cannot address it either: `delta:`/`covered:` enumerate WAL hexes, and these have none; covering `#NNNN` tokens would be off-contract and inert (they never enter `W`). **Accepted as benign on the same rationale as [`8577896`](context_log.md#8577896ffaab461491f13e086994dd2e--observation--2026-06-03):** settled foundational bootstrap history, built-upon and largely superseded by the subsequent forest; dogfood-only (adopters emit canonical hex-first headers, so their WALs stay fully visible). **Rejected:** assigning hexes (in-place header rewrite — FP3 violation, breaks `#NNNN` anchor links); `rollback` entries to re-anchor them (would falsely assert still-valid foundational decisions no longer hold — semantic corruption, not coverage plumbing). The only instrument that ever surfaces this tier is a manual full-header canonicality sweep; this entry is its standing answer.

**Refs:** [`8577896`](context_log.md#8577896ffaab461491f13e086994dd2e--observation--2026-06-03) (the date-first legacy census this extends/corrects to the full pre-standardization surface); [`b1b516f7`](context_log.md#b1b516f710454799b009481a2fe4a800--decision--2026-05-31) (audit-cache certificate-log mechanism)

## d11d2451b97241de99df766eee87af2d — observation — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**The Claude-host deterministic boot hook does not travel across clones when the adopter gitignores `.claude/` — observed in a real adopter (stoa-evals).** That repo (v0.11.3, reinstalled 2026-06-04) carries `.claude/` in `.gitignore:11` — a near-universal convention for keeping local agent settings/creds out of git. The Claude SessionStart wiring lives in committed `.claude/settings.json` per the merge-and-coexist model ([`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30)), which *assumed* that file is committed; under a gitignored `.claude/` it never enters git, so the deterministic boot backstop ([`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30)) does not reach teammates or fresh clones — boot silently reverts to discipline-only until each clone re-runs `install.sh`. Codex's equivalent wiring (`.codex/hooks.json`) IS tracked in that repo, so the Codex boot hook travels — a host asymmetry. Empirical cost is visible in that repo's `.stoa/beta_tracker.md`: 11 monothematic boot-discipline breaches (2026-05-29 to 06-02), zero first-tool-call self-catches, all converging on the very SessionStart hook Stoa shipped — yet for the Claude host where every breach occurred, the fix does not travel.

The stoa-ai dogfood commits `.claude/` (not gitignored), so it never exhibits this — the dogfood-masks-adopter pattern ([`b985cb71`](context_log.md#b985cb715d6f47ecb2ac88ce93ca9d9e--decision--2026-05-29), [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)); `ed66428c`'s self-healing-fresh-clone validation used a copied dogfood clone, leaving the gitignored case unexercised. This adds a fifth degradation-floor trigger — wiring-never-arrived-because-gitignored — beyond the trust-declined / policy / clobbered / non-Claude set named in `ed66428c`, and unlike those it is plausibly the common case rather than belt-and-suspenders. Fix direction (installer detects a gitignored `.claude/` and warns; and/or negates the ignore for Stoa-owned `.claude/` files with operator consent) is an open decision pending operator engagement, not settled here.

**Refs:** [`dfb944ba`](context_log.md#dfb944bab9a242c1b776b193f3270de6--decision--2026-05-30), [`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30), [`ed66428c`](context_log.md#ed66428c977b4b56bab92626509e7ec4--observation--2026-05-30), [`314a397e`](context_log.md#314a397eaa8b422e90fdb990ae4e7470--decision--2026-05-30), [`b985cb71`](context_log.md#b985cb715d6f47ecb2ac88ce93ca9d9e--decision--2026-05-29), [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)

## c5839a7498784e04aba217d83654276d — decision — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**install.sh and bootcheck both guard against a gitignored Stoa install that never reaches the team; install.sh also reminds the operator to commit.** Empirical anchor: a real adopter gitignored `.claude/`, stranding the committed SessionStart wiring so the deterministic boot backstop — and via `core.hooksPath` self-activation, the whole git-hook spine — never traveled to teammates ([`d11d2451`](context_log.md#d11d2451b97241de99df766eee87af2d--observation--2026-06-04)). Settled fix: (1) `install.sh` runs `git check-ignore` over the must-travel Stoa file set after placement and emits a loud terminal warning (ANSI color + icon, TTY/`NO_COLOR`-guarded) naming any ignored file — the primary catch, since the installer is the one who can edit `.gitignore`; (2) `install.sh` ends with a loud reminder that the artifacts must be committed for the install to take effect for the team; (3) `bootcheck-probe` runs the same guard and emits a Status-band `[stoa]` line, catching the installed-locally-but-not-committed case (hook fires for the installer, not teammates). Detection is `git check-ignore` on the actual committed paths, NOT hand-parsing `.gitignore` — it respects negations, so the recommended remediation (`.claude/` + `!.claude/settings.json`) does not false-positive. We warn; we never auto-edit the adopter's `.gitignore` (they must commit; we can't commit for them), consistent with the don't-touch-operator-config posture. Aligns with [`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30) ("committed install travels with the repo"); net-new guard neighboring [`b985cb71`](context_log.md#b985cb715d6f47ecb2ac88ce93ca9d9e--decision--2026-05-29) under the adopter-applicability discipline ([`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)). Artifact-coherence: docs/getting_started.md.

**Refs:** [`d11d2451`](context_log.md#d11d2451b97241de99df766eee87af2d--observation--2026-06-04), [`0daf84d4`](context_log.md#0daf84d42a1e4eda8682b93317772041--decision--2026-05-30), [`b985cb71`](context_log.md#b985cb715d6f47ecb2ac88ce93ca9d9e--decision--2026-05-29), [`04e12001`](context_log.md#04e120016a6a46bf93f6b4b26eb31f5d--decision--2026-05-26)

## 7625c8e56e9b406abef995b150b5f834 — decision — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**The vector-index contract shifts from quiet/gated remediation to an aggressive boot nudge: bootcheck reports an absent index whenever absent, and the agent surfaces a loud warning + asks to build.** `bootcheck-probe` emits a Status-band `[stoa]` line when the local index is absent (no `.stoa/index/wal_index.sqlite`), suppressed only by `STOA_NO_INDEX=1`; the agent renders it as a loud `===*WARNING*=== NO LOCAL INDEX` nudge (color/icon are unreliable in injected boot context, so a plain loud-marker string is the in-session convention) and asks whether to build, running `bash .stoa/index/bootstrap.sh` on consent. The probe stays read-only ([`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17) invariant) — it reports; the agent acts. **Fire-whenever-absent, NOT WAL-size-gated:** a byte/entry threshold is arbitrary and model-relative (a WAL too big for one model is fine for another), so gating on it is meaningless; the escape is `STOA_NO_INDEX=1`, advertised in [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md). This **supersedes** the no-nag / quiet-remediation stance for the index-absent case: [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17) ("No `[stoa]` suggestions for action"), [`c86ea98f`](context_log.md#c86ea98f450f41a9abf7de0476173e2f--decision--2026-05-18) ("not a warning that demands operator action"), and [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03) commitment 3 (remediation gated on WAL-over-slurp-threshold AND index-absent) no longer hold for this surface. Scoped supersession — the slurp-primary USE posture (index is a fallback; [`d45489b7`](context_log.md#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18), [`f16a4142`](context_log.md#f16a414274554962a92fdf50470f1777--rollback--2026-06-03)) and the always-ship/best-effort-install commitments of [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03) are UNCHANGED; only the boot-surface restraint changes (an absent index is now an install-incomplete state worth surfacing under the always-install posture). Fits the two-band boot model as a Status-band remediation line, not a `*No operator action needed*` anchor ([`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27)). Artifact-coherence: docs/getting_started.md.

**Refs:** [`d11d2451`](context_log.md#d11d2451b97241de99df766eee87af2d--observation--2026-06-04), [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17), [`c86ea98f`](context_log.md#c86ea98f450f41a9abf7de0476173e2f--decision--2026-05-18), [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03), [`d45489b7`](context_log.md#d45489b75cb246298c9ddb9fe6717e46--rollback--2026-05-18), [`f16a4142`](context_log.md#f16a414274554962a92fdf50470f1777--rollback--2026-06-03), [`37360049`](context_log.md#37360049b75d46ff48815d61774b630d--decision--2026-05-27)

## 2fd4f8c5c2964cfe97eebbd530fb5e5d — observation — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**The `.gitignore` negation that re-includes Stoa files must glob the dir CONTENTS (`.claude/*`), not the bare dir (`.claude/`) — git won't re-include a path whose parent directory is excluded.** Caught by a regression test while implementing [`c5839a74`](context_log.md#c5839a7498784e04aba217d83654276d--decision--2026-06-04): the recommendation first shipped in the warning text (`.claude/` then `!.claude/settings.json`) does NOT clear the travel guard — git never descends into an excluded dir, so the file negation is inert and the Stoa file stays ignored. Correct pattern: `.claude/*` + `!.claude/settings.json` (+ `!.claude/commands/`, `!.claude/agents/`); `.claude/settings.local.json` stays ignored. Fixed in the `install.sh` and `bootcheck-probe` warning text; `docs/getting_started.md` already used the correct `.claude/*` form. Encoded as a regression in `tests/bootcheck-probe-test.sh`: Case 24 (bare-dir + file negation still flags) vs Case 23 (`.claude/*` + negation clears). Note: an earlier chat message drafted for the adopter carried the bare-dir form and is superseded by the `.claude/*` pattern.

**Refs:** [`c5839a74`](context_log.md#c5839a7498784e04aba217d83654276d--decision--2026-06-04)

## a42d42f7c4b349588b0c1d5f5285c832 — decision — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Adopter `.gitignore` remediation guidance simplified: ignore only the per-user-local file(s) (for Claude Code, `.claude/settings.local.json`), never the `.claude/` or `.codex/` dir — sidestepping the negation footgun entirely.** The travel-guard remediation ([`c5839a74`](context_log.md#c5839a7498784e04aba217d83654276d--decision--2026-06-04)) first recommended ignoring the dir and re-including Stoa files via negations, which hit the git re-inclusion gotcha ([`2fd4f8c5`](context_log.md#2fd4f8c5c2964cfe97eebbd530fb5e5d--observation--2026-06-04)) and is fiddly even in its working `.claude/*`+negation form. Simpler correct guidance: only `.claude/settings.local.json` is genuinely per-user-local; everything else under `.claude/` (settings.json, commands/, agents/) is shared project config and should be committed — so adopters ignore the specific local file(s), never the dir. No glob, no negation. The `.claude/*`+negation form still works for unusual layouts but is dropped from the shipped warning text. Updated in `install.sh` + `bootcheck-probe` warning text and `docs/getting_started.md`; supersedes the negation *recommendation* in [`2fd4f8c5`](context_log.md#2fd4f8c5c2964cfe97eebbd530fb5e5d--observation--2026-06-04) (whose git-reinclusion *fact* remains true). Artifact-coherence: docs/getting_started.md.

**Refs:** [`c5839a74`](context_log.md#c5839a7498784e04aba217d83654276d--decision--2026-06-04), [`2fd4f8c5`](context_log.md#2fd4f8c5c2964cfe97eebbd530fb5e5d--observation--2026-06-04)

## bd64fcd91f6e428ba90e9e6d22ab5ddc — observation — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Live Codex in an adopter repo (acme-platform) surfaced a subagent-spawn gate ABOVE `features.multi_agent`: a session tool policy that allows spawning only when the operator explicitly asks — and the adapter's autonomous-spawn directive alone did not clear it.** At boot, the EC:STRONG coverage anchor fired and Codex moved to delegate the internal sweep; it found the spawn tool present and `multi_agent` enabled, but reported its tool policy restricted spawning to explicit operator requests, so it fell back to inline degradation (treating absence of an explicit delegation request as a hard gate). The autonomous-spawn directive from [`3a5583d8`](context_log.md#3a5583d8af64433e995c4a2b3cf22fdd--decision--2026-06-01) lives in the adapter — a spec the agent *reads* — which proved too little authority against a tool policy. Adding a host-neutral standing authorization to the **AGENTS.md dispatcher block** (project-authority instructions, loaded not merely referenced) cleared it: on restart Codex spawned the `stoa-coherence-internal-sweep` subagent autonomously and appended a clean coverage certificate, no operator prompt. Two further observations: (a) this Codex runtime exposed only a *generic* subagent launcher — no named `stoa-*` selector — and Codex delegated by passing the target `.codex/agents/stoa-*.toml` path to a generic child to read and follow; (b) the prior model treating `multi_agent` + project-trust as the whole gate ([`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30), [`fc6ce18e`](context_log.md#fc6ce18e458f479aa5791ea8ec6465ed--observation--2026-06-01)) was incomplete — dogfood never hit the explicit-ask policy, so the gate went unobserved until an adopter session with a stricter policy.

**Refs:** [`3a5583d8`](context_log.md#3a5583d8af64433e995c4a2b3cf22fdd--decision--2026-06-01), [`fc6ce18e`](context_log.md#fc6ce18e458f479aa5791ea8ec6465ed--observation--2026-06-01), [`0c76deb8`](context_log.md#0c76deb8c13c4d1ba9aa6e7a6dcf4907--decision--2026-05-30)

## f05eb1a757f54f06a3987d63db510b49 — decision — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Subagent spawn-authorization is added as a host-neutral standing authorization in the AGENTS.md dispatcher block (`src/dispatcher.md`) — not as Codex-specific adopter prose, and not in the adapter alone.** The tool-policy gate ([`bd64fcd9`](context_log.md#bd64fcd91f6e428ba90e9e6d22ab5ddc--observation--2026-06-04)) showed the adapter directive is read with too little authority to satisfy a runtime that gates spawning behind explicit operator authorization; only AGENTS.md (project-authority, auto-loaded) carries enough. Chosen over two alternatives: (i) a separate `STOA::CODEX-GLOBAL` managed block — Codex's literal patch — rejected because it needs new installer machinery to lay/replace/uninstall a second marked block, redundant with the existing one; (ii) the adapter-only home of [`3a5583d8`](context_log.md#3a5583d8af64433e995c4a2b3cf22fdd--decision--2026-06-01), insufficient per the finding. Folded into the existing `STOA::DISPATCHER` block instead: the unified installer already lays + marker-replaces it ([`d1693ec1`](context_log.md#d1693ec18fc14873a84e7e016ad0a460--decision--2026-05-31), [`e4c1a2d8`](context_log.md#e4c1a2d8320f490c8c24d6bc77bc0978--decision--2026-05-29)), so it reaches existing adopters on reinstall with zero new machinery. Framed host-neutrally ("Stoa's `stoa-*` procedural subagents are pre-authorized to spawn; if your runtime gates spawning behind explicit user authorization, this satisfies it") to preserve the block's settled host-neutrality ([`aeec6b10`](context_log.md#aeec6b1065734af89de61bd2dad1cb88--decision--2026-05-27)): a no-op for Claude, load-bearing for Codex, inherited free by future hosts with similar gates. Refines — does not supersede — [`3a5583d8`](context_log.md#3a5583d8af64433e995c4a2b3cf22fdd--decision--2026-06-01): autonomous-spawn is still the disposition; this adds the project-authority backing it lacked. Verified live: Codex spawned the internal-sweep subagent autonomously after the change. Artifact-coherence: tests/codex-smoke-test.md.

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Cadence #3's empty-T1 resolution changes from "append an aggregated negative-finding observation" to a scoped `STOA_NO_DECISION=1` commit flag — no WAL entry for a non-decision.** When the pre-commit `wal-audit` check fires (tracked artifact staged, `context_log.md` not) and the AI's cadence-#3 re-audit finds T1 genuinely empty, the AI re-commits with `STOA_NO_DECISION=1` set; `wal-audit` honors the flag and skips ONLY its own Phase-2 check, leaving the Phase-1 adopter-hook chain ([`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11)) untouched. No WAL entry is written. Rationale: recording "no decision was made" logs the *absence* of signal — it would generalize to every non-substantive turn (the AI makes the emit-or-not judgment constantly, answer usually "no"), and a WAL of "nothing here" entries is the opposite of OP1's curated signal density. The negative-finding observation was never justified on signal value — only as a mechanical way to stage `context_log.md` so Pass A passed ([`0780b922`](context_log.md#0780b922117545158beab900eb4cd23c--decision--2026-05-26)); this **scoped-supersedes that mechanic** while **reaffirming `0780b922`'s rejection of `--no-verify`**: `--no-verify` skips EVERY client-side hook (incl. the adopter's own linters / secret-scanners), so it stays off-limits; the env flag is scoped to the single Stoa check, and env-flag control of the hook follows the `STOA_QUIET` precedent in [`b7e2f04`](context_log.md#b7e2f04--decision--2026-05-11). The gate's real and only job is preserved ([`8278d792`](context_log.md#8278d792bbda4ce786472ea8d8bd2ac0--decision--2026-05-25), [`c2a6d18`](context_log.md#c2a6d18--decision--2026-05-11)): force the cadence-#3 T1 re-audit at the commit boundary and catch *pending-but-unflushed* T1 candidates (real signal) — the empty-T1 false positive now resolves to "proceed, write nothing." Historical zero-finding observations from the prior rule are left intact (FP3 — valid under the then-rule; superseded going forward, not retroactively excised). Artifact-coherence: none.

## 9e5643e0905448ea8c4a5e4227096b80 — decision — 2026-06-04

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**`/stoa audit` sweep observations become conditional: append a WAL `observation` only for a substantive STANDING finding, never on a clean sweep.** Both observation-mandating sweeps in the `/stoa audit` dispatcher change — cross-cutting drift (was "Append an observation recording the sweep") and WAL-internal-conflict (was "Always append… including a clean-sweep observation"). New rule: append only when the sweep surfaces a standing finding (an unresolved tracked item; an un-noted convergence recorded; a conflict + its resolution). A clean sweep — or one whose fixes were applied in place — gets NO observation. Rationale: a clean-audit record logs the absence of an inflection (the same anti-pattern as the cadence-#3 no-op resolved by [`c8c3c6d1`](context_log.md#c8c3c6d1d32148ecb173f7cd24d0bd06--decision--2026-06-04)); the coherence verdict is already carried by the internal-sweep's snapshot certificate (the bootcheck probe reads the cert, never an audit observation), the audit event by the git commit, and applied fixes are self-evidencing. This **scoped-supersedes** the clean-sweep clause of [`1b5d9f7`](context_log.md#1b5d9f7--decision--2026-05-12) ("a clean sweep also gets an observation — useful audit-trail data," written before the certificate existed) and **refines** its substance-finding half (still append on a real finding); finishes the resolution [`c8c3c6d1`](context_log.md#c8c3c6d1d32148ecb173f7cd24d0bd06--decision--2026-06-04) started (it set the zero-finding rule to "all cadences silent on zero, no WAL entry" but left this dispatcher text stale); and extends the index-coherency sweep's existing "no observation — substrate health, not project-state finding" carve-out to the other sweeps. The snapshot certificate + prune (internal-sweep step 6) is UNCHANGED — load-bearing. Artifact-coherence: none.

## 955bbc78b3fc4093befa913942183b06 — observation — 2026-06-08

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Host-harness survey for running Stoa on local open-weight models — the MLX stack is an inference server, not a harness; Aider misfits, Zed/opencode fit.** While scoping Stoa on local models (Qwen3.6-27B, Gemma-4-31B served via an MLX/`mlx-serve` OpenAI-compatible endpoint at `localhost:8000/v1`), a reframing surfaced: Stoa host adapters bind to an *agent harness* (session loop, tool/subagent orchestration, boundary hooks, dispatcher), never to a model. The MLX stack exposes only `/v1/chat/completions` — a model endpoint, no harness — so there is no "MLX adapter"; the local model is an interpreter swapped into an existing harness's brain socket. Research-grounded capability survey (per the [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30) four-axis method, extended to eight bindings: provider / instruction-load / tool-calling / subagents / lifecycle-hooks / dispatcher / structured-selection / git-hooks): **Aider** — architectural misfit (2/8): a narrow edit loop that rejects model-driven function-calling by design, no subagents/lifecycle-hooks/custom-commands, bypasses git hooks by default. **Zed Agent** — strong fit (6/8): custom OpenAI-compatible provider, auto-loaded instruction file, autonomous tool-calling + MCP, `spawn_agent` depth-1 subagents, Skills-as-slash-commands at the *same* `.agents/skills/` path Stoa already ships for Codex, git hooks honored; the two gaps are designed-for degradations — no agent-lifecycle hook (→ AI-runs-bootcheck floor) and no structured-selection tool (→ that cue stays dormant) — plus a single-file first-match instruction-load wrinkle. **opencode** — a genuine agentic harness (operator's selected target), binding surface not yet audited. Reuse for a Zed/opencode adapter is high: the generic-launcher subagent fallback ([`867ef095`](context_log.md#867ef095c7c64394883547a237fc8831--decision--2026-06-04)) and the host-neutral standing subagent authorization ([`f05eb1a7`](context_log.md#f05eb1a757f54f06a3987d63db510b49--decision--2026-06-04)) are inherited free. The model-capability question is harness-independent and dominant.

**Refs:** [`5a1835bb`](context_log.md#5a1835bb2fd54cab9c27d76ee4fde121--decision--2026-05-27), [`05380045`](context_log.md#05380045f8f7455e867bbba6b83cc6e2--observation--2026-05-30), [`5ee220d1`](context_log.md#5ee220d1--decision--2026-05-28), [`bd8df424`](context_log.md#bd8df424--decision--2026-05-28), [`867ef095`](context_log.md#867ef095c7c64394883547a237fc8831--decision--2026-06-04), [`f05eb1a7`](context_log.md#f05eb1a757f54f06a3987d63db510b49--decision--2026-06-04)

## 3c9fa31ec0b74f8f9e791030561cc61b — won't-do — 2026-06-08

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Aider ruled out as a Stoa host harness — architectural misfit.** Aider will not be pursued as a Stoa host. It is a narrow, well-engineered code-editing loop, not a general agentic harness: its founding design bet rejects model-driven function-calling in favor of a fixed edit-format protocol, so the model never acts as a free-form interpreter; the Stoa spec would ride as appended read-only context atop Aider's dominant edit-centric system prompt with no way to reframe the agent; and it offers no subagent spawning, no session-lifecycle hooks, and no custom slash-command registration, and bypasses git pre-commit hooks by default (`--no-verify` unless `--git-commit-verify`). Of Stoa's eight host bindings only provider-connectivity and git-auto-commit land. The operator's harness requirement moved from Aider to opencode; this records the foreclosure. Revisitable if Aider later adds general tool-calling plus an extension surface. Artifact-coherence: none.

**Prospective local-LLM Stoa hosts = opencode + Zed, gated on a model-suitability eval first (prove-then-build).** Pursue **opencode** and **Zed Agent** as the prospective harnesses for running Stoa on local open-weight models, but gate all adapter-build work on a **model-suitability evaluation of Qwen3.6-27B and Gemma-4-31B first**. Consequence for interpretation: temp>0 makes the N≥3 **consistency metric meaningful** — the earlier 1.00 consistencies were partly a greedy-decode artifact; the first-pass numbers remain on disk as a thinking-off comparison point.

Overall accuracy: Opus 15/15; `gemma-4-31b-6-128` 14/15, `gemma-4-26b-moe-4-256` 14/15, `Qwen3.6-27B` 14/15; `gemma-4-31b-4-256`, `gemma-4-31b-4-256-UD`, `gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128` 13/15. **All errors fall in the Adjacent class, concentrated on three deliberately-hard boundary fixtures (COH-013/014/015).** COH-013 is the discriminator: missed (read as Superseding) by 5 of 6 local models; Opus adjudged the Adjacent label correct but the Superseding read "genuinely defensible — the most contestable case in the set" (the candidate's `[stoa]` nudge tensions against the target's explicit "No `[stoa]` suggestions" clause, visible only in the full body, not the headline). ## 4c021c2922c04f8c91bb212f08555300 — observation — 2026-06-09

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

Source-level comparison of two external token-reduction tools, prompted by an operator question on how they relate to Stoa. **RTK** — a Rust CLI-output proxy; a host hook rewrites shell commands (`git`/`grep`/`read`/build tools) so their output is filtered before reaching context. Deterministic, lossy + one-shot (no original recovery), ~zero model-side self-cost, scope limited to dev/CLI output. **Headroom** (`headroom-ai`) — intercepts at the model-API layer (HTTP proxy via `*_BASE_URL` redirect, SDK wrapper, or MCP server). Its compression path is also fully deterministic (local ONNX models — Magika content-detect, a ModernBERT token-classifier "Kompress", bge embeddings; no LLM call to save tokens), and CCR (Compress-Cache-Retrieve) makes compression reversible via a SHA-keyed cache + retrieve-on-demand. But it carries real self-cost: ~200–300 tok of always-on MCP tool defs (or ~80–120 tok sticky retrieve-tool + ~20–25 tok/marker in proxy mode) plus hidden retrieval round-trips; and its feature set includes memory + failure-learning that author durable records into `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`/`MEMORY.md`. Headroom bundles RTK in its `wrap` mode (treats the two as complementary layers, not rivals).

Load-bearing finding for Stoa: both tools assume tool output is low-density and lossily compressible — the **inverse of OP1**'s curated, every-line-signal WAL. Pointed at `context_log.md` / `.stoa/` they would silently corrupt gap computation and coherence verdicts (RTK's grep cap is 200 results vs the 439-header boot scan; line-truncation would chop the ~400-hex audit-cache snapshot line). Headroom's memory/learn writes are an authored competing record in tension with FP2 ([`24677f8e`](context_log.md#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19)); its ephemeral compression cache is not. The only real prior break — RTK eating the pre-commit hook's stderr ([`9c4d8a2`](context_log.md#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15), resolved by [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15)) — is a *distinct* mechanism (a detection-signal channel) from this content-read-fidelity concern, and its "make it pure-AI" resolution does not transfer (you cannot make reading the WAL pure-AI). Storage lens: Stoa already accepts the WAL as ~0.5–1% of whole-session-preservation ([`401c5619`](context_log.md#401c5619de1046deb9d98ad38c6c225b--decision--2026-06-03)); Headroom's memory is that preservation alternative.

**Refs:** [`9c4d8a2`](context_log.md#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15), [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15), [`401c5619`](context_log.md#401c5619de1046deb9d98ad38c6c225b--decision--2026-06-03), [`24677f8e`](context_log.md#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19), [`8439b819`](context_log.md#8439b81979e74fe3944a5cff82953f37--decision--2026-06-01), [`717a71fc`](context_log.md#717a71fc0e4f49c8b5835761be4c3f16--decision--2026-05-18)

## 520461d7674d4d7cadce94df9fb1883e — decision — 2026-06-09

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

Settled Stoa's stance on external output-compression tools (RTK / Headroom class). They operate one layer below Stoa (transport) and run safely alongside it on the execute-phase surface, provided two conditions hold: coherence surfaces (`context_log.md`, all of `.stoa/` — especially `audit-cache` — and spec-owned files) are exempted from filtering, and durable "memory/learn" features that author a competing session record are kept off (FP2). **Declined to encode this in the composed runtime.** Reasons: it is an operator-environment configuration concern, not Stoa behavior; it is non-actionable by the AI at runtime (a transparent proxy filters without the AI's knowledge or choice, so a "be byte-faithful" directive cannot be acted on); there is no active failure driving it (the only real break — RTK vs hook-stderr, [`9c4d8a2`](context_log.md#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15) / [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15) — was a distinct detection-signal mechanism already resolved, and its resolution does not transfer to content reads); and the runtime is near its slim floor ([`a29ad739`](context_log.md#a29ad73973560e7f686c36a5f1e28147--decision--2026-05-27), [`4e8f6e05`](context_log.md#4e8f6e05376544cc9845caf456001a65--decision--2026-06-03): cut anything that doesn't change AI behavior). Shipped instead as adopter guidance — a "Coexisting with token-reduction proxies" section in [`docs/getting_started.md`](docs/getting_started.md). Recorded as considered-and-rejected so a future session does not re-propose the runtime clause.

**Refs:** [`4c021c29`](context_log.md#4c021c2922c04f8c91bb212f08555300--observation--2026-06-09), [`5e2c8b9`](context_log.md#5e2c8b9--decision--2026-05-15), [`9c4d8a2`](context_log.md#9c4d8a2--observation--2026-05-15), [`4e8f6e05`](context_log.md#4e8f6e05376544cc9845caf456001a65--decision--2026-06-03), [`a29ad739`](context_log.md#a29ad73973560e7f686c36a5f1e28147--decision--2026-05-27), [`24677f8e`](context_log.md#24677f8e0dcd43d09d1a8ff0baff7615--decision--2026-05-19)

## 32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9 — decision — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Balanced per-model sampling param set locked and deployed to the local-model clients (opencode / aider / OpenWebUI) — one set per family serving both interactive coding and Stoa reasoning.** Deployed values: **Gemma family** (all five variants — dense 6-bit/4-bit/4-bit-UD, MoE 8-128/4-256): `temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 64, repetition_penalty 1.08, max_tokens 32768, thinking_budget 16384, enable_thinking true` (no `min_p`, no `presence_penalty`). **Qwen3.6-27B:** `temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0.03, presence_penalty 0.3, max_tokens 81920, thinking_budget 49152, enable_thinking true`. Rationale: a single per-family set that holds for BOTH agentic coding AND Stoa's coherence/deliberation reasoning, so the operator runs one profile per model rather than task-switching presets. The Qwen `min_p 0.03 + presence_penalty 0.3` pairing is the **loop-brake** that tames the thinking-spiral — last session a coding-tuned Qwen preset (presence 0, low temp) ran away to ~50k thinking tokens and crashed the mlx inference server. **Enabling backend fix:** the mlx-vlm continuous-batching path's `_PositionedTargetSampler` silently dropped `top_k`/`min_p` (they never reached the sampler on the batched generation path), so the loop-brake was a no-op until fixed in the `pyai/mlx-vlm` repo (rewrote the positioned sampler to apply top_p/min_p/top_k filtering on the full batch before the keyed categorical draw; defaults stay byte-identical no-ops; regression tests added). **Revises** the param VALUES recorded in [`cfdb702a`](context_log.md#cfdb702a906940a789045ecbbeafd3e2--decision--2026-06-08) (Qwen `top_p 0.8→0.95`, `presence_pen 1.5→0.3`, adds `min_p 0.03`; Gemma `thinking_budget 24576→16384`) and reframes the set's purpose from eval-config to deployed-client-config; cfdb702a's re-run *methodology* (thinking-ON across all six, per-model sampling, seed-varied N≥3) is unchanged and stands. Artifact-coherence: none (values live in the external `pyai/mlx_local_stack` client configs; no tracked stoa-ai artifact content changes).

## 37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Stage-1 re-run under the deployed balanced params confirms the [`5bb2ac13`](context_log.md#5bb2ac13bae445cda147135f2dbfd8bb--observation--2026-06-09) verdict and validates the Qwen loop-brake — 100% Superseding-recall across all six, MoE Pareto-dominant, no spiral.** Re-ran the 15 labeled COH fixtures × N=3 seed-varied against all six `mlx-local` models, thinking-ON, with the [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11) balanced param set — and crucially **post-backend-fix**, so `top_k`/`min_p` actually reached the sampler this run (distinct empirical event from `5bb2ac13`, which measured the pre-fix / old-param config). Results (accuracy / Superseding-recall / consistency / latency): `Qwen3.6-27B` 93% / 100% / 1.00 / 180.6s (think ~5932 ch); `gemma-4-26b-moe-4-256` 93% / 100% / 1.00 / 22.9s; `gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128` 93% / 100% / 1.00 / 22.9s; `gemma-4-31b-4-256-UD` 87% / 100% / 1.00 / 71.7s; `gemma-4-31b-6-128` 87% / 100% / 1.00 / 79.9s; `gemma-4-31b-4-256` 80% / 100% / 0.98 / 60.7s. **Findings:** (1) **100% Superseding-recall on every model** — the safety-critical missed-conflict metric is universally satisfied even by the 80% model. (2) **The MoE pair is Pareto-dominant** — tied-best accuracy (93%) AND ~8× faster than Qwen, ~3× faster than the dense 31B models; `moe-4-256` is the standout for an interactive harness. (3) **Qwen spiral is tamed** — avg ~5.9k thinking chars, every call completed, no timeout, no server crash (validates the `32235820` loop-brake; the prior session's 50k-token runaway did not recur). (4) **Unsloth dynamic 4-bit beats standard 4-bit** at equal width (87%/1.00 vs 80%/0.98); accuracy otherwise tracks quantization monotonically. **Converges** with `5bb2ac13` on the headline verdict (local models are viable Stoa coherence classifiers → proceed to Stage 2 behavioral), now re-established under the deployed/corrected param set. Per-model JSON + logs under `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/balanced-stage1/`.

## 493ad1dee0d849e09ffe8631b4c83494 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Correction to [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11): the Stage-1 accuracy spread (80–93%) is NOT a capability or quantization ranking — it is a 1-to-3-case difference on three deliberately-contestable boundary fixtures, within fixture noise.** Operator pushback ("dense models lower accuracy seems off") prompted a case-level re-examination of the balanced-stage1 results. **All six models agree perfectly on 12 of 15 cases** — every Superseding fixture (COH-001…005), every Converging fixture (006…009), and Adjacent 010…012. The entire accuracy spread lives in **COH-013/014/015** — all labeled Adjacent, all "deliberately hard" per the fixture design — and every miss is in the **Adjacent→Superseding (or →Converging) over-flagging direction**, i.e. the *safe* error (the conservative bias [`c171912f`](context_log.md#c171912f--decision--2026-05-19) prefers), on cases where even Opus called the Superseding read "genuinely defensible" (COH-013, missed by 5/6 incl. Qwen — see `5bb2ac13`). With n=15, one case = 6.7%, so the 80/87/93% figures reduce to: how many of three coin-flip cases each model happened to call. **Therefore `37c8f97e`'s sub-claims "accuracy tracks quantization monotonically" and "Unsloth dynamic 4-bit beats standard 4-bit" do not hold** — the UD-vs-standard gap is a single case (COH-015), and the dense-vs-MoE gap is 1–2 cases, all on the contested triplet; a dense 31B is not a weaker classifier than a 26B MoE on anything unambiguous. `37c8f97e`'s headline findings are unaffected and stand: 100% Superseding-recall across all six, MoE Pareto-dominance **on latency** (the real, large, robust signal), and the tamed Qwen spiral. **Consequence:** Stage-1 accuracy does not discriminate these models; model selection rests on Stage-2 behavioral + latency, not Stage-1 accuracy. Re-confirms `5bb2ac13`'s own caveat that 15 in-distribution Stoa fixtures is too thin to resolve fine capability differences — the deeper synthetic-corpus N-sweep ([`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24)) remains the instrument for that and stays deferred.

**Refs:** [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11), [`5bb2ac13`](context_log.md#5bb2ac13bae445cda147135f2dbfd8bb--observation--2026-06-09), [`c171912f`](context_log.md#c171912f--decision--2026-05-19), [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24)
