## 040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**MoE Stage-2 behavioral: Stage-1 classification did NOT predict live-session competence — `moe-8-128` is a strong Stoa operator, `moe-4-256` is not, despite tying at classification.** Ran the `versioning` behavioral scenario (7 turns × N=3, balanced params, post-sampler-fix backend) against both MoE models → `results/balanced-stage2/`. **`gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128`:** Tier 1 (explicit) 8/8, Tier 2 (conversational) 2/2, Tier 3 (agent-trapped) 2/2, Tier 4 (agent-led) 0/2, AI-led floor **pass** ×3, FP 0; WAL mix 12 `decision` + 2 `rollback` (handles supersession); clean convergence, no spiral, ~29 min/3 runs. **`gemma-4-26b-moe-4-256`:** Tier 1 4/8, Tier 2 1/2, Tier 3 0/2, Tier 4 0/2, AI-led floor **fail** ×3, FP 0; WAL mix 5 `decision` only; **turn-6 spiral to ~129k reasoning chars / ~17 min emitting 0 WAL blocks** (convergence failure), ~75 min/3 runs. **Findings:** (1) **Classification accuracy does not predict behavioral competence** — the two tied at Stage 1 (both 93% / 100% Superseding-recall / 1.00 consistency, [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11)) yet diverged 5/14 → 12/14 on cue recognition; the behavioral instrument is essential and non-redundant with classification. (2) **The thinking-spiral is model-specific, not param- or hardware-bound** — under identical balanced params + `thinking_budget 16384`, `moe-8-128` stays bounded every turn while `moe-4-256` runs away on the hard distractor turn; the Gemma loop-brake (`repetition_penalty 1.08`, no `min_p`/`presence_penalty`) suffices for one MoE and not the other, and the `tb` cap did NOT prevent a 17-min zero-output runaway (qualifies [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11)'s spiral-tamed claim, which held for Qwen). (3) **Both MoE models emit zero `observation` entries** (decisions ± rollbacks only) — systematic under-capture of the EC:WEAK half of the WAL vs the parity Stoa expects; neither reaches Tier 4 (fully agent-led), though `moe-8-128` clears the AI-led floor. Both keep FP 0 (disciplined). **Provisional direction:** `moe-8-128` is a viable Stoa live-session operator; `moe-4-256` is not. Dense (×3) + Qwen Stage-2 paused for operator decision. Per-run transcripts + scores under `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/balanced-stage2/`.

**Refs:** [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11), [`5d12dff5`](context_log.md#5d12dff54a2648fabe82c41ee5ac4f4d--decision--2026-06-08), [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11), [`5bb2ac13`](context_log.md#5bb2ac13bae445cda147135f2dbfd8bb--observation--2026-06-09)

## cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Correction to [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11): the "`moe-8-128` is a viable Stoa operator" verdict is RETRACTED — operator-challenged and overturned on entry-type fidelity. It collapses Stoa's 5-type vocabulary to 2 (`decision` + `rollback`), and the keyword-based tier scorer was blind to it.** Operator pushed back ("if it doesn't capture observations it is not reliable"). Re-examined `moe-8-128`'s generated WALs + the versioning ground-truth. **Evidence:** all three runs are exactly **12 `decision` + 2 `rollback` — zero `won't-do`, zero `observation`, zero `table`** — despite the harness prompt and the full spec (in its system context) offering all five types. The c8 cue ("we won't support per-endpoint deprecation"; ground-truth type = **`won't-do`**) was logged as a `decision` ("Adopt all-or-nothing deprecation") — a foreclosure reframed as an affirmative commitment. **Why the tier scores misled (and why [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11) over-credited it):** `grading/score.sh` scores a true-positive on substance *keywords*, **type-agnostic** (Tier 3/4 only additionally require a `rollback` to exist anywhere in the WAL); so "Tier 1 8/8" measured topic-recall, not type fidelity, and masked both the `won't-do` mis-type and the type-collapse. **Why it disqualifies:** type→class is load-bearing across the spec (`won't-do` forecloses re-proposal; `observation` is EC:WEAK no-commitment; `table` is EC:DEFERRED; the class axis drives the coherence cadences + certificate emission). A model that stamps everything `decision` yields a WAL whose commitment-strength (EC) axis is corrupt — foreclosed alternatives read as commitments, empirical findings are lost or over-elevated. **Revised verdict: neither MoE model is a reliable Stoa operator** — `moe-8-128` has better cue-recall + handles blatant supersession (`rollback`) but shares the type-collapse; `moe-4-256` is worse on recall and spirals (040a4ebf's factual tier/spiral/FP data stands; only its "viable" conclusion is superseded). **Two implications:** (1) the eval needs a **type-fidelity metric** — score the expected entry *type*, not just topic keywords; the current scorer overstates behavioral quality. (2) **Entry-type fidelity is the discriminating axis** to track for the dense models + Qwen — the open question becomes whether *any* local model in this set produces faithful 5-type WALs.

**Refs:** [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11), [`5d12dff5`](context_log.md#5d12dff54a2648fabe82c41ee5ac4f4d--decision--2026-06-08), [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11)

## d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**mlx stack: request `seed` is inert and `thinking_budget` is a complete no-op — the "identical N=3 runs" are seed-replays, and the spiral is a `max_tokens` limit-bounce, not natural completion.** Direct probe of the resident MoE (`gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128`) settles two diagnostics raised by the byte-identical Stage-2 runs. **(1) `seed` is inert:** seed=0 and seed=1 (same prompt, temp 0.7, same sampling) returned byte-identical output — reasoning 3224 ch, content 4811 ch, identical token-for-token. **(2) temperature DOES reach the model:** temp 0.7 vs 1.3 diverged (reasoning 3224→3086 ch) — so sampling params propagate (the top_k/min_p fix [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11) holds); the cross-seed determinism is specifically the position-keyed `_PositionedTargetSampler` ignoring the request `seed`. **(3) `thinking_budget` is ignored:** thinking_budget=150 produced byte-identical output to no-budget (reasoning ran ~800 tokens, ~5× the "cap") — the server does not enforce it at all (consistent with [`e4f2a76a`](context_log.md#e4f2a76a030843ee8bb2a7bebff71802--observation--2026-06-08): vision-type models, reasoning-parser is dead config; budget enforcement rides the same dead path). **Consequences:** (a) the N≥3 **consistency metric is meaningless** on this stack — seed-varied runs are identical replays; the 0.98 outlier reported in [`5bb2ac13`](context_log.md#5bb2ac13bae445cda147135f2dbfd8bb--observation--2026-06-09) / [`37c8f97e`](context_log.md#37c8f97e3df841f2bc005dee17eeece3--observation--2026-06-11) was not sampling variance (likely batch nondeterminism). **Run N=1 going forward.** (b) The `moe-4-256` turn-6 spiral (~128,840 chars ≈ 32,768 tokens = `max_tokens`) is a confirmed **limit-bounce**: thinking is bounded ONLY by `max_tokens` (`thinking_budget` cannot trim it), so a runaway eats the whole token budget and truncates with `finish='length'` and zero answer. (c) **This is a real deployment defect, not an eval artifact** — opencode/aider also send `thinking_budget` and the server also ignores it, so these models spiral in actual sessions too; the eval faithfully reproduces deployed behavior. (d) Sampling-param tuning can only reduce spiral *propensity*, never hard-bound it; the real bounds are a **backend `thinking_budget` enforcement fix** (pyai/mlx-vlm, same class as the top_k/min_p fix) or the **client char-watchdog** built this session (the eval's spiral guard — discards the spiraled turn rather than masking it). Qualifies [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11) (its deployed `thinking_budget` values are inert) and the spiral framing in [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11).

## e307b3ad90874fcd93f2c7a6650435de — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**`thinking_budget` backend fix attempt: detection generalized to the multi-format registry (committed `630e343` in pyai/mlx-vlm, submodule-bumped), but runtime enforcement STILL fails — every offline component verifies correct, so the remaining bug is runtime-only and needs a debug-logging cycle to close.** Following [`d02b3eca`](context_log.md#d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7--observation--2026-06-11) (thinking_budget is a no-op on this stack), implemented the fix per the operator-approved plan: root cause was that the budget path (`_prompt_has_open_thinking` + `ThinkingBudgetCriteria`) scanned only the hardcoded `<think>` while the SSE splitter used the `prompt_utils.THINKING_FORMATS` registry — so Gemma (which opens thinking with `<|think|>`, not `<think>`) never registered and the criteria seeded `in_thinking=False`. Fix added `prompt_is_inside_thinking` (registry-based multi-format detector) and routed `_prompt_has_open_thinking` through it; committed as `630e343` "honor thinking budget" (note: commit message overstates — detection improved, enforcement not yet achieved) and deployed (mlx_local_stack submodule bumped 0652a84→630e343, server restarted). **Live probe (tb=150, gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128): budget still ignored — reasoning ~806 tokens, no truncation.** Exhaustive offline verification ruled out every checkable cause: the chat endpoint forwards `enable_thinking` to the template; the Gemma prompt carries `<|think|>`; the mlx tokenizer **wrapper** `decode(input_ids)` preserves `<|think|>` (not special-token stripping); `prompt_is_inside_thinking` returns True on that prompt; and the criteria is correctly wired into the continuous-batching loop (`ar.py` calls `criteria(tok)` per token AND feeds the forced token back to `self._next_tokens` at 1347-1349). So all components work in isolation; the failure is runtime-only — most likely `_prompt_has_open_thinking` returning False live (criteria seeded off) for a reason invisible offline (the `args.enable_thinking` value on the criteria path, or the actual admitted `input_ids`). **Closing it needs one debug-logging cycle** (log criteria-build state → bump → restart → probe). **Decision pending: shelve the backend fix and proceed with the eval using the already-working client char-watchdog** (spirals bounded for the dense/Qwen runs; the type-fidelity disqualifier [`cac4120d`](context_log.md#cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4--observation--2026-06-11) is independent of the budget). The detection improvement in `630e343` stands as a partial step regardless.

**Refs:** [`d02b3eca`](context_log.md#d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7--observation--2026-06-11), [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11), [`cac4120d`](context_log.md#cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4--observation--2026-06-11)

## 0f998963966e42a489526cb1e61bb0f8 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**`thinking_budget` enforcement FIXED and verified end-to-end — resolves the [`e307b3ad`](context_log.md#e307b3ad90874fcd93f2c7a6650435de--observation--2026-06-11) open thread (operator chose "fix", not "shelve"). The budget now caps runaway thinking and the model emits an answer.** Runtime debug logging pinpointed the root cause that exhaustive static analysis had missed: **the live generation path for mlx-serve backends is `dispatch.py`, not `generation.py`** (which I first patched — its criteria-build never fired, confirmed by 0 build-log hits). `dispatch.py` built `ThinkingBudgetCriteria` with the hardcoded `<think>`/`</think>` and gated `enable_thinking` on the `<think>` token-id appearing in the prompt. For Gemma those are **not real tokens** — both `<think>` and `</think>` tokenize to subword pieces ending in `">"` (id 236813) — so `enable_thinking` was forced False (criteria no-op) and the forced closer would have been a bare `">"`. **Fix** (pyai/mlx-vlm `28f11a1` + cleanup `aea0993`, pushed to origin/main; mlx_local_stack submodule auto-pulls via `git submodule update --remote`): added `prompt_is_inside_thinking` to `prompt_utils` (registry-based multi-format open-thinking detection); `dispatch.py` + `generation.py` now detect via the registry and feed the criteria the model's **real** delimiters (Gemma opener `<|think|>` id 98, per-turn closer `<channel|>` id 101), preferring a single-token closer so the forced close sequence is exact; regression test added. **Verified** (tb=150, gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128): reasoning capped at ~159 tokens, `finish=stop`, real answer emitted (content 6065 ch) — vs 806 tokens / `finish=length` / spiral-to-max_tokens before; trace confirmed seeded `in_thinking=True`, `start_id=98`/`end_id=101`, budget EXCEEDED at count 151, forced closer recognized. **Supersedes [`d02b3eca`](context_log.md#d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7--observation--2026-06-11)'s "thinking_budget is a no-op" conclusion** — it *was* a no-op; now fixed. **Consequence:** the deployed `thinking_budget` safety limits ([`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11)) now actually bound runaway thinking, so the spiral-prone Stage-2 models (moe-4-256, dense 31B, Qwen) get a fair test — bounded thinking plus a chance to answer — rather than spiraling to max_tokens with zero output. The client char-watchdog remains as belt-and-suspenders. (Operational aside: the fix verification was delayed by a stale 15h mlx-serve manager + two concurrent `runserver` sessions, not by the code.)

## 84b8469bbfee4f9b9c9f1d2d818ff51c — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**`moe-4-256`'s thinking-spiral is intrinsic and NOT tunable — sampling params relocate it across heavy turns but never eliminate it; over-tightening degrades WAL capture. Model selection, not tuning, is the lever. (Also confirms the [`0f998963`](context_log.md#0f998963966e42a489526cb1e61bb0f8--observation--2026-06-11) budget fix is single-turn-only.)** Per operator request ("tune moe4 to converge"), swept `gemma-4-26b-moe-4-256` sampling params on the versioning Stage-2 scenario (N=1, seed inert per [`d02b3eca`](context_log.md#d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7--observation--2026-06-11)): **baseline** (temp 0.7) spiraled on turn 3 (107k ch); **t05** (temp 0.5) → turn 7 (117k); **t05_tight** (temp 0.5 + min_p 0.05 + rep 1.12 + top_p 0.9/top_k 40) → turn 4 (128k); **t03_tight** (temp 0.3 + same tail) → turn 6 (124k). **Every set had exactly one runaway turn (~30k tokens, ~18 min, 0 useful output) and it RELOCATED each time** — because seed is deterministic, cooling/tightening reshapes the whole trajectory and the spiral resurfaces on a different heavy turn. No set produced a clean 7-turn run. **WAL capture:** t05 (temp 0.5, else default) best at 7 entries; t05_tight worst at 3 — tightening the tail + raising the penalty suppressed legitimate captures, so over-cooling is counterproductive for methodology behavior. **Conclusion:** the spiral is an intrinsic instability of this model on heavy reasoning turns, not a sampler mistune; tuning whack-a-moles it. Contrast `gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128` ([`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11)), which did NOT spiral on the same scenario at the same base params — **stability is a per-model property; selection beats tuning.** The only reliable backstop for a spiral-prone model is a hard cap (the client char-watchdog, or `thinking_budget` once its multi-turn gap is fixed), accepting that the capped turn yields no useful output. **Multi-turn budget gap:** all spirals reached ~30k tokens, exceeding the 16384 budget — so `0f998963`'s fix (verified single-turn) does NOT hold multi-turn; prior turns' closed thinking blocks make `prompt_is_inside_thinking` return False, seeding the criteria off. **Implication for the eval:** don't invest the same tuning effort on the dense models (predicts whack-a-mole); run dense + Qwen Stage-2 with the watchdog bounding spirals, measuring intrinsic stability + cue recognition + type fidelity directly. Sweep artifacts under `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/tuning-moe4/`.

**Refs:** [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11), [`32235820`](context_log.md#32235820f9634746a255d9024dff67d9--decision--2026-06-11), [`d02b3eca`](context_log.md#d02b3ecaf4314acdaecf2fda1164b2a7--observation--2026-06-11), [`0f998963`](context_log.md#0f998963966e42a489526cb1e61bb0f8--observation--2026-06-11)

## 3590e7cf0aa1424bacf7092351c98f65 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Correction to [`84b8469b`](context_log.md#84b8469bbfee4f9b9c9f1d2d818ff51c--observation--2026-06-11): the moe-4 non-convergence is a QUANTIZATION property, not a per-model one — and tuning remains a worthwhile activity.** Operator pushed back on the "stability is a per-model property; selection beats tuning" framing. Confirmed from `main_models.yaml`: `gemma-4-26b-moe-4-256` = `mlx-community/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it-**4bit**` and `gemma-4-26b-moe-8-128` = `...-a4b-it-**8bit**` — the **same base model** (gemma-4-26b-a4b MoE) at different quants. So the spiral comparison isn't two different models; it's **4-bit (spirals on heavy reasoning) vs 8-bit (converges) of one model**. That is textbook **quantization-degradation on heavy reasoning load** (documented for coding/math), not an intrinsic model defect. 84b8469b's sweep finding stands (sampling tuning relocates rather than eliminates the spiral *for the 4-bit variant*), but its conclusion is corrected: the lever isn't "select a different model," it's quant level — and **tuning is still worth pursuing** (the operator explicitly declines to discount the Gemma-4 family from the tuning activity). **Revised plan (operator):** tune **one model at a time**, starting with **Qwen3.6-27B (6-bit UD)** — search prior research for sampling combinations that make reasoning models converge faster with no quality drop, then trial them. Supersedes 84b8469b's "selection beats tuning" takeaway.

## dbd8a8726bf7403c86961793f7d7453a — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Qwen3.6-27B (6-bit UD) has NO convergence problem — it terminates cleanly with a full, high-quality answer at every tested sampling setting; the deployed params are already fastest, and research-recommended changes don't improve convergence. Strongly supports the quant-property hypothesis ([`3590e7cf`](context_log.md#3590e7cf0aa1424bacf7092351c98f65--observation--2026-06-11)).** Per operator plan (tune one model at a time, start with Qwen; research-backed combinations). Prior research applied: Qwen3.6-27B official thinking-mode params are temp 0.6 (precise) / 1.0 (general), top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0.0, presence_penalty **0.0** (the dense 27B, unlike the 35B-A3B MoE which uses 1.5); docs warn greedy/near-zero temp causes endless repetition; overthinking research ([arXiv 2508.17627](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17627v1), [2509.26522](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2509.26522)) frames the spiral as continuing past the Reasoning Completion Point, with presence_penalty as the documented anti-repetition dial. **Convergence probe** (one fixed heavy-reasoning prompt — API-versioning design — across 5 settings, single-turn, budget non-binding): all 5 finished `stop` with ~9.4–12.3k reasoning chars (~2.4–3k tokens) and full 8–8.9k-char answers — **no spiral at any setting**, nothing like the 4-bit Gemma's 30k-token runaway. **Counter-intuitively, the deployed `current` set (temp 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0.03, presence 0.3) had the SHORTEST reasoning (9445 ch) and was fastest (516s);** dropping to temp 0.6 *lengthened* reasoning (11.1k), and adding presence_penalty lengthened it further (presence 1.0 → 12.3k) — penalizing token-reuse pushes Qwen to keep exploring rather than converge. Answer quality was comparable across all (coherent, decisive, same recommendations) — **no quality drop**. **Conclusion: no Qwen param change is warranted from this probe** — the convergence collapse was specific to the 4-bit quant, not the model or its sampler; the 6-bit Qwen reasons and stops. **Caveat:** single-turn probe; the real spiral risk is multi-turn (where the 4-bit Gemma failed), so validate Qwen on the full multi-turn Stage-2 scenario before closing — that run doubles as the parked Qwen behavioral eval (cue-recognition tiers + type fidelity). Probe artifacts under `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/tuning-qwen/`.

**Refs:** [`3590e7cf`](context_log.md#3590e7cf0aa1424bacf7092351c98f65--observation--2026-06-11), [`84b8469b`](context_log.md#84b8469bbfee4f9b9c9f1d2d818ff51c--observation--2026-06-11), [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11)

## ce330f2661c445b2883e0223ab1f67b2 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Qwen3.6-27B (6-bit) Stage-2: severe MULTI-turn spiral (back half, turns 4–7, all watchdog-aborted) + type-collapse + weak cue recognition (4/14). Corrects [`dbd8a872`](context_log.md#dbd8a8726bf7403c86961793f7d7453a--observation--2026-06-11): the single-turn probe badly misled — Qwen is the WEAKEST operator tested despite the BEST Stage-1 classification.** Ran Qwen full Stage-2 (deployed params, N=1, watchdog 50k). **Turns 1–3 converged** (1720/1378/6095 ch — including turn 3, where the 4-bit Gemma spiraled), **but turns 4, 5, 6, 7 ALL spiraled** — each hit the 50k watchdog at ~25 min and was discarded. The back half collapsed: turns 4/5 are the F1-A override-asks (contradiction-handling), but turn 6 is ordinary c9/c10 decisions and spiraled too — so it's **cumulative** (once it tips into spiraling on turn 4, the growing context — now carrying discarded-turn markers — keeps it there), not purely override-ask-triggered. **Scores:** Tier 1 (explicit) 4/8, Tier 2 (conversational) 0/2, Tier 3 (agent-trapped) 0/2, Tier 4 (agent-led) 0/2, AI-led floor FAIL, FP 0. **WAL mix: 4 entries, all `decision`** (type-collapse, identical to both Gemma MoEs). **Corrects dbd8a872's "no convergence problem"** — that conclusion was single-turn-only and wrong; Qwen's spiral lives multi-turn (the single-prompt probe can't surface it). 6-bit raises the threshold (Qwen clears turns 1–3 incl. the 4-bit Gemma's death turn) but does NOT eliminate the spiral under sustained multi-turn load. **Cross-model synthesis:** (1) Qwen is the weakest Stage-2 operator (4/14 cues, spirals 4/7) despite the best Stage-1 classification (93%) — [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11)'s "classification ≠ behavioral" in its strongest form. (2) **Type-collapse is universal** — all four models tested (moe-8-128, moe-4-256, Qwen) emit only `decision` (+rollback for moe-8); none produce `won't-do`/`observation`/`table`. That is the dominant Stoa-operator disqualifier ([`cac4120d`](context_log.md#cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4--observation--2026-06-11)), independent of quant/architecture/spiral. **Implication:** convergence tuning won't rescue Qwen as a Stoa operator (type-collapse + weak cues are deeper than the spiral); and a proper multi-turn Qwen convergence sweep is expensive (~1h+/run, Qwen slow + spirals). Run artifacts: `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/balanced-stage2/Qwen3.6-27B-UD-MLX-6bit/`.

## e7b624a6e82c4c318d06fa5aff731039 — observation — 2026-06-11

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Dense Gemma Stage-2: `31b-6-128` (6-bit) ties `moe-8-128` as the best operator (12/14 cues, no spiral, AI-led pass, handles rollbacks); `31b-4-256-UD` (dynamic 4-bit) FULLY recovers convergence but loses behavioral depth. Type-collapse remains universal across all 5 models tested.** Ran both dense Gemmas full Stage-2 (N=1, warmup + watchdog 50k). **`gemma-4-31b-6-128` (6-bit):** all 7 turns converged, zero spirals (incl. both F1-A override-asks + the execute turn); Tier 1 8/8, Tier 2 2/2, Tier 3 2/2, Tier 4 0/2; AI-led floor PASS; FP 0; WAL mix **13 decision + 2 rollback**. **`gemma-4-31b-4-256-UD` (dynamic 4-bit):** all 7 turns converged, zero spirals — the Unsloth dynamic quant **fully recovers convergence** where the standard 4-bit MoE ([`84b8469b`](context_log.md#84b8469bbfee4f9b9c9f1d2d818ff51c--observation--2026-06-11)) and 6-bit Qwen ([`ce330f26`](context_log.md#ce330f2661c445b2883e0223ab1f67b2--observation--2026-06-11)) both spiraled; BUT Tier 1 8/8, Tier 2 2/2, Tier 3 **0/2**, Tier 4 0/2; AI-led floor **FAIL**; WAL mix **11 decision (decision-ONLY, no rollback)**. **Synthesis across all 5 models (moe-8-128, moe-4-256, Qwen, 31b-6-128, 31b-4-256-UD):** (1) **Convergence is quant × architecture × model, not pure bit-width** — 6-bit-Gemma-dense + 4-bit-UD-dense + 8-bit-MoE converge cleanly; standard-4bit-MoE + 6-bit-**Qwen** spiral. Dynamic quant and the Gemma-dense family favor convergence; the standard 4-bit and Qwen(at 6-bit) do not — so the operator's quant-degradation effect is real but model/arch and quant *type* (dynamic vs standard) also matter. (2) **Behavioral depth scales with quant:** 6-bit (rollbacks, AI-led pass, Tier-3 2/2) > 4-bit-UD (no rollback, AI-led fail, Tier-3 0/2) even when convergence holds — lower quant shallows the hard methodology behaviors. (3) **Type-collapse is UNIVERSAL and quant-independent:** every model caps at 2 types (`decision`+`rollback`, the 6/8-bit models) or 1 (`decision`-only: 4-bit-UD, 4-bit-MoE, Qwen); NONE emit `won't-do`/`observation`/`table`. This is the dominant Stoa-operator disqualifier ([`cac4120d`](context_log.md#cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4--observation--2026-06-11)), independent of convergence/quant/architecture. **Best operators:** `31b-6-128` (6-bit dense) and `moe-8-128` (8-bit MoE) — both 12/14, no spiral, AI-led pass, handle supersession. **Bottom line for "can local models do Stoa":** at the right quant they handle the *easier-to-mid* methodology (cue recognition, decisions, rollbacks, convergence) — but uniformly fail the full type vocabulary and the agent-led tier. Convergence is fixable by quant/model selection; **type fidelity is the remaining blocker — and it's comprehension/prompt-driven, not sampling.** Highest-value next step: attack type-collapse via prompt/spec on a best operator. Artifacts under `stress-test-harness/local-model-eval/results/balanced-stage2/`.

**Refs:** [`ce330f26`](context_log.md#ce330f2661c445b2883e0223ab1f67b2--observation--2026-06-11), [`040a4ebf`](context_log.md#040a4ebf4d6444dabb060e7eb445b74b--observation--2026-06-11), [`3590e7cf`](context_log.md#3590e7cf0aa1424bacf7092351c98f65--observation--2026-06-11), [`cac4120d`](context_log.md#cac4120d17dd42b0808b99efc425f1a4--observation--2026-06-11)

Scoped to these models, NOT a foreclosure of the local-model track.** The model-suitability eval gated by [`0dade311`](context_log.md#0dade311b9f54fda98c2e0e92d5fd221--decision--2026-06-08) has produced sufficient evidence: the evaluated local MLX models — the Gemma-4 family (`gemma-4-31b` dense + `gemma-4-26b-a4b` MoE, across quants) and `Qwen3.6-27B` — do not cut it as a Stoa operator. ## c9b62bf1d9594ee6b038b4f47abeb3ff — observation — 2026-06-12

**Thinking level was NOT controlled in the v0.11.5 cross-model run, but transcript forensics show it was symmetric (zero captured extended-thinking for both models) — so the Opus>Sonnet headline holds, while the absolute scores and the post-F1-E baseline-tracking sub-claim in [`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12) are confounded on the thinking axis.** The drive agents were spawned via the Workflow `agent()` interface, which exposes only a model-tier lever (`{model: 'opus'|'sonnet'}`) and no reasoning-effort parameter; thinking was left at the workflow-subagent runtime default. Forensics over all 18 drive transcripts: model assignment was correct (9 × `claude-opus-4-8`, 9 × `claude-sonnet-4-6`), and **zero `thinking` content blocks appear in any transcript for either model** (498 Sonnet assistant messages, 768 Opus). So whatever the regime, it was the SAME for both tiers — thinking is not a *differential* confound between Opus and Sonnet here, and the autonomous-tier gap (T3/T4) stands. **But** this is a no-extended-thinking regime, which differs from (a) the operator's real Stoa usage and (b) the prior baselines, which were run at **thinking effort xhigh** ([`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24), [`54823200`](context_log.md#5482320056734bbfab0d65a4cfb54dc0--observation--2026-05-28)). Consequences: the absolute fidelity numbers (Opus 0.93 / Sonnet 0.82) are a *floor* and likely understate both models' ceiling; the "v0.11.5-on-Opus tracks post-F1-E (light 0.94 vs 0.89)" claim in [`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12) is NOT apples-to-apples (xhigh baseline vs no-thinking run) and should be discounted; and whether the gap widens or narrows with thinking enabled is **unmeasured** (thinking could help Sonnet disproportionately and shrink the gap, or lift both equally). Certainty caveat: absence of `thinking` blocks could mean thinking was disabled OR that traces weren't persisted to the subagent jsonl — cannot fully distinguish, but the symmetric absence supports a uniform regime. Tooling note: per-subagent reasoning effort is not settable through the `Agent`/Workflow `agent()` path used here; a thinking-on comparison needs a drive path that exposes it (interactive sessions, or a harness reasoning-effort knob).

**Refs:** [`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12), [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24), [`54823200`](context_log.md#5482320056734bbfab0d65a4cfb54dc0--observation--2026-05-28), [`718bdc29`](context_log.md#718bdc294c594d6e961895488c5edfc2--observation--2026-05-20)

## 4db2e9454d9645c5a27d32accc76082b — observation — 2026-06-14

**Resolved the open tooling question from [`c9b62bf1`](context_log.md#c9b62bf1d9594ee6b038b4f47abeb3ff--observation--2026-06-12): a thinking-controlled stress run IS drivable — via the headless `claude -p --effort <level>` CLI (top-level session), NOT via the Agent/Workflow subagent path.** Investigated three ways. (1) Docs/capability (claude-code-guide): the per-subagent reasoning lever exists only as Agent SDK `AgentDefinition.effort`; the Claude Code `Agent`/Task tool exposes no effort parameter (open issue anthropics/claude-code#25669), and thinking-trigger keywords ("ultrathink") do NOT propagate to spawned subagents. (2) Empirical subagent test: a spawned `claude-opus-4-8` agent prompted with "ultrathink" emitted **0 thinking blocks** — keyword path dead for subagents. (3) The decisive find: the `claude` CLI (v2.1.177) itself has `--effort {low,medium,high,xhigh,max}` for `--print` (headless) sessions. Smoke test `claude -p "<reasoning task>" --effort xhigh --model sonnet` produced a genuine thinking block (867 chars) in its session transcript. The Agent SDK wraps this same CLI, so the SDK is unnecessary — and no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is needed (the CLI reuses existing Claude Code auth). **Implication:** the option-3 thinking-on re-run (apples-to-apples with the xhigh baselines [`425c34e4`](context_log.md#425c34e4ecd84ceb8aaf45d5c3bf3a9d--decision--2026-05-24)) is drivable by invoking `claude -p <drive-prompt> --model opus|sonnet --effort xhigh --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools …` once per run, identical effort across both tiers — into fresh run-roots (e.g. `…-opus48-xhigh` / `…-sonnet46-xhigh`) so the no-thinking floor run [`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12) is preserved for the thinking-lift delta. Why the original run had no thinking: the in-session Workflow `agent()`/`Agent` path I drove it with cannot set effort, so subagents ran the runtime default (no extended thinking) — confirmed by zero thinking blocks across all 18 drive transcripts.

## 9b4824cb0e2c4172b4166cccd7f1ea9a — observation — 2026-06-15

**Pre-commit `wal-audit` hook emitted spurious SIGPIPE stderr (`printf: Broken pipe` / `write error`) on every commit that stages `context_log.md` — adopter-facing noise; fixed by switching the Pass-A short-circuit check from a `printf | grep -q` pipe to a herestring.** Surfaced when committing [`b785947`]: the hook's `printf '%s\n' "$staged" | grep -qFx context_log.md` line emits broken-pipe noise because `grep -q` exits on first match and closes the pipe before `printf` finishes writing. Benign (Pass A still passed, the commit landed), but it fires on the common case — ANY commit that stages the WAL — for every adopter, not just this dogfood repo. Fix: `grep -qFx context_log.md <<<"$staged"` — no upstream process to receive SIGPIPE, identical match semantics, and herestrings work on bash 2.05b+ so it is adopter-safe even on macOS's stock bash 3.2. Edited canonical [`src/hooks/wal-audit`](src/hooks/wal-audit), propagated via `build/compose.sh` + `dist/install.sh install` (regenerated `dist/.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`, dogfood `.stoa/hooks/wal-audit`, and the `.stoa/installed` marker hashes). The sibling `grep -Fxf` intersection line reads all stdin and never short-circuits, so it does not SIGPIPE and was left unchanged. An inline comment was added at the fix site so the herestring is not later "simplified" back into a pipe.

## 926bd525628848958d3938fe948a7761 — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

New operational principle (sibling to OP4): **Stoa defines what DONE means and verifies semantic render↔forest coherence; Stoa does not own the loop that drives mechanical checks (tests, builds) to satisfaction.** Surfacing the agent-harness market against the operator's thesis (the right human↔AI surface is decisions, not code-diffs) collapsed an apparent "capture vs verify" two-layer split: there is one substrate — the decision forest — and "verifying that produced work satisfies the spec" is just coherence-checking a *render* against that forest, the same primitive Stoa already runs WAL↔WAL and WAL↔artifact. Semantic satisfaction (does the render embody the forest's decisions; what does the forest say DONE means) is methodology and in scope. Mechanical satisfaction (the iterate-to-green test/build loop) is host / agentic-coder territory — Stoa carries no tooling and no opinion on it.

This is a sibling to OP4 on a *different axis*: OP4 (`ddf0b6f8`) partitions git scope (methodology stops at T2); this principle partitions verification scope (semantic coherence is methodology; the mechanical-check loop is host integration). Same "Stoa is methodology, not the host loop" shape — it does NOT redraw OP4's T2/T3 line. It recasts (does not contradict) the capture-only framing under which cadence #7 (`6e1b3c4`) and F3-A (`fe65d949`) were written: those treat the end-of-impl reach into renders as capture; this principle reveals capture and verification as one render↔forest coherence pass. Grounds in FP4 (verification is coherence — AI's job) and the philosophical-over-mechanical bias (prefer the existing coherence primitive to a new verification layer). Spec realization (placement as "OP5", exact wording) pending operator reconsideration per the AI-instruction-block edit rule.

**Refs:** [`ddf0b6f8`](context_log.md#ddf0b6f8a63d41c88c512216f8921e82--decision--2026-05-20), [`2b16472f`](context_log.md#2b16472ff1fc4339a52b98f34d61333f--decision--2026-05-19), [`6e1b3c4`](context_log.md#6e1b3c4--decision--2026-05-14), [`fe65d949`](context_log.md#fe65d949d037277330739f132d9a5b9a--decision--2026-05-27), [`90b08641`](context_log.md#90b08641fbf94e9db0ad990f5a596070--decision--2026-05-26)

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Forest-as-DONE-oracle (A1).** New methodology language: at the end-of-implementation moment — when the agent is about to use arc-completion language (*"done"*, *"work complete"*, *"tests pass"*, *"ready for your review"*) or offer a next step — the agent grounds *"is this done?"* in the decision forest via the WAL-librarian, not only auditing T1 for unflushed candidates (cadence #7's prior capture role). This layers a *verification* lens onto cadence #7, whose origin (`6e1b3c4`) and F3-A extension (`fe65d949`) were capture-focused — consistent with the F3-A/F3-D precedent of layering onto #7, not a supersession. Trigger rides the existing "done"/"ready-for-review" cue surface; no new cadence. The reporting surface is constrained to decision-vocabulary (see the surface-constraint decision that references this one). Grounds in the new satisfaction-boundary principle (`926bd525`), the decision-forest definition (`5bcbe16a`), and agent-first quality (`717a71fc` — the agent's reasoning over the curated forest IS the verification engine).

## 6638a3ac4d954ea580bccd8adeab85f5 — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Render-relative decision line (A2).** Generalize F3-A's code-specific "architecture line" (`fe65d949`, sharpened by F3-D `0c0508c6`) into a render-agnostic **decision line**: in every render there is a threshold above which a choice is an inflection worth surfacing to the decision layer, and below which it is render-internal texture. *Where the line sits is render-relative, and the agent interprets it per render type* — architecture / contracts / naming-conventions for code; characters / storylines / arcs for prose; schema / relationships for a data model. Below the line stays in the render (variable names; word choice; column aliases); above it elevates to a decision.

This corrects a software over-fit in the substrate-sweep language: the principle was always render-agnostic (every artifact is a downstream render of decisions, `9f70a1f3`; humans interact with rendered surfaces, not raw bytes, `a62ef52e`), but the wording enumerated only code examples. Generalizes — does not supersede — F3-A/F3-D; their code instances become one render-type's reading of the decision line, and the F3-A→F3-D→F1-E cluster wording must be coordinated to bridge cleanly. Pure FP1 / philosophical-over-mechanical: trust the agent to interpret the line per render rather than enumerate a threshold per render type. Grounds in `926bd525`.

## cbee400ee2f84e948be4fb8079518ec0 — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Verification-surface constraint (A3).** Forest-verification (A1, `3fc3c595`) reports ONLY in decision vocabulary — never render-level (diff/word) critique — with exactly three legal outputs, all reusing existing machinery: render *confirms* a decision → optional `observation` citing the render as evidence; render *contradicts* a decision → override-ask (F1-A, `aaf9a6bd`); render surfaces an *undecided* inflection above the decision line → record candidate / surface ambiguity. The agent never narrates the diff (*"I changed handleAuth, added a guard"*) — that is the diff-review surface the thesis exists to escape; the book analogue is nudges about characters and storylines, never word choice.

This is the guardrail that keeps A1 from collapsing back into code-review: the human's interaction stays at the decision layer (PNG-bytes, `a62ef52e` — interact with rendered surfaces, not raw artifacts). Net-new — no prior entry scoped Stoa's reporting surface, so nothing to supersede. Declarative-over-imperative (`4b3c686b`): constrain the *vocabulary* of the report, not enumerate forbidden phrasings. Grounds in the satisfaction-boundary principle (`926bd525`).

## 1fbb34b4943e48c483fd9cd5ea8a556d — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

New WAL attribution **provenance value: `auto-discovered`**. Some entries record decisions that exist embodied in an artifact (a produced render, a pre-existing doc/codebase) but were never settled live in a Stoa deliberation — origin not established (a missed operator cue, an un-recorded AI choice, or an out-of-band / non-Stoa edit). Such an entry carries `auto-discovered` in the Authors slot in the standalone-AI shape: `[auto-discovered;<tool>(<model>)]` — `auto-discovered` is the origin/role, the tool+model is the AI that surfaced it. Honest on two axes: the choice's force is real (it's embodied/shipping) so its TYPE is whatever fits (per F3-A: choice→`decision`, fact→`observation`), while its PROVENANCE records that no identified actor settled it live — we also can't claim WHO introduced it.

Extends the attribution grammar (`9d1c5b4`) additively — a new origin classification, not a closed-set change (the "no backfill" rule there concerns missing attribution on old entries, not new provenance values). **Endorsement flow:** if the operator later accepts an auto-discovered decision (e.g. a "ship it" response to the backstop nudge), record their acceptance as a separate operator-authored `observation` Refs-ing the auto-discovered entry; the auto-discovered entry keeps its provenance ("operator didn't reject" ≠ "operator authored"). Reverting follows the normal rollback mechanism.

**Refs:** [`9d1c5b4`](context_log.md#9d1c5b4--decision--2026-05-12), [`926bd525`](context_log.md#926bd525628848958d3938fe948a7761--decision--2026-06-19)

## 4b92a4dee61e48baa743fbfd525a2628 — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Cadence #7(d) becomes bidirectional.** Existing direction is forest→render (for each EC:STRONG decision: render confirms / contradicts→override-ask / leaves-unmet). Added: **render→forest** — scan the render for choices above the decision line (`6638a3ac`) that NO decision covers. Motivated by the Opus baseline (`dc435185`): the forest-anchored scan reliably catches contradictions/confirmations/missing-tests but missed NEW-choice detection 0/3 — a decision-driven scan never examines render elements no decision points at.

**Defect class — render-ahead-of-WAL:** the artifact embodies a decision the WAL doesn't record. Three provenances — missed operator cue, un-recorded AI choice, out-of-band/non-Stoa edit — that refining-time cadences don't fully cover; the backstop is the ONLY path for the out-of-band case. **Handling:** for each uncovered above-the-line choice, auto-record at its true type (F3-A `fe65d949`: choice→`decision`, fact→`observation`) with `auto-discovered` provenance (`1fbb34b4`), and emit ONE aggregated substance-language nudge inviting ship-or-revisit — never WAL-language, never silent acceptance. This is NOT a "T2-before-settlement" violation: an already-embodied (shipping) choice is settled de-facto, so recording it with honest provenance is coherence — distinct from pre-committing an in-flight deliberation (a render that *contradicts an existing* decision stays held in the transcript per `cbee400e`/`dc435185`). Auto-discovered decisions are EC:STRONG, so Layer-1 grounding runs before seal — an uncovered choice that turns out to contradict the forest surfaces as Superseding→override-ask, not a clean auto-write.

**Backstop, not primary:** primary capture is refining-time (settling cues; F3-A for the AI's own deliberate execute choices). Scoped extension of `019d0aff` ("operator mutations out of scope to detect proactively; git history is recovery") — not a reversal: that rule scopes out proactive detection of mutations to the WAL *substrate*; this detects decisions embodied in the produced *render* at DONE-check time — a different surface at a different moment.

**Refs:** [`3fc3c595`](context_log.md#3fc3c595822d40e98afc42711a11f9cc--decision--2026-06-19), [`6638a3ac`](context_log.md#6638a3ac4d954ea580bccd8adeab85f5--decision--2026-06-19), [`cbee400e`](context_log.md#cbee400ee2f84e948be4fb8079518ec0--decision--2026-06-19), [`dc435185`](context_log.md#dc435185b9ad4082a0c1faed781add04--observation--2026-06-19), [`fe65d949`](context_log.md#fe65d949d037277330739f132d9a5b9a--decision--2026-05-27), [`1fbb34b4`](context_log.md#1fbb34b4943e48c483fd9cd5ea8a556d--decision--2026-06-19), [`019d0aff`](context_log.md#019d0aff04524191aed79734366f3e43--decision--2026-05-25)

No prior WAL entry covers decision-forest backfill (knowledge-base *file* ingestion is reference material, not forest-backfill; the "no backfill" attribution rule is its opposite) — genuinely new ground, parked so it isn't lost. Not now; revisit when adoption onboarding is prioritized.

## 65ccd2fac41545ac8c86fdfbd184d6f0 — won't-do — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Declined: an explicit "unmet" disposition rule for cadence #7(d).** The run-3 variance flagged in `0ed27449` (runs 1–2 recorded a "DF2 unmet" observation; run-3 left it as the chat no-ship verdict only) is NOT a defect, and #7(d)'s silence on the unmet outcome is correct. Rationale (operator): the **WAL ⊇ artifact surface** by design — the WAL is source-of-truth, artifacts are downstream renders (`a62ef52e` PNG-bytes, `9f70a1f3` artifact-as-render). A decision the render hasn't yet materialized is render-BEHIND-WAL: the normal, expected *leading* relationship — the decision is already in the forest; the render simply hasn't caught up. Nothing new to record. So "unmet" reports into the no-ship verdict (a chat surface) and writes nothing; runs 1–2 mildly over-captured (an observation for a non-anomaly), run-3 was correct. No imperative rule added — FP1: don't over-rule a mild non-failure derivable from the WAL⊇artifact principle.

This names the invariant the bidirectional #7(d) maintains: **WAL ⊇ artifact.** render→forest writes only for the one state that *violates* it — render-AHEAD (a choice in the artifact no decision covers; WAL < artifact) → A5 (`4b92a4de`) backfills as `auto-discovered`. The other forest→render outcomes are the invariant's normal states: confirm (materialized), contradict (render challenges a decision → override-ask), unmet (render-behind, decision leads → no action). A5 is therefore the repair operator for the invariant, not a bolt-on. **Residual (separate, pending operator confirm):** a judge-prompt calibration note — the judge penalized run-3 (0.72) for the WAL not showing render-behind status; per WAL⊇artifact it should not (its `silent_decisions` signal should fire on render-AHEAD only).

**Refs:** [`0ed27449`](context_log.md#0ed27449400840ce811ba2a897c5cf63--observation--2026-06-19), [`4b92a4de`](context_log.md#4b92a4dee61e48baa743fbfd525a2628--decision--2026-06-19), [`a62ef52e`](context_log.md#a62ef52e9b6e46f697ba274d770fd737--decision--2026-05-19), [`9f70a1f3`](context_log.md#9f70a1f3b299483cad04fd2bb6382e44--decision--2026-05-19)

## a50669350b9e4609a63ed191e38a43d7 — observation — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

Cross-model v0.12.1 daf-adherence comparison (calibrated judge — reads transcript, WAL⊇artifact fix applied — 1× per run). Opus 4.8 (`results/2026-06-19-v0.12.1-b0b768b-opus48`) median fidelity **0.92** (0.92/0.95/0.82); Codex gpt-5.5 (`...-codex-gpt55`, `codex exec --full-auto` on `stoa-codex.md`) median **0.90** (0.92/0.90/0.55). **Headline:** the **core DONE-check** (forest→render: contradiction→override-ask, confirmations, unmet, no-ship verdict, surface-purity) is **robust on both models (3/3 each)**. The **newer render→forest backstop** (proactively auto-discovering uncovered choices — pagination + PII — with `auto-discovered` provenance) is **reliable on Opus (3/3)** but **variable on gpt-5.5 (2/3)**: Codex run-3 missed both uncovered choices entirely (caught only the forest→render side), scoring 0.55. The harder/newer half — scanning the render for what NO decision covers — is the cross-model weak spot, consistent with autonomous-discovery being gpt-5.5's relative weakness in the prior sweep (`9b145490`).

Judge-fix effect: the WAL⊇artifact calibration (`65ccd2fa`) raised the render-behind-penalized run (Opus worst 0.72→0.82) but didn't fully eliminate the penalty at 1× (sonnet instruction-following imperfect on the nuance). Caveats: 1× judge (variance ~0.05–0.10 — the 0.92-vs-0.90 median gap is within noise; the real signal is backstop reliability 3/3 vs 2/3 and the floor 0.82 vs 0.55); Codex confound (host + model + `--full-auto` bundled); single scenario. Opus is the v0.12.1 daf-adherence baseline; gpt-5.5 is viable on the core DONE-check, weaker on the backstop. 3× median would tighten the per-run numbers before promotion.

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;codex(gpt-5)]

The render→forest miss in the v0.12.1 Codex run should be addressed with the quality-max harness path: add a broader render-ahead scenario family that validates uncovered-choice discovery across multiple render surfaces, and make the validation apply to Claude and Codex rather than treating it as a Codex-only regression. The target behavior is general `WAL ⊇ artifact` preservation: for consumer-facing choices embodied in a render but uncovered by the forest, the agent auto-records with `auto-discovered` provenance and surfaces one aggregated decision-vocabulary nudge.

The near-term spec proposal remains a review item rather than a landed change: sharpen cadence #7(d) so Forest→render and Render→forest are separate passes, and add a Codex adapter phase-separation nudge only if empirical reruns justify host-specific pressure. The harness enhancement should land first so both Claude and Codex can be re-evaluated against the same cross-surface backstop before changing the runtime.

## 4e24a49fb6394218813fd827ffae1fcc — decision — 2026-06-19

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Render→forest phase-separation, landed (v0.12.2).** The v0.12.1 cross-model eval (`4d93574a`) showed gpt-5.5 reproducibly skipping the render→forest backstop (run-3, all 3× judges): it completed forest→render (contradiction / confirmations / unmet + a no-ship verdict) and terminated before the unanchored render→forest sweep. Two changes:

- **Core (host-neutral, #7(d)):** a one-clause declarative addition — the two directions are separate passes; finishing forest→render (including reaching a no-ship verdict) does not complete the check, and render→forest still runs. States the independence property for every host; helps any model that prematurely terminates. Not execution-coaching.
- **Codex adapter:** a `DONE-check phase separation` directive — run the two directions as distinct sequential passes; don't end once the decisions are accounted for or a no-ship verdict is reached. Execution reinforcement placed where the empirical weakness is (gpt-5.5), per the core/adapter split: core states the principle, adapter coaches the execution. Opus needed neither (3/3 on the identical core), so the reinforcement is adapter-scoped — not core imperative-creep.

Also adopts Codex's eval hardening: the `render_to_forest` judge dimension (credits only an independent render-led pass that finds uncovered above-the-line choices; does NOT credit confirmations / contradictions / unmet / no-ship), and the cross-surface `render-ahead` scenario family (code + config + prose; tier-5) which tests generalization rather than overfitting the daf-adherence endpoint. Validation pending: cross-model (Opus + Codex) on both `daf-adherence` + `render-ahead` before the v0.12.2 baseline promotes. Supersedes `e104fb78`'s sequencing (spec-as-review-item / harness-first) — the operator landed the spec+adapter now, alongside the harness; `e104fb78`'s render-ahead + cross-model recommendation is carried forward here.

**Refs:** [`4b92a4de`](context_log.md#4b92a4dee61e48baa743fbfd525a2628--decision--2026-06-19), [`4d93574a`](context_log.md#4d93574a02b5443d86318cdea808fd3e--observation--2026-06-19), [`e104fb78`](context_log.md#e104fb7826f64a04a44bd166e49e5a0f--decision--2026-06-19), [`1fbb34b4`](context_log.md#1fbb34b4943e48c483fd9cd5ea8a556d--decision--2026-06-19)

## b79e0c9753d94222add40a4ad1fc51bc — decision — 2026-06-25

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8[1m])]

**Ship an advisory entry-well-formedness check (Pass B) in the pre-commit `wal-audit` hook — Stoa v0.12.3.** On any commit staging `context_log.md`, Pass B scans the **staged diff** for newly-added entry headers and emits a non-blocking `[stoa-wal-audit]` advisory (exit code unchanged) when a new entry has a missing `**Authors:**` line, an unrecognized type (outside the five: `decision`/`won't-do`/`table`/`rollback`/`observation`), or a malformed header (bad date). **Staged-diff-scoped** — only entries added in *this* commit, never re-scanning existing or imported history, so an adopter's prior entries and the grandfathered pre-attribution band are untouched. Structure-only; no content heuristics.

Responds to [`fe41ae07`](context_log.md#fe41ae079bf44bb78875de06ef2057af--observation--2026-06-25): the six-entry gap ran 6-for-6 silently because Pass A checks only co-staging, never content. **Advisory-not-blocking is deliberate** — it threads the precedent rather than overturning it: a *blocking* content validator (Pass C) was rolled back after false-positives ([`22b364ac`](context_log.md#22b364acec524f4e8eeaa52a40d78500--rollback--2026-05-26)), and attribution was deliberately made AI-discipline + `git blame` fallback, not a gate ([`9d1c5b4`](context_log.md#9d1c5b4--decision--2026-05-12)). ## f1a967ebc4524cac855501b12e21dde3 — decision — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Establish fresh cross-model baselines for the rebuilt synthetic stress-test harness — the "first run" that [`e3ead4fd`](context_log.md#e3ead4fd9dda49e399ee51e565c5436e--decision--2026-06-25) deferred when it reset `baselines.md` and dropped all historical `results/`. **Scope: the full matrix** — 3 drivers (Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Codex gpt-5.5) × 5 conditions (versioning-light, versioning-heavy, xheavy, daf-adherence, render-ahead) × 3 runs = 45 driven runs. Operator chose the full grid over the historical split (Claude→versioning+xheavy, Codex→render-verification) for complete per-driver-per-scenario coverage — it fills the gaps prior runs never had: a Claude render-ahead baseline and a Codex planning-arc baseline. **Execution staged light-first** (operator cost-control): every light condition across all three drivers is driven + validated before the heavy token-burners (versioning-heavy, xheavy) spin up, so harness defects surface cheaply.

**Method — held constant with the prior cross-model arc so future comparisons stay valid:**
- Drive at max reasoning via the per-run effort control the Agent/Workflow path lacks ([`4db2e945`](context_log.md#4db2e9454d9645c5a27d32accc76082b--observation--2026-06-14)): headless `claude -p --model opus|sonnet --effort xhigh`; `codex exec -m gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`. Codex effort is pinned explicitly to xhigh to close the `--full-auto`-default-effort confound flagged in [`9b145490`](context_log.md#9b145490b58144e7bd9051abad529708--observation--2026-06-15).
- Judge 3× per run, median fidelity ([`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21)), **held constant on Sonnet at `--effort xhigh`** — judges run headless because the plain Agent path can't set effort. Holding judge=Sonnet preserves comparability with the prior cross-model numbers ([`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12), [`3163853092`](context_log.md#3163853092a342948e37e306f9614420--observation--2026-06-14), `9b145490`), which now survive only in this WAL.
- Record per [`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21): run-root aggregates + `baselines.md` + `arc-capture-quality.md` committed (path-clean-verified), per-run raw gitignored; the public export keeps that shape.

Per-driver result numbers land as `observation` entries as each driver's runs complete.

**Refs:** [`377ddb2c`](context_log.md#377ddb2cd9414fb4a48bf1f53ce65e20--decision--2026-06-25), [`e3ead4fd`](context_log.md#e3ead4fd9dda49e399ee51e565c5436e--decision--2026-06-25), [`4db2e945`](context_log.md#4db2e9454d9645c5a27d32accc76082b--observation--2026-06-14), [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21), [`9b145490`](context_log.md#9b145490b58144e7bd9051abad529708--observation--2026-06-15), [`ae783256`](context_log.md#ae783256a3b644c3a778a2a4e02ca804--decision--2026-05-21), [`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12), [`3163853092`](context_log.md#3163853092a342948e37e306f9614420--observation--2026-06-14)

## c9529fadbcb147d0bb45e12a63bd6555 — observation — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Cross-model baselines for the rebuilt synthetic harness at **v0.12.3**, established per the method in [`f1a967eb`](context_log.md#f1a967ebc4524cac855501b12e21dde3--decision--2026-06-26) (full matrix; drive xhigh / gpt-5.5-xhigh; judge held constant on Sonnet at xhigh; 3× median per run). Judge fidelity (mean across run-medians):

| Condition | Opus 4.8 | Sonnet 4.6 | Codex gpt-5.5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| versioning-light | 0.94 | 0.863 | 0.903 |
| versioning-heavy | 0.94 | 0.883 | 0.92 |
| xheavy-xheavy | 0.853 | 0.79 | 0.84 *(N=2)* |
| daf-adherence-light | 0.877 | 0.847 | 0.773 |
| render-ahead-light | 0.947 | 0.733 | 0.82 |
| **overall mean** | **0.911** | **0.823** | **0.851** |

Ordering **Opus > Codex > Sonnet** and the xhigh band are consistent with the prior cross-model arc ([`e106e163`](context_log.md#e106e163722b4fea80f87bcc7a353dc1--observation--2026-06-12) Opus 0.93 / Sonnet 0.82; [`3163853092`](context_log.md#3163853092a342948e37e306f9614420--observation--2026-06-14) xhigh narrows the Opus/Sonnet gap; [`9b145490`](context_log.md#9b145490b58144e7bd9051abad529708--observation--2026-06-15) Codex ~0.90). Signals: Opus strong across the board (floors 3/3, done-match 9/9, render→forest perfect); Codex competitive — beats Sonnet on both planning-heavy conditions (versioning-heavy 0.92, xheavy 0.84) — but weaker on render-verification (daf 0.773) and under-uses the literal `auto-discovered;` marker (mechanical AI-led floor 1/3 daf, 2/3 render-ahead/xheavy) even where the judge confirms render→forest 9/9; Sonnet weakest overall, notably render-ahead 0.733 (render-led pass completed only 5/9) and high silent-decision counts on xheavy (17).

**Codex xheavy caveat — N=2, not 3.** The full matrix exhausted the Codex (OpenAI) workspace credits during the xheavy tail: run-2 completed clean; run-1 completed a full 7-turn arc + 581-line `ci.yaml` (32 entries: 24 decision / 5 observation / 2 rollback / 1 won't-do) but hit "workspace out of credits" at the turn-8 wrap (exit 1) — included as a valid data point; run-3 hit the wall immediately (empty) and is the one true gap. ## d65b3577aa354334ac61e122f79b4c3e — observation — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Judge-instrument robustness finding from the v0.12.3 baseline run. Sonnet-as-judge ([`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21)) occasionally emits **strict-invalid JSON** — unescaped inner double-quotes when a `notes` field quotes brace-heavy code (e.g. the `{"error": {...}}` error-shape snippets the daf-adherence scenario elicits). 2 of 81 light judges were affected; the verdict content was complete and high-quality, only unparseable. Fix: the harness extractor (`judge-one.sh`) was hardened to a three-tier parse — whole-text strict → string-aware balanced-brace scan (braces inside string values no longer miscount) → regex fallback for the scalar fields (fidelity + done-verdict/surface-purity/render→forest) flagged `_recovered`. The 2 affected light verdicts were recovered from their existing raw outputs (no re-judge); the 51 heavy judges then parsed with **0 failures**. Parser-only change — the judge prompt was held byte-constant across light+heavy per the constant-instrument requirement; tightening the prompt to demand strict-valid JSON is a separate future change, out of scope for an in-flight baseline.

**Refs:** [`f1a967eb`](context_log.md#f1a967ebc4524cac855501b12e21dde3--decision--2026-06-26), [`8cd705bd`](context_log.md#8cd705bd669d46bc8860a542c4206553--decision--2026-05-21)

## 94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af — decision — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Relocate the per-clone vector-index *runtime* out of the repo tree. The runtime (the `venv`, `wal_index.sqlite[-shm/-wal]`, `health`, `audit-state`, `post-commit.log`, bytecode) was stored in-repo under `.stoa/index/`. In this dogfood clone — `~/Documents/stoa-ai`, an iCloud-synced location — that meant iCloud re-uploaded the ~600MB venv and the constantly-rewritten SQLite on every embed/refresh; that churn is the breakage the operator reported. **Decision:** move all per-clone *derived* index state to `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/stoa/<cache-id>/`, with `STOA_CACHE_DIR` as an explicit override; `.stoa/index/` keeps only the committed, hash-tracked scripts. To honor `7e9c4a3`'s "per-operator local; no shared mutable state," each clone is namespaced by a per-clone UUID written once to the gitignored `.stoa/state/cache-id` — it survives a repo move (the id travels with the clone), is unique per clone, and maps to a per-machine `~/.cache`, so it stays collision-free even when the repo itself is synced across machines.

This **refines** `7e9c4a3` rather than superseding it: that entry's load-bearing conclusion (vector index as primary substrate; two-layer; derived / gitignored / rebuildable; WAL canonical) stands fully — only the asserted storage path (`.stoa/index/wal_index.sqlite`, never weighed against `~/.cache` at the time) is updated here. The model already lives in the shared HuggingFace cache (`~/.cache/huggingface/`), and `a5e3c92` already endorsed `~/.cache/stoa/models/` as industry-standard, so this extends an existing out-of-repo pattern rather than overturning a deliberate in-repo choice. The best-effort install ladder + `STOA_NO_INDEX` opt-out (`e192c0fc`, `7f8ed313`) and the `audit-state` watermark lifecycle (`2f8b6d1`) carry over unchanged to the relocated path.

**Refs:** [`7e9c4a3`](context_log.md#7e9c4a3--decision--2026-05-17), [`a5e3c92`](context_log.md#a5e3c92--decision--2026-05-17), [`2f8b6d1`](context_log.md#2f8b6d1--decision--2026-05-17), [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03), [`7f8ed313`](context_log.md#7f8ed313c5244cbc8d701874198461dc--decision--2026-06-03)

## a3a7bea4007c4e2abd07fc040d23d5d2 — decision — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Decouple index-script callers from the venv location via a stable launcher. With the venv relocated out of `.stoa/index/` (see `94b5492b`), the ~7 call sites that hardcode `.stoa/index/venv/bin/python3 .stoa/index/query.py` (the subagent WAL-tools doc, `/stoa query|index-refresh|audit`, and the `post-commit` hook) would each have to name the new home-dir path. **Decision:** introduce a committed launcher (`.stoa/index/run`) plus a single sourced path resolver (`.stoa/index/cache-dir.sh`). The launcher resolves the cache dir, exports `STOA_CACHE_DIR`, sets `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` so bytecode also stays out of the synced tree, and execs the relocated venv's python against the in-repo script. Callers invoke `.stoa/index/run query.py …` — a stable in-repo path — so the relocation is a one-time ripple and future relocations never touch callers. The resolver is the **single source** of the path logic across bash (launcher, `bootstrap.sh`, `post-commit`) and Python (`embed.py` / `query.py` read `$STOA_CACHE_DIR`, falling back to self-compute). Chosen over rewriting each caller to the new explicit path, which would re-ripple on every future move. `run` and `cache-dir.sh` become spec-owned, hash-tracked files (filenames illustrative; the load-bearing commitment is "one launcher + one resolver, callers never name the venv").

**Refs:** [`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26), [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03), [`7f8ed313`](context_log.md#7f8ed313c5244cbc8d701874198461dc--decision--2026-06-03)

## 62f39a1dde474eb0b292d195604e3e74 — decision — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Uninstall reaches into `$HOME` to remove only this repo's own cache key. Today uninstall is `rm -rf .stoa/index` (inside the repo); with the per-clone runtime relocated to `~/.cache/stoa/<cache-id>/` (`94b5492b`), uninstall must reach outside the repo to clean it. **Decision:** `install.sh uninstall` resolves and `rm -rf`s *this repo's own namespaced cache key only* — never a broad `~/.cache/stoa/` wipe. This is defensible despite the "never touch the operator's home" posture (cf. the global-git-config prohibition in AGENTS.md): the target is Stoa-derived, rebuildable, and scoped to this clone's UUID — categorically unlike operator data such as `~/.gitconfig`. It mirrors the prior `rm -rf .stoa/index` semantics, just at the relocated path. Paired with this: a one-time install-time migration that sweeps any pre-existing in-repo `.stoa/index/venv` / `*.sqlite` (gitignored derived state) so existing adopters upgrading do not leave ~600MB orphaned in their tree.

**Refs:** [`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26), [`e192c0fc`](context_log.md#e192c0fc55f4404aac5aad91ea35fdbf--decision--2026-06-03)

## aeb04156b3f44550b02f5e45d5df93b7 — observation — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Execute-phase hardening + live validation of the index relocation. During the security review of the destructive uninstall path (`62f39a1d`), the guard gained a defense-in-depth layer not spelled out in the original decision: the cache-dir resolver (`cache-dir.sh`) validates that the stored `cache-id` is a clean alphanumeric token — a non-token id (e.g. a path-traversal `../../…`) is rejected, so in `probe` mode it resolves to empty and the prefix-guarded `rm -rf` never matches a path outside `~/.cache/stoa/`. Layered with the `unset STOA_CACHE_DIR` subshell and the `…/stoa/?*` prefix guard, this means no `cache-id` content (garbage, traversal, tampered) can redirect the uninstall deletion outside the namespaced cache. Empirically exercised in `tests/index-install-test.sh` (a `../../../../SENTINEL` payload leaves the sentinel intact) and confirmed by the whole-branch review.

The relocation was validated end-to-end on the dogfood clone: `dist/install.sh install` built the substrate at `~/.cache/stoa/<cache-id>/` (venv + `wal_index.sqlite` + `health`/`audit-state`, 538 WAL entries embedded), with the in-repo `.stoa/index/` holding only the committed scripts — no runtime leaked back into the (iCloud-synced) repo tree, which was the motivating breakage.

**Refs:** [`62f39a1d`](context_log.md#62f39a1dde474eb0b292d195604e3e74--decision--2026-06-26), [`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26)

## 7139747a88b442a4ae3a361081cfba27 — observation — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Test-harness hygiene fix flowing from the index relocation ([`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26)). Found while running a throwaway adopter-install test: sandbox-install scenarios in [`tests/harness.sh`](tests/harness.sh) **orphan `~/.cache/stoa/<cache-id>` directories**. Pre-relocation the trial venv lived inside the trial repo and was cleaned with it; post-relocation it lives in the home cache, so `harness.sh clean` (which removed only `/tmp/stoa-trial-*`) left the cache behind. Confirmed by an orphan from an earlier `INSTALL-4` run.

Fix (harness-scoped, no shipped-code change): (1) `install_stoa_baseline` + `setup_BOOT_DRIFT` now default `STOA_NO_INDEX="1"` on the trial install — install-lifecycle scenarios don't need a real built index, so this skips the ~600MB build (INSTALL-4 setup dropped from minutes to ~2s) and is overridable for any scenario that wants a real build; (2) `harness.sh clean` now reads each trial's per-clone `cache-id` and prunes that one cache dir (alphanumeric-guarded, scoped to caches whose trial dirs it is removing) before deleting the trials. Verified: a trial cache is created at setup and gone after clean, with the live stoa-ai/stoa-test caches untouched.

Related shipped-code wrinkle surfaced (NOT fixed here): `bootstrap.sh` resolves `stoa_cache_dir` and `mkdir -p ""` **before** the `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` check, so a skipped install still writes a `cache-id` and an empty `~/.cache/stoa/<id>/` dir rather than being a true no-op. Harmless (bootcheck still reports the index absent), but it violates the clean-skip contract and affects adopters who set `STOA_NO_INDEX=1`. Fix would be a one-line reorder (skip check before cache resolution) + recompose/reinstall — deferred to operator decision.

**Refs:** [`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26), [`aeb04156`](context_log.md#aeb04156b3f44550b02f5e45d5df93b7--observation--2026-06-26)

## 3c4972d8a58c4c96a0c6102f701bbc4e — decision — 2026-06-26

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-opus-4-8)]

Make `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` a true no-op in `bootstrap.sh`. The relocation ([`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26)) introduced cache-dir resolution (`stoa_cache_dir` + `mkdir -p ""`) at the top of `bootstrap.sh`, *before* the `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` skip check — so a deliberately-skipped install still wrote a `cache-id` and created an empty `~/.cache/stoa/<id>/` dir, violating the documented clean-skip contract (surfaced in [`7139747a`](context_log.md#7139747a88b442a4ae3a361081cfba27--observation--2026-06-26)). **Decision:** move the `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` check above the cache-dir sourcing/resolution so a skip bails before touching anything; the idempotency check stays below (it needs ``). Now `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` truly does nothing — no cache-id, no cache dir. Verified live (a `STOA_NO_INDEX=1` reinstall created no cache dir) and regression-tested (`tests/index-bootstrap-test.sh` asserts no cache-id / no cache dir after a skip). Adopter-facing cleanliness fix for CI / constrained-env / defer-to-later installs.

**Refs:** [`7139747a`](context_log.md#7139747a88b442a4ae3a361081cfba27--observation--2026-06-26), [`94b5492b`](context_log.md#94b5492be2054890b1a5f50c13b4d1af--decision--2026-06-26)

## bc48abbb6ef74aa1a993e372ab475e4a — decision — 2026-07-09

**Authors:** [@ivan-avramov;claude-code(claude-sonnet-5)]

Ahead of building the public open-source export, a full PII/attribution sweep of `context_log.md` itself — previously exempted wholesale from the taint-clean grep pool under the FP3 "dead backlinks stay" rationale ([`e5574a25`](context_log.md#e5574a254c364e9c8271bf48638dcfeb--decision--2026-06-26)) — found the exemption had been applied too broadly: FP3 governs stale *file-path cross-references*, not real identifiers. Seven live instances had slipped through: two real local machine paths, two distinct real GitHub-Pages codename hostnames (three mentions total), one line spelling out the internal repo/company names directly ([`855a7550`](context_log.md#855a7550e67e9c8f849b1f1d043ce3c8--decision--2026-06-25)), and one real org-name mention introduced by the taint-clean entry itself while asserting cleanliness ([`e5574a25`](context_log.md#e5574a254c364e9c8271bf48638dcfeb--decision--2026-06-26)). None had reached any remote — local `main` was still ahead of `origin/main` with nothing pushed.

**Decision:** operator authorized a scoped, one-time exception to the WAL's append-only rule — mutate `context_log.md` in place to redact these seven instances (real paths → the file's existing `username` placeholder convention; Pages hostnames → a generic `<pages-codename>` form; the internal repo/company names and the real org name → their established synthetic equivalents). Scope held strictly to PII + attribution-handle content; no other editorializing of these entries' claims or reasoning. Verified clean by re-running the full sweep post-edit.

Separately, all `Authors:` lines across the WAL already use the public-form handle (`@ivan` / `@ivan-avramov`) — no attribution fix was needed there. The actual attribution leak was in git commit *authorship metadata*: every commit in this repo's history carries an internal-linked GitHub identity. That is a git-level fix (mailmap rewrite scoped to the export build), not a WAL content change, and is not covered by this entry.

**Why the exemption doesn't generalize going forward:** leaving stale cross-references unedited (FP3) preserves historical accuracy about what existed when; it was never license to leave real identifiers unaudited. Future taint-clean claims should treat `context_log.md` as in-scope for identifier checks, even though its stale *links* stay untouched per FP3.

**Refs:** [`855a7550`](context_log.md#855a7550e67e9c8f849b1f1d043ce3c8--decision--2026-06-25), [`e5574a25`](context_log.md#e5574a254c364e9c8271bf48638dcfeb--decision--2026-06-26)
